calgb49907.results: The design stopped accrual with 633 patients. At 10 years, recurrence-free survival was 56% with standard chemotherapy and 50% with capecitabine (HR 0.80, P = .03). Breast cancer-specific survival was 88% and 82% (HR 0.62, P = .03). Overall survival was 62% and 56% (HR 0.84, P = .16). Standard chemotherapy remained superior in hormone receptor-negative patients (HR 0.66, P = .02) but not in receptor-positive patients (HR 0.89, P = .43). 43.9% of patients had died.

calgb9343.methods: Between July 1994 and February 1999, 636 women aged 70 years or older with clinical stage I (T1N0M0) estrogen receptor-positive breast carcinoma treated by lumpectomy were randomly assigned to tamoxifen plus radiation therapy (317 women) or tamoxifen alone (319 women). Primary endpoints were time to local or regional recurrence, frequency of mastectomy, breast cancer-specific survival, time to distant metastasis and overall survival.
calgb9343.results: Median follow-up for treated patients was 12.6 years. At 10 years, 98% of women given tamoxifen plus radiation (95% CI 96% to 99%) were free from local and regional recurrence, compared with 90% of those given tamoxifen alone (95% CI 85% to 93%). Time to mastectomy, time to distant metastasis, breast cancer-specific survival and overall survival did not differ significantly. Ten-year overall survival was 67% (62% to 72%) with radiation and 66% (61% to 71%) without.

calgb9741.methods: This adjuvant trial used a 2 x 2 factorial design in women with axillary node-positive breast cancer. 2005 patients were randomly assigned to one of four regimens. These were sequential doxorubicin, then paclitaxel, then cyclophosphamide, four doses each, given every 3 weeks or every 2 weeks with filgrastim, or concurrent doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide for four cycles followed by four cycles of paclitaxel, given every 3 weeks or every 2 weeks with filgrastim. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival.
calgb9741.results: At a protocol-specified analysis at median follow-up of 36 months, 315 patients had relapsed or died against 515 expected treatment failures. Dose-dense treatment improved disease-free survival (risk ratio 0.74, P = .010) and overall survival (risk ratio 0.69, P = .013). Four-year disease-free survival was 82% for the dose-dense regimens and 75% for the others. Concurrent and sequential schedules did not differ. There was no interaction between density and sequence. Severe neutropenia was less frequent with dose-dense treatment.

calor.methods: CALOR was a pragmatic, open-label, randomised trial. It accrued patients with histologically proven, completely excised isolated locoregional recurrence after unilateral breast cancer treated by mastectomy or lumpectomy with clear surgical margins. Patients were centrally randomised 1:1 to chemotherapy, type selected by the investigator, or to no chemotherapy, stratified by previous chemotherapy, hormone receptor status and location of the recurrence. Endocrine therapy, radiotherapy for involved margins and anti-HER2 therapy were specified separately. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival.
calor.results: From August 2003 to January 2010, 85 patients were assigned chemotherapy and 77 no chemotherapy. At a median follow-up of 4.9 years, 24 of 85 (28%) in the chemotherapy group had a disease-free survival event, compared with 34 of 77 (44%). Five-year disease-free survival was 69% with chemotherapy and 57% without (hazard ratio 0.59, 95% CI 0.35-0.99, p=0.046). Benefit was greater for oestrogen receptor-negative recurrence (p interaction 0.046). Serious adverse events occurred in 12 of 81 treated patients.

cambria1.methods: CAMBRIA-1 is a phase 3, randomised, open-label trial in patients with ER-positive, HER2-negative early breast cancer at intermediate or high risk of recurrence. It compares 5 years of the next-generation oral selective estrogen receptor degrader camizestrant with standard endocrine therapy, either an aromatase inhibitor or tamoxifen. Patients enter after 2 to 5 years of standard endocrine therapy, with or without a CDK4/6 inhibitor, and without recurrence. The primary endpoint is invasive breast cancer-free survival.

cambria2.methods: CAMBRIA-2 is a phase 3, randomised, open-label trial in patients with ER-positive, HER2-negative early breast cancer at intermediate or high risk of recurrence. It compares 7 years of upfront adjuvant camizestrant, a next-generation oral selective estrogen receptor degrader, with standard endocrine therapy, either an aromatase inhibitor or tamoxifen. Abemaciclib is permitted in both arms for the first 2 years. The primary endpoint is invasive breast cancer-free survival. Secondary endpoints include invasive disease-free survival, distant recurrence-free survival and overall survival.

capitello-290.methods: Randomised global phase 3 trial. Patients with previously untreated metastatic triple-negative breast cancer were randomised 1:1 to paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 on day 1 of weeks 1 to 3 of each 4-week cycle plus either capivasertib 400 mg or placebo twice daily on days 2 to 5 of those weeks. PIK3CA, AKT1 and PTEN alterations were analysed by retrospective central molecular testing. Dual primary endpoints were overall survival overall and in altered tumours, with investigator-assessed progression-free survival a key secondary endpoint.
capitello-290.results: 812 patients were randomised from July 2019 to February 2022 and 30.7% had PIK3CA, AKT1 or PTEN alterations. Median overall survival was 17.7 versus 18.0 months (hazard ratio 0.92, 95% CI 0.78 to 1.08, p=0.3239), and 20.4 months in both arms among altered tumours (hazard ratio 1.05, p=0.7602). Median progression-free survival was 5.6 versus 5.1 months (hazard ratio 0.72), and 7.5 versus 5.6 months in altered tumours (hazard ratio 0.70). Grade 3 or worse diarrhoea occurred in 12.7% versus 0.7%.

capitello291.methods: This was a phase 3, randomised, double-blind trial. It enrolled pre-, peri- and postmenopausal women and men with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer who had relapsed or progressed during or after an aromatase inhibitor, with or without previous CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy. Patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to capivasertib plus fulvestrant or placebo plus fulvestrant. The dual primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival in the overall population and in patients with AKT pathway-altered tumours. Safety was assessed.
capitello291.results: 708 patients underwent randomisation. 289 (40.8%) had AKT pathway alterations and 489 (69.1%) had previously received a CDK4/6 inhibitor for advanced disease. In the overall population median progression-free survival was 7.2 months with capivasertib-fulvestrant and 3.6 months with placebo-fulvestrant (hazard ratio 0.60, 95% CI 0.51-0.71, P<0.001). In the AKT pathway-altered population it was 7.3 versus 3.1 months (hazard ratio 0.50, 0.38-0.65, P<0.001). Grade 3 or higher rash occurred in 12.1% versus 0.3%, diarrhoea in 9.3% versus 0.3%.

carpenter-letrozole-duration.methods: Multicentre, prospective, longitudinal phase IV study to establish the optimal duration of neoadjuvant letrozole that would allow breast conservation surgery in patients with early breast cancer who were initially unsuitable. Patients with primary, invasive, oestrogen receptor- and/or progesterone receptor-positive breast cancer and large tumours (T2 or more, over 20 mm) not initially suitable for breast conservation received letrozole 2.5 mg daily. Treatment continued until patients became eligible for breast conservation, progressed, failed to meet the criteria and withdrew for scheduled mastectomy, withdrew for other reasons, or completed 12 months of letrozole without a decision on breast conservation.
carpenter-letrozole-duration.results: A total of 146 patients were enrolled; seven without a valid post-baseline tumour assessment were excluded from the final efficacy analysis. At study closure 69% (96 of 139) were eligible for breast conservation surgery. The median time to a tumour response sufficient to allow breast conservation was 7.5 months (95% CI 6.3 to 8.5). Letrozole was well tolerated and most adverse events were grade 1 or 2.

cbcsg006.methods: Open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial at 12 Chinese centres. Patients aged 18 to 70 years with previously untreated metastatic triple-negative breast cancer and ECOG 0 or 1 were assigned 1:1 to cisplatin 75 mg/m2 on day 1 with gemcitabine 1250 mg/m2 on days 1 and 8, or paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 on day 1 with the same gemcitabine, every 3 weeks for up to eight cycles. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival, with a non-inferiority margin of 1.2.
cbcsg006.results: 236 of 240 randomised patients received at least one dose and were analysed, 118 per group. After median follow-up of about 16 months the hazard ratio for progression-free survival was 0.692 (95% CI 0.523 to 0.915), non-inferiority p<0.0001 and superiority p=0.009. Median progression-free survival was 7.73 months with cisplatin and gemcitabine versus 6.47 months with paclitaxel and gemcitabine. Grade 3 or 4 anaemia (33% versus 5%) and thrombocytopenia (32% versus 3%) were more common with cisplatin.

checkmate7fl.methods: This was a randomised, multicentre, double-blind phase 3 trial. 510 patients with newly diagnosed, high-risk, grade 3 or grade 2 (ER 1 to 10% or less) ER-positive, HER2-negative primary breast cancer were randomised to anthracycline and taxane-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy with either intravenous nivolumab or placebo. The primary endpoint was pathological complete response.
checkmate7fl.results: Pathological complete response was 24.5% with nivolumab and 13.8% with placebo (P = 0.0021). In patients with PD-L1-positive tumours (VENTANA SP142 1% or above) the rates were 44.3% and 20.2%. No new safety signals were identified. Five deaths occurred in the nivolumab arm, two of them related to study drug toxicity. No deaths occurred in the placebo arm.

chemo-n0.methods: Final 10-year analysis of the prospective randomised Chemo-N0 trial (recruitment 1993 to 1998, n = 647, 12 centres), with a median follow-up of 113 months. Patients with low tumour levels of uPA and PAI-1 (n = 283) were observed. Of 364 patients with high uPA and/or PAI-1, 242 agreed to randomisation to CMF chemotherapy (n = 117) or observation (n = 125). External quality assurance standardised the uPA/PAI-1 ELISA.
chemo-n0.results: The actuarial 10-year recurrence rate without adjuvant systemic therapy was 23.0% for observed high-uPA/PAI-1 patients, randomised and non-randomised, against 12.9% for low-uPA/PAI-1 patients (log-rank p = 0.011). High-risk patients randomised to CMF had a 26.0% lower estimated probability of recurrence than those randomised to observation (intention to treat HR 0.74, 0.44 to 1.27; p = 0.28). The per-protocol analysis showed a significant benefit (HR 0.48, 0.26 to 0.88; p = 0.019, disease-free survival Cox regression adjusted for tumour stage and grade).

chn-hypopmrt.methods: Randomised, non-inferiority, open-label phase 3 trial at a national cancer centre in China. Women aged 18 to 75 with high-risk breast cancer after modified radical mastectomy and axillary dissection were randomly assigned 1:1 to conventional fractionated radiotherapy (50 Gy in 25 fractions over 5 weeks) or hypofractionated radiotherapy (43.5 Gy in 15 fractions over 3 weeks) to the chest wall and supraclavicular region. The primary endpoint was 5-year cumulative locoregional recurrence in the modified intention-to-treat population, with a 5% non-inferiority margin. In this prespecified long-term analysis, 10-year outcomes were analysed without additional confirmatory non-inferiority testing.
chn-hypopmrt.results: Between June 2008 and June 2016, 820 patients were randomly assigned, 414 to conventional and 406 to hypofractionated radiotherapy, and 810 were analysed. Median follow-up was 11.5 years, median age 49 years, and 761 (94%) had stage III disease. At 10 years, cumulative locoregional recurrence was 10.3% (7.3 to 13.3) with conventional and 12.0% (8.8 to 15.2) with hypofractionated radiotherapy (HR 1.19, 0.79 to 1.82). Grade 3 adverse events at 10 years were few and similar, led by ischaemic heart disease (five patients in each group), and no grade 4 to 5 events, brachial plexopathy or treatment-related deaths occurred.

ciboma.methods: Phase 3 trial in patients with operable triple-negative breast cancer, either node-positive or node-negative with a tumour of 1 cm or more, who had received prior anthracycline and/or taxane chemotherapy. Triple-negative status was confirmed centrally by immunohistochemistry. Patients were randomly assigned to capecitabine or observation. Stratification was by institution, prior taxane-based therapy, involved axillary nodes, and centrally determined basal or non-basal phenotype. The primary objective was to compare disease-free survival between the arms.
ciboma.results: 876 patients were assigned to capecitabine (448) or observation (428). Median age was 49 years, 55.9% were node-negative, 73.9% had a basal phenotype, and 67.5% had received anthracyclines plus taxanes. Median follow-up was 7.3 years. The disease-free survival hazard ratio was 0.82 (95% CI 0.63 to 1.06, P=.136). In non-basal patients the disease-free survival hazard ratio was 0.53 versus 0.94 in basal disease (interaction P=.0694), and overall survival 0.42 versus 1.23 (interaction P=.0052).

citrine.methods: Randomised, open label, phase 3 trial at one centre in China between March 2020 and March 2022. Female patients with operable high risk triple negative breast cancer, node positive or node negative with Ki-67 of 50% or more, were randomised 1:1 after surgery. The carboplatin arm received four cycles of two weekly epirubicin and cyclophosphamide then four cycles of weekly paclitaxel with carboplatin. The control arm received four cycles of three weekly or two weekly epirubicin and cyclophosphamide then four cycles of weekly paclitaxel. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival.
citrine.results: 808 patients were enrolled and 807 received treatment. At a median follow-up of 44.7 months, three year disease-free survival was 92.3% with carboplatin and 85.8% in the control arm (hazard ratio 0.64, 95% CI 0.43 to 0.95, P=0.03), but the proportional hazards assumption was violated (P=0.02). Three year overall survival was 98.0% versus 94.0% (hazard ratio 0.41, 0.20 to 0.83, P=0.01). Grade 3-4 treatment related adverse events occurred in 66.7% versus 55.0%.

cleopatra.methods: Double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial at 204 centres in 25 countries. Eligible patients were 18 years or older with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer, no previous chemotherapy or biological treatment for metastatic disease, and ECOG performance status 0 or 1. Patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to pertuzumab or placebo, each with trastuzumab and docetaxel given intravenously every 3 weeks, stratified by geographical region and previous treatment. This prespecified end-of-study analysis was descriptive.
cleopatra.results: 808 patients were randomly assigned, 402 to pertuzumab and 406 to placebo. 50 patients crossed over from placebo to pertuzumab. Median follow-up was 99.9 months in the pertuzumab group and 98.7 months in the placebo group. Median overall survival was 57.1 months versus 40.8 months (hazard ratio 0.69, 95% CI 0.58 to 0.82). The 8-year landmark overall survival rate was 37% versus 23%. The most common grade 3-4 adverse event was neutropenia, in 49% versus 46%.

clever.methods: Randomised phase 2 trial in breast cancer survivors within 5 years of diagnosis who had detectable disseminated tumour cells on bone marrow aspirate. Patients received hydroxychloroquine, everolimus, or the combination. Primary endpoints were feasibility and safety. Secondary endpoints included disseminated tumour cell reduction or clearance and recurrence-free survival.
clever.results: 51 patients with detectable disseminated tumour cells started hydroxychloroquine (15), everolimus (15), or both (21). Treatment was feasible and tolerable, and one patient stopped early for grade 3 toxicity. At 42 months median follow-up, landmark 3-year recurrence-free survival was 91.7% for hydroxychloroquine, 92.9% for everolimus, and 100% for the combination, and was greater in patients who cleared disseminated tumour cells (hazard ratio 0.21, 95% CI 0.01 to 3.4). Estimated disseminated tumour cell reductions were 80%, 78%, and 87%.

comet.methods: Prospective randomised noninferiority trial at 100 US Alliance clinical trial sites from 2017 to 2023. It enrolled 995 women aged 40 years or older with newly diagnosed hormone receptor-positive grade 1 or 2 ductal carcinoma in situ without invasive cancer. Randomisation was to active monitoring with imaging and physical examination every 6 months (n=484) or guideline-concordant care, surgery with or without radiation (n=473). The primary outcome was 2-year cumulative ipsilateral invasive cancer, with a noninferiority bound of 5%.
comet.results: 957 participants were analysed. Median follow-up was 36.9 months. 346 patients had surgery for ductal carcinoma in situ, 264 in the guideline-concordant care group and 82 in the active monitoring group. 46 women were diagnosed with invasive cancer, 19 with active monitoring and 27 with guideline-concordant care. The 2-year cumulative rate of ipsilateral invasive cancer was 4.2% with active monitoring and 5.9% with guideline-concordant care, a difference of -1.7% with an upper 95% CI limit of 0.95%.

compassher2-rd.methods: Ongoing prospective, multicentre, phase 3 randomised trial in the United States and Canada. Eligible patients have high-risk HER2-positive residual disease after a predefined course of neoadjuvant chemotherapy and HER2-directed treatment, high risk being oestrogen receptor-negative and/or node-positive. Patients are randomised 1:1 to adjuvant T-DM1 plus placebo or T-DM1 plus tucatinib, alongside adjuvant radiotherapy and endocrine therapy where indicated. The primary objective is invasive disease-free survival.

compassher2pcr.methods: Single-arm trial in patients with clinical stage II or IIIa HER2-positive breast cancer. Patients received four cycles of trastuzumab and pertuzumab with either weekly paclitaxel for 12 weeks or docetaxel every 3 weeks for four cycles, followed by surgery. This report covers the secondary endpoints of pathologic complete response and associated factors. The HER2DX pCR score was measured on diagnostic biopsies in a subset. Logistic regression identified factors associated with response.
compassher2pcr.results: 2,175 patients were enrolled, 781 oestrogen receptor-negative and 1,394 oestrogen receptor-positive. Among the 2,141 who started treatment the pathologic complete response rate was 43.8%, 63.7% in oestrogen receptor-negative and 32.4% in oestrogen receptor-positive tumours. Higher rates occurred with negative or low oestrogen and progesterone receptor expression, HER2 immunohistochemistry 3+, and weekly paclitaxel. T3 disease had a lower rate in oestrogen receptor-negative tumours. Among 569 patients tested, a high HER2DX score independently predicted response.

confirm.methods: Double-blind, parallel-group, multicentre phase 3 study in postmenopausal women with oestrogen receptor-positive advanced breast cancer who had progressed after prior endocrine therapy. Patients were randomly assigned to fulvestrant 500 mg, given intramuscularly on days 0, 14 and 28 and every 28 days thereafter, or fulvestrant 250 mg every 28 days. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival. Secondary endpoints included objective response rate, clinical benefit rate, duration of clinical benefit, overall survival and quality of life.
confirm.results: Progression-free survival was longer with fulvestrant 500 mg (n=362) than 250 mg (n=374), hazard ratio 0.80, 95% CI 0.68 to 0.94, P=.006. Objective response rate was 9.1% versus 10.2% and clinical benefit rate 45.6% versus 39.6%. Duration of clinical benefit was 16.6 versus 13.9 months and overall survival 25.1 versus 22.8 months. The final overall survival report gave median survival of 26.4 versus 22.3 months, hazard ratio 0.81, 95% CI 0.69 to 0.96.

coopera.methods: Open-label, randomised, controlled phase 2 study at 59 hospital or clinic sites in 11 countries, testing whether giredestrant, a potent non-steroidal oral selective oestrogen receptor degrader, has a stronger antiproliferative effect than anastrozole after two weeks. Postmenopausal women aged 18 or older with untreated clinical T1c to T4a-c oestrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative early breast cancer, ECOG performance status 0 to 1 and a baseline Ki67 score of at least 5% were randomly assigned 1:1 to giredestrant 30 mg or anastrozole 1 mg orally daily on days 1 to 14, stratified by clinical T stage, baseline Ki67 score and progesterone receptor status. A 16-week neoadjuvant phase then gave the same regimen plus palbociclib 125 mg orally daily on days 1 to 21 of a 28-day cycle for four cycles. The primary endpoint was the geometric mean relative Ki67 change from baseline to week 2 in patients with complete central Ki67 scores at both timepoints. The report covers both the primary and the final analyses.
coopera.results: Between Sept 4, 2020, and June 22, 2021, 221 patients were enrolled and randomly assigned, 112 to giredestrant plus palbociclib and 109 to anastrozole plus palbociclib, with a median age of 62.0 years in both groups. At the primary analysis cutoff the geometric mean relative reduction of Ki67 from baseline to week 2 was -75% (95% CI -80 to -70) with giredestrant and -67% (-73 to -59) with anastrozole (p=0.043), meeting the primary endpoint. The most common grade 3-4 adverse events at the final analysis were neutropenia, in 29 of 112 and 29 of 109, and decreased neutrophil count, in 17 and 16. Serious adverse events occurred in five patients in the giredestrant group and two in the anastrozole group, with no treatment-related deaths and one death from myocardial infarction in the giredestrant group. The authors conclude that giredestrant shows encouraging antiproliferative and antitumour activity alone and with palbociclib.

coralleen.methods: Multicentre, randomised, open-label phase 2 trial at 21 hospitals in Spain. Postmenopausal women with stage I-IIIA hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative, PAM50 luminal B breast cancer and an operable tumour of at least 2 cm were randomly assigned 1:1 to six cycles of ribociclib plus letrozole or to four cycles of doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide followed by 12 weeks of paclitaxel. Neoadjuvant treatment lasted 24 weeks. The primary endpoint was the proportion with PAM50 low risk-of-relapse disease at surgery.
coralleen.results: 106 patients were enrolled. At baseline 92 (87%) had high risk-of-relapse disease and 14 (13%) intermediate. Median follow-up was 200 days. At surgery 23 of 49 patients (46.9%, 95% CI 32.5 to 61.7) in the ribociclib plus letrozole group and 24 of 52 (46.1%, 32.9 to 61.5) in the chemotherapy group were low risk-of-relapse. The most common grade 3-4 adverse event was neutropenia, in 43% and 60%. No deaths occurred.

crad001j2101.methods: Phase 2 multicentre study in adults with HER2-positive advanced breast cancer resistant to trastuzumab and pretreated with a taxane, who received everolimus 10 mg/day with paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 on days 1, 8 and 15 every 4 weeks and trastuzumab (4 mg/kg loading, then 2 mg/kg weekly) in 28-day cycles. Endpoints included overall response rate, progression-free survival, overall survival and safety.
crad001j2101.results: Fifty-five patients were enrolled, with a median of 3.5 prior chemotherapy lines for advanced disease (range 1 to 11); one remained on treatment at data cutoff. The overall response rate was 21.8%, the clinical benefit rate 36.4%, median progression-free survival 5.5 months (95% CI 4.99 to 7.69) and median overall survival 18.1 months (12.85 to 24.11). Grade 3/4 haematological adverse events included neutropenia (25.5% grade 3, 3.6% grade 4), anaemia and thrombocytopenia; non-haematological grade 3 events included stomatitis (20.0%), diarrhoea, vomiting, fatigue and pneumonia (5.5% each).

crad001j2102.methods: Phase 1b multicentre Bayesian dose-escalation study to determine a feasible dose and schedule of everolimus, an oral mTOR inhibitor, with vinorelbine and trastuzumab in HER2-overexpressing metastatic breast cancer pretreated with trastuzumab. Fifty patients received everolimus 5 mg/day, 20 mg/week or 30 mg/week with vinorelbine 25 mg/m2 on days 1 and 8 every 3 weeks and trastuzumab 2 mg/kg weekly. Endpoints included end-of-cycle-1 dose-limiting toxicity rate (primary), safety, relative dose intensity, overall response rate and pharmacokinetics.
crad001j2102.results: Grade 3/4 neutropenia was the commonest end-of-cycle-1 dose-limiting toxicity, in 10 of 30 patients at 5 mg/day and 4 of 14 at 30 mg/week; other dose-limiting toxicities were single cases of febrile neutropenia, stomatitis, anorexia and acneiform dermatitis, all at 5 mg/day. Everolimus 5 mg/day and 30 mg/week were chosen as the optimal daily and weekly doses. Among 47 patients evaluable for efficacy, the overall response rate was 19.1%, disease control 83.0% and median progression-free survival 30.7 weeks. No drug interaction between everolimus and vinorelbine was observed.

create-x.methods: 910 patients with HER2-negative residual invasive breast cancer after neoadjuvant chemotherapy containing anthracycline, taxane, or both were randomly assigned to standard postsurgical treatment either with capecitabine or without it. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival. Secondary endpoints included overall survival.
create-x.results: The trial stopped early because the prespecified interim analysis met the primary endpoint. At 5 years, disease-free survival was 74.1% with capecitabine versus 67.6% in controls (hazard ratio 0.70, 95% CI 0.53 to 0.92, P=0.01) and overall survival was 89.2% versus 83.6% (hazard ratio 0.59, 95% CI 0.39 to 0.90, P=0.01). In triple-negative disease, disease-free survival was 69.8% versus 56.1% (hazard ratio 0.58) and overall survival 78.8% versus 70.3% (hazard ratio 0.52). Hand-foot syndrome affected 73.4%.

ctrak-tn.methods: Multicentre phase 2 trial with integrated prospective circulating tumour DNA surveillance by digital PCR. Patients had early-stage triple-negative breast cancer with residual disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy, or stage II or III disease treated with adjuvant chemotherapy. Blood was sampled every three months to 12 months. Patients with detected circulating tumour DNA were randomised 2:1 to pembrolizumab or observation, and the observation group was closed by amendment. Co-primary endpoints were detection rate and sustained clearance on pembrolizumab.
ctrak-tn.results: 208 patients registered, 185 had tumour sequenced, 171 (92.4%) had trackable mutations and 161 entered surveillance. Circulating tumour DNA was detected by 12 months in 27.3% (44 of 161). Seven patients relapsed without prior detection. Forty-five patients entered the therapeutic component, 31 to intervention and 14 to observation. Of those allocated to intervention, 72% (23 of 32) had metastases on staging, and four declined pembrolizumab. None of the five who started pembrolizumab achieved sustained clearance.

curb.methods: Phase 2, open-label, randomised controlled trial of stereotactic body radiotherapy in patients with oligoprogressive metastatic breast cancer or non-small-cell lung cancer after at least first-line systemic therapy. Oligoprogression was defined as five or fewer progressive lesions on PET-CT or CT. Patients aged 18 years or older were enrolled from a tertiary cancer centre in New York and six affiliated regional centres. They were randomised 1:1 to standard of care or to stereotactic body radiotherapy plus standard of care, stratified by number of progressive sites, receptor or driver alteration status, primary site and type of prior systemic therapy. Neither patients nor investigators were masked. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival measured up to 12 months, with a prespecified subgroup analysis by disease site, in the intention-to-treat population.
curb.results: From January 2019 to July 2021, 106 patients were randomly assigned, 51 to standard of care (23 with breast cancer, 28 with NSCLC) and 55 to stereotactic body radiotherapy plus standard of care (24 with breast cancer, 31 with NSCLC). Of the 47 patients with breast cancer, 16 (34%) had triple-negative disease. The study closed to accrual before reaching its target sample size, after the primary efficacy endpoint was met at a preplanned interim analysis. Median follow-up was 11.6 months with standard of care and 12.1 months with radiotherapy. Median progression-free survival was 3.2 months (95% CI 2.0 to 4.5) with standard of care against 7.2 months (4.5 to 10.0) with radiotherapy, hazard ratio 0.53 (95% CI 0.35 to 0.81), p = 0.0035. In NSCLC it was 10.0 against 2.2 months, hazard ratio 0.41 (95% CI 0.22 to 0.75), p = 0.0039. No difference was found in breast cancer, 4.4 against 4.2 months, hazard ratio 0.78 (95% CI 0.43 to 1.43), p = 0.43. Grade 2 or worse adverse events occurred in 21 (41%) patients with standard of care and 34 (62%) with radiotherapy. Nine (16%) patients in the radiotherapy group had grade 2 or worse toxicity related to it.

d-care.methods: International double-blind placebo-controlled phase 3 trial at 389 centres in 39 countries. 4509 women with stage II or III breast cancer were randomly assigned 1:1 to denosumab 120 mg or placebo subcutaneously every 3 to 4 weeks alongside neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy for about six months, then every 12 weeks to five years. The primary endpoint was the composite bone metastasis-free survival.
d-care.results: 2256 received denosumab and 2253 placebo. Bone metastasis-free survival did not differ, median not reached in either group, hazard ratio 0.97 (0.82-1.14), p=0.70. Positively adjudicated osteonecrosis of the jaw occurred in 122 of 2241 treated patients, 5%, against four of 2218 on placebo. Treatment-emergent hypocalcaemia occurred in 7% against 4%.

daisy.methods: Phase 2 trial of trastuzumab deruxtecan in metastatic breast cancer, enrolling three cohorts by HER2 status: HER2-overexpressing (n=72), HER2-low (n=74) and HER2 non-expressing (n=40). The primary endpoint was confirmed objective response rate. Secondary endpoints included safety. Tumour samples were examined for T-DXd staining and ERBB2 expression.
daisy.results: In the full analysis set of 177 patients, the confirmed objective response rate was 70.6% (95% CI 58.3 to 81) in the HER2-overexpressing cohort, 37.5% (26.4 to 49.7) in HER2-low and 29.7% (15.9 to 47) in non-expressing disease. The primary endpoint was met in the first two cohorts. No new safety signals were observed. Among HER2 immunohistochemistry 0 patients, 5 of 14 (35.7%) with below-median ERBB2 expression responded versus 3 of 10 (30%) above the median.

daphne.methods: Single-arm prospective phase 2 trial. Patients with treatment-naive stage II to III HER2-positive breast cancer received neoadjuvant weekly paclitaxel for 12 doses with trastuzumab and pertuzumab every 3 weeks for 4 doses, then surgery. Adjuvant therapy was guided by pathologic response, with antibody doublet alone for patients with pathologic complete response. The primary endpoint was receipt of adjuvant non-HER2-directed cytotoxic chemotherapy.
daphne.results: Ninety-eight patients received at least one dose. Median age was 50 years, 86 percent had stage II tumours and 34 percent were hormone receptor negative. Five patients with incomplete clinical response received doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide before surgery and were classified as non-pCR. The overall pCR rate was 56.7 percent. Adherence to antibody-only adjuvant therapy was 98.2 percent. At median follow-up of 19.1 months there were no recurrences.

dart-metaplastic.methods: Prospective, open-label, multicenter phase 2 trial with a two-stage design, run as cohort 36 of the DART / SWOG S1609 basket study of dual anti-CTLA-4 and anti-PD-1 blockade in rare tumours. Patients with advanced metaplastic breast cancer received ipilimumab 1 mg/kg intravenously every 6 weeks plus nivolumab 240 mg intravenously every 2 weeks. The primary endpoint was objective response rate. Secondary endpoints included progression-free survival, overall survival and toxicity.
dart-metaplastic.results: 17 evaluable patients enrolled, median age 60 years (range 26 to 85), with a median of 2 prior lines of therapy (range 0 to 5). The objective response rate was 18%, 3 of 17 patients achieving an objective response, 1 complete and 2 partial, in 2 spindle cell and 1 chondromyxoid tumour, all ongoing at 28+, 33+ and 34+ months. Median progression-free survival was 2 months and median overall survival 12 months. 11 patients (65%) had adverse events including one grade 5 event, and 8 (47%) had an immune-related adverse event, with adrenal insufficiency in all 3 responders. Responses occurred in tumours with low tumour mutational burden, low PD-L1 and absent tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes.

data.methods: Prospective, randomised, open-label, multicentre phase 3 study in 79 hospitals in the Netherlands. Postmenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive early breast cancer and no sign of recurrence after 2 to 3 years of adjuvant tamoxifen were randomly assigned 1:1 to 3 or 6 years of anastrozole 1 mg once daily. Stratification was by nodal status, hormone receptor status, HER2 status and duration of tamoxifen. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival starting beyond 3 years after randomisation.
data.results: 1912 patients were screened, 955 assigned to 3 years and 957 to 6 years of anastrozole. 1860 were eligible and 1660 were disease free 3 years after randomisation. Five-year adapted disease-free survival was 83.1% (95% CI 80.0 to 86.3) in the 6-year group and 79.4% in the 3-year group (hazard ratio 0.79, 95% CI 0.62 to 1.02, p=0.066). The 6-year group had more arthralgia or myalgia, 58% versus 53%, and more osteopenia or osteoporosis, 21% versus 16%.

dawna-1.methods: Double-blind randomised phase 3 trial. Patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer whose disease had progressed after endocrine therapy were randomised 2 to 1 to dalpiciclib plus fulvestrant or placebo plus fulvestrant. The primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival. The report is an interim analysis.
dawna-1.results: A total of 361 patients were randomised. Median progression-free survival was 15.7 months (95% CI 11.1 to not reached) with dalpiciclib plus fulvestrant versus 7.2 months (95% CI 5.6 to 9.2) with placebo plus fulvestrant, hazard ratio 0.42 (95% CI 0.31 to 0.58), one-sided p less than 0.0001. Grade 3 or 4 neutropenia occurred in 84.2 percent and leukopenia in 62.1 percent. Serious adverse events occurred in 5.8 percent versus 6.7 percent.

dawna-2.methods: Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial at 42 hospitals in China. Patients with untreated hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer were randomly assigned 2 to 1 to oral dalpiciclib 150 mg daily for 3 weeks of every 4, or matching placebo. Both groups received letrozole 2.5 mg or anastrozole 1 mg daily. Randomisation was stratified by visceral metastasis, previous endocrine therapy and endocrine partner. The primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival.
dawna-2.results: 456 patients were randomised, 303 to dalpiciclib and 153 to placebo. At median follow-up of 21.6 months, median progression-free survival was 30.6 months (95% CI 30.6 to not reached) versus 18.2 months (95% CI 16.5 to 22.5), stratified hazard ratio 0.51 (95% CI 0.38 to 0.69), one-sided p less than 0.0001. Grade 3 or 4 adverse events occurred in 90 percent versus 12 percent, most often neutropenia and leukopenia. Two treatment-related deaths occurred with dalpiciclib.

debbrah.methods: Ongoing single-arm, five-cohort phase 2 study in pretreated HER2-positive or HER2-low advanced breast cancer with stable, untreated or progressing brain metastases, or leptomeningeal carcinomatosis. This report covers HER2-positive patients with non-progressing brain metastases after local therapy (cohort 1, 8 patients), asymptomatic untreated brain metastases (cohort 2, 4 patients) and brain metastases progressing after local therapy (cohort 3, 9 patients). Patients received trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg intravenously every 21 days.
debbrah.results: Twenty-one patients received trastuzumab deruxtecan. The 16-week progression-free survival rate was 87.5 percent (95% CI 47.3 to 99.7) in cohort 1. Intracranial objective response rate was 50.0 percent in cohort 2 and 44.4 percent in cohort 3, and 46.2 percent overall in patients with active brain metastases. Objective response among patients with measurable lesions was 66.7 percent, all partial. Two patients (9.5 percent) had grade 1 interstitial lung disease.

debbrah-cohort-5.methods: Single-arm, open-label, five-cohort phase 2 trial. Cohort 5 enrolled seven patients with HER2-positive or HER2-low advanced breast cancer and pathologically confirmed leptomeningeal disease. They received trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg intravenously every 21 days until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. The primary endpoint was overall survival, with progression-free survival and safety as key secondary endpoints.
debbrah-cohort-5.results: At a median follow-up of 12.0 months, median overall survival was 13.3 months (95% CI 5.7 to not available, p less than 0.001) and median progression-free survival was 8.9 months (95% CI 2.1 to not available). Two of seven patients remained on treatment at 18.6 and 11.9 months. None of the five patients who progressed and died had intracranial progression. Prolonged stabilisation for at least 24 weeks occurred in 71.4 percent.

decensi-low-dose-tamoxifen.methods: 120 women with oestrogen receptor-positive breast cancer were randomly assigned to tamoxifen 1, 5 or 20 mg daily for 4 weeks before surgery. Expression of the proliferation marker Ki-67 and blood biomarkers of breast cancer, cardiovascular and bone fracture risk were measured before and after treatment and compared with two nonrandomised control groups, 34 women with oestrogen receptor-negative and 29 women with oestrogen receptor-positive breast cancer.
decensi-low-dose-tamoxifen.results: Ki-67 expression decreased in all three tamoxifen groups with no difference in the size of the reduction between groups (P = .81). Relative to baseline, Ki-67 fell by a median of 15.0% (0.0% to 24.1%) in the tamoxifen groups and rose by 12.8% (0.0% to 19.6%) in the nonrandomised controls. Several blood biomarkers showed dose-response relationships with tamoxifen, including lower insulin-like growth factor-I, higher sex hormone-binding globulin, and lower LDL cholesterol, ultrasensitive C-reactive protein, fibrinogen and antithrombin-III.

demaria-paclitaxel-til.methods: Analysis of whether changes in local antitumour immunity take place after neoadjuvant paclitaxel and whether they correlate with response. Neoadjuvant paclitaxel 200 mg/m2 every 2 weeks for 4 treatments was followed by definitive surgery. Histological sections from the pre- and post-treatment specimens of 25 patients were analysed for the extent of lymphocytic infiltration and the presence of tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), and the cumulative apoptotic response after the first dose was studied in 10 of the 25.
demaria-paclitaxel-til.results: Pretreatment lymphocytic infiltrate was minimal in most patients and unrelated to clinical response. Among patients without TILs before treatment, TILs developed after treatment in 0 of 3 (0%) with stable disease, 3 of 12 (25%) with a clinical partial response and 4 of 6 (67%) with a clinical complete response and pathological residual disease. These changes correlated with the tumour cell apoptotic response to the first dose of paclitaxel.

denosumab-versus-zoledronic-acid-in-bm.methods: Randomised double-blind trial in patients with breast cancer and bone metastases. Patients received either subcutaneous denosumab 120 mg with intravenous placebo, or intravenous zoledronic acid 4 mg adjusted for creatinine clearance with subcutaneous placebo, every 4 weeks. Daily calcium and vitamin D were strongly recommended in both arms. The primary endpoint was time to first on-study skeletal-related event, defined as pathological fracture, radiation or surgery to bone, or spinal cord compression.
denosumab-versus-zoledronic-acid-in-bm.results: Denosumab was superior to zoledronic acid for time to first skeletal-related event, hazard ratio 0.82 (95% CI 0.71 to 0.95, P = .01), and for first and subsequent events, rate ratio 0.77 (95% CI 0.66 to 0.89, P = .001). Reduction in bone turnover markers was greater with denosumab. Overall survival, disease progression and rates of adverse events were similar. Renal adverse events and acute-phase reactions were more frequent with zoledronic acid, and hypocalcaemia with denosumab. Osteonecrosis of the jaw occurred in 2.0% on denosumab and 1.4% on zoledronic acid, P = .39.

deposein.methods: Randomised open-label phase 3 study. Patients with newly diagnosed leptomeningeal metastasis from breast cancer, defined by tumour cells in the cerebrospinal fluid or by combined clinical and neuroimaging signs, were randomised to systemic therapy alone or systemic therapy plus intrathecal liposomal cytarabine. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival related to leptomeningeal metastasis.
deposein.results: Thirty-seven patients were assigned to control and 36 to the experimental group. The median number of liposomal cytarabine injections was 5. Median leptomeningeal progression-free survival was 2.2 months (95% CI 1.3 to 3.1) versus 3.8 months (95% CI 2.3 to 6.8), hazard ratio 0.61 (95% CI 0.38 to 0.98), p equal to 0.04. Median overall survival was 4.0 versus 7.3 months, hazard ratio 0.85, p equal to 0.51. Serious adverse events occurred in 22 and 30 patients.

destiny-b03.methods: A phase 3, multicenter, open-label, randomized trial compared trastuzumab deruxtecan, a HER2 antibody-drug conjugate, with trastuzumab emtansine. Patients had HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer previously treated with trastuzumab and a taxane. The primary end point was progression-free survival as determined by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included overall survival, objective response, and safety.
destiny-b03.results: Among 524 randomly assigned patients, 75.8% were alive without disease progression at 12 months with trastuzumab deruxtecan versus 34.1% with trastuzumab emtansine, hazard ratio 0.28. Alive at 12 months were 94.1% versus 85.9%, hazard ratio 0.55. Overall response occurred in 79.7% versus 34.2%. Adjudicated drug-related interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis occurred in 10.5% versus 1.9%. The long-term survival analysis reported median overall survival of 52.6 versus 42.7 months, hazard ratio 0.73.

destiny-b04.methods: A phase 3 trial enrolled patients with HER2-low metastatic breast cancer who had received one or two previous lines of chemotherapy. HER2-low was defined as immunohistochemistry 1+, or 2+ with negative in situ hybridization. Patients were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to trastuzumab deruxtecan or the physician's choice of chemotherapy. The primary end point was progression-free survival in the hormone receptor-positive cohort. Key secondary end points were progression-free survival in all patients and overall survival.
destiny-b04.results: Of 557 patients randomized, 494 (88.7%) had hormone receptor-positive disease. In that cohort median progression-free survival was 10.1 months with trastuzumab deruxtecan and 5.4 months with physician's choice, hazard ratio 0.51. Median overall survival in that cohort was 23.9 versus 17.5 months, hazard ratio 0.64. Among all patients progression-free survival was 9.9 versus 5.1 months, hazard ratio 0.50. Overall survival was 23.4 versus 16.8 months, hazard ratio 0.64.

destiny-b05.methods: A phase 3, open-label, international, randomized trial compared postneoadjuvant trastuzumab deruxtecan at 5.4 mg per kilogram with trastuzumab emtansine at 3.6 mg per kilogram. Patients had HER2-positive breast cancer with residual invasive disease and node-positive disease at surgery, or inoperable disease at diagnosis. The primary end point was invasive disease-free survival. The key secondary end point was disease-free survival. Other end points included overall survival, distant recurrence-free interval, brain metastasis-free interval, and safety.
destiny-b05.results: A total of 1635 patients were randomly assigned, 818 to trastuzumab deruxtecan and 817 to trastuzumab emtansine. Median follow-up was about 30 months. Invasive-disease events or deaths occurred in 51 patients (6.2%) versus 102 patients (12.5%), hazard ratio 0.47. Three-year invasive disease-free survival was 92.4% versus 83.7%. Three-year disease-free survival was 92.3% versus 83.5%. Adjudicated drug-related interstitial lung disease occurred in 9.6% versus 1.6%. Two patients with interstitial lung disease in the trastuzumab deruxtecan group died.

destiny-b06.methods: A phase 3, multicenter, open-label trial enrolled patients with hormone receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer with HER2-low expression (immunohistochemistry 1+ or 2+ with negative in situ hybridization) or HER2-ultralow expression (immunohistochemistry 0 with membrane staining). All had received one or more lines of endocrine-based therapy and no chemotherapy for metastatic disease. Patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to trastuzumab deruxtecan or physician's choice of chemotherapy. The primary end point was progression-free survival in HER2-low disease.
destiny-b06.results: Of 866 patients randomized, 713 had HER2-low disease and 153 had HER2-ultralow disease. Among those with HER2-low disease, median progression-free survival was 13.2 months with trastuzumab deruxtecan and 8.1 months with chemotherapy, hazard ratio 0.62. Results were consistent in the exploratory HER2-ultralow population. Overall survival data were immature. Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 52.8% versus 44.4%. Adjudicated interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis occurred in 49 patients (11.3%) versus 1 patient (0.2%).

destiny-b09.methods: A phase 3 trial enrolled patients with HER2-positive advanced or metastatic breast cancer and no previous chemotherapy or HER2-directed therapy for metastatic disease. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to trastuzumab deruxtecan plus pertuzumab, trastuzumab deruxtecan plus placebo, or a taxane with trastuzumab and pertuzumab. The primary end point was progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included objective response, duration of response, and safety.
destiny-b09.results: At the February 26, 2025 data cutoff, median progression-free survival was 40.7 months with trastuzumab deruxtecan plus pertuzumab (383 patients) and 26.9 months with taxane, trastuzumab, and pertuzumab (387 patients), hazard ratio 0.56. Confirmed response occurred in 85.1% versus 78.6%, with complete responses in 15.1% and 8.5%. Median duration of response was 39.2 versus 26.4 months. Adjudicated drug-related interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis occurred in 12.1% versus 1.0%.

destiny-b11.methods: This open-label phase III trial ran at 147 sites in 18 countries. Adults with high-risk (at least cT3cN0 or cT0-4cN1-3) HER2-positive early breast cancer were randomised 1:1:1 to trastuzumab deruxtecan for eight cycles, trastuzumab deruxtecan for four cycles followed by paclitaxel, trastuzumab, and pertuzumab for four, or dose-dense doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide followed by the same four cycles. Enrolment in the trastuzumab deruxtecan alone arm closed early. The primary endpoint was pathological complete response.
destiny-b11.results: 286 patients were randomised to trastuzumab deruxtecan, 321 to trastuzumab deruxtecan followed by paclitaxel, trastuzumab, and pertuzumab, and 320 to dose-dense doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide followed by the same. Pathological complete response rates were 43.0%, 67.3%, and 56.3%. The difference between the two combination sequences was 11.2 percentage points (95% CI 4.0 to 18.3, P = 0.003). The event-free survival hazard ratio was 0.56 (95% CI 0.26 to 1.17) at 4.5% maturity.

destiny-b12.methods: The phase 3b/4 study was single-arm and open-label in patients with HER2-positive advanced or metastatic breast cancer, 263 with stable or active brain metastases and 241 without. All had received one or more prior anti-HER2-based regimens and received trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg per kg. Primary endpoints were progression-free survival in the brain metastases cohort and objective response rate by RECIST version 1.1 in the cohort without. No formal hypothesis testing was conducted.
destiny-b12.results: In the brain metastases cohort, 12-month progression-free survival was 61.6% and 12-month central nervous system progression-free survival was 58.9%. In the cohort without brain metastases, objective response rate was 62.7%. Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 51% of the brain metastases cohort and 49% of the cohort without. Investigator-reported interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis occurred in 16% of patients with brain metastases and 13% of those without.

destiny-breast01.methods: Two-part, open-label, single-group, multicentre phase 2 study in adults with pathologically documented HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer previously treated with trastuzumab emtansine. Part one evaluated three doses to establish a recommended dose, and part two evaluated efficacy and safety at that dose. The primary endpoint was objective response by independent central review.
destiny-breast01.results: 184 patients with a median of six previous treatments received trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg. Response occurred in 112 patients, 60.9 percent (95% CI 53.4 to 68.0). Median response duration was 14.8 months and median progression-free survival was 16.4 months at 11.1 months of follow-up. Grade 3 or higher events included decreased neutrophil count in 20.7 percent. Adjudicated interstitial lung disease occurred in 13.6 percent, including grade 5 in 2.2 percent.

destiny-breast02.methods: Randomised, open-label, multicentre phase 3 trial at 227 sites. Eligible patients had unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer that had progressed after trastuzumab emtansine, with ECOG performance status 0 or 1. Patients were randomly assigned 2 to 1 to trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg every 3 weeks or treatment of physician's choice, either capecitabine plus trastuzumab or capecitabine plus lapatinib. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival by blinded independent central review.
destiny-breast02.results: 608 patients were randomised, 406 to trastuzumab deruxtecan and 202 to physician's choice. Median progression-free survival was 17.8 months (95% CI 14.3 to 20.8) versus 6.9 months (95% CI 5.5 to 8.4), hazard ratio 0.36 (95% CI 0.28 to 0.45), p less than 0.0001. Grade 3 or higher treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 53 percent versus 44 percent. Drug-related interstitial lung disease occurred in 10 percent versus less than 1 percent.

dher2-lapatinib.methods: Phase 1 study in which women (n = 12) with metastatic, trastuzumab-refractory, HER2-overexpressing breast cancer were immunised with dHER2, a recombinant protein of the HER2 extracellular domain and part of the intracellular domain, with the adjuvant AS15, while receiving lapatinib 1250 mg daily. Peripheral blood antibody and T-cell responses were measured.
dher2-lapatinib.results: The regimen was well tolerated, with no cardiotoxicity. Anti-HER2 antibody was induced in all patients, whereas HER2-specific T cells were detected in one. Patient serum inhibited downstream signalling in HER2-expressing tumour cells in preliminary analyses. Median time to progression was 55 days, most patients progressing before peak immune responses, and 300-day overall survival was 92% (95% CI 77% to 100%).

disis-her2-icd-protein-vaccine.methods: Evaluation of the safety of a HER-2/neu intracellular domain (ICD) protein vaccine and of whether vaccine dose affects immunogenicity. Twenty-nine patients with HER-2/neu-overexpressing breast or ovarian cancer and no evidence of disease after standard therapy received a low (25 μg), intermediate (150 μg) or high (900 μg) dose, intradermally, monthly for 6 months, with granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor as adjuvant. Toxicity and cellular and humoral HER-2/neu-specific immunity were evaluated.
disis-her2-icd-protein-vaccine.results: The vaccine was well tolerated. Most patients (89%) developed HER-2/neu ICD-specific T-cell immunity and 82% developed HER-2/neu-specific IgG antibody immunity; vaccine dose predicted neither the magnitude of the T-cell response nor the magnitude or avidity of the antibody response. Detectable immunity developed significantly earlier with the high than the low dose (P = .003). Over half the patients retained HER-2/neu-specific T-cell immunity 9 to 12 months after immunizations ended.

dora.methods: Phase 2 non-comparative randomized trial. Patients with advanced triple-negative breast cancer, taken as estrogen or progesterone receptor expression of 10% or less, who had ongoing stable disease or a complete or partial response to first- or second-line platinum-based chemotherapy were randomized 1:1 to olaparib 300 mg twice daily with or without durvalumab 1,500 mg on day 1 every 4 weeks. The primary objective was to compare progression-free survival in each arm with a historical control of continued platinum-based therapy. Clinical benefit rate, defined as stable disease for at least 24 weeks or a complete or partial response, was also assessed. Germline BRCA mutation status and PD-L1 status were examined.
dora.results: 45 patients were randomized, 23 to olaparib alone and 22 to the combination, 3 of them with estrogen or progesterone receptor expression of 1% to 10%. At 9.8 months median follow-up, median progression-free survival from randomization was 4.0 months (95% CI 2.6 to 6.1) with olaparib and 6.1 months (95% CI 3.7 to 10.1) with the combination, both significantly longer than the historical control (P = 0.0023 and P < 0.0001 respectively). Clinical benefit rates, stable disease for at least 24 weeks or a complete or partial response, were 44% (95% CI 23% to 66%) with olaparib alone and 36% (95% CI 17% to 59%) with the combination. Sustained clinical benefit was seen irrespective of germline BRCA mutation or PD-L1 status but tended to be associated with a complete or partial response to prior platinum, particularly in the olaparib-alone arm. No new safety signals were reported.

ds8201-a-j101.methods: First-in-human, two-part phase 1 dose-escalation and dose-expansion study of trastuzumab deruxtecan, a HER2-directed antibody-drug conjugate with a topoisomerase I inhibitor payload, in advanced HER2-expressing or HER2-mutated solid tumours. This report covers patients with advanced or metastatic HER2-low breast cancer, defined as IHC 1+ or IHC 2+ with negative in situ hybridisation, refractory to standard therapies, who received the recommended doses for expansion of 5.4 or 6.4 mg/kg intravenously every 3 weeks until withdrawal of consent, unacceptable toxicity or progression. Antitumour activity and safety were assessed.
ds8201-a-j101.results: Between August 2016 and August 2018, 54 patients were enrolled and received at least one dose at the recommended doses, after a median of 7.5 prior therapies. The confirmed objective response rate by independent central review was 20 of 54 (37.0%, 95% CI 24.3% to 51.3%), with a median duration of response of 10.4 months (95% CI 8.8 months to not evaluable). 53 of 54 patients (98.1%) had at least one treatment-emergent adverse event, grade 3 or higher in 34 (63.0%), most often decreased neutrophil, platelet and white cell counts, anaemia, hypokalaemia, raised AST, decreased appetite and diarrhoea. Three patients treated at 6.4 mg/kg had fatal interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis that an independent committee attributed to the drug.

e2112.methods: E2112 was a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase III study. It enrolled men and women with advanced hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer whose disease progressed after a nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor. Participants were randomly assigned to exemestane 25 mg daily with either entinostat 5 mg weekly or placebo. Primary end points were progression-free survival by central review and overall survival. Secondary end points included safety, objective response rate, and lysine acetylation change in peripheral blood mononuclear cells.
e2112.results: 608 patients were randomly assigned between March 2014 and October 2018. Median progression-free survival was 3.3 months with entinostat versus 3.1 months with placebo, hazard ratio 0.87, P = .30. Median overall survival was 23.4 versus 21.7 months, hazard ratio 0.99, P = .94. Objective response rate was 5.8% versus 5.6%. The most common grade 3 or 4 event with entinostat was neutropenia at 20%.

e3194.methods: Phase 1B/2 trial (E3194) conducted by the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group of 2B1, a bispecific murine monoclonal antibody that binds the extracellular domains of HER2/neu and FcgammaRIII and promotes lysis of HER2/neu-overexpressing tumour cells by natural killer cells and mononuclear phagocytes, in 20 women with metastatic breast cancer.
e3194.results: The median age was 51 years, and all but one patient had received prior chemotherapy. After the first dose, three of the first eight patients had dose-limiting toxicities requiring dose reduction, so the remaining 12 received 1 mg/m2/day instead of 2.5 mg/m2/day. No objective antitumour responses were seen. 2B1 induced adaptive immune responses to both intracellular and extracellular domains of HER2/neu.

e5194.methods: The Oncotype DX DCIS Score was measured in patients with ductal carcinoma in situ treated with surgical excision without radiation in the ECOG E5194 study. The score was calculated from seven cancer-related genes and five reference genes. Its association with the risk of an ipsilateral breast event, defined as local recurrence of ductal carcinoma in situ or invasive carcinoma, was analyzed by Cox regression. The prespecified primary analysis adjusted for tamoxifen use.
e5194.results: 327 patients had adequate tissue for analysis. The continuous DCIS Score was significantly associated with the risk of an ipsilateral breast event, hazard ratio 2.31 (95% CI 1.15 to 4.49, P=.02), and with invasive ipsilateral breast event, unadjusted hazard ratio 3.68 (95% CI 1.34 to 9.62, P=.01). For the low, intermediate, and high risk groups, 10-year risks of an ipsilateral breast event were 10.6%, 26.7%, and 25.9%, and of an invasive event 3.7%, 12.3%, and 19.2%.

ea1131.methods: Patients with clinical stage II or III triple-negative breast cancer and at least 1 cm of residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy were randomly assigned to platinum, carboplatin or cisplatin, once every 3 weeks for four cycles, or capecitabine on 14 of every 21 days for six cycles. Triple-negative subtype, basal or nonbasal, was assigned by PAM50 on the residual disease. The design tested noninferiority with a superiority alternative, assuming 4-year invasive disease-free survival of 67% with capecitabine.
ea1131.results: 410 of a planned 775 participants were randomly assigned between 2015 and 2021. After median follow-up of 20 months and 120 invasive disease-free survival events, representing 61% of full information, in the 308 patients (78%) with basal subtype disease, 3-year invasive disease-free survival was 42% (95% CI 30 to 53) with platinum and 49% (95% CI 39 to 59) with capecitabine. Grade 3 and 4 toxicities were more common with platinum.

ea2108.methods: Randomised trial in women presenting with metastatic breast cancer and an intact primary tumour. All received systemic therapy for 4 to 8 months, and those without progression were randomly assigned to locoregional therapy of the primary site, surgery and radiotherapy to the standards used in non-metastatic disease, or to continuing systemic therapy. The primary endpoint was overall survival, with locoregional control and quality of life secondary.
ea2108.results: Of 390 enrolled, 256 were randomised, 125 to early locoregional therapy and 131 to continued systemic therapy. 3-year overall survival was 68.4% and 67.9%, hazard ratio 1.11 (90% CI 0.82-1.52), p=0.57, with median survival 54.9 and 53.1 months. Locoregional progression at 3 years was 16.3% against 39.8%, p<0.001. Quality of life was largely similar.

ecog-e1199.methods: 4,950 women with axillary lymph node-positive or high-risk lymph node-negative breast cancer were enrolled. All first received four cycles of intravenous doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide at 3-week intervals. They were then assigned to intravenous paclitaxel or docetaxel, given at 3-week intervals for four cycles or at 1-week intervals for 12 cycles. The primary end point was disease-free survival.
ecog-e1199.results: Against standard paclitaxel every 3 weeks, the odds ratio for disease-free survival was 1.27 with weekly paclitaxel (P=0.006), 1.23 with docetaxel every 3 weeks (P=0.02) and 1.09 with weekly docetaxel (P=0.29). Weekly paclitaxel also improved survival, odds ratio 1.32, P=0.01. An exploratory subgroup whose tumours expressed no HER2 protein showed similar gains regardless of hormone receptor expression. Grade 2 to 4 neuropathy was more frequent with weekly paclitaxel, 27% versus 20%.

efect.methods: This was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter phase III trial in postmenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive advanced breast cancer progressing or recurring after a nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor. Fulvestrant used a loading-dose regimen of 500 mg intramuscularly on day 0, 250 mg on days 14 and 28, then 250 mg every 28 days. Exemestane was 25 mg orally once daily. The primary end point was time to progression.
efect.results: 693 women were randomly assigned, 351 to fulvestrant and 342 to exemestane. About 60% had received at least two prior endocrine therapies. Median time to progression was 3.7 months in both groups, hazard ratio 0.963 (95% CI 0.819 to 1.133, P=.6531). Overall response rate was 7.4% versus 6.7% (P=.736) and clinical benefit rate 32.2% versus 31.5% (P=.853). Median duration of clinical benefit was 9.3 and 8.3 months.

egf100151.methods: Women with HER2-positive locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer that had progressed after regimens including an anthracycline, a taxane and trastuzumab were randomly assigned to lapatinib 1,250 mg per day continuously plus capecitabine 2,000 mg per square metre on days 1 through 14 of a 21-day cycle, or to capecitabine alone 2,500 mg per square metre on days 1 through 14 of a 21-day cycle. The primary end point was time to progression by blinded independent review.
egf100151.results: The interim analysis of time to progression met the criteria for early reporting on grounds of superiority in the combination arm. The hazard ratio for independently assessed time to progression was 0.49 (95% CI 0.34 to 0.71, P<0.001), with 49 events in the combination arm and 72 in the monotherapy arm. Median time to progression was 8.4 months with the combination and 4.4 months with monotherapy, without more serious toxic effects or symptomatic cardiac events.

egf104900.methods: Patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer whose disease progressed during prior trastuzumab-based therapies were randomly assigned to lapatinib monotherapy or lapatinib in combination with trastuzumab. Overall survival and updated progression-free survival were presented with Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank tests stratified for hormone receptor status and visceral disease status. Subgroup analyses sought characteristics of patients deriving the greatest clinical benefit.
egf104900.results: Among the 291 patients randomly assigned with strata, lapatinib plus trastuzumab remained superior to lapatinib alone for progression-free survival, hazard ratio 0.74 (95% CI 0.58 to 0.94, P=.011), and gave an overall survival benefit, hazard ratio 0.74 (95% CI 0.57 to 0.97, P=.026). Absolute overall survival rates were 10% higher at 6 months and 15% higher at 12 months with the combination. Performance status 0, nonvisceral disease and fewer than three metastatic sites were associated with better survival.

egf30008.methods: Postmenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer were randomly assigned to daily letrozole 2.5 mg orally plus lapatinib 1,500 mg orally, or letrozole plus placebo, as first-line treatment. The primary end point was progression-free survival in the HER2-positive population. A preplanned Cox regression analysis examined factors in the HER2-negative population.
egf30008.results: In 219 hormone receptor-positive, HER2-positive patients, adding lapatinib reduced the risk of progression, hazard ratio 0.71 (95% CI 0.53 to 0.96, P=.019), with median progression-free survival of 8.2 versus 3.0 months. Clinical benefit was 48% versus 29% (P=.003). The 952 centrally confirmed HER2-negative patients had no progression-free survival improvement. Grade 3 or 4 diarrhea occurred in 10% versus 1% and rash in 1% versus 0%.

electroacupuncture-gabapentin.methods: Randomised controlled trial in 120 breast cancer survivors with bothersome hot flashes twice a day or more, assigned to 8 weeks of electroacupuncture or gabapentin once a day with validated placebo controls, sham acupuncture or placebo pills. The primary end point was change in the hot flash composite score between sham acupuncture and placebo pills at week 8; secondary end points were group comparisons and durability at week 24.
electroacupuncture-gabapentin.results: By week 8, sham acupuncture reduced the composite score more than placebo pills (-2.39, 95% CI -4.60 to -0.17). Mean reduction was greatest with electroacupuncture, then sham acupuncture, gabapentin and placebo pills (-7.4 vs -5.9 vs -5.2 vs -3.4, P < .001). Treatment-related adverse events were more frequent with pills: gabapentin 39.3%, placebo pills 20.0%, electroacupuncture 16.7% and sham acupuncture 3.1% (P = .005). At week 24 the reduction was greatest with electroacupuncture, then sham acupuncture, placebo pills and gabapentin (-8.5 vs -6.1 vs -4.6 vs -2.8, P = .002).

eliot.methods: Single-centre, randomised, phase 3 equivalence trial at the European Institute of Oncology, Milan. Women aged 48 to 75 with a unicentric carcinoma no larger than 25 mm on ultrasound, clinically negative axillary nodes and suitability for breast-conserving surgery were randomly assigned 1:1, stratified by clinical tumour size, to postoperative whole-breast irradiation (50 Gy in 25 fractions plus a 10 Gy boost) or to 21 Gy of intraoperative electron radiotherapy in a single dose to the tumour bed. The trial was open label. The primary endpoint was ipsilateral breast tumour recurrence; equivalence was defined as a 5-year rate in the intraoperative group not exceeding 7.5%. Overall survival was the secondary endpoint.
eliot.results: Between November 2000 and December 2007, 1305 women were randomly assigned, 654 to whole-breast irradiation and 651 to intraoperative radiotherapy. After a median follow-up of 12.4 years, 86 (7%) had ipsilateral breast tumour recurrence, 70 (11%) in the intraoperative group and 16 (2%) in the whole-breast group (HR 4.62, 2.68 to 7.95, p<0.0001). Recurrence rates at 5, 10 and 15 years were 4.2%, 8.1% and 12.6% with intraoperative radiotherapy and 0.5%, 1.1% and 2.4% with whole-breast irradiation. Deaths did not differ (98 vs 95; HR 1.03, 0.77 to 1.36, p = 0.85), and 15-year overall survival was 83.4% and 82.4%.

elipse.methods: Multicentre window-of-opportunity trial of preoperative elacestrant in postmenopausal women with early breast cancer, run to investigate the biological changes induced by a short preoperative course. Eligible patients had untreated T1c (at least 1.5 cm) to T3, N0, ER-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer with locally assessed Ki67 of 10% or more. They received elacestrant at a daily dose of 345 mg for 4 weeks. The primary efficacy endpoint was complete cell cycle arrest, defined as Ki67 of 2.7% or less, on day 28. Molecular change was assessed with PAM50-based gene signatures and gene expression.
elipse.results: 22 patients were evaluable for the primary endpoint. Elacestrant was associated with a complete cell cycle arrest rate of 27.3% and a statistically significant Ki67 geometric mean change of -52.9% (P = 0.007; 95% CI -67.4 to -32.1). Treatment shifted tumours towards a more endocrine-sensitive and less proliferative phenotype on PAM50-based gene signatures, increased expression of the immune-response genes GZMB, CD4 and CD8A, and suppressed the proliferation and estrogen-signalling genes MKI67, ESR1 and AR. These biological changes were independent of the level of Ki67 suppression on day 28. The most common adverse events were grade 1 anemia (21.7%), hot flushes (8.7%), constipation (8.7%) and abdominal pain (8.7%), and one patient had a grade 3 cutaneous rash leading to treatment discontinuation.

ellner-mannosyl-dextran-dose.methods: Study of the biodistribution and safety at different molar doses of [99mTc]DTPA-mannosyl-dextran, a receptor-binding radiopharmaceutical designed for sentinel lymph node mapping. Twenty-four women with breast cancer were studied in four groups of six, given 0.2, 1.0 or 5.0 nmol of [99mTc]DTPA-mannosyl-dextran or filtered [99mTc]sulfur colloid. Injection site clearance was monitored by dynamic imaging for three hours, whole body scans were acquired, and lymph nodes were assayed for radioactivity after gamma-guided sentinel lymph node biopsy.
ellner-mannosyl-dextran-dose.results: Injection site clearance of [99mTc]DTPA-mannosyl-dextran did not differ significantly by dose, while sentinel node uptake was dose dependent (p = 0.03). There were no clinically significant changes in laboratory parameters at any dose level 4 or 24 hours after injection compared with preoperative levels. Radiation absorbed doses did not differ among the three dose levels and were lower than with filtered [99mTc]sulfur colloid.

ember3.methods: In a phase 3, open-label trial, patients with ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer that recurred or progressed during or after aromatase inhibitor therapy, given alone or with a CDK4/6 inhibitor, were assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to imlunestrant, standard endocrine monotherapy, or imlunestrant with abemaciclib. Primary end points were investigator-assessed progression-free survival for imlunestrant versus standard therapy in patients with ESR1 mutations and in all patients, and for imlunestrant-abemaciclib versus imlunestrant among concurrently randomized patients.
ember3.results: 874 patients underwent randomization, with 331 assigned to imlunestrant, 330 to standard therapy, and 213 to imlunestrant-abemaciclib. Among 256 patients with ESR1 mutations, median progression-free survival was 5.5 months with imlunestrant and 3.8 months with standard therapy, P<0.001. In the overall population median progression-free survival was 5.6 versus 5.5 months, hazard ratio 0.87. Among 426 patients compared concurrently, it was 9.4 months with imlunestrant-abemaciclib versus 5.5 months with imlunestrant, hazard ratio 0.57.

embraca.methods: A randomized, open-label, phase 3 trial assigned patients with advanced breast cancer and a germline BRCA1/2 mutation in a 2:1 ratio to talazoparib 1 mg once daily or standard single-agent therapy of the physician's choice, which was capecitabine, eribulin, gemcitabine, or vinorelbine in continuous 21-day cycles. The primary end point was progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review.
embraca.results: Of 431 patients randomized, 287 received talazoparib and 144 standard therapy. Median progression-free survival was 8.6 months with talazoparib versus 5.6 months with standard therapy, hazard ratio 0.54, P<0.001. The interim median hazard ratio for death was 0.76. Objective response rate was 62.6% versus 27.2%. Grade 3-4 hematologic adverse events occurred in 55% versus 38%. The final overall survival analysis reported median overall survival of 19.3 versus 19.5 months, hazard ratio 0.848.

embrace.methods: In this phase 3 open-label study, women with locally recurrent or metastatic breast cancer were randomly allocated 2:1 to eribulin mesilate 1.4 mg/m2 given intravenously on days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle or to treatment of physician's choice. Patients had received two to five previous chemotherapy regimens, including an anthracycline and a taxane. Randomisation was stratified by geographical region, previous capecitabine treatment, and HER2 status. The primary endpoint was overall survival in the intention-to-treat population.
embrace.results: 762 women were allocated to treatment, 508 to eribulin and 254 to treatment of physician's choice. Median overall survival was 13.1 months with eribulin versus 10.6 months with physician's choice, hazard ratio 0.81, p=0.041. The most common adverse events in both groups were asthenia or fatigue, in 54% on eribulin and 40% on physician's choice, and neutropenia, in 52% and 30%. Peripheral neuropathy led to discontinuation of eribulin in 24 patients (5%).

emerald.methods: Randomised open-label phase 3 trial. Eligible patients had ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer with one or two prior lines of endocrine therapy. Prior treatment with a CDK4/6 inhibitor was required. No more than one line of chemotherapy was allowed. Patients were assigned to elacestrant 400 mg orally once daily or to standard-of-care endocrine monotherapy. Primary endpoints were progression-free survival by blinded independent central review in all patients and in patients with a detectable ESR1 mutation.
emerald.results: 239 patients were assigned to elacestrant and 238 to standard of care. A mutation was detected in 47.8% of patients. 43.4% had received two prior endocrine therapies. The progression-free survival hazard ratio was 0.70 (95% CI 0.55 to 0.88) in all patients and 0.55 (0.39 to 0.77) in mutation-positive patients. Treatment-related grade 3 or 4 adverse events occurred in 7.2% on elacestrant and 3.1% on standard of care. Any-grade nausea occurred in 35.0% versus 18.8%.

emilia.methods: Patients with HER2-positive advanced breast cancer previously treated with trastuzumab and a taxane were randomly assigned to trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1) or to lapatinib plus capecitabine. Primary endpoints were progression-free survival by independent review, overall survival and safety. Secondary endpoints included investigator-assessed progression-free survival, objective response rate and time to symptom progression. Two interim analyses of overall survival were conducted.
emilia.results: Among 991 randomly assigned patients, median progression-free survival by independent review was 9.6 months with T-DM1 versus 6.4 months with control (hazard ratio 0.65, 95% CI 0.55 to 0.77). Median overall survival at the second interim analysis was 30.9 versus 25.1 months (hazard ratio 0.68, 0.55 to 0.85). The objective response rate was 43.6% versus 30.8%. The 2017 final overall survival analysis reported medians of 29.9 versus 25.9 months (hazard ratio 0.75, 0.64 to 0.88).

enmd-2076.methods: Dual-institution, single-arm, two-stage phase 2 trial in patients with locally advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer treated with one to three prior lines of chemotherapy in the advanced setting. Patients received ENMD-2076 250 mg orally once daily continuously in 4-week cycles until progression or unacceptable toxicity. The primary endpoint was the 6-month clinical benefit rate; secondary endpoints included progression-free survival, pharmacokinetics, safety and biological correlates in archival and serial tumour biopsies.
enmd-2076.results: Forty-one patients were enrolled. The 6-month clinical benefit rate was 16.7% (95% CI 6% to 32.8%), including two partial responses, and the 4-month clinical benefit rate 27.8% (14% to 45.2%), with an average duration of benefit of 6.5 cycles. Common adverse events were hypertension, fatigue, diarrhoea and nausea. Treatment decreased cellular proliferation and microvessel density and increased p53 and p73 expression.

enobosarm.methods: Randomised, open-label, multicentre, multinational, parallel design phase 2 trial at 35 cancer treatment centres in nine countries. Postmenopausal women aged 18 years or older with previously treated oestrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative, locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 to 2 were enrolled. Participants were stratified on the setting of the immediately preceding endocrine therapy and the presence of bone-only metastasis, and randomly assigned 1:1 to 9 mg or 18 mg oral enobosarm daily using an interactive web response system. The primary endpoint was clinical benefit rate at 24 weeks in those with centrally confirmed androgen receptor-positive disease, the evaluable population. The premise of the trial is that the androgen receptor is a tumour suppressor in oestrogen receptor-positive breast cancer.
enobosarm.results: Between Sept 10, 2015 and Nov 28, 2017, 136 of 172 patients deemed eligible (79%) were randomly assigned to 9 mg (n=72) or 18 mg (n=64) oral enobosarm daily, and 102 of those 136 (75%) formed the evaluable population, 50 in the 9 mg group and 52 in the 18 mg group. Median age was 60.5 years in the 9 mg group and 62.5 years in the 18 mg group, and median follow-up was 7.5 months. At 24 weeks, 16 of 50 (32%, 95% CI 20 to 47) in the 9 mg group and 15 of 52 (29%, 17 to 43) in the 18 mg group had clinical benefit. Grade 3 or grade 4 drug-related adverse events occurred in 6 of 75 patients who received 9 mg (8%) and 10 of 61 who received 18 mg (16%), most often raised hepatic transaminases, hypercalcaemia and fatigue. Four deaths, one in the 9 mg group and three in the 18 mg group, were deemed unrelated to the study drug. The authors concluded that enobosarm has anti-tumour activity and that androgen receptor activation can produce clinical benefit.

eortc-10853.methods: Between 1986 and 1996, 1010 women with complete local excision of DCIS smaller than 5 cm were randomly assigned to no further treatment (n = 503) or radiotherapy (n = 507). The analysis covers the long-term risk of local recurrence and its effect on survival, at a median follow-up of 15.8 years.
eortc-10853.results: Radiotherapy reduced the risk of any local recurrence by 48% (HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.40 to 0.68, P < .001). The 15-year local recurrence-free rate was 69% after excision alone and 82% with radiotherapy, and the 15-year invasive local recurrence-free rate 84% and 90% (HR 0.61, 0.42 to 0.87). Breast cancer-specific survival (HR 1.07, 0.60 to 1.91) and overall survival (HR 1.02, 0.71 to 1.44) did not differ. Women with an invasive local recurrence had worse breast cancer-specific (HR 17.66) and overall survival (HR 5.17) than those without recurrence.
