The salvage mastectomy rate after recurrence was 13% with radiotherapy and 19% without.

eortc-10902.methods: Between 1991 and 1999, 698 patients with early breast cancer were randomised to four cycles of fluorouracil, epirubicin and cyclophosphamide before or after surgery. Endpoints were breast-conserving therapy, disease-free survival, overall survival and tumour response to preoperative chemotherapy. Tumour tissue was examined for ER, PgR, HER2, p21, p53 and bcl-2 expression.
eortc-10902.results: With a median follow-up of 10 years there was no significant difference between the arms in overall survival (HR 1.09, 0.83 to 1.42, P = 0.54), disease-free survival (HR 1.12, 0.90 to 1.39, P = 0.30) or locoregional recurrence (HR 1.16, 0.77 to 1.74). Preoperative chemotherapy increased breast-conserving therapy rates, and breast conservation made possible in part by downsizing was not associated with more locoregional recurrence or worse survival. Only tumour stage, nodal stage and grade were independent prognostic factors for overall survival.

eortc-10994.methods: Open-label phase 3 study at 42 European centres. Women under 71 with locally advanced, inflammatory or large operable breast cancer were randomly assigned 1:1, by minimisation stratified by institution and initial tumour stage, to a standard anthracycline regimen (six cycles of FEC100 or tailored FEC every 21 days) or a taxane-based regimen (three cycles of docetaxel 100 mg/m2 followed by three cycles of epirubicin 90 mg/m2 and docetaxel 75 mg/m2, T-ET). The primary endpoint was progression-free survival according to TP53 status, analysed by intention to treat; this is the trial's final analysis.
eortc-10994.results: 928 patients were enrolled in each group. TP53 status could not be assessed in 183 (20%) patients in the FEC group and 204 (22%) in the T-ET group, mainly because of low tumour-cell content. In TP53-mutated tumours, 5-year progression-free survival was 59.5% with T-ET (n = 326) and 55.3% with FEC (n = 318; HR 0.84, 98% CI 0.63 to 1.14; p = 0.17). In TP53 wild-type tumours it was 66.8% (n = 398) and 64.7% (n = 427; HR 0.89, 98% CI 0.68 to 1.18; p = 0.35). For all patients it was 65.1% with T-ET and 60.8% with FEC (HR 0.85, 98% CI 0.71 to 1.02; p = 0.035). Febrile neutropenia was more frequent with T-ET (21% vs 9% at FEC100 sites).

eortc-22952-26001.methods: Phase 3 randomised trial. Patients with one to three brain metastases of solid tumours, excluding small-cell lung cancer, with stable systemic disease or asymptomatic primary tumours and WHO performance status 0 to 2 were treated with complete surgery or radiosurgery. They were then randomly assigned to adjuvant whole-brain radiotherapy of 30 Gy in 10 fractions or to observation. The primary endpoint was time to WHO performance status deterioration beyond 2.
eortc-22952-26001.results: Of 359 patients, 199 had radiosurgery and 160 had surgery. Median time to performance status worse than 2 was 10.0 months with observation and 9.5 months with radiotherapy (P = .71). Median overall survival was 10.7 versus 10.9 months (P = .89). Radiotherapy lowered 2-year relapse at initial sites (surgery 59% to 27%; radiosurgery 31% to 19%) and at new sites (42% to 23%; 48% to 33%). Intracranial progression caused death in 44% versus 28%.

eortc22922.methods: Women with a centrally or medially located primary tumour, irrespective of axillary involvement, or an externally located tumour with axillary involvement were randomly assigned to two groups. One group received whole-breast or thoracic-wall irradiation plus internal mammary and medial supraclavicular nodal irradiation. The control group received whole-breast or thoracic-wall irradiation alone. The primary endpoint was overall survival. Secondary endpoints were disease-free survival, survival free from distant disease, and death from breast cancer.
eortc22922.results: Between 1996 and 2004, 4004 patients underwent randomisation. 76.1% had breast-conserving surgery. At a median follow-up of 10.9 years, 811 patients had died. Ten-year overall survival was 82.3% with nodal irradiation versus 80.7% (hazard ratio 0.87, 95% CI 0.76 to 1.00). Disease-free survival was 72.1% versus 69.1% (hazard ratio 0.89). Distant disease-free survival was 78.0% versus 75.0% (hazard ratio 0.86). Breast-cancer mortality was 12.5% versus 14.4% (hazard ratio 0.82).

etna.methods: Multicentre open-label phase 3 trial. Patients with newly diagnosed, centrally confirmed HER2-negative breast cancer were randomly assigned to paclitaxel 90 mg/m2 (349 patients) or nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 (346 patients). Each drug was given on weeks 1, 2 and 3 followed by one week of rest for 4 cycles, before 4 cycles of an anthracycline regimen chosen by the investigator. The primary endpoint was pathological complete response, ypT0/is ypN0.
etna.results: 814 patients were registered and 695 were randomly assigned. Pathological complete response was 22.5% with nab-paclitaxel versus 18.6% with paclitaxel (odds ratio 0.77, 95% CI 0.52 to 1.13, P = .19). Serious adverse events occurred in 54 of 337 patients (16.0%) on nab-paclitaxel and 38 of 335 (11.3%) on paclitaxel. Grade 3 or higher peripheral neuropathy occurred in 4.5% versus 1.8%. Tumour subtype was the strongest factor influencing outcome (odds ratio 4.85).

evera.methods: Phase 3, open-label, randomised trial in patients with ER-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer whose disease had progressed or recurred after a CDK4/6 inhibitor plus endocrine therapy. Patients were assigned 1:1 to oral giredestrant plus everolimus or to standard endocrine therapy (exemestane, fulvestrant or tamoxifen) plus everolimus. The primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival, evaluated first in patients with ESR1-mutated tumours and then in the overall trial population.
evera.results: Of 373 patients randomised, 183 were assigned to giredestrant-everolimus and 190 to standard therapy-everolimus. Among 207 patients with ESR1-mutated tumours, median progression-free survival was 10.0 months with giredestrant-everolimus and 5.5 months with standard therapy-everolimus (hazard ratio for progression or death 0.38, 95% CI 0.27 to 0.54, P<0.001). In the overall population it was 8.8 and 5.5 months (hazard ratio 0.56, 95% CI 0.44 to 0.71, P<0.001). Adverse events occurred in 98.9% of patients given giredestrant-everolimus and 96.8% of those given standard therapy-everolimus. The commonest were stomatitis (47.3% and 48.9%), diarrhoea (26.9% and 22.6%) and anaemia (23.6% and 21.0%).

everolimus-trastuzumab-pooled.methods: Pooled analysis (n = 47) of two trials run concurrently at The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center, Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center and Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Patients with HER2-overexpressing metastatic breast cancer that had progressed on trastuzumab-based therapy received trastuzumab every 3 weeks with daily everolimus.
everolimus-trastuzumab-pooled.results: Among 47 patients, everolimus with trastuzumab gave partial responses in seven (15%) and stable disease lasting 6 months or longer in nine (19%), a clinical benefit rate of 34%. Median progression-free survival was 4.1 months. Fatigue, infection and mucositis were the main non-haematological toxicities. Trastuzumab did not significantly influence everolimus pharmacokinetics. PTEN loss was associated with decreased overall survival (P = .048) but not with progression-free survival.

extenet.methods: Multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial at 495 centres. Eligible women had stage 1-3 HER2-positive breast cancer and had completed neoadjuvant and adjuvant trastuzumab up to 2 years before randomisation. Criteria were later amended to stage 2-3 disease completed within 1 year. Patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to oral neratinib 240 mg per day or matching placebo, stratified by hormone receptor status, nodal status and trastuzumab regimen. The primary outcome was invasive disease-free survival at 2 years.
extenet.results: 2840 women were assigned to neratinib (n=1420) or placebo (n=1420). Median follow-up was 24 months. At 2 years there were 70 invasive disease-free survival events with neratinib versus 109 with placebo (stratified hazard ratio 0.67, 95% CI 0.50 to 0.91, p=0.0091). Two-year invasive disease-free survival was 93.9% versus 91.6%. Grade 3 diarrhoea occurred in 40% versus 2%. The 2023 final analysis reported 8-year overall survival of 90.1% versus 90.2% (stratified hazard ratio 0.95, 0.75 to 1.21).

fabian-duavee-pilot.methods: Pilot study of 6 months of the tissue selective estrogen complex bazedoxifene (20 mg) and conjugated estrogen (0.45 mg), Duavee, to assess feasibility and effects on risk biomarkers for postmenopausal breast cancer. Risk biomarkers were fully automated mammographic volumetric density (Volpara), benign breast tissue Ki-67 (MIB-1 immunochemistry), and serum levels of progesterone, IGF-1, IGFBP3, bioavailable estradiol and testosterone. Perimenopausal and postmenopausal women at increased risk were enrolled in two cohorts by baseline Ki-67, below 1% (cohort A) or 1% to 4% (cohort B).
fabian-duavee-pilot.results: Twenty-eight women were enrolled, 13 in cohort A and 15 in cohort B, and all completed the study with more than 85% drug adherence. Significant changes in biomarkers, uncorrected for multiple comparisons, were a decrease in mammographic fibroglandular volume (P = 0.043); decreases in serum progesterone, bioavailable testosterone and IGF-1 (P < 0.01); an increase in serum bioavailable estradiol (P < 0.001); and, in cohort B, a reduction in Ki-67 (P = 0.017). The median hot flash score improved from 15 at baseline to 0 at 6 months, and menopause-specific quality of life total, vasomotor and sexual domain scores improved (P < 0.001).

face.methods: Randomised phase 3 trial. Postmenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive, node-positive early breast cancer were assigned to adjuvant letrozole 2.5 mg or anastrozole 1 mg once daily for 5 years or until recurrence of disease. Patients were stratified by number of involved lymph nodes and by HER2 status. The primary endpoint was 5-year disease-free survival, with overall survival and safety as key secondary endpoints.
face.results: 4136 patients were assigned to letrozole (2061) or anastrozole (2075). The final analysis was done at 709 disease-free survival events, 341 (16.5%) with letrozole and 368 (17.7%) with anastrozole. 5-year disease-free survival was 84.9% versus 82.9% (hazard ratio 0.93, 95% CI 0.80 to 1.07, P = .3150), with similar results across subgroups. 5-year overall survival was 89.9% versus 89.2% (hazard ratio 0.98, P = .7916). Grade 3 to 4 arthralgia occurred in 3.9% versus 3.3%.

fact.methods: Open-label randomised phase 3 trial. Postmenopausal women, or premenopausal women receiving a gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist, with oestrogen receptor or progesterone receptor positive disease at first relapse after primary treatment of localised disease were randomly assigned to a fulvestrant loading dose regimen followed by monthly injection plus anastrozole 1 mg daily, or to anastrozole 1 mg daily alone. The primary endpoint was time to progression.
fact.results: 514 women were assigned to fulvestrant plus anastrozole (258) or anastrozole alone (256). About two thirds had received adjuvant antiestrogens and only eight had received an aromatase inhibitor. Median time to progression was 10.8 versus 10.2 months (hazard ratio 0.99, 95% CI 0.81 to 1.20, P = .91). Median overall survival was 37.8 versus 38.2 months (hazard ratio 1.0, P = 1.00). Hot flashes occurred in 24.6% versus 13.8% (P = .0023).

fairlane.methods: Hypothesis-generating, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomised phase II trial. Patients with early triple-negative breast cancer (T 1.5 cm or larger, N0 to N2) were randomised 1:1 to weekly paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 with ipatasertib 400 mg or placebo on days 1 to 21 every 28 days for 12 weeks before surgery. Co-primary end points were the pathological complete response rate (ypT0/TisN0) in the intention-to-treat and immunohistochemistry PTEN-low populations; secondary end points included the rate in PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered tumours and response by MRI.
fairlane.results: Pathological complete response rates with ipatasertib against placebo were 17% and 13% in the intention-to-treat population (N = 151), 16% and 13% in the PTEN-low population (N = 35), and 18% and 12% in the PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered subgroup (N = 62). Overall and complete response by MRI favoured ipatasertib in all three populations (complete response 39% vs 9% in the altered subgroup). Grade 3 or worse adverse events were more frequent with ipatasertib (32% vs 16%), especially diarrhoea (17% vs 1%).

faktion.methods: Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 trial at 19 UK hospitals. Postmenopausal women aged at least 18 years with ECOG performance status 0 to 2 and oestrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative metastatic or locally advanced inoperable breast cancer who had relapsed or progressed on an aromatase inhibitor were randomly assigned 1:1 to fulvestrant 500 mg every 28 days plus either capivasertib 400 mg or placebo twice daily on a 4 days on, 3 days off schedule.
faktion.results: 183 patients were screened and 140 were randomly assigned, 69 to capivasertib and 71 to placebo. At the primary analysis 112 progression-free survival events had occurred, 49 (71%) with capivasertib and 63 (89%) with placebo. Median progression-free survival was 10.3 months versus 4.8 months (hazard ratio 0.58, 95% CI 0.39 to 0.84, p = 0.0044). Common grade 3 to 4 events were hypertension (32% versus 24%), diarrhoea (14% versus 4%) and rash (20% versus 0).

falcon.methods: Phase 3 randomised double-blind trial at 113 hospitals and community centres in 20 countries. Eligible patients were postmenopausal, endocrine therapy-naive, with oestrogen receptor-positive or progesterone receptor-positive locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer, WHO performance status 0-2 and at least one measurable or non-measurable lesion. Patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to fulvestrant 500 mg intramuscularly on days 0, 14 and 28 then every 28 days, or anastrozole 1 mg orally daily. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival.
falcon.results: 524 patients were enrolled and 462 were randomised, 230 to fulvestrant and 232 to anastrozole. Progression-free survival favoured fulvestrant (hazard ratio 0.797, 95% CI 0.637 to 0.999, p=0.0486). Median progression-free survival was 16.6 versus 13.8 months. The most common adverse events were arthralgia (17% versus 10%) and hot flushes (11% versus 10%). The 2025 final overall survival analysis reported medians of 44.8 versus 42.7 months (hazard ratio 0.97, 0.77 to 1.21) after 314 deaths.

fast-forward.methods: Multicentre phase 3 randomised non-inferiority trial at 97 UK centres. Patients aged at least 18 years with invasive breast carcinoma (pT1-3, pN0-1, M0) after breast conservation surgery or mastectomy were eligible. Allocation was to 40 Gy in 15 fractions over 3 weeks, 27 Gy in five fractions over 1 week, or 26 Gy in five fractions over 1 week, to the whole breast or chest wall. The primary endpoint was ipsilateral breast tumour relapse.
fast-forward.results: 4096 patients were recruited, 1361 to 40 Gy, 1367 to 27 Gy and 1368 to 26 Gy. At a median follow-up of 71.5 months, 79 primary endpoint events occurred (31, 27 and 21). Hazard ratios versus 40 Gy were 0.86 (95% CI 0.51 to 1.44) for 27 Gy and 0.67 (0.38 to 1.16) for 26 Gy. Five-year relapse incidence after 40 Gy was 2.1%. Moderate or marked clinician-assessed normal tissue effects at 5 years were 9.9%, 15.4% and 11.9%.

fata-gim3.methods: Multicentre, open-label, randomised phase 3 trial of six treatments. Postmenopausal women with completely resected hormone receptor-positive invasive breast cancer, any tumour size and nodal status, and no previous tamoxifen, were assigned in equal ratio to oral anastrozole 1 mg, exemestane 25 mg or letrozole 2.5 mg daily upfront for 5 years, or to tamoxifen 20 mg daily for 2 years followed by one of those aromatase inhibitors for 3 years. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival.
fata-gim3.results: 3697 patients were enrolled. After a median follow-up of 60 months, 401 disease-free survival events occurred, 211 of 1850 on the switch strategy and 190 of 1847 on upfront treatment. 5-year disease-free survival was 88.5% versus 89.8% (hazard ratio 0.89, 95% CI 0.73 to 1.08, p = 0.23). By drug it was 90.0% with anastrozole, 88.0% with exemestane and 89.4% with letrozole (p = 0.24). Grade 3 to 4 musculoskeletal events occurred in 7% of each strategy.

femzone.methods: Prospectively randomised phase II trial comparing the clinical response to neoadjuvant letrozole alone or with zoledronic acid. Patients were randomly assigned to letrozole 2.5 mg daily (n = 79) or letrozole 2.5 mg daily with seven infusions of zoledronic acid 4 mg every 4 weeks (n = 89) for 6 months. The primary endpoint was clinical response rate by mammogram reading. The study was terminated prematurely for insufficient recruitment, and this is an exploratory analysis.
femzone.results: Central assessment of tumour size during treatment was available for 131 patients, 66 on letrozole and 65 on letrozole plus zoledronic acid. Complete or partial clinical responses were seen in 54.5% (41.8% to 66.9%) with letrozole and 69.2% (56.6% to 80.1%) with letrozole plus zoledronic acid (P = 0.106). A multivariate model gave an odds ratio of 1.72 (0.83 to 3.59) for the experimental arm.

fenretinide-second-breast.methods: 2972 women aged 30-70 years with surgically removed stage I breast cancer or ductal carcinoma in situ were randomly assigned to oral fenretinide 200 mg per day for 5 years or no treatment. The primary end point was the incidence of contralateral or ipsilateral breast cancer 7 years after randomisation. Outcomes stratified by menopausal status, distant metastases, overall mortality and tumours in other organs were considered post hoc. Hazards were estimated by Cox regression.
fenretinide-second-breast.results: At a median observation time of 97 months there were no statistically significant differences in contralateral (P = .642) or ipsilateral breast cancer (P = .177) between the arms. An interaction between fenretinide and menopausal status was found for both outcomes (P = .045), with a possible benefit in premenopausal women (contralateral adjusted HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.41 to 1.07; ipsilateral 0.65, 0.46 to 0.92) and an opposite effect in postmenopausal women (contralateral 1.32, 0.82 to 2.15; ipsilateral 1.19, 0.75 to 1.89). Tumours in other organs, distant metastasis and all-cause mortality did not differ.

finher.methods: Randomised trial. 1010 women with axillary node-positive or high-risk node-negative breast cancer were assigned to three cycles of docetaxel or vinorelbine, each followed by three cycles of fluorouracil, epirubicin and cyclophosphamide. The 232 women whose tumours had an amplified HER2/neu gene were further assigned to receive or not to receive nine weekly trastuzumab infusions. The primary endpoint was recurrence-free survival.
finher.results: 3-year recurrence-free survival was 91% with docetaxel and 86% with vinorelbine (hazard ratio 0.58, 95% CI 0.40 to 0.85, P = 0.005), with no difference in overall survival (P = 0.15). Among HER2-positive patients, 3-year recurrence-free survival was 89% with trastuzumab and 78% without (hazard ratio 0.42, 95% CI 0.21 to 0.83, P = 0.01). Docetaxel caused more adverse effects. Trastuzumab was not associated with decreased left ventricular ejection fraction or cardiac failure.

finxx.methods: Exploratory analysis of the multicentre FinXX randomised trial, which accrued 1500 women in Finland and Sweden between January 2004 and May 2007. About half received three cycles of docetaxel followed by three cycles of cyclophosphamide, epirubicin and fluorouracil (T+CEF), and the other half three cycles of docetaxel plus capecitabine followed by three cycles of cyclophosphamide, epirubicin and capecitabine (TX+CEX). The main outcome was recurrence-free survival, compared overall and within subgroups defined by steroid hormone receptor and HER2 status.
finxx.results: 747 women received T+CEF and 753 TX+CEX; five were excluded from the intention-to-treat population. Of the remaining 1495, median age was 53 years, 157 (11%) had node-negative disease, 1142 (76%) oestrogen receptor-positive and 282 (19%) HER2-positive cancer. After a median follow-up of 10.3 years, neither recurrence-free survival (HR 0.88, 0.71 to 1.08, P = .23) nor overall survival (HR 0.84, 0.66 to 1.07, P = .15) differed significantly, and breast cancer-specific survival tended to favour capecitabine (HR 0.79, 0.60 to 1.04, P = .10). In triple-negative disease TX+CEX was more effective than T+CEF for recurrence-free survival (HR 0.53, 0.31 to 0.92, P = .02) and survival (HR 0.55, 0.31 to 0.96, P = .03).

first.methods: Phase 2 randomised open-label multicentre study in postmenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive advanced breast cancer receiving first-line endocrine therapy. Patients received fulvestrant 500 mg per month plus 500 mg on day 14 of month 1, or anastrozole 1 mg daily. The primary endpoint was clinical benefit rate, defined as objective response or stable disease for at least 24 weeks. The primary analysis was done 6 months after the last patient was randomly assigned.
first.results: Clinical benefit rate was 72.5% for fulvestrant 500 mg (n=102) and 67.0% for anastrozole (n=103), odds ratio 1.30, 95% CI 0.72 to 2.38, P=.386. Objective response rate was 36.0% versus 35.5%. Median time to progression was not reached with fulvestrant versus 12.5 months with anastrozole, hazard ratio 0.63, 95% CI 0.39 to 1.00, P=.0496. Both treatments were well tolerated with no significant difference in prespecified adverse events.

fourlight-1.methods: Open-label randomised phase 2 study in patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer whose disease progressed on prior adjuvant or first-line CDK4/6 inhibitor treatment. Patients were randomised 1:1 to atirmociclib, a highly selective CDK4 inhibitor, 300 mg orally twice daily without a break, with fulvestrant, or to investigator's choice of fulvestrant alone or everolimus plus exemestane. The primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival. Secondary endpoints included overall survival, objective response rate, duration of response, clinical benefit rate and safety.
fourlight-1.results: At the data cutoff of 12 January 2026, 263 patients were enrolled, 126 to atirmociclib and 137 to investigator's choice, with a median age of 57 years. Progression-free survival was significantly improved with atirmociclib (stratified hazard ratio 0.60, 95% CI 0.440 to 0.825, one-sided P = 0.0007), with medians of 9.4 versus 6.6 months and a consistent benefit across most subgroups. In patients with baseline measurable disease the objective response rate was 19.3% (21 patients) versus 11.3% (13), nominal two-sided P = 0.0901. Median duration of response was 14.8 versus 9.3 months. The clinical benefit rate was 61.9% versus 46.0%. The commonest any-grade treatment-emergent adverse events with atirmociclib were neutropenia (47.2%), leukopenia (33.6%) and diarrhoea (28.0%), and 6.4% of patients discontinued atirmociclib because of them.

francini-exemestane-switch.methods: Randomised study of longitudinal changes in body composition and lipid profiles in postmenopausal women switched from tamoxifen to exemestane. 60 overweight or obese postmenopausal patients were enrolled. Anthropometric data, body composition including fat mass and fat-free mass, lipid profiles, caloric intake and physical activity were assessed 1 week before randomisation and 6 and 12 months later.
francini-exemestane-switch.results: 55 patients, 27 on tamoxifen and 28 on exemestane, completed the 1-year study period. Fat mass decreased significantly by month 12 in the exemestane group but not in the tamoxifen group, with a significant between-group difference (P < 0.01). The ratio of fat-free to fat mass increased in the exemestane group but not the tamoxifen group (between-group P < 0.05). In the exemestane group triglycerides and HDL cholesterol decreased significantly (P < 0.01 and P < 0.05) and LDL cholesterol increased significantly (P < 0.01) at the end of the year.

ganea-2.methods: GANEA 2 assessed the accuracy and safety of sentinel lymph node biopsy after neoadjuvant chemotherapy in early breast cancer. Before chemotherapy, patients with cytologically proven node involvement were allocated to the pN1 group and the others to the cN0 group. After chemotherapy, pN1 patients underwent sentinel node biopsy and axillary lymph node dissection, while cN0 patients underwent dissection only for mapping failure or sentinel node involvement. The main endpoint was the sentinel node false negative rate; secondary endpoints were predictive factors for a positive axillary dissection and survival of patients treated with sentinel node biopsy alone.
ganea-2.results: From 2010 to 2014, 957 patients were included. Among the 419 cN0 patients treated with sentinel node biopsy alone, one axillary relapse occurred during follow-up. In the pN1 group, 103 patients with successful mapping had a negative sentinel node, and the false negative rate was 11.9% (95% CI 7.3% to 17.9%). In multivariate analysis, residual breast tumour of 5 mm or more after chemotherapy and lympho-vascular invasion were independent predictors of an involved axillary dissection.

gap70.methods: Cluster-randomised trial in 40 community oncology practice clusters across the USA. Eligible patients were aged 70 years and older with incurable solid tumours or lymphoma, had at least one impaired geriatric assessment domain, and were starting a new regimen. Clusters were randomly assigned 1:1 to the intervention, in which oncologists received a tailored geriatric assessment summary and management recommendations, or usual care. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients with any grade 3-5 toxic effect over 3 months.
gap70.results: 718 patients were enrolled. Mean age was 77.2 years and 311 of 718 participants (43%) were female. The mean number of impaired geriatric assessment domains was 4.5. Grade 3-5 toxic effects occurred in 177 of 349 patients (51%) in the intervention group versus 263 of 369 (71%) with usual care (relative risk 0.74, 95% CI 0.64 to 0.86, p=0.0001). Falls over 3 months were 12% versus 21% (adjusted relative risk 0.58).

gbg-26-big-03-05.methods: Randomised trial in patients with HER2-positive breast cancer progressing during trastuzumab. Patients were assigned to capecitabine 2,500 mg/m2 on days 1 through 14, given as 1,250 mg/m2 twice daily, alone or with continuation of trastuzumab 6 mg/kg, in 3-week cycles. The primary endpoint was time to progression.
gbg-26-big-03-05.results: 78 patients were assigned to capecitabine and 78 to capecitabine plus trastuzumab. During 15.6 months of follow-up there were 65 events and 38 deaths with capecitabine and 62 events and 33 deaths with capecitabine plus trastuzumab. Median time to progression was 5.6 versus 8.2 months, hazard ratio 0.69, 95% CI 0.48 to 0.97, P=.0338. Overall response rate was 27.0% versus 48.1%, odds ratio 2.50, P=.0115. Toxicity was not increased.

gec-estro-apbi.methods: Randomised, phase 3, non-inferiority trial at 16 centres in seven European countries. Patients aged 40 or older with early invasive breast cancer or ductal carcinoma in situ treated with breast-conserving surgery were centrally randomised 1:1 to whole-breast irradiation (50 Gy in 25 daily fractions with a 10 Gy tumour-bed boost) or to accelerated partial breast irradiation by multicatheter brachytherapy (30.1 Gy in seven or 32.0 Gy in eight high-dose-rate fractions, or 50 Gy pulsed-dose-rate, over 5 days). The primary endpoint was ipsilateral local recurrence in the as-treated population, with a non-inferiority margin of 3 percentage points defined for the 5-year results.
gec-estro-apbi.results: Between April 2004 and July 2009, 1328 patients were randomised, 673 to whole-breast irradiation and 655 to partial-breast irradiation, of whom 551 and 633 were eligible for analysis. At a median follow-up of 10.36 years, 10-year local recurrence was 1.58% (0.37 to 2.8) with whole-breast irradiation and 3.51% (1.99 to 5.03) with partial-breast irradiation, a difference of 1.93% (-0.018 to 3.87; p = 0.074). Treatment-related grade 3 late side-effects were less frequent with partial-breast irradiation (seven of 470, 1%, vs 17 of 393, 4%; p = 0.021). No grade 4 events or treatment-related deaths occurred.

geicam-9805.methods: 1060 women with axillary node-negative breast cancer and at least one high-risk factor for recurrence by the 1998 St Gallen criteria were randomly assigned to TAC or FAC every 3 weeks for six cycles after surgery. The primary end point was disease-free survival after at least 5 years of follow-up; secondary end points included overall survival and toxicity.
geicam-9805.results: At a median follow-up of 77 months, 87.8% of the 539 women given TAC and 81.8% of the 521 given FAC were alive and disease-free, a 32% reduction in the risk of recurrence with TAC (HR 0.68, 0.49 to 0.93; P = 0.01), consistent across hormone receptor status, menopausal status and number of high-risk factors. Survival (95.2% vs 93.5%) did not differ significantly (HR 0.76, 0.45 to 1.26), with few events (26 and 34). Grade 3 or 4 adverse events occurred in 28.2% with TAC and 17.0% with FAC (P<0.001), and TAC toxicity was lower with primary G-CSF prophylaxis.

generations.methods: Randomised, blinded trial in women aged 60 to 85 years with osteoporosis, defined as a femoral neck or lumbar spine bone mineral density T-score of -2.5 or less or a vertebral fracture, and women with low bone mass, a T-score of -1.0 or less and above -2.5, assigned to arzoxifene 20 mg or placebo daily. The primary end points were new vertebral fracture in those with osteoporosis and invasive breast cancer in the overall population.
generations.results: After 3 years, the cumulative incidence of vertebral fracture in women with osteoporosis was 2.3% lower with arzoxifene, a 41% relative risk reduction (95% CI 0.45 to 0.77, p < .001). In the overall population, the 4-year cumulative incidence of invasive breast cancer was reduced by 1.3%, a 56% relative reduction (HR 0.44, 0.26 to 0.76, p < .001). Nonvertebral fracture was not significantly reduced. Venous thromboembolic events rose by 0.7%, a 2.3-fold relative increase (1.5 to 3.7).

gennari-trastuzumab-adcc.methods: Extension of a pilot trial of preoperative trastuzumab in primary operable breast tumours overexpressing HER2, whose preliminary results suggested a role for antibody-dependent cell cytotoxicity (ADCC). To examine the factors affecting ADCC intensity and variability, the study was extended to phenotypic and functional analysis of circulating mononuclear cells in 18 patients.
gennari-trastuzumab-adcc.results: ADCC was induced by trastuzumab therapy in 15 of 18 patients (83%). Inability to develop ADCC in three patients did not depend on inadequate trastuzumab levels, as a further increase in concentration in vitro was ineffective; susceptibility was fairly predicted by testing with trastuzumab before therapy and correlated with the number of lymphocytes coexpressing CD16 and CD56. Natural killer cells and CD56-positive T cells were involved, and the killing efficiency of CD16-positive lymphocytes was influenced by the 158 V/F polymorphism of Fc gamma RIII. A complete pathological response was seen in one patient with ADCC of outstanding intensity, four partial responses showed intermediate ADCC, and none of the three patients unable to mount ADCC had significant tumour regression.

geparduo.methods: Phase III study of 913 women with untreated operable breast cancer (T2-3, N0-2, M0) randomly assigned to doxorubicin 50 mg/m2 plus docetaxel 75 mg/m2 every 14 days for four cycles with filgrastim (ADOC), or doxorubicin 60 mg/m2 plus cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m2 every 21 days followed by docetaxel 100 mg/m2 every 21 days for four cycles each (AC-DOC). The primary end point was pathological complete (invasive and noninvasive) response in the breast and axillary nodes.
geparduo.results: Pathological complete response was achieved in 94 patients (10.6%), more often with AC-DOC (14.3%, n = 63) than with ADOC (7.0%, n = 31; odds ratio 2.22, 90% CI 1.52 to 3.24; P < .001). Sequential therapy, high tumour grade and negative hormone receptor status independently predicted a pathological complete response. Response by palpation and by imaging was higher with AC-DOC (85.0% and 78.6%) than with ADOC (75.2% and 68.6%; both P < .001), and breast-conserving surgery was done in 63.4% and 58.1% (P = .05).

geparnuevo.methods: Randomised phase 2 double-blind placebo-controlled study. Patients with primary cT1b-cT4a-d centrally confirmed triple-negative breast cancer were randomised to durvalumab or placebo every 4 weeks in addition to nab-paclitaxel followed by standard epirubicin and cyclophosphamide. In a window phase, durvalumab or placebo alone was given 2 weeks before the start of nab-paclitaxel. Randomisation was stratified by stromal tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes. The primary objective was pathological complete response (ypT0 ypN0).
geparnuevo.results: 174 patients were randomised and 117 took part in the window phase. Median age was 49.5 years. Pathological complete response was 53.4% with durvalumab versus 44.2% with placebo (P=0.287, odds ratio 1.45). In the window cohort it was 61.0% versus 41.4% (odds ratio 2.22, P=0.035, interaction P=0.048). Thyroid dysfunction of any grade occurred in 47%. The 2022 survival report gave 3-year overall survival of 95.2% versus 83.5% (hazard ratio 0.24, 95% CI 0.08 to 0.72).

geparola.methods: Randomised, multicentre, prospective, open-label phase II trial. Patients with untreated primary HER2-negative breast cancer, cT2-cT4a-d or cT1c with clinically or sentinel-node positive disease or cT1c triple-negative or cT1c with Ki-67 above 20%, all with homologous recombination deficiency defined by a high HRD score and/or a germline or tumour BRCA1/2 mutation, were randomised to paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 weekly plus olaparib 100 mg twice daily for 12 weeks or to paclitaxel plus carboplatin AUC 2 weekly for 12 weeks, both followed by epirubicin and cyclophosphamide. Stratification was by hormone receptor status and by age under 40 against 40 or older. The primary endpoint was pathological complete response, ypT0/is ypN0, with a two-sided one-group chi-square test planned to exclude a pCR rate of 55% or lower in the olaparib arm. Secondary endpoints were other pCR definitions, breast conservation rate, clinical and imaging response, tolerability and safety, and in the long-term report invasive disease-free survival, distant disease-free survival and overall survival with a planned median follow-up beyond four years.
geparola.results: 107 patients were randomised between September 2016 and July 2018 and 106 started treatment, 69 on paclitaxel plus olaparib and 37 on paclitaxel plus carboplatin. Median age was 47.0 years, 86.8% had grade 3 tumours, 89.6% had Ki-67 above 20%, 72.6% were triple-negative and 56.2% had a confirmed germline BRCA1/2 mutation. The pCR rate was 55.1%, 90% CI 44.5 to 65.3, with olaparib against 48.6%, 90% CI 34.3 to 63.2, with carboplatin, so a pCR rate of 55% or lower could not be excluded, while higher pCR rates with olaparib were seen in patients under 40 and in hormone receptor-positive patients and olaparib was significantly better tolerated. After a median follow-up of 49.8 months there were 18 invasive disease-free survival events, 15 on olaparib and 3 on carboplatin, and 7 deaths, 6 and 1. Four-year invasive disease-free survival was 76.0% against 88.5%, hazard ratio 2.86, 95% CI 0.83 to 9.90, distant disease-free survival 81.2% against 93.4%, hazard ratio 3.03, 95% CI 0.67 to 13.67, and overall survival 89.2% against 96.9%, hazard ratio 3.27, 95% CI 0.39 to 27.20, all tending to be inferior with olaparib. Patients without a germline or tumour BRCA1/2 mutation benefited from carboplatin, 7 of 30 with an event on olaparib against 0 of 16 on carboplatin, log-rank P = 0.037, whereas no difference was seen in mutation carriers, hazard ratio 1.16, log-rank P = 0.83.

geparquattro.methods: Patients (n = 1495) with tumours cT3 or larger, or hormone receptor-negative status, or hormone receptor-positive and clinically node-positive disease received four cycles of epirubicin and cyclophosphamide and were then randomly assigned to four cycles of docetaxel, four cycles of docetaxel with capecitabine over 24 weeks, or four cycles of docetaxel followed by capecitabine over 36 weeks. Patients with HER2-positive tumours received 1 year of trastuzumab starting with the first chemotherapy cycle. This report gives disease-free and overall survival at a median follow-up of 5.4 years.
geparquattro.results: Outcome was not improved by capecitabine (disease-free survival HR 0.92, P = 0.463; overall survival P = 0.618) or by 36 weeks of chemotherapy (disease-free survival HR 0.97, P = 0.818; overall survival HR 0.97, P = 0.825). Trastuzumab-treated patients with HER2-positive disease had disease-free survival similar to (P = 0.305), and adjusted overall survival significantly better than (P = 0.040), patients with HER2-negative disease treated with chemotherapy alone. Recorded long-term cardiac toxicity was low.

geparquinto-her2.methods: Patients with HER2-positive tumours (n = 615) received neoadjuvant epirubicin plus cyclophosphamide followed by docetaxel, combined with either lapatinib (n = 308) or trastuzumab (n = 307). All patients received adjuvant trastuzumab, for 12 months in total in the trastuzumab arm and 18 months in the lapatinib arm. This report gives long-term outcomes at a median follow-up of 55 months.
geparquinto-her2.results: Three-year disease-free survival, distant disease-free survival and overall survival did not differ significantly between the arms. Long-term outcomes correlated with pathological complete response (disease-free survival HR 0.63, P = .042; distant disease-free survival HR 0.55, P = .021; overall survival HR 0.31, P = .004). Overall survival was significantly better in hormone receptor-positive patients treated with neoadjuvant lapatinib followed by adjuvant trastuzumab (HR 0.32, P = .019), with no difference in hormone receptor-negative patients, where events were few.

geparquinto-her2-negative.methods: Patients (n = 1948) with HER2-negative tumours of median size 4 cm were randomly assigned to neoadjuvant epirubicin and cyclophosphamide followed by docetaxel, with or without eight infusions of bevacizumab every 3 weeks before surgery. Patients without clinical response to EC with or without bevacizumab were randomised to 12 weekly cycles of paclitaxel with or without everolimus 5 mg daily. The bevacizumab comparison required 379 events to detect a hazard ratio of 0.75. This report gives disease-free and overall survival.
geparquinto-her2-negative.results: With a median follow-up of 3.8 years, 3-year disease-free survival was 80.8% and 3-year overall survival 89.7%. Outcome did not differ with bevacizumab (disease-free survival HR 1.03, P = 0.784; overall survival HR 0.974, P = 0.842), including in triple-negative disease (HR 0.99, P = 0.941, and HR 1.02, P = 0.891), and no other predefined subgroup showed a significant benefit. Disease-free (HR 0.997, P = 0.987) and overall survival (HR 1.11, P = 0.658) did not differ for non-early-responding patients given paclitaxel with or without everolimus.

geparsepto-gbg-69.methods: Phase 3 randomised trial in patients with previously untreated primary invasive breast cancer, assigned 1:1 with minimisation by subtype, Ki67 and SPARC expression. Patients received nab-paclitaxel 150 mg/m2, later amended to 125 mg/m2, or solvent-based paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 on days 1, 8 and 15 for four 3-week cycles, followed by epirubicin plus cyclophosphamide for four cycles. Patients with HER2-positive tumours also received trastuzumab and pertuzumab. The primary endpoint was pathological complete response.
geparsepto-gbg-69.results: 1229 women were randomly assigned and 1206 started treatment. The nab-paclitaxel dose was reduced to 125 mg/m2 after 464 participants because of discontinuation and neuropathy. Pathological complete response occurred in 233 patients (38%) given nab-paclitaxel versus 174 (29%) given solvent-based paclitaxel, odds ratio 1.53, 95% CI 1.20 to 1.95, p=0.00065. Grade 3-4 sensory neuropathy occurred in 10% versus 3% and grade 3-4 anaemia in 2% versus 1%. Four deaths occurred on treatment.

geparsixto.methods: Randomised phase 2 trial. Patients with previously untreated, non-metastatic, stage II-III triple-negative or HER2-positive breast cancer received 18 weeks of weekly paclitaxel plus non-pegylated liposomal doxorubicin. Triple-negative patients also received bevacizumab. HER2-positive patients also received trastuzumab and lapatinib. Patients were randomly assigned 1:1, stratified by subtype and Ki-67, to weekly carboplatin AUC 1.5 (AUC 2.0 for the first 329 patients) or no carboplatin. The primary endpoint was pathological complete response (ypT0 ypN0).
geparsixto.results: 296 patients were assigned carboplatin and 299 no carboplatin. Pathological complete response was 43.7% (129 patients) versus 36.9% (108 patients), odds ratio 1.33, p=0.107. In triple-negative disease it was 53.2% (84 of 158) versus 36.9% (58 of 157), p=0.005. In HER2-positive disease it was 32.8% (45 of 137) versus 36.8% (50 of 136), p=0.581, interaction p=0.015. Grade 3 or 4 neutropenia occurred in 65% versus 27%.

gepartrio.methods: 2072 patients were treated with two cycles of docetaxel, doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide (TAC). Early responders were randomly assigned to four (n = 704) or six (n = 686) additional TAC cycles, and early non-responders to four cycles of TAC (n = 321) or of vinorelbine and capecitabine (NX; n = 301) before surgery. This report gives disease-free and overall survival.
gepartrio.results: Disease-free survival was longer in early responders receiving TAC x8 than in those receiving TAC x6 (HR 0.78, 0.62 to 0.97; P = .026) and in early non-responders receiving TAC-NX than in those receiving TAC x6 (HR 0.59, 0.49 to 0.82; P = .001). In an exploratory analysis, response-guided chemotherapy (TAC x8 or TAC-NX) gave longer disease-free survival (HR 0.71, 0.60 to 0.85) and overall survival (HR 0.79, 0.63 to 0.99; P = .048) than conventional TAC x6. The disease-free survival gain was seen in hormone receptor-positive tumours (luminal A HR 0.55, luminal B HER2-negative HR 0.40, luminal B HER2-positive HR 0.56) but not in HER2-positive non-luminal (HR 1.01) or triple-negative tumours (HR 0.87), and pathological complete response did not predict these survival effects.

gim2.methods: Open-label 2x2 factorial phase 3 trial at 81 Italian centres. Patients aged 18-70 years with operable, node-positive, early-stage breast cancer were randomly allocated 1:1:1:1. Allocation was to dose-dense chemotherapy every 2 weeks with pegfilgrastim support or standard-interval chemotherapy every 3 weeks, and to fluorouracil plus epirubicin, cyclophosphamide and paclitaxel (FEC-P) or to EC-P alone. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival in the intention-to-treat population.
gim2.results: 2091 patients were recruited and median follow-up was 7.0 years. For the dose-density comparison, 5-year disease-free survival was 81% with every-2-week treatment versus 76% with every-3-week treatment (hazard ratio 0.77, 95% CI 0.65 to 0.92, p=0.004). Five-year overall survival was 94% versus 89% (hazard ratio 0.65, 0.51 to 0.84, p=0.001). For the chemotherapy-type comparison, 5-year disease-free survival was 78% with FEC-P versus 79% with EC-P (hazard ratio 1.06, p=0.561).

gim4.methods: Multicentre open-label randomised phase 3 trial at 69 Italian hospitals. Eligible women were postmenopausal with stage I to III operable hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, had taken adjuvant tamoxifen for 2 to 3 years with no sign of recurrence, and had ECOG performance status 2 or lower. Patients were assigned 1:1 to letrozole 2.5 mg once daily for 2 to 3 years or for 5 years. The primary endpoint was invasive disease-free survival.
gim4.results: 2056 patients were assigned to letrozole for 2 to 3 years (n=1030) or 5 years (n=1026). After a median follow-up of 11.7 years, disease-free survival events occurred in 262 control patients (25.4%) and 212 extended patients (20.7%). 12-year disease-free survival was 62% versus 67%, hazard ratio 0.78, 95% CI 0.65 to 0.93, p=0.0064. Grade 3 or 4 arthralgia occurred in 2.2% versus 3.0%. No deaths were related to toxic effects.

gmcsf-vaccine-cy-dox.methods: 3 x 3 factorial (response surface) dose-ranging study of cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin and a HER2-positive, allogeneic, GM-CSF-secreting tumour vaccine in 28 patients with metastatic breast cancer. Patients received three monthly immunisations, with a boost 6 to 8 months from entry. Primary objectives were safety and the chemotherapy doses that maximise HER2-specific immunity.
gmcsf-vaccine-cy-dox.results: Twenty-eight patients received at least one immunisation and 16 received four. No dose-limiting toxicities were observed. HER2-specific delayed-type hypersensitivity developed in most patients who received vaccine alone or with cyclophosphamide 200 mg/m2. HER2-specific antibody responses were enhanced by cyclophosphamide 200 mg/m2 and doxorubicin 35 mg/m2, which together produced the highest antibody responses, whereas higher cyclophosphamide doses suppressed immunity.

gmcsf-vaccine-trastuzumab.methods: Single-arm feasibility study of cyclophosphamide, an allogeneic HER2-positive GM-CSF-secreting breast tumour vaccine and weekly trastuzumab in 20 patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer, after experiments in neu transgenic mice. Patients received three monthly vaccinations with a boost 6 to 8 months from entry. Primary objectives were safety and clinical benefit (complete response, partial response or stable disease); secondary objectives were HER2-specific T-cell responses by delayed-type hypersensitivity and intracellular cytokine staining.
gmcsf-vaccine-trastuzumab.results: The combination was safe, with clinical benefit rates at 6 months and 1 year of 55% (95% CI 32% to 77%, P = 0.013) and 40% (19% to 64%). Median progression-free and overall survival were 7 months (4 to 16) and 42 months (22 to 70). HER2-specific delayed-type hypersensitivity increased in 7 of 20 patients, 4 of whom had clinical benefit, with a trend to longer progression-free and overall survival in responders, and polyfunctional HER2-specific CD8 T cells expanded across vaccination cycles.

gono-mig-1.methods: In the Italian multicentre phase 3 randomised MIG-1 trial, node-positive and high-risk node-negative breast cancer patients were randomised to six cycles of adjuvant fluorouracil, epirubicin and cyclophosphamide every 3 weeks (FEC21) or every 2 weeks (FEC14). The primary endpoint was overall survival and the secondary endpoint event-free survival.
gono-mig-1.results: From 1992 to 1997, 1214 patients were included and median follow-up was 15.8 years. Fifteen-year overall survival was 71% with FEC14 and 68% with FEC21 (HR 0.89; p = 0.25), and 15-year event-free survival 47% and 43% (HR 0.87; p = 0.18). In a pre-planned subgroup of hormone receptor-negative tumours, 15-year overall survival was 70% and 65% (HR 0.73, 0.51 to 1.06) and 15-year event-free survival 58% and 43% (HR 0.70, 0.51 to 0.96).

gp2-vaccine.methods: Four-arm, prospective, randomised, single-blinded, multicentre phase II trial of two HER2-derived peptide vaccines: AE37, which mainly elicits a CD4+ response, and GP2, which mainly elicits a CD8+ response. Disease-free node-positive and high-risk node-negative breast cancer patients were enrolled after standard of care therapy and received six monthly inoculations of vaccine or control as the primary series, with four boosters at 6-month intervals. Demographic, safety, immunological and disease-free survival data were evaluated in this final landmark analysis.
gp2-vaccine.results: 456 patients were enrolled: 154 to vaccine and 147 to control for AE37, and 89 to vaccine and 91 to control for GP2. Disease-free survival did not differ between AE37 and control. In prespecified exploratory subgroups AE37 showed trends towards benefit in advanced stage (HR 0.573, 0.275 to 1.193), HER2 under-expression (HR 0.756, 0.499 to 1.145) and triple-negative disease (HR 0.443, 0.114 to 1.717), and a significant benefit in patients with both HER2 under-expression and advanced stage (HR 0.375, 0.142 to 0.988, p = 0.039). GP2 did not significantly change disease-free survival; HER2-positive patients given GP2 had no recurrences, with a trend towards improved disease-free survival (p = 0.052).

h0648g.methods: Randomised trial of trastuzumab added to chemotherapy in women with metastatic breast cancer overexpressing HER2. 234 patients were assigned to standard chemotherapy alone and 235 to standard chemotherapy plus trastuzumab. Patients with no prior adjuvant anthracycline received doxorubicin, or epirubicin in 36 women, plus cyclophosphamide, alone in 138 women or with trastuzumab in 143. Patients with prior adjuvant anthracycline received paclitaxel alone in 96 women or paclitaxel with trastuzumab in 92.
h0648g.results: Adding trastuzumab lengthened time to progression (median 7.4 versus 4.6 months, P<0.001), raised objective response (50 versus 32 percent, P<0.001), lengthened response duration (median 9.1 versus 6.1 months, P<0.001), lowered death at 1 year (22 versus 33 percent, P=0.008) and lengthened median survival (25.1 versus 20.3 months, P=0.01). Class III or IV cardiac dysfunction occurred in 27 percent given anthracycline, cyclophosphamide and trastuzumab, 8 percent without trastuzumab, 13 percent given paclitaxel with trastuzumab and 1 percent without.

healer.methods: Phase 3, multicentre, open-label, randomised trial conducted in China. Patients with HER2-positive advanced breast cancer were randomly assigned 1:1 to anbenitamab, a HER2-targeted bispecific antibody, plus albumin-bound docetaxel (HB1801), or to docetaxel, trastuzumab and pertuzumab (THP). The primary endpoint was progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review. Objective response was a secondary endpoint.
healer.results: Of 885 patients enrolled, 445 were assigned to anbenitamab plus HB1801 and 440 to THP. The prespecified interim analysis came at 401 progression or death events and a median follow-up of 21.0 months. Estimated 24-month progression-free survival was 58.5% versus 34.4%, hazard ratio for progression or death 0.46 (95% CI 0.37 to 0.56), P<0.001. Objective response occurred in 87.6% versus 73.4%. Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 204 of 444 patients (45.9%) versus 151 of 439 (34.4%). Neutropenia was the most common of them in both groups, at 13.1% versus 8.4%. Adverse events leading to death occurred in 2 patients in each group.

heart.methods: 353 Chinese postmenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive early breast cancer were randomised to anastrozole or tamoxifen after optimal primary therapy. The primary end-point was fatty liver disease, defined as a liver-spleen ratio below 0.9 on computed tomography. Secondary end-points included abnormal liver function and treatment failure during 3 years of follow-up.
heart.results: The 3-year cumulative incidence of fatty liver disease was lower with anastrozole than with tamoxifen (14.6% vs 41.1%, P < 0.0001; relative risk 0.30, 0.21 to 0.45). The cumulative incidence of abnormal liver function did not differ (24.6% vs 24.7%, P = 0.61). Treatment failure was more frequent with tamoxifen, with median times to treatment failure of 15.1 months with tamoxifen and 37.1 months with anastrozole (HR 0.27, 0.20 to 0.37; P < 0.0001). The most common adverse events were reproductive system disorders with tamoxifen (17.1%) and musculoskeletal disorders with anastrozole (14.6%).

helen-006.methods: Multicentre randomised phase 3 trial at six hospitals in China. Patients aged 18 to 70 with untreated stage II to III HER2-positive breast cancer were assigned 1:1, stratified by tumour stage, nodal status and hormone receptor status. One group received nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 on days 1, 8 and 15 for six 3-week cycles, the other docetaxel 75 mg/m2 plus carboplatin AUC 6 for six 3-week cycles. Both received concurrent trastuzumab and pertuzumab. The primary endpoint was pathological complete response.
helen-006.results: 689 of 789 screened patients were randomly assigned and 669 started treatment. All were Asian women with a median age of 50 years, and median follow-up was 26 months. Pathological complete response occurred in 220 patients (66.3%, 95% CI 61.2 to 71.4) given nab-paclitaxel versus 194 (57.6%, 52.3 to 62.9) given docetaxel plus carboplatin, odds ratio 1.54, 95% CI 1.10 to 2.14, p=0.011. Grade 3-4 adverse events occurred in 30% versus 38%.

her2-dc1-dcis.methods: Randomised trial to establish safety and evaluate immune and clinical responses to HER2 peptide-pulsed DC1 vaccination by intralesional, intranodal, or both intralesional and intranodal injection. Fifty-four HER2-positive patients, 42 with pure ductal carcinoma in situ and 12 with early invasive breast cancer, received the vaccine before surgery, randomised to intralesional (19), intranodal (19) or both (16). Immune responses were measured in peripheral blood and sentinel lymph nodes, and pathological response in the resected specimens.
her2-dc1-dcis.results: Vaccination by all routes was well tolerated. Immune response rates did not differ by route (84.2% vs 89.5% vs 66.7%, P = 0.30). The pathological complete response rate was higher in DCIS than in invasive cancer (28.6% vs 8.3%). DCIS patients with (12) and without (30) a pathological complete response had similar peripheral blood anti-HER2 responses, but all patients with a complete response had an anti-HER2 CD4 response in the sentinel node, higher by response repertoire (P = 0.03) and cumulative response (P = 0.04).

her2-helper-peptide-vaccine.methods: Sixty-four patients with HER-2/neu-overexpressing breast, ovarian or non-small-cell lung cancer were enrolled and vaccinated intradermally with peptides derived from potential T-helper epitopes of the HER-2/neu protein admixed with GM-CSF. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells were evaluated at baseline and after vaccination for antigen-specific T-cell immunity. Immunological data are presented on the 38 who completed six vaccinations and toxicity data on all 64.
her2-helper-peptide-vaccine.results: Ninety-two percent of patients developed T-cell immunity to HER-2/neu peptides (stimulation index 2.1 to 59) and 68% to a HER-2/neu protein domain (2 to 31). Epitope spreading was observed in 84% and correlated significantly with protein-specific T-cell immunity (P = .03). At 1-year follow-up, immunity to the HER-2/neu protein persisted in 38%.

her2-heterogeneity.methods: Prospective phase II neoadjuvant trial designed to assess the impact of HER2 heterogeneity on response to HER2-targeted therapy. 164 patients with centrally confirmed HER2-positive early-stage breast cancer were treated with neoadjuvant trastuzumab emtansine plus pertuzumab. HER2 heterogeneity was assessed on pretreatment biopsies taken from two locations of each tumour, and was defined as an area with HER2 amplification in more than 5% but fewer than 50% of tumour cells, or a HER2-negative area by FISH. Single-cell FISH analysis of cellular heterogeneity was also performed. The comparison of pathological complete response by heterogeneity status was adjusted for hormone receptor status.
her2-heterogeneity.results: HER2 heterogeneity was detected in 10% of evaluable cases, 16 of 157. The pathological complete response rate was 55% in the non-heterogeneous subgroup and 0% in the heterogeneous group, P < 0.0001 after adjustment for hormone receptor status. Single-cell FISH analysis identified the fraction of HER2 non-amplified cells as a driver of therapeutic resistance. The authors conclude that HER2 heterogeneity is associated with resistance to HER2-targeted therapy and should be considered in efforts to optimise treatment strategies.

her2-icd-dna-vaccine.methods: Single-arm phase 1 trial of 66 patients with advanced-stage ERBB2 (HER2)-positive breast cancer treated at an academic medical centre between 2001 and 2010, with 10-year postvaccine toxicity assessments. Patients were sequentially enrolled to three dose arms (10, 100 and 500 μg) of a plasmid-based vaccine encoding the ERBB2 intracellular domain (ICD), given intradermally once a month with soluble GM-CSF as adjuvant for 3 immunizations. Safety was graded by CTCAE version 3.0 and ERBB2 ICD immune responses measured by interferon-γ ELISPOT; secondary objectives were whether dose was associated with immunity and the persistence of plasmid DNA at the vaccine site, measured by biopsy at weeks 16 and 36.
her2-icd-dna-vaccine.results: Sixty-six patients, median age 51 years (range 34 to 77), were enrolled. Most vaccine-related toxic effects were grade 1 and 2 and did not differ significantly between dose arms. Arms 2 (100 μg) and 3 (500 μg) had higher-magnitude ERBB2 ICD type 1 immune responses at most time points than arm 1 (10 μg) after adjustment for baseline factors (coefficient 181, 95% CI 60 to 303, P = .003, and 233, 102 to 363, P < .001). Immunity after the end of immunizations was significantly lower on average in patients with DNA persistence at week 16, and the highest dose was associated with the greatest incidence of persistent DNA at the injection site.

her2-p369-vaccine.methods: Six HLA-A2-positive patients with HER-2/neu-overexpressing stage III or IV breast or ovarian cancer received six monthly vaccinations of 500 microg of the HER-2/neu peptide p369-377 admixed with 100 microg of GM-CSF, to test whether peptide-specific CD8 T-cell immunity could be elicited by an immunodominant HLA-A2 peptide alone. Immune responses were measured by IFN-gamma enzyme-linked immunosorbent spot assay.
her2-p369-vaccine.results: Before vaccination the median precursor frequency to p369-377 was 0 per 10^6 peripheral blood mononuclear cells. After vaccination the median in four evaluable patients was 0 (range 0 to 116), and peptide-specific precursors developed in two of four. The responses were short-lived and not detectable 5 months after the final vaccination. Patients were immunocompetent, with responses to tetanus toxoid and influenza.

her2climb.methods: Randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial. Patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer previously treated with trastuzumab, pertuzumab and trastuzumab emtansine, with or without brain metastases, were assigned to tucatinib or placebo in combination with trastuzumab and capecitabine. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival among the first 480 patients randomised. Secondary endpoints in the total population of 612 patients included overall survival, progression-free survival in patients with brain metastases, confirmed objective response rate and safety.
her2climb.results: One-year progression-free survival was 33.1% with tucatinib versus 12.3% with placebo (hazard ratio 0.54, 95% CI 0.42 to 0.71), with medians of 7.8 and 5.6 months. Two-year overall survival was 44.9% versus 26.6% (hazard ratio 0.66, 0.50 to 0.88), with medians of 21.9 and 17.4 months. Among patients with brain metastases, 1-year progression-free survival was 24.9% versus 0% (hazard ratio 0.48, 0.34 to 0.69), with medians of 7.6 and 5.4 months.

her2climb-02.methods: Phase III randomised trial in patients with HER2-positive locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer previously treated with trastuzumab and a taxane in any setting, including patients with brain metastases. Patients were assigned 1:1 to trastuzumab emtansine 3.6 mg/kg intravenously every 21 days with either tucatinib 300 mg orally twice daily or placebo twice daily.
her2climb-02.results: 463 patients were randomly assigned. After a median follow-up of 24.4 months, median progression-free survival was 9.5 months with tucatinib versus 7.4 months with placebo, hazard ratio 0.76, 95% CI 0.61 to 0.95, P=0.0163, with benefit across all prespecified subgroups including patients with brain metastases. Discontinuation for treatment-emergent adverse events was 22.1% versus 11.6% and grade 3 or higher events 68.8% versus 41.2%, most often raised alanine and aspartate aminotransferase.

her2climb-05.methods: Phase III randomised trial in patients with centrally confirmed HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer who had no progression after induction therapy and had no or asymptomatic brain metastases. Patients were assigned 1:1 to tucatinib 300 mg or placebo twice a day combined with trastuzumab and pertuzumab. The primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival. Secondary endpoints included overall survival, progression-free survival by blinded independent central review, CNS progression-free survival and safety.
her2climb-05.results: 654 patients were assigned to tucatinib (n=326) or placebo (n=328) between March 2022 and July 2024. Median age was 54 years, 69.3% had de novo metastatic disease, 52.6% were hormone receptor-positive and 12.4% had baseline brain metastases. Median progression-free survival was 24.9 versus 16.3 months, hazard ratio 0.641, 95% CI 0.514 to 0.799, P<.0001, with benefit regardless of brain metastases or hormone receptor status. Diarrhoea affected 72.7% of tucatinib patients.

hera.methods: International multicentre open-label phase 3 randomised trial of 5102 women with HER2-positive early breast cancer, enrolled in 39 countries between December 2001 and June 2005. After completion of all primary therapy, including surgery, chemotherapy and radiotherapy as indicated, patients were randomly assigned 1:1:1 to trastuzumab for 1 year, trastuzumab for 2 years, or observation. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival in the intention-to-treat population. The 2-year versus 1-year comparison used 366-day landmark analyses.
hera.results: 5099 patients were analysed, 1697 in observation, 1702 in the 1-year group and 1700 in the 2-year group. After a median follow-up of 11 years, 1 year of trastuzumab reduced disease-free survival events (hazard ratio 0.76, 95% CI 0.68 to 0.86) and death (0.74, 0.64 to 0.86) versus observation. Two years did not improve disease-free survival over 1 year (hazard ratio 1.02, 0.89 to 1.17). Ten-year disease-free survival was 63%, 69% and 69%. 884 observation patients (52%) crossed over.

heritage.methods: Multicentre, double-blind, randomised, parallel-group phase 3 equivalence study in patients with ERBB2-positive metastatic breast cancer without prior treatment for metastatic disease. From December 2012 to August 2015, 500 patients were randomised 1:1 to a proposed biosimilar or trastuzumab, each with a taxane; chemotherapy was given for at least 24 weeks, followed by antibody alone until unacceptable toxic effects or progression. The primary outcome was week 24 overall response rate, with equivalence boundaries of 0.81 to 1.24 for the response ratio (90% CI) and -15% to 15% for the difference (95% CI).
heritage.results: The intention-to-treat population included 458 women and the safety population 493. The overall response rate was 69.6% with the proposed biosimilar and 64.0% with trastuzumab; the ratio (1.09, 90% CI 0.974 to 1.211) and the difference (5.53, 95% CI -3.08 to 14.04) were within the equivalence boundaries. At week 48 there was no significant difference in time to tumour progression (41.3% vs 43.0%), progression-free survival (44.3% vs 44.7%) or overall survival (89.1% vs 85.1%). At least one adverse event occurred in 98.6% and 94.7%, most commonly neutropenia (57.5% vs 53.3%), peripheral neuropathy (23.1% vs 24.8%) and diarrhoea (20.6% vs 20.7%).

horizon-breast06.methods: Open-label, randomised, multicentre phase 3 trial at 73 hospitals in China. Eligible patients were women aged 18 to 75 with centrally confirmed HER2-low (immunohistochemistry 1+, or 2+ with negative in situ hybridisation) unresectable locally recurrent or metastatic breast cancer who had received one or fewer prior lines of chemotherapy for metastatic disease, with prior endocrine therapy required for hormone receptor-positive disease. Patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to trastuzumab rezetecan 6.4 mg/kg intravenously every 3 weeks or to physician's choice of chemotherapy. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival by blinded independent central review in chemotherapy-naive patients and in the overall population.
horizon-breast06.results: Between June 30, 2023, and August 20, 2025, 551 patients were randomised, 277 to trastuzumab rezetecan and 274 to chemotherapy, with a mean age of 54.9 years. At the data cutoff of March 20, 2026, median progression-free survival in chemotherapy-naive patients was 16.6 months (95% CI 14.0 to 19.4) with trastuzumab rezetecan versus 6.8 months (5.7 to 7.0) with chemotherapy, hazard ratio 0.25 (95% CI 0.19 to 0.33), P < .001. In the overall population it was 16.4 months (14.0 to 16.8) versus 6.8 months (5.7 to 6.9), hazard ratio 0.27 (0.21 to 0.34), P < .001. In hormone receptor-negative disease median progression-free survival was 16.5 versus 6.8 months, hazard ratio 0.34 (0.22 to 0.54). In hormone receptor-positive disease it was 16.4 versus 6.7 months, hazard ratio 0.24 (0.18 to 0.33). Grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events occurred in 84.1% (232 of 276) versus 67.9% (184 of 271), most commonly decreased neutrophil count, in 65.2% versus 54.2%.

hot.methods: Phase III trial in 1884 recently postmenopausal women on hormone replacement therapy, randomly assigned to tamoxifen 5 mg per day or placebo for 5 years. The primary end point was breast cancer incidence.
hot.results: After a mean follow-up of 6.2 years there were 24 breast cancers on placebo and 19 on tamoxifen (RR 0.80, 95% CI 0.44 to 1.46). Tamoxifen showed favourable trends in luminal A tumours (RR 0.32, 0.12 to 0.86), in women who had used HRT for less than 5 years (RR 0.35, 0.15 to 0.82) and in women completing at least 12 months of treatment (RR 0.49, 0.23 to 1.02). Serious adverse events did not differ, including coronary heart syndrome (6 vs 4), cerebrovascular events (2 vs 5), venous thromboembolism (2 vs 5) and uterine cancers (3 vs 1), placebo vs tamoxifen. Vasomotor symptoms were 50% more frequent on tamoxifen.

hypnosis-hot-flashes.methods: Sixty breast cancer survivors with hot flashes were randomly assigned to a hypnosis intervention of five weekly sessions or no treatment. Eligible women had a history of primary breast cancer without detectable disease and 14 or more weekly hot flashes for at least 1 month. The major outcome was a bivariate construct of hot flash frequency and hot flash score, analysed by a sums-and-differences comparison; secondary outcomes were self-reported interference of hot flashes with daily activities.
hypnosis-hot-flashes.results: Fifty-one women completed the study. By the end of treatment, hot flash scores (frequency times average severity) fell 68% from baseline in the hypnosis arm (P < .001). Self-reported anxiety, depression, interference of hot flashes with daily activities and sleep improved significantly with hypnosis compared with no treatment (P < .005).

ibcsg-22-00.methods: Randomised phase III trial that enrolled 1086 women (1081 intent-to-treat) from November 2000 to December 2012. Women with oestrogen and progesterone receptor-negative (below 10% positive cells) early breast cancer of any nodal and HER2 status were randomly assigned, between primary surgery and 56 days after the first day of the last adjuvant chemotherapy course, to cyclophosphamide 50 mg daily continuously and methotrexate 2.5 mg twice daily on days 1 and 2 of every week for 1 year, or to no maintenance. The primary end point was disease-free survival, including invasive recurrence, second malignancy and death.
ibcsg-22-00.results: After a median follow-up of 6.9 years, disease-free survival was not significantly better with maintenance, overall (HR 0.84, 0.66 to 1.06; P = .14) or in triple-negative disease (n = 814; HR 0.80, 0.60 to 1.06). Patients with triple-negative node-positive disease had a nonsignificant reduction (n = 340; HR 0.72, 0.49 to 1.05). Seventy-one (13%) of 542 patients assigned to maintenance did not start it. Of 473 who received at least one dose, 64 (14%) had a grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse event, most often raised serum transaminases (7%).

ibcsg-23-01.methods: Multicentre, randomised, controlled, open-label, non-inferiority phase 3 trial at 27 centres in nine countries. Women of any age with breast cancer of 5 cm or smaller and one or more sentinel nodes with metastases all of 2 mm or smaller, without extracapsular extension, were randomly assigned 1:1 before surgery to no axillary dissection or axillary dissection, stratified by centre and menopausal status. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival by intention to treat, tested one-sided for non-inferiority with a hazard ratio margin of 1.25. This 10-year analysis was not prespecified.
ibcsg-23-01.results: Between April 2001 and February 2010, 934 patients were randomly assigned, 469 to no axillary dissection and 465 to axillary dissection. At a median follow-up of 9.7 years, 10-year disease-free survival was 76.8% (72.5% to 81.0%) without and 74.9% (70.5% to 79.3%) with axillary dissection (HR 0.85, 0.65 to 1.11; log-rank p = 0.24; non-inferiority p = 0.0024). Long-term lymphoedema occurred in 4% without and 13% with dissection, sensory neuropathy in 13% and 19%, and motor neuropathy in 3% and 9%.

ibcsg-41-13.methods: Premenopausal women with stage cT2 to 4b, any N, M0 breast cancer, oestrogen and progesterone receptor above 50% and HER2-negative, were randomly assigned to triptorelin 3.75 mg intramuscularly on day 1 of every cycle or degarelix 240 mg subcutaneously on day 1 of cycle 1 then 80 mg on day 1 of cycles 2 to 6, both with letrozole 2.5 mg daily for six 28-day cycles, with surgery 2 to 3 weeks after the last injection. The primary end point was time to optimal ovarian function suppression, the first centrally assessed oestradiol of 2.72 pg/mL or less.
ibcsg-41-13.results: Between February 2014 and January 2017, 51 patients were enrolled, 26 to triptorelin plus letrozole and 25 to degarelix plus letrozole. Time to optimal suppression was three times faster with degarelix (median 3 vs 14 days; HR 3.05, 1.65 to 5.65; P < .001). Suppression was maintained in all degarelix patients in later cycles, whereas 15.4% of triptorelin patients had suboptimal suppression after cycle 1 (six events in 127 measurements). Adverse events were as expected.

ibis1.methods: Randomised controlled trial in premenopausal and postmenopausal women aged 35-70 years at increased risk of breast cancer, assigned 1:1 to oral tamoxifen 20 mg daily or matching placebo for 5 years by central block randomisation, with participants and investigators masked. The primary endpoint was the occurrence of breast cancer, invasive or ductal carcinoma in situ, by intention to treat. Active treatment is complete and long-term follow-up continues, with participants and investigators still largely masked.
ibis1.results: Between 1992 and 2001, 7154 eligible women were randomly allocated, 3579 to tamoxifen and 3575 to placebo. After a median follow-up of 16.0 years, 601 breast cancers were reported, 251 (7.0%) with tamoxifen and 350 (9.8%) with placebo (HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.60 to 0.83, p<0.0001). The risk reduction was similar in years 0-10 (HR 0.72, 0.59 to 0.88) and after 10 years (HR 0.69, 0.53 to 0.91). The greatest reductions were in invasive oestrogen receptor-positive cancer (HR 0.66, 0.54 to 0.81) and ductal carcinoma in situ (0.65, 0.43 to 1.00), with no effect on invasive oestrogen receptor-negative cancer (HR 1.05, 0.71 to 1.57).

ibis2-dcis.methods: Double-blind, multicentre, randomised placebo-controlled trial. Postmenopausal women with locally excised, hormone-receptor-positive DCIS were randomly assigned 1:1 by central computer allocation to 1 mg oral anastrozole or 20 mg oral tamoxifen daily for 5 years. Randomisation was stratified by major centre or hub and done in blocks. Trial personnel, participants and clinicians were masked. The primary endpoint was all recurrence, including recurrent DCIS and new contralateral tumours. Analysis was modified intention to treat.
ibis2-dcis.results: Between March 2003 and February 2012, 2980 postmenopausal women from 236 centres in 14 countries were enrolled, with 1449 analysed on anastrozole and 1489 on tamoxifen. Median follow-up was 7.2 years and 144 breast cancer recurrences were recorded. Overall recurrence was 67 with anastrozole versus 77 with tamoxifen, HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.64-1.23). Deaths numbered 33 versus 36, HR 0.93 (0.58-1.50), p=0.78. Any adverse event was reported by 1323 women (91%) versus 1379 (93%).

ibis2-prevention.methods: International, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial. Postmenopausal women at increased risk of breast cancer were randomly assigned 1:1 to anastrozole 1 mg per day orally or matching placebo daily for 5 years. After treatment, women were followed yearly for breast cancer incidence, death, other cancers and major adverse events (cardiovascular events and fractures). The primary outcome was all breast cancer, invasive or ductal carcinoma in situ.
ibis2-prevention.results: 3864 women were recruited between 2003 and 2012, 1920 to anastrozole and 1944 to placebo. After a median follow-up of 131 months, breast cancer was reduced by 49% with anastrozole (85 vs 165 cases, HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.39 to 0.66, p<0.0001). The reduction was larger in the first 5 years (35 vs 89, HR 0.39, 0.27 to 0.58) but still significant after 5 years (50 vs 76, HR 0.64, 0.45 to 0.91). Invasive oestrogen receptor-positive cancer was reduced by 54% (HR 0.46, 0.33 to 0.65) and ductal carcinoma in situ by 59% (HR 0.41, 0.22 to 0.79). Deaths did not differ (69 vs 70, HR 0.96, 0.69 to 1.34). Non-breast cancers fell (147 vs 200, odds ratio 0.72), mainly non-melanoma skin cancer, and no excess of fractures or cardiovascular disease was seen.

icarus-breast01.methods: Multicentre phase 2 study evaluating the efficacy, safety and biomarkers of response and resistance to patritumab deruxtecan (HER3-DXd) in hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer. Eligible patients had previously progressed on CDK4/6 inhibitors and one line of chemotherapy. From May 2021 to June 2023, 99 patients were enrolled to receive HER3-DXd 5.6 mg/kg intravenously every 3 weeks. The primary endpoint was overall response rate. Baseline and on-treatment tumour samples were analysed for HER3 expression and spatial distribution, ESR1 mutation status, antibody-drug conjugate intratumoral distribution and interferon response.
icarus-breast01.results: The study met its primary endpoint, showing an overall response rate of 53.5% (90% CI 44.8 to 62.1). The most frequent adverse events were fatigue in 83%, nausea in 75%, diarrhoea in 53% and alopecia in 40%. Exploratory analysis of baseline tumour samples suggested preliminary associations between overall response rate and both HER3 spatial distribution and the absence of ESR1 mutations, and between progression-free survival and HER3 expression, pending further validation. Analysis of on-treatment tumour samples showed that treatment efficacy seems to be associated with antibody-drug conjugate intratumoral distribution and interferon response. The authors conclude that HER3-DXd showed promising activity and manageable tolerability after progression on CDK4/6 inhibitors, and that larger trials are needed to define its efficacy relative to other drugs, including other antibody-drug conjugates.

ice-ii.methods: Patients aged 65 or older with a Charlson comorbidity index of 2 or less and pT1/2 pN0/1 disease that was HER2-positive, hormone receptor-negative, grade 3 or high in uPA/PAI-1, or any pT3/4 pN2/3 breast cancer, were randomised to four cycles of adjuvant epirubicin and cyclophosphamide or six cycles of CMF, versus six cycles of nab-paclitaxel 100 mg/m2 on days 1, 8 and 15 plus capecitabine 2000 mg/m2 on days 1 to 14 every 21 days (nPX). The primary endpoints were treatment discontinuation and the overall frequency of adverse events.
ice-ii.results: Thirteen of 198 patients (6.6%) discontinued EC or CMF and 69 of 193 (35.8%) discontinued nPX (P < .001), with one and five deaths during treatment. Grade 3 to 5 adverse events were more frequent with EC or CMF (90.9%) than with nPX (64.8%; P < .001), haematological toxicity being more frequent with EC or CMF (88.4% vs 22.3%) and nonhaematological toxicity with nPX (58.5% vs 18.7%). No geriatric score independently predicted grade 3 to 5 toxicity or discontinuation. Survival did not differ between groups after 22.8 months.

iceberg1.methods: Phase 2 study at 16 centres in Australia, Germany, Spain, Sweden, the UK and the USA of olaparib, an oral PARP inhibitor, in women aged 18 years or older with confirmed BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations and recurrent, advanced breast cancer. Women were assigned to two sequential cohorts: the first (n = 27) received continuous oral olaparib at the maximum tolerated dose of 400 mg twice daily and the second (n = 27) a lower dose of 100 mg twice daily. The primary efficacy endpoint was objective response rate.
iceberg1.results: Patients had received a median of three previous chemotherapy regimens (range 1 to 5 in cohort 1 and 2 to 4 in cohort 2). Objective response was 11 of 27 (41%, 95% CI 25 to 59) at 400 mg twice daily and 6 of 27 (22%, 11 to 41) at 100 mg twice daily. Toxicities were mainly low grade. The most frequent causally related adverse events at 400 mg were fatigue (grade 1 or 2 in 41%, grade 3 or 4 in 15%), nausea (41% and 15%), vomiting (11% and 11%) and anaemia (4% and 11%); at 100 mg they were nausea (grade 1 or 2 in 41%) and fatigue (grade 1 or 2 in 26%, grade 3 or 4 in 4%).

ideal.methods: Randomised phase III trial. Postmenopausal patients with hormone receptor-positive breast cancer were randomly allocated to either 2.5 or five years of letrozole after an initial five years of any endocrine therapy. The primary end point was disease-free survival. Secondary end points were overall survival, distant metastasis-free interval, new primary breast cancer, and safety. Hazard ratios were determined by Cox regression analysis. All analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle.
ideal.results: 1824 patients were assigned to 2.5 years (n=909) or five years (n=915) of letrozole, with median follow-up of 6.6 years. A disease-free survival event occurred in 152 patients in the five-year group and 163 in the 2.5-year group, HR 0.92 (95% CI 0.74 to 1.16). Overall survival HR was 1.04 (0.78 to 1.38). Distant metastasis-free interval HR was 1.06 (0.78 to 1.45). Second primary breast cancer was reduced with five years, HR 0.39 (0.19 to 0.81).
