ies.methods: 4724 postmenopausal patients with unilateral invasive, oestrogen-receptor-positive or oestrogen-receptor-unknown breast cancer who were disease-free on 2-3 years of tamoxifen were randomly assigned to switch to exemestane (n=2352) or to continue tamoxifen (n=2372) for the remainder of a 5-year endocrine treatment period. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival. Overall survival was a secondary endpoint. Efficacy analyses were intention to treat.
ies.results: After a median follow-up of 55.7 months, 809 disease-free survival events were reported, 354 with exemestane and 455 with tamoxifen. The unadjusted hazard ratio was 0.76 (95% CI 0.66-0.88, p=0.0001) in favour of exemestane, an absolute benefit of 3.3% (1.6-4.9) by the end of treatment. There were 222 deaths with exemestane and 261 with tamoxifen, hazard ratio 0.85 (0.71-1.02, p=0.08), and 0.83 (0.69-1.00, p=0.05) after excluding 122 patients with oestrogen-receptor-negative disease.

immu-132-01.methods: Phase 1/2 single-group, multicentre trial in patients with advanced epithelial cancers who received sacituzumab govitecan-hziy, an antibody-drug conjugate of a humanised anti-Trop-2 antibody and SN-38, intravenously on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle until progression or unacceptable toxicity. This report covers 108 patients with metastatic triple-negative breast cancer who received 10 mg per kilogram after at least two previous anticancer therapies for metastatic disease. End points included safety, objective response rate by RECIST 1.1 assessed locally, duration of response, clinical benefit rate, progression-free survival and overall survival; post hoc analyses assessed response by blinded independent central review.
immu-132-01.results: The 108 patients had received a median of 3 previous therapies (range 2 to 10). Four deaths occurred during treatment and 3 patients (2.8%) discontinued because of adverse events. Grade 3 or 4 adverse events in 10% or more included anaemia and neutropenia, and 10 patients (9.3%) had febrile neutropenia. The response rate (3 complete and 33 partial) was 33.3% (95% CI 24.6 to 43.1) with a median duration of response of 7.7 months (4.9 to 10.8); by independent central review these were 34.3% and 9.1 months. The clinical benefit rate was 45.4%, median progression-free survival 5.5 months (4.1 to 6.3) and median overall survival 13.0 months (11.2 to 13.7).

impact.methods: Postmenopausal women with ER-positive, invasive, nonmetastatic, operable or locally advanced potentially operable breast cancer were randomly assigned to neoadjuvant tamoxifen 20 mg daily, anastrozole 1 mg daily, or the combination for 3 months. Tumour objective response was assessed by caliper and by ultrasound. Further comparisons covered clinical versus ultrasound response, actual and feasible surgery against feasible surgery at baseline, response in HER2-positive cancers, and tolerability.
impact.results: Objective response did not differ significantly between the three arms in the intention-to-treat population. Among 124 patients judged at baseline to require mastectomy, 44% had breast-conserving surgery after anastrozole versus 31% after tamoxifen (P = .23). Among those their surgeon deemed feasible for breast-conserving surgery the difference reached significance, 46% versus 22% (P = .03). Objective response in 34 HER2-positive cancers was 58% with anastrozole versus 22% with tamoxifen (P = .18). All treatments were well tolerated.

impassion030.methods: Open-label international randomised phase 3 trial in more than 330 centres in 31 countries. Patients undergoing surgery as initial treatment for stage II or III triple-negative breast cancer were enrolled between August 2018 and November 2022. They were randomised 1:1 to standard chemotherapy for 20 weeks with atezolizumab for up to 1 year (n=1101) or without it (n=1098). The primary end point was invasive disease-free survival. The last follow-up was August 2023.
impassion030.results: The independent data monitoring committee halted enrolment at 2199 of 2300 planned patients. All patients stopped atezolizumab after a planned early interim and futility analysis. At the premature final analysis, invasive disease-free survival events had occurred in 141 patients (12.8%) on atezolizumab plus chemotherapy and 125 (11.4%) on chemotherapy alone, with median follow-up 32 months. The stratified hazard ratio was 1.11 (95% CI 0.87-1.42, P=.38). Treatment-related grade 3 or 4 adverse events were 54% versus 44%.

impassion031.methods: Double-blind, randomised, phase 3 study at 75 academic and community sites in 13 countries. Patients with previously untreated stage II-III triple-negative breast cancer were randomly assigned 1:1 to chemotherapy plus intravenous atezolizumab 840 mg or placebo every 2 weeks. Chemotherapy was weekly nab-paclitaxel for 12 weeks followed by doxorubicin plus cyclophosphamide every 2 weeks for 8 weeks, then surgery. Co-primary endpoints were pathological complete response in the all-randomised and PD-L1-positive populations.
impassion031.results: Of 333 eligible patients, 165 were randomly assigned to atezolizumab plus chemotherapy and 168 to placebo plus chemotherapy. Pathological complete response was documented in 95 patients (58%, 95% CI 50-65) versus 69 (41%, 34-49), a rate difference of 17% (6-27). In the PD-L1-positive population it was documented in 53 of 77 (69%) versus 37 of 75 (49%), a difference of 20% (4-35). The final analysis at 3 years reported overall survival hazard ratio 0.56 (0.30-1.04).

impassion050.methods: Patients with a primary tumour larger than 2 cm and histologically confirmed positive nodes (T2-4, N1-3, M0) were randomly assigned 1:1 to atezolizumab or placebo with dose-dense doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide, then paclitaxel, plus pertuzumab and trastuzumab. After surgery patients continued atezolizumab or placebo with pertuzumab and trastuzumab to complete 1 year of HER2-targeted therapy, and those with residual disease could switch to ado-trastuzumab emtansine. Coprimary endpoints were pathologic complete response rates in the intention-to-treat and PD-L1-positive populations.
impassion050.results: At the February 5, 2021 cutoff, pathologic complete response was 62.7% (143 of 228) with placebo and 62.4% (141 of 226) with atezolizumab, a difference of -0.33% (95% CI -9.2 to 8.6, P = .9551). In PD-L1-positive tumours the rates were 72.5% and 64.2%, a difference of -8.26% (95% CI -20.6 to 4.0, P = .1846). Grade 3-4 and serious adverse events were more frequent with atezolizumab, and five grade 5 events occurred, all with atezolizumab.

impassion130.methods: Phase 3 trial. Patients with untreated metastatic triple-negative breast cancer were randomly assigned 1:1 to atezolizumab plus nab-paclitaxel or placebo plus nab-paclitaxel, continued until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. Stratification was by receipt of neoadjuvant or adjuvant taxane, presence of liver metastases at baseline, and PD-L1 expression at baseline. The two primary end points were progression-free survival in the intention-to-treat population and the PD-L1-positive subgroup, and overall survival tested first in the intention-to-treat population.
impassion130.results: Each group included 451 patients, with median follow-up 12.9 months. In the intention-to-treat analysis median progression-free survival was 7.2 months with atezolizumab plus nab-paclitaxel versus 5.5 months with placebo, hazard ratio 0.80 (95% CI 0.69-0.92, P=0.002). In PD-L1-positive tumours it was 7.5 versus 5.0 months, hazard ratio 0.62 (0.49-0.78). Median overall survival was 21.3 versus 17.6 months, hazard ratio 0.84 (0.69-1.02, P=0.08). The final overall survival analysis reported 21.0 versus 18.7 months, hazard ratio 0.87 (0.75-1.02).

impassion131.methods: Eligible patients had advanced triple-negative breast cancer with no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease or at least 12 months since neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy. They were randomised 2:1 to atezolizumab 840 mg or placebo on days 1 and 15, both with paclitaxel 90 mg/m2 on days 1, 8 and 15, every 28 days until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Stratification used PD-L1 status, prior taxane, liver metastases and region. The primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival.
impassion131.results: Of 651 randomised patients, 45% had PD-L1-positive disease. Adding atezolizumab did not improve investigator-assessed progression-free survival in the PD-L1-positive population, hazard ratio 0.82 (95% CI 0.60 to 1.12, P = 0.20), median 6.0 versus 5.7 months. Unconfirmed best overall response was 63% versus 55% and median duration of response 7.2 versus 5.5 months. Final overall survival showed no difference, hazard ratio 1.11 (95% CI 0.76 to 1.64), median 22.1 versus 28.3 months. Intention-to-treat results were consistent.

import-low.methods: Multicentre, randomised, phase 3, non-inferiority trial at 30 UK radiotherapy centres. Women aged 50 years or older who had breast-conserving surgery for unifocal invasive ductal adenocarcinoma up to 3 cm, with none to three positive axillary nodes and microscopic margins of 2 mm or more, were randomly assigned 1:1:1 to 40 Gy whole-breast radiotherapy, 36 Gy whole breast plus 40 Gy partial breast, or 40 Gy partial breast alone, in 15 fractions. The primary endpoint was ipsilateral local relapse.
import-low.results: Between May 2007 and October 2010, 2018 women were recruited and two withdrew consent. 674 patients were analysed in the whole-breast control group, 673 in the reduced-dose group, and 669 in the partial-breast group. Median follow-up was 72.2 months. Five-year cumulative incidence of local relapse was 1.1% (95% CI 0.5-2.3) in the control group, 0.2% (0.02-1.2) in the reduced-dose group, and 0.5% (0.2-1.4) in the partial-breast group. Non-inferiority was shown for both experimental groups.

inavo120.methods: Phase 3, double-blind, randomised trial. Patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer carrying a mutation in the gene encoding the p110 alpha catalytic subunit of PI3K, who had relapsed during or within 12 months after completing adjuvant endocrine therapy, received first-line inavolisib 9 mg orally once daily plus palbociclib and fulvestrant or placebo plus palbociclib and fulvestrant. The primary end point was investigator-assessed progression-free survival.
inavo120.results: 161 patients were assigned to the inavolisib group and 164 to the placebo group, with median follow-up 21.3 and 21.5 months. Median progression-free survival was 15.0 months (95% CI 11.3 to 20.5) with inavolisib and 7.3 months (5.6 to 9.3) with placebo, hazard ratio 0.43 (0.32 to 0.59, P<0.001). Objective response occurred in 58.4% versus 25.0%. The final overall survival analysis reported median 34.0 versus 27.0 months, hazard ratio 0.67 (0.48 to 0.94, P=0.02).

inform.methods: Randomised multicentre phase 2 trial. Germline BRCA1/2 carriers with cT1-3 tumours of at least 1.5 cm and cN0-3 HER2-negative breast cancer were randomly assigned to preoperative cisplatin 75 mg/m2 every 3 weeks for four doses or to doxorubicin 60 mg/m2 with cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m2 every 2 to 3 weeks for four doses, followed by surgery. Pathological responses were confirmed by central review. The primary comparison was pathological complete response (ypT0/is, N0); secondary objectives were combined residual cancer burden 0 or 1 and toxicity. The goal was to determine whether pathological complete response was at least 20% higher with cisplatin than with doxorubicin-cyclophosphamide.
inform.results: 118 patients were randomly assigned and 117 were included in the outcome analyses. Mean age was 42 years, range 24 to 73; clinical stage was I in 19%, II in 63% and III in 18%, and 45% had nodal involvement at baseline. Seventy percent had triple-negative disease, and clinical and tumour characteristics were well matched between arms. Pathological complete response was 18% with cisplatin and 26% with doxorubicin-cyclophosphamide, risk ratio 0.70 (90% CI 0.39 to 1.2), and residual cancer burden 0 or 1 was 33% versus 46%, risk ratio 0.73 (90% CI 0.50 to 1.1). Both regimens were generally well tolerated without unexpected toxicities.

iniparib-phase2.methods: Open-label phase 2 study comparing gemcitabine (1000 mg per square metre) and carboplatin (AUC 2) on days 1 and 8, with or without iniparib (5.6 mg per kilogram) on days 1, 4, 8 and 11, every 21 days, in 123 randomly assigned patients with metastatic triple-negative breast cancer. Primary end points were the rate of clinical benefit, objective response plus stable disease for 6 months or more, and safety; additional end points included objective response, progression-free survival and overall survival.
iniparib-phase2.results: Adding iniparib improved the rate of clinical benefit from 34% to 56% (P = 0.01) and the rate of overall response from 32% to 52% (P = 0.02). Median progression-free survival was prolonged from 3.6 to 5.9 months (hazard ratio for progression 0.59, P = 0.01) and median overall survival from 7.7 to 12.3 months (hazard ratio for death 0.57, P = 0.01). The most frequent grade 3 or 4 adverse events included neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, anaemia, fatigue or asthenia, leukopenia and increased alanine aminotransferase, with no significant difference in adverse events between the groups.

insema.methods: Prospective randomised non-inferiority trial. Patients with clinically node-negative invasive breast cancer staged T1 or T2 at 5 cm or less, scheduled for breast-conserving surgery, were randomly assigned 1:4 to omission of axillary surgery or to sentinel lymph node biopsy. Non-inferiority required a 5-year invasive disease-free survival of at least 85% and an upper confidence limit for the hazard ratio below 1.271.
insema.results: 5502 patients were randomised and 4858 analysed per protocol, 962 without axillary surgery and 3896 with sentinel node biopsy. At a median 73.6 months, 5-year invasive disease-free survival was 91.9% and 91.7%, hazard ratio 0.91 (0.73-1.14). Axillary recurrence was 1.0% against 0.3% and death 1.4% against 2.4%. Lymphoedema was less frequent and arm mobility better without axillary surgery.

intrathecal-trastuzumab-bonneau-phase-i.methods: This multicentre phase I dose-escalation study gave intrathecal trastuzumab once weekly for at least 4 weeks at dose levels of 30, 60, 100 and 150 mg to patients with meningeal carcinomatosis from HER2-positive breast cancer. The maximum tolerated dose was defined by achieving an intra-cerebrospinal fluid trastuzumab concentration close to a conventional therapeutic plasma concentration of 30 mg/L and by dose-limiting toxicity. Cerebrospinal fluid was sampled before each injection for pharmacokinetics. Sixteen patients were treated.
intrathecal-trastuzumab-bonneau-phase-i.results: No dose-limiting toxicity was observed. Eleven patients had no toxicity attributed to intrathecal trastuzumab. At 60 mg and above, minor attributed toxicities were headache in 2 patients, nausea in 2, vomiting in 1, cervical pain in 1 and peripheral neuropathy in 1. Two patients had immediate headache or vomiting. Mean residual cerebrospinal fluid trastuzumab concentration at the 150 mg level was 27.9 mg/L. Three patients had a clinical response, seven had stable disease and four had progressive disease.

intrathecal-trastuzumab-kumthekar-phase-.methods: This multicentre combined phase I/II study enrolled 34 patients with HER2-positive leptomeningeal disease to determine the maximum tolerated dose of intrathecal trastuzumab and its efficacy. Any HER2-positive histology was allowed in phase I, while phase II was limited to HER2-positive breast cancer. Cerebrospinal fluid pharmacokinetics were sampled during treatment.
intrathecal-trastuzumab-kumthekar-phase-.results: Intrathecal trastuzumab was well tolerated, with one dose-limiting toxicity of grade 4 arachnoiditis at 80 mg twice weekly, the dose taken forward as the recommended phase II dose. Among 26 patients evaluated at 80 mg, 5 (19.2%) had a partial response, 13 (50.0%) stable disease and 8 (30.8%) progressive disease. Median overall survival was 8.3 months at the phase II dose and 10.5 months in phase II breast cancer patients. Cerebrospinal fluid concentrations stayed stable with repeated dosing.

intrathecal-trastuzumab-oberkampf-phase-.methods: This phase II study gave weekly intrathecal trastuzumab 150 mg, the recommended dose from a preceding phase I dose-escalation study, to patients with HER2-positive breast cancer and leptomeningeal metastasis. The primary endpoint was clinical neurologic progression-free survival related to leptomeningeal disease after 8 weeks. Overall survival, toxicity and quality of life were secondary endpoints. Nineteen patients were enrolled.
intrathecal-trastuzumab-oberkampf-phase-.results: Of the 19 patients enrolled, 16 (84%) had concomitant brain metastases and 15 of these had received prior brain radiotherapy. All had received at least one line of systemic anti-HER2 therapy. At 8 weeks, 14 patients (74%) were free of neurological progression. Median leptomeningeal-related progression-free survival was 5.9 months and median overall survival was 7.9 months. Global health-related quality of life on the QLQ-C30 and BN20 scales appeared preserved, and no toxicity above grade 3 was observed.

ipatunity130-cohort-a.methods: In cohort A of this randomised double-blind placebo-controlled phase III trial, taxane-eligible patients with PIK3CA, AKT1 or PTEN-altered measurable advanced triple-negative breast cancer and no prior chemotherapy for advanced disease were randomised 2:1 to ipatasertib 400 mg on days 1 to 21 or placebo, both with paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 on days 1, 8 and 15, every 28 days until progression or unacceptable toxicity. The primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival.
ipatunity130-cohort-a.results: Between February 2018 and April 2020, 255 patients were randomised, 168 to ipatasertib and 87 to placebo. Progression-free survival did not differ, hazard ratio 1.02 (95% CI 0.71 to 1.45), median 7.4 versus 6.1 months. Overall survival did not differ, hazard ratio 1.08 (95% CI 0.73 to 1.58), median 24.4 versus 24.9 months. Ipatasertib caused more grade 3 or higher diarrhoea (9% versus 2%) and more dose reductions (39% versus 14%).

ispy2.methods: Multicenter platform trial of women with operable clinical stage 2 or 3 breast cancer, no prior surgery or systemic therapy, and primary tumours 2.5 cm or larger. Participants were adaptively randomised within molecular subtypes to one of several investigational regimens or control therapy from March 2010 through 2016. Treatment was taxane with or without an investigational agent or combination, followed by doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide. Measures were pathologic complete response and 3-year event-free and distant recurrence-free survival.
ispy2.results: Of 950 participants with median age 49 years, 330 (34.7%) achieved pathologic complete response. Three-year event-free survival and distant recurrence-free survival for those patients were both 95%. Hazard ratios for pathologic complete response versus no pathologic complete response were 0.19 for event-free survival (95% CI 0.12-0.31) and 0.21 for distant recurrence-free survival (0.13-0.34). These were similar across molecular subtypes, ranging from 0.14 to 0.18 for event-free survival and 0.10 to 0.20 for distant recurrence-free survival.

ispy2-pembro.methods: I-SPY2 is an ongoing open-label, multicenter, adaptively randomised phase 2 platform trial in high-risk stage II or III breast cancer, with standard neoadjuvant chemotherapy as the common control arm. Patients with ERBB2-negative breast cancer were eligible for randomisation to pembrolizumab between November 2015 and November 2016. They received taxane- and anthracycline-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy with or without four cycles of pembrolizumab, followed by definitive surgery. The primary end point was pathologic complete response.
ispy2-pembro.results: Of 250 women in the final analysis, 181 were randomised to standard control chemotherapy and 69 to pembrolizumab with weekly paclitaxel followed by doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide, 40 hormone receptor-positive and 29 triple-negative. Pembrolizumab graduated in all three biomarker signatures. Final estimated pathologic complete response rates were 44% versus 17% in ERBB2-negative disease, 30% versus 13% in hormone receptor-positive ERBB2-negative disease, and 60% versus 22% in triple-negative disease. Thyroid abnormalities occurred in 13.0% and adrenal insufficiency in 8.7%.

italian-tamoxifen-prevention.methods: From October 1992 to December 1997, 5408 otherwise healthy women who had undergone hysterectomy were randomly assigned in a double-blind manner to tamoxifen 20 mg daily or placebo for 5 years. Rates of breast cancer and other events in the two groups were compared by risk ratios with 95% confidence intervals.
italian-tamoxifen-prevention.results: After 11 years of follow-up, 136 women developed breast cancer, 74 on placebo and 62 on tamoxifen (RR 0.84, 95% CI 0.60 to 1.17; annual rates 2.48 and 2.07 per 1000 women-years). Rates were similar among women who had had bilateral oophorectomy and women at low risk of hormone receptor-positive disease, but much lower with tamoxifen among women at high risk (6.26 vs 1.50 per 1000 women-years, RR 0.24, 0.10 to 0.59). During treatment, tamoxifen caused more hot flashes (RR 1.78), vaginal discharge (RR 3.44) and urinary disturbances (RR 1.52) and fewer headaches (RR 0.68). Hypertriglyceridaemia (RR 4.33), thromboembolic events (RR 1.63) and cardiac arrhythmia or atrial fibrillation (RR 1.73) were also more frequent with tamoxifen.

javelin-solid-tumor.methods: Phase 1 trial (JAVELIN Solid Tumor) in which patients with metastatic breast cancer refractory to or progressing after standard-of-care therapy received avelumab, a PD-L1 inhibitor, intravenously at 10 mg/kg every 2 weeks. Tumours were assessed every 6 weeks by RECIST 1.1 and adverse events graded by NCI-CTCAE 4.0. Membrane PD-L1 expression was assessed by immunohistochemistry (Dako PD-L1 IHC 73-10 pharmDx).
javelin-solid-tumor.results: 168 patients with metastatic breast cancer, 58 with triple-negative disease, were treated for 2 to 50 weeks and followed for 6 to 15 months, after a median of three prior therapies for metastatic or locally advanced disease. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 13.7%, including two treatment-related deaths. The confirmed objective response rate was 3.0% overall (one complete and four partial responses) and 5.2% in triple-negative disease. Response was higher with PD-L1-positive than PD-L1-negative tumour-associated immune cells, 16.7% against 1.6% overall and 22.2% against 2.6% in triple-negative disease.

jcog1017.methods: Patients with de novo stage IV breast cancer were enrolled at a first registration and received systemic therapy according to clinical subtype. Those without progression after 3 months of primary systemic therapy were randomly assigned 1:1 to systemic therapy alone (arm A) or primary tumour resection plus systemic therapy (arm B). The primary endpoint was overall survival, and secondary endpoints included local relapse-free survival.
jcog1017.results: 570 patients were enrolled between May 2011 and May 2018, and 407 were randomised, 205 to arm A and 202 to arm B. At a median follow-up of 60 months the difference in overall survival was not statistically significant (hazard ratio 0.86, 90% CI 0.69 to 1.07, one-sided p=0.13), with median overall survival of 69 months in arm A and 75 months in arm B. In subgroup analyses resection was associated with improved overall survival in premenopausal patients and in those with single-organ metastasis. Local relapse-free survival was longer in arm B, median 63 versus 20 months (hazard ratio 0.42, 95% CI 0.33 to 0.53, p<0.0001). There were no treatment-related deaths.

jcog1204.methods: Randomised phase III trial of whether intensive follow-up is superior to standard follow-up for overall survival in high-risk breast cancer, defined by an expected recurrence rate of over 30% within 5 years after surgery. The intensive group undergoes physical examination, bone scintigraphy, chest and abdominal computed tomography, brain magnetic resonance imaging or computed tomography and frequent tumour marker evaluations. The standard group undergoes physical examination at the same frequency, with tumour markers once a year. Mammography once a year is planned for both groups. The primary endpoint is overall survival. Accrual started in November 2013, with 1700 patients to be enrolled over 3 years and followed for 7 years after accrual closes.

jlgk0901.methods: This prospective observational study at 23 Japanese facilities enrolled patients with one to ten newly diagnosed brain metastases, largest tumour under 10 mL and 3 cm and total volume at most 15 mL, with Karnofsky performance status 70 or higher. Stereotactic radiosurgery was given without whole-brain radiotherapy, 22 Gy at the periphery for tumours under 4 mL and 20 Gy for those of 4 to 10 mL. The primary endpoint was overall survival, with a non-inferiority margin of 1.30.
jlgk0901.results: Between March 2009 and February 2012, 1194 eligible patients were enrolled. Median overall survival was 13.9 months in 455 patients with one tumour, 10.8 months in 531 with two to four tumours and 10.8 months in 208 with five to ten tumours. Survival did not differ between the two multiple-tumour groups, hazard ratio 0.97 (95% CI 0.81 to 1.18, p = 0.78). Radiosurgery-induced adverse events occurred in 101 patients (8%), and four patients died.

jpbo-abemaciclib-cns-study.methods: Nonrandomised phase II study in four subtype specific cohorts. Cohort A was hormone receptor positive HER2 negative brain metastases, cohort B hormone receptor positive HER2 positive brain metastases, cohort C leptomeningeal metastases, cohort D brain metastases undergoing surgical resection. Abemaciclib 200 mg twice daily was given as monotherapy or with endocrine therapy, or 150 mg twice daily with trastuzumab. Cohorts A and B used a Simon two stage design.
jpbo-abemaciclib-cns-study.results: Cohort A (58 patients) had 3 confirmed responders, an intracranial objective response rate of 5.2 percent and a clinical benefit rate of 24 percent, with median overall survival 12.5 months. Cohort B (27 patients) had no confirmed intracranial responses and a clinical benefit rate of 11 percent, with median overall survival 10.1 months. Cohort C (10 patients) had one complete parenchymal response. In cohort D, unbound brain drug concentrations exceeded the CDK4 and CDK6 targets 96 fold and 19 fold.

js001-tnbc.methods: Phase 1 open-label study (NCT02838823) of JS001, a humanised IgG4 PD-1 antibody, to evaluate safety, tolerability and antitumour activity in advanced triple-negative breast cancer refractory to standard systemic therapy. The design was a 3 + 3 dose escalation with planned cohorts at 1, 3 and 10 mg/kg every 2 weeks, followed by dose expansion at 3 mg/kg.
js001-tnbc.results: From August 2016 to October 2017, 20 heavily pretreated patients were enrolled into three dose cohorts (6 at 1 mg/kg, 8 at 3 mg/kg and 6 at 10 mg/kg). No dose-limiting toxicity was observed and no maximum tolerated dose was reached; no adverse events were grade 4 or 5, and treatment-related grade 3 events (15%) were hyponatraemia, rash and bronchospasm. Among 20 evaluable patients the objective response rate was 5%, one partial response at 10 mg/kg in a tumour with strong PD-L1 staining, continuing at 24 months, and six had stable disease, a disease control rate of 35%. Median progression-free survival was 1.8 months (95% CI 1.4 to 4.6). In the 45% with PD-L1 of 1% or more, response was 11.1% and disease control 22.2%.

kaitlin.methods: Phase III study in adults with excised HER2-positive early breast cancer that was node-positive, or node-negative, hormone receptor-negative with tumour greater than 2.0 cm. After surgery patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to anthracycline-based chemotherapy for three or four cycles followed by 18 cycles of trastuzumab emtansine plus pertuzumab, or by taxane for three or four cycles plus trastuzumab plus pertuzumab. Coprimary end points were invasive disease-free survival in the node-positive and overall intention-to-treat populations.
kaitlin.results: Median follow-up was 57.1 months for taxane plus trastuzumab plus pertuzumab (n=918) and 57.0 months for trastuzumab emtansine plus pertuzumab (n=928). Invasive disease-free survival did not differ in the node-positive population (n=1658, stratified hazard ratio 0.97, 95% CI 0.71 to 1.32) or the overall population (n=1846, stratified hazard ratio 0.98, 0.72 to 1.32). Three-year invasive disease-free survival was 94.2% with the taxane arm and 93.1% with the conjugate arm. Treatment completion was 88.4% versus 65.0%.

kamilla.methods: Ongoing single arm phase IIIb study of trastuzumab emtansine in HER2 positive locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer previously treated with HER2 targeted therapy and chemotherapy. Patients received trastuzumab emtansine 3.6 mg/kg intravenously every 3 weeks until unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal of consent, or progression. This post hoc exploratory analysis assessed tumour response and outcomes in patients with baseline brain metastases, using best overall response rate, clinical benefit rate, progression free survival, overall survival and safety.
kamilla.results: Of 2002 treated patients, 398 had baseline brain metastases. In 126 with measurable brain metastases the best overall response rate was 21.4 percent and the clinical benefit rate 42.9 percent. Lesion diameter sums fell by at least 30 percent in 42.9 percent, and in 49.3 percent of 67 patients without prior brain radiotherapy. Across the 398 patients, median progression free survival was 5.5 months and median overall survival 18.9 months. Nervous system adverse events were commoner with brain metastases.

kate2.methods: Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 study at 68 centres in nine countries across Asia, Australia, North America and western Europe, testing whether atezolizumab potentiates the anticancer immunity and HER2-directed cytotoxic activity of trastuzumab emtansine. Eligible patients were adults with performance status 0 or 1 and centrally confirmed, measurable, HER2-positive advanced breast cancer previously treated with trastuzumab and a taxane. Patients were randomly assigned 2:1 to trastuzumab emtansine 3.6 mg/kg plus atezolizumab 1200 mg or trastuzumab emtansine plus placebo, all given intravenously every 3 weeks. Randomisation used a permuted block scheme stratified by PD-L1 status, world region and liver metastases, and patients, investigators and study team were masked. The primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival in the intention-to-treat population.
kate2.results: Between September 2016 and August 2017, 330 patients were screened and 202 were randomly allocated, 133 to atezolizumab and 69 to placebo. Treatment assignment was unmasked in December 2017 on the recommendation of the independent data monitoring committee because of futility and a numerically higher frequency of adverse events with atezolizumab, and that date became the clinical cutoff for the primary analysis. Median follow-up was 8.5 months with atezolizumab and 8.4 months with placebo. Median progression-free survival was 8.2 months (95% CI 5.8-10.7) versus 6.8 months (95% CI 4.0-11.1), stratified hazard ratio 0.82 (95% CI 0.55-1.23; p=0.33). The commonest grade 3 or worse adverse events were thrombocytopenia, in 17 (13%) of 132 patients given atezolizumab versus three (4%) of 68 given placebo, and raised aspartate aminotransferase; serious adverse events occurred in 43 (33%) versus 13 (19%), and one patient given atezolizumab died of treatment-related haemophagocytic syndrome.

katherine.methods: Phase 3, open-label trial in patients with HER2-positive early breast cancer who were found to have residual invasive disease in the breast or axilla at surgery after neoadjuvant therapy containing a taxane, with or without anthracycline, and trastuzumab. Patients were randomly assigned to adjuvant trastuzumab emtansine or trastuzumab for 14 cycles. The primary end point was invasive disease-free survival.
katherine.results: At the interim analysis of 1486 randomly assigned patients, 743 per group, invasive disease or death had occurred in 91 patients (12.2%) on trastuzumab emtansine and 165 (22.2%) on trastuzumab. Freedom from invasive disease at 3 years was 88.3% versus 77.0%, hazard ratio 0.50 (95% CI 0.39 to 0.64, P<0.001). The survival update at 8.4 years median follow-up reported 7-year overall survival of 89.1% versus 84.4%, hazard ratio 0.66 (0.51 to 0.87, P=0.003).

keynote-b49.methods: Phase 3 placebo-controlled trial in locally recurrent inoperable or metastatic hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer with a PD-L1 combined positive score of 1 or more. Participants had had prior endocrine therapy and were candidates for first-line chemotherapy. They were randomised to pembrolizumab 200 mg or placebo every 3 weeks, each with chemotherapy. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival per RECIST v1.1 by blinded independent central review in participants with a combined positive score of 1 or more. Overall survival in the same population was the key secondary endpoint. Progression-free and overall survival at a combined positive score of 10 or more, and safety, were secondary endpoints. The sample size was reduced by protocol amendment because of low PD-L1 prevalence.
keynote-b49.results: 342 participants were randomised. At the interim analysis, at a median follow-up of 29.1 months, the hazard ratio for progression-free survival was 0.74 (95% CI 0.58 to 0.95, P = 0.0089, significance criterion met), favouring pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy over placebo plus chemotherapy. Median progression-free survival was 6.7 (6.2 to 8.3) versus 6.0 (4.2 to 8.1) months. At a combined positive score of 10 or more, the hazard ratio for progression-free survival numerically favoured pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy, 0.59 (95% CI 0.35 to 0.98). At the final analysis, at a median follow-up of 34.9 months, the hazard ratio for overall survival was 1.04 (95% CI 0.81 to 1.33, P = 0.6185). Median overall survival was 21.0 (18.9 to 22.9) versus 22.2 (17.6 to 26.3) months. Grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events occurred in 38% of participants given pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy and 33% of those given placebo plus chemotherapy. Treatment-related adverse events led 11% and 5% to discontinue treatment.

keynote012.methods: KEYNOTE-012 was a multicentre, nonrandomised phase Ib trial of single-agent pembrolizumab 10 mg/kg intravenously every 2 weeks in patients with advanced PD-L1-positive (expression in stroma or in at least 1% of tumour cells by immunohistochemistry) triple-negative breast, gastric, urothelial and head and neck cancer. This report focuses on the triple-negative breast cancer cohort.
keynote012.results: Of 111 patients with triple-negative breast cancer whose tumours were screened, 58.6% were PD-L1-positive. Thirty-two women, median age 50.5 years, were enrolled and assessed for safety and antitumour activity, and received a median of five doses. Common toxicities were mild (arthralgia, fatigue, myalgia, nausea); five patients (15.6%) had grade 3 or higher toxicity and there was one treatment-related death. Among 27 patients evaluable for antitumour activity the overall response rate was 18.5%, the median time to response 17.9 weeks (range 7.3 to 32.4) and the median duration of response not yet reached (range 15.0 to at least 47.3 weeks).

keynote086.methods: Phase II study of pembrolizumab as second or later line of treatment in cohort A. Eligible patients had centrally confirmed metastatic triple-negative breast cancer, at least one systemic therapy for metastatic disease, prior anthracycline and taxane in any disease setting, and progression on or after the most recent therapy. Patients received pembrolizumab 200 mg intravenously every 3 weeks for up to 2 years. Primary end points were objective response rate in the total and PD-L1-positive populations, and safety; secondary end points included duration of response, disease control rate, progression-free survival and overall survival.
keynote086.results: All 170 enrolled patients were women; 61.8% had PD-L1-positive tumours and 43.5% had received three or more previous lines for metastatic disease. Objective response was 5.3% (95% CI 2.7 to 9.9) in the total and 5.7% (2.4 to 12.2) in the PD-L1-positive populations, and disease control 7.6% and 9.5%. Median duration of response was not reached. Median progression-free survival was 2.0 months (95% CI 1.9 to 2.0) and median overall survival 9.0 months (95% CI 7.6 to 11.2). Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 103 patients (60.6%), grade 3 or 4 in 22 (12.9%), with no deaths due to adverse events.

keynote119.methods: Randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial at 150 centres in 31 countries. Patients aged 18 years or older with centrally confirmed metastatic triple-negative breast cancer, ECOG status 0 or 1, one or two previous systemic treatments for metastatic disease, and prior anthracycline or taxane were assigned 1:1 to pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks for 35 cycles or investigator's choice of capecitabine, eribulin, gemcitabine, or vinorelbine. Primary endpoints were overall survival by PD-L1 combined positive score and in all participants.
keynote119.results: 622 of 1098 assessed patients were randomly assigned, 312 to pembrolizumab and 310 to chemotherapy. Median follow-up was about 31.4 months. Median overall survival with CPS 10 or more was 12.7 versus 11.6 months (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.57 to 1.06; p=0.057). With CPS 1 or more it was 10.7 versus 10.2 months (HR 0.86, 0.69 to 1.06; p=0.073). Overall it was 9.9 versus 10.8 months (HR 0.97, 0.82 to 1.15).

keynote355.methods: Patients with previously untreated locally recurrent inoperable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer were randomly assigned 2:1 to pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks plus investigator's choice of chemotherapy (nab-paclitaxel, paclitaxel, or gemcitabine-carboplatin) or to placebo plus chemotherapy. The primary endpoints were progression-free survival, reported previously, and overall survival among patients with a PD-L1 combined positive score of 10 or more, those with a score of 1 or more, and the intention-to-treat population. Safety was also assessed.
keynote355.results: 847 patients were randomised, 566 to pembrolizumab-chemotherapy and 281 to placebo-chemotherapy. Median follow-up was 44.1 months. In the CPS-10 subgroup median overall survival was 23.0 versus 16.1 months (HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.55 to 0.95; P=0.0185). In the CPS-1 subgroup it was 17.6 versus 16.0 months (HR 0.86, 0.72 to 1.04; P=0.1125). In the intention-to-treat population it was 17.2 versus 15.5 months (HR 0.89, 0.76 to 1.05).

keynote522.methods: Phase 3 trial. Patients with previously untreated stage II or III triple-negative breast cancer were randomly assigned 2:1 to four cycles of pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks plus paclitaxel and carboplatin (784 patients) or placebo plus the same chemotherapy (390 patients), then four further cycles with doxorubicin-cyclophosphamide or epirubicin-cyclophosphamide. After definitive surgery patients received adjuvant pembrolizumab or placebo for up to nine cycles. Primary endpoints were pathological complete response and event-free survival.
keynote522.results: Among the first 602 randomised patients, pathological complete response was 64.8% with pembrolizumab-chemotherapy and 51.2% with placebo-chemotherapy, a difference of 13.6 percentage points (95% CI 5.4 to 21.8; P<0.001). After median follow-up of 15.5 months, 58 of 784 patients (7.4%) versus 46 of 390 (11.8%) had progression precluding surgery, recurrence, second primary, or death (HR 0.63, 0.43 to 0.93). The 2024 overall survival report gave 60-month overall survival of 86.6% versus 81.7% (P=0.002).

keynote756.methods: In this double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 study, patients with untreated ER-positive, HER2-negative grade 3 high-risk invasive breast cancer (T1c-2 at least 2 cm cN1-2, or T3-4 cN0-2) were assigned 1:1 to neoadjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg or placebo every 3 weeks with weekly paclitaxel for 12 weeks, then four cycles of doxorubicin or epirubicin with cyclophosphamide. After surgery they received adjuvant pembrolizumab or placebo for nine cycles with endocrine therapy. Dual primary endpoints were pathological complete response and event-free survival.
keynote756.results: 635 patients were assigned to pembrolizumab-chemotherapy and 643 to placebo-chemotherapy. At the prespecified first interim analysis the pathological complete response rate was 24.3% (95% CI 21.0 to 27.8) versus 15.6% (95% CI 12.8 to 18.6), a treatment difference of 8.5 percentage points (95% CI 4.2 to 12.8; P=0.00005). Event-free survival was not mature. During the neoadjuvant phase, grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 52.5% and 46.4% of patients.

kristine.methods: Randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial at 68 centres in Asia, Europe, the USA, and Canada. Patients aged 18 years or older with centrally confirmed HER2-positive stage II-III operable breast cancer larger than 2 cm, ECOG status 0-1, and left ventricular ejection fraction of at least 55% were assigned 1:1 to six neoadjuvant 3-weekly cycles of trastuzumab emtansine plus pertuzumab or of docetaxel, carboplatin, and trastuzumab plus pertuzumab. The primary endpoint was pathological complete response (ypT0/is ypN0).
kristine.results: 444 patients were randomly assigned, 223 to trastuzumab emtansine plus pertuzumab and 221 to docetaxel, carboplatin, and trastuzumab plus pertuzumab. Pathological complete response occurred in 99 patients (44.4%) versus 123 (55.7%), a difference of -11.3 percentage points (95% CI -20.5 to -2.0; p=0.016). Grade 3-4 adverse events occurred in 29 of 223 (13%) versus 141 of 219 (64%). The 3-year report found a higher event-free survival event risk with trastuzumab emtansine plus pertuzumab (HR 2.61, 1.36 to 4.98).

landscape.methods: Single arm, open label, multicentre phase 2 study. Eligible patients had HER2 positive metastatic breast cancer with brain metastases not previously treated with whole brain radiotherapy, capecitabine or lapatinib. Treatment was given in 21 day cycles of lapatinib 1250 mg orally daily and capecitabine 2000 mg/m2 orally on days 1 to 14. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients with a confirmed objective central nervous system response. Efficacy analyses included all patients who received study drugs and were assessable.
landscape.results: 45 patients were enrolled between April 2009 and August 2010, and 44 were assessable, with median follow up 21.2 months. 29 patients had an objective central nervous system response, 65.9 percent (95% CI 50.1 to 79.5), all partial. Grade 3 or 4 treatment related adverse events occurred in 22 of 45 patients, most often diarrhoea and hand foot syndrome, each in 9. 14 patients had a severe adverse event and 4 stopped for toxicity. No toxic deaths occurred.

lapatinib-eap.methods: The Lapatinib Expanded Access Program was designed to provide lapatinib plus capecitabine to patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer who had previously received an anthracycline, a taxane and trastuzumab and had no other treatment options. It opened globally and enrolled until lapatinib was approved in each participating country. Patients were assessed for progression-free and overall survival and monitored for serious adverse events.
lapatinib-eap.results: By 30 September 2008, 4283 patients from 45 countries had enrolled, with a median treatment duration of 24.7 weeks. The commonest drug-related serious adverse events were diarrhoea (9.7%), vomiting (4.3%) and nausea (2.4%), mainly grade 3 or higher; decreased left ventricular ejection fraction (0.5%), interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis (0.2%) and serious hepatobiliary events (0.4%) were rare. Median progression-free and overall survival were 21.1 (95% CI 20.1 to 22.3) and 39.6 (37.7 to 40.7) weeks in 4006 patients, longer in those without prior capecitabine.

lccc1025.methods: Phase II study in patients with progressive HER2-positive breast cancer brain metastases, opened on the rationale that two-thirds of such metastases show activation of the PI3K/mTOR pathway driving resistance to anti-HER2 therapy. Patients received everolimus, a brain-permeable mTOR inhibitor, with trastuzumab and vinorelbine. The primary endpoint was intracranial response rate. Secondary objectives were CNS clinical benefit rate, extracranial response rate, time to progression, overall survival, and targeted sequencing of tumours from enrolled patients. A two-stage design was used to distinguish an intracranial response rate of 5% from one of 20%.
lccc1025.results: 32 patients were evaluable for toxicity and 26 for efficacy. The intracranial response rate was 4%, a single partial response. CNS clinical benefit rate was 27% at 6 months and 65% at 3 months, median intracranial time to progression was 3.9 months (95% CI 2.2 to 5) and overall survival was 12.2 months (95% CI 0.6 to 20.2). Grade 3 to 4 toxicities included neutropenia in 41%, anemia in 16% and stomatitis in 16%. Mutations in TP53 and PIK3CA were common in the brain metastases, but mutations in the PI3K/mTOR pathway were not associated with response; ERBB2 amplification was higher in brain metastases than in the primary tumour, and ERBB2 amplification in the primary trended toward worse overall survival.

leap-005.methods: Triple-negative breast cancer cohort of the multicohort, open-label, single-arm phase 2 LEAP-005 study of lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab in advanced solid tumours. Eligible patients had metastatic or unresectable triple-negative breast cancer with progression after one or two lines of therapy and received lenvatinib 20 mg daily plus pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks for up to 35 cycles. The primary end points were objective response rate by RECIST 1.1 and safety; duration of response, progression-free survival and overall survival were secondary.
leap-005.results: Thirty-one patients were enrolled. The objective response rate was 23% (95% CI 10% to 41%) by investigator and 32% (17% to 51%) by blinded independent central review, and by central review 50% with a PD-L1 combined positive score of 10 or more (n = 8) and 27% below 10 (n = 22). Median duration of response by central review was 12.1 months, median progression-free survival 5.1 months (1.9 to 11.8) and median overall survival 11.4 months (4.1 to 21.7). Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 94% (grade 3 in 52%, none grade 4), and one patient died of a treatment-related subarachnoid haemorrhage.

liber.methods: Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase III trial. Postmenopausal women aged 40 to 70 years carrying a germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation were randomly allocated to 5 years of letrozole 2.5 mg per day or placebo. Women with a prior breast cancer in remission for more than 5 years were eligible, to assess the risk of a second cancer. Randomisation was stratified by BRCA1 versus BRCA2, previous bilateral oophorectomy and prior breast cancer. The primary endpoint was the 5-year incidence of invasive breast cancer.
liber.results: Between 2008 and 2013, 170 women were randomised, 86 to placebo and 84 to letrozole. Adherence at 5 years was 73.5% with placebo and 76.7% with letrozole. After a median follow-up of 72.7 months, the 5-year incidence of invasive breast cancer was 13.1% with placebo and 7.8% with letrozole (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.29 to 1.66, p = 0.416). Safety events and quality of life did not differ statistically between the arms.

lidocaine-dyspareunia.methods: Postmenopausal breast cancer survivors not using estrogen, with moderate or severe dyspareunia, were examined to locate genital tenderness and randomised to a double-blind application of topical aqueous 4% lidocaine or normal saline for 3 minutes to the tender areas. Changes in reported numerical rating scale values were compared by the Wilcoxon rank-sum test.
lidocaine-dyspareunia.results: Forty-nine women aged 37-69 years had a median coital pain score of 8 of 10. All had tenderness in the vulvar vestibule; one also had vaginal mucosal tenderness and two pelvic floor myalgia. All had vulvovaginal atrophy. Lidocaine reduced vestibular tenderness at all painful sites: pain at the worst site went from a median of 5 to 0, against 6 to 4 with saline (P < .001). After lidocaine, speculum placement was not tender in the 47 without myalgia or vaginal mucosal tenderness.

litton-neoadjuvant-talazoparib.methods: Patients with a known germline BRCA pathogenic variant and operable breast cancer, an invasive tumour of 1 cm or larger, were eligible; HER2-positive tumours were excluded. Twenty patients underwent a pretreatment biopsy and 6 months of once-daily oral talazoparib 1 mg, followed by definitive surgery, with adjuvant therapy at the physician's discretion. The primary end point was residual cancer burden (RCB); with 20 patients the RCB-0 plus RCB-I response rate could be estimated with a 95% CI of half-width less than 20%.
litton-neoadjuvant-talazoparib.results: Twenty patients were enrolled from August 2016 to September 2017, median age 38 years; 16 carried BRCA1 and 4 BRCA2 variants, 15 had triple-negative and 5 hormone receptor-positive disease, and clinical stage was I in 5, II in 12 and III in 3. One patient chose chemotherapy before surgery and was not included in the RCB analyses. The RCB-0 (pathological complete response) rate was 53% and the RCB-0/I rate 63%. Eight patients (40%) had grade 3 anaemia requiring transfusion, three had grade 3 neutropenia and one grade 4 thrombocytopenia, and nine needed dose reduction.

ljm716.methods: Open-label dose-finding phase 1 study of LJM716, an anti-HER3 monoclonal antibody, with dose escalation followed by expansion in patients with squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck or oesophagus and HER2-overexpressing metastatic breast or gastric cancer. During dose escalation patients received LJM716 intravenously once weekly or every two weeks in 28-day cycles, guided by an adaptive Bayesian logistic regression model. The primary objective was the maximum tolerated dose and/or recommended dose for expansion and schedule; secondary objectives were safety, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics and preliminary antitumour activity.
ljm716.results: Patients received LJM716 3 to 40 mg/kg weekly or 20 mg/kg every two weeks (54 patients; 36 at 40 mg/kg weekly). No dose-limiting toxicities occurred during dose escalation, and one patient had two (grade 3 diarrhoea and hypokalaemia) in expansion. The recommended dose for expansion was 40 mg/kg weekly. One patient with gastric cancer had an unconfirmed partial response and 17 of 54 had stable disease, two lasting over 30 weeks. Phospho-HER3 was down-modulated in paired tumour samples.

llombart-letrozole-maximum-response.methods: Phase 2 multicentre, open-label trial of letrozole over a preoperative period of 4 months to 1 year as primary systemic therapy in postmenopausal patients over 65 with ER/PgR-positive operable breast cancer, recruited in four centres. The primary endpoint was the optimal duration of treatment, defined as the time required to attain the maximum response by clinical palpation.
llombart-letrozole-maximum-response.results: Seventy patients were recruited, median age 79 years (66 to 91) and median tumour size 35 mm (25 to 100 mm). No severe adverse events were reported. Of 56 patients evaluable for the primary objective, 43 (76.8%) achieved an objective response, 29 (51.8%) partial and 14 (25.0%) complete. The median time to objective response was 3.9 months (95% CI 3.3 to 4.5) and the median time to maximum response 4.2 months (4.0 to 4.5).

lord.methods: Randomised international multicentre open-label phase III non-inferiority trial led by the Dutch Breast Cancer Research Group and the EORTC. It compares standard treatment with active surveillance in 1240 women aged 45 years or older with asymptomatic, screen-detected, pure low-grade ductal carcinoma in situ diagnosed on vacuum-assisted biopsy of microcalcifications. Both arms are monitored with annual digital mammography for 10 years. The primary endpoint is the 10-year ipsilateral invasive breast cancer free percentage.

loris.methods: Phase III trial of surgery versus active monitoring in women with screen-detected or asymptomatic low grade ductal carcinoma in situ, or intermediate grade disease with low grade features. It is designed to determine whether such women can be managed by active monitoring rather than by surgical treatment.

lotus.methods: Randomised, placebo controlled, double blind phase 2 trial at 44 hospitals in eight countries. Women aged 18 or older with measurable inoperable locally advanced or metastatic triple negative breast cancer untreated with systemic therapy were assigned 1:1 to intravenous paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 on days 1, 8 and 15 with either ipatasertib 400 mg or placebo daily on days 1 to 21 every 28 days, until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Stratification used prior therapy, chemotherapy free interval and PTEN status.
lotus.results: 124 patients were enrolled between September 2014 and February 2016, 62 to ipatasertib and 62 to placebo. Median follow up was 10.4 and 10.2 months. Median progression free survival was 6.2 versus 4.9 months, stratified hazard ratio 0.60 (p=0.037), and in 48 PTEN low patients 6.2 versus 3.7 months, hazard ratio 0.59 (p=0.18). Grade 3 or worse diarrhoea occurred in 14 of 61 ipatasertib patients and none on placebo. Serious adverse events occurred in 17 versus 9 patients.

ltmbc.methods: Randomised controlled trial of locoregional treatment in de novo metastatic breast cancer that had not progressed on systemic therapy. Patients were randomised to locoregional treatment or to continued systemic therapy. Locoregional treatment was a free-margin lumpectomy or mastectomy with axillary surgery, with or without adjuvant radiotherapy. All patients then received maintenance systemic therapy and were seen every 3 months. The primary endpoint was overall survival.
ltmbc.results: Between 2018 and 2023, 250 patients were randomly assigned, 158 to locoregional treatment and 92 to systemic therapy alone. The groups were similar in age and subtype. Two-year overall survival was 81% and five-year overall survival 43% in the whole cohort. Median time to death was 53 months (95% CI 45 to 61) with locoregional treatment and 55 months (44 to 66) with systemic therapy alone. The log-rank test showed no difference (p = 0.6). HER2-positive disease (HR 1.86, 95% CI 1.21 to 2.87) and lung metastasis (HR 1.5, 1.04 to 2.26) carried a higher risk of death.

lucitanib-phase1.methods: Open-label phase 1/2a study of lucitanib, an oral inhibitor of FGFR1-2, VEGFR1-3 and PDGFR alpha and beta, with dose escalation to determine the maximum tolerated dose, recommended dose and pharmacokinetics in advanced solid tumours, followed by dose expansion in patients who could benefit, with FGF-aberrant (FGFR1- or FGF3/4/19-amplified) or angiogenesis-sensitive tumours.
lucitanib-phase1.results: Doses from 5 to 30 mg were evaluated, with dose-limiting toxic effects from VEGF inhibition at 30 mg (one grade 4 depressed consciousness and two grade 3 thrombotic microangiopathy). The commonest adverse events were hypertension (91%), asthenia (42%) and proteinuria (57%), and the half-life was 31 to 40 hours. Seventy-six patients were included, all but one stage IV and 42% with more than three prior chemotherapy lines; 64 were assessable for response. In the angiogenesis-sensitive group the RECIST response rate was 26% (7 of 27) and progression-free survival 25 weeks. In assessable FGF-aberrant breast cancer, 6 of 12 (50%) had a partial response, with a median progression-free survival of 40.4 weeks for all treated patients.

lumina.methods: Prospective single-group cohort study. Women at least 55 years of age who had undergone breast-conserving surgery for T1N0, grade 1 or 2, luminal A breast cancer (estrogen receptor at least 1%, progesterone receptor above 20%, HER2-negative, Ki67 index 13.25% or less) and who received adjuvant endocrine therapy were enrolled after central Ki67 testing and did not receive radiotherapy. The primary outcome was local recurrence in the ipsilateral breast, with an acceptable 5-year cumulative incidence below 5%.
lumina.results: Of 740 registered patients, 500 eligible patients were enrolled. At 5 years after enrollment, local recurrence was reported in 2.3% of patients (90% CI 1.3 to 3.8; 95% CI 1.2 to 4.1), which met the prespecified boundary. Breast cancer occurred in the contralateral breast in 1.9% of patients (90% CI 1.1 to 3.2). Recurrence of any type was observed in 2.7% (90% CI 1.6 to 4.1).

lux-breast1.methods: Open-label phase 3 trial at 350 hospitals in 41 countries in female patients with HER2-overexpressing metastatic breast cancer who had progressed on or following adjuvant trastuzumab or first-line trastuzumab for metastatic disease. Patients were assigned 2:1 to oral afatinib 40 mg/day plus intravenous vinorelbine 25 mg/m2 per week, or to intravenous trastuzumab (2 mg/kg per week after a 4 mg/kg loading dose) plus vinorelbine, stratified by previous trastuzumab (adjuvant vs first line), hormone receptor status and region. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival in the intention-to-treat population.
lux-breast1.results: Between August 2010 and April 2013, 508 patients were enrolled, 339 to afatinib and 169 to trastuzumab. Recruitment was stopped on April 26, 2013, after a benefit-risk assessment by the independent data monitoring committee was unfavourable for the afatinib group. Median follow-up was 9.3 months. Median progression-free survival was 5.5 months with afatinib and 5.6 months with trastuzumab (hazard ratio 1.10, 95% CI 0.86 to 1.41, p=0.43). The most common drug-related grade 3 or higher adverse events were neutropenia (56% vs 60%), leucopenia (19% vs 20%) and diarrhoea (18% vs none).

m77001.methods: Randomised multicentre trial comparing first line trastuzumab plus docetaxel with docetaxel alone in patients with HER2 positive metastatic breast cancer. Patients were randomly assigned to six cycles of docetaxel 100 mg/m2 every 3 weeks, with or without trastuzumab given as a 4 mg/kg loading dose followed by 2 mg/kg weekly until disease progression.
m77001.results: 186 patients received at least one dose. Trastuzumab plus docetaxel was superior for overall response rate, 61 percent versus 34 percent (p=0.0002), median overall survival, 31.2 versus 22.7 months (p=0.0325), median time to progression, 11.7 versus 6.1 months (p=0.0001), median time to treatment failure, 9.8 versus 5.3 months (p=0.0001), and median duration of response, 11.7 versus 5.7 months (p=0.009). Grade 3 to 4 neutropenia occurred in 32 percent versus 22 percent and febrile neutropenia in 23 percent versus 17 percent.

ma-27.methods: Open label randomised phase III trial of 5 years of exemestane versus 5 years of anastrozole in postmenopausal women with hormone dependent early breast cancer. The two sided superiority design was powered to detect a 2.4 percent improvement with exemestane in 5 year event free survival. Secondary objectives were overall survival, distant disease free survival, incidence of contralateral new primary breast cancer, and safety.
ma-27.results: 7576 women with a median age of 64.1 years were enrolled. At median follow up 4.1 years, 4 year event free survival was 91 percent with exemestane and 91.2 percent with anastrozole, stratified hazard ratio 1.02 (95% CI 0.87 to 1.18, p=0.85). Distant disease free survival and disease specific survival were also similar. 31.6 percent of patients discontinued treatment for adverse effects, concomitant disease or refusal. Osteoporosis or osteopenia, hypertriglyceridaemia, vaginal bleeding and hypercholesterolaemia were less frequent with exemestane.

ma17.methods: Double-blind, placebo-controlled trial testing five years of letrozole in postmenopausal women with breast cancer who had completed five years of tamoxifen therapy. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival.
ma17.results: 5187 women were enrolled, with median follow-up of 2.4 years. At the first interim analysis there were 207 local or metastatic recurrences or new contralateral primary cancers, 75 in the letrozole group and 132 in the placebo group. Estimated four-year disease-free survival was 93% versus 87% (P<=0.001). 31 women taking letrozole and 42 taking placebo died (P=0.25). New osteoporosis was diagnosed in 5.8% versus 4.5% (P=0.07), with similar fracture rates.

ma17r.methods: Double-blind, placebo-controlled trial assessing extended use of letrozole for an additional 5 years after 5 years of aromatase-inhibitor therapy given up front or after tamoxifen. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival.
ma17r.results: 1918 women were enrolled. After median follow-up of 6.3 years there were 165 events of disease recurrence or contralateral breast cancer, 67 with letrozole and 98 with placebo, and 200 deaths, 100 in each group. Five-year disease-free survival was 95% versus 91% (HR 0.66; P=0.01). Five-year overall survival was 93% versus 94% (HR 0.97; P=0.83). Annual contralateral breast cancer incidence was 0.21% versus 0.49% (HR 0.42; P=0.007).

ma20.methods: Randomised trial in women with node-positive or high-risk node-negative breast cancer treated with breast-conserving surgery and adjuvant systemic therapy. Women were assigned to whole-breast irradiation plus regional nodal irradiation covering the internal mammary, supraclavicular, and axillary nodes, or to whole-breast irradiation alone. The primary outcome was overall survival. Secondary outcomes were disease-free survival, isolated locoregional disease-free survival, and distant disease-free survival.
ma20.results: 1832 women were assigned between March 2000 and February 2007, 916 to each group. Median follow-up was 9.5 years. At 10 years, overall survival was 82.8% with nodal irradiation and 81.8% with control (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.72 to 1.13; P=0.38). Disease-free survival was 82.0% versus 77.0% (HR 0.76, 0.61 to 0.94; P=0.01). Grade 2 or greater acute pneumonitis occurred in 1.2% versus 0.2% (P=0.01) and lymphedema in 8.4% versus 4.5% (P=0.001).

ma32.methods: Phase 3 randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial in Canada, Switzerland, the USA, and the UK. 3649 patients with high-risk nonmetastatic breast cancer receiving standard therapy were enrolled between August 2010 and March 2013 and randomised to oral metformin 850 mg twice a day (n=1824) or placebo twice a day (n=1825) for 5 years, stratified by hormone receptor status, body mass index, HER2 status, and any chemotherapy. The primary outcome was invasive disease-free survival in hormone receptor-positive disease.
ma32.results: Mean age was 52.4 years and 3643 patients (99.8%) were women. Futility was declared for ER/PgR-negative patients, so the primary analysis covered 2533 ER/PgR-positive patients followed for a median of 96.2 months. 465 of them had invasive disease-free survival events, at 2.78 versus 2.74 per 100 patient-years (HR 1.01, 95% CI 0.84 to 1.21; P=.93). Death rates were 1.46 versus 1.32 per 100 patient-years (HR 1.10, 0.86 to 1.41; P=.47).

ma5.methods: Between 1989 and 1993, 710 pre- and perimenopausal women with axillary node-positive breast cancer were randomly assigned to CEF (cyclophosphamide 75 mg/m2 orally days 1 to 14, epirubicin 60 mg/m2 and fluorouracil 500 mg/m2 intravenously days 1 and 8) or to CMF (cyclophosphamide 100 mg/m2 orally days 1 to 14, methotrexate 40 mg/m2 and fluorouracil 600 mg/m2 intravenously days 1 and 8). The original analysis at a median follow-up of 59 months had shown significantly better relapse-free and overall survival with CEF; this report updates the trial to a median follow-up of 10 years.
ma5.results: Ten-year relapse-free survival was 52% with CEF and 45% with CMF (hazard ratio for CMF against CEF 1.31, stratified log-rank P = .007). Ten-year overall survival was 62% and 58% (hazard ratio 1.18, P = .085). Acute leukaemia rates were unchanged from the original report, and congestive heart failure occurred in four patients (1.1%) given CEF and one (0.3%) given CMF.

mahajan-postoperative-srs-trial.methods: Randomised controlled phase 3 trial at a single tertiary cancer centre in the USA. Eligible patients were older than 3 years, had a Karnofsky Performance Score of 70 or higher, could have an MRI, and had complete resection of one to three brain metastases with a cavity of 4 cm or less. Patients were assigned 1:1 to stereotactic radiosurgery of the cavity within 30 days of surgery or to observation, stratified by primary tumour histology, metastasis size and number.
mahajan-postoperative-srs-trial.results: 132 patients were randomly assigned between August 2009 and February 2016, 68 to observation and 64 to stereotactic radiosurgery, with 128 analysed after four were found ineligible. Median follow up was 11.1 months. Freedom from local recurrence at 12 months was 43 percent in the observation group and 72 percent in the radiosurgery group, hazard ratio 0.46 (95% CI 0.24 to 0.88, p=0.015). There were no adverse events or treatment related deaths in either group.

maintain.methods: Investigator-initiated, phase 2, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial. Patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer whose disease progressed during endocrine therapy and a CDK4/6 inhibitor switched endocrine therapy to fulvestrant or exemestane and were randomly assigned 1:1 to ribociclib or placebo. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival, measured from random assignment to disease progression or death. The planned sample was 120 patients, with 80% power to detect a hazard ratio of 0.58.
maintain.results: Of the 119 randomly assigned participants, 103 (86.5%) had previously received palbociclib and 14 (11.7%) had received ribociclib. Median progression-free survival was 5.29 months (95% CI 3.02 to 8.12) with switched endocrine therapy plus ribociclib versus 2.76 months (95% CI 2.66 to 3.25) with placebo (HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.39 to 0.85; P=.006). Progression-free survival rates with ribociclib were 41.2% at 6 months and 24.6% at 12 months, versus 23.9% and 7.4% with placebo.

male.methods: Multicentre phase 2 randomised clinical trial that assessed 56 male patients with hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, recruited from 24 breast units across Germany between October 2012 and May 2017. Patients were randomised to one of three arms, tamoxifen alone, tamoxifen plus a gonadotropin-releasing hormone analogue, or an aromatase inhibitor plus a gonadotropin-releasing hormone analogue, each for 6 months. The primary endpoint was the change in estradiol levels from baseline to 3 months. Secondary endpoints were changes in estradiol after 6 months, changes in additional hormonal parameters, adverse effects, sexual function and quality of life after 3 and 6 months. The last patient completed 6 months of treatment in December 2017, the analysis data set was locked on 24 August 2018 and analysis was completed on 19 December 2018.
male.results: Of the 56 patients, 52 started treatment, with a median age of 61.5 years, range 37 to 83. Three patients discontinued study treatment prematurely, one in each arm, and 50 patients were evaluable for the primary endpoint. After 3 months median estradiol levels increased by 67 percent, a change of +17.0 ng/L, with tamoxifen, decreased by 85 percent, -23.0 ng/L, with tamoxifen plus GnRH analogue, and decreased by 72 percent, -18.5 ng/L, with aromatase inhibitor plus GnRH analogue, p less than 0.001. After 6 months median estradiol levels increased by 41 percent, +12 ng/L, with tamoxifen, decreased by 61 percent, -19.5 ng/L, with tamoxifen plus GnRH analogue, and decreased by 64 percent, -17.0 ng/L, with aromatase inhibitor plus GnRH analogue, p less than 0.001. Sexual function and quality of life decreased when the GnRH analogue was added but were unchanged with tamoxifen alone.

map2.methods: Healthy postmenopausal women were randomised to exemestane 25 mg daily or placebo for 12 months and followed for 24 months. The primary endpoint was change in percent breast density between the baseline and 12-month mammograms; secondary endpoints were changes in serum lipids, bone biomarkers and bone mineral density.
map2.results: Ninety-eight women were randomised, 49 to each arm, and 65 had density data at baseline and 12 months. With exemestane, percent density was not significantly changed from baseline at 6, 12 or 24 months and was not different from placebo. Exemestane raised N-telopeptide at 12 months compared with placebo, without differences in lumbar spine or femoral neck bone mineral density at 12 or 24 months. Total cholesterol fell more at 6 months and HDL cholesterol at 3, 6 and 12 months with exemestane; LDL and triglycerides did not differ.

map3.methods: Randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial of exemestane designed to detect a 65% relative reduction in invasive breast cancer. Eligible postmenopausal women aged 35 or older had at least one risk factor: age 60 or older, Gail 5-year risk above 1.66%, prior atypical ductal or lobular hyperplasia or lobular carcinoma in situ, or ductal carcinoma in situ with mastectomy. Toxic effects and health-related and menopause-specific quality of life were measured.
map3.results: 4560 women, median age 62.5 years and median Gail risk 2.3%, were randomly assigned to exemestane or placebo. At a median follow-up of 35 months there were 11 invasive breast cancers with exemestane and 32 with placebo, a 65% relative reduction in annual incidence (0.19% vs 0.55%; HR 0.35, 95% CI 0.18 to 0.70; P=0.002). Invasive plus noninvasive cancer had an annual incidence of 0.35% vs 0.77% (HR 0.47, 0.27 to 0.79). Adverse events occurred in 88% vs 85% (P=0.003), with no significant differences in skeletal fractures, cardiovascular events, other cancers or treatment-related deaths. Quality-of-life differences were minimal.

marianne.methods: Patients with centrally assessed HER2-positive advanced breast cancer and no prior therapy for advanced disease were randomly assigned 1:1:1 to control trastuzumab plus taxane, to T-DM1 plus placebo, or to T-DM1 plus pertuzumab, all at standard doses. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival by independent review.
marianne.results: Median progression-free survival was 13.7 months with trastuzumab plus taxane, 14.1 months with T-DM1, and 15.2 months with T-DM1 plus pertuzumab. Response rates were 67.9%, 59.7%, and 64.2%. Median response duration was 12.5, 20.7, and 21.2 months. Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 54.1%, 45.4%, and 46.2% of patients.

martelli-elderly-t1n0.methods: Randomised clinical trial in 238 women aged 65 to 80 with clinically node-negative breast cancer of radiographic diameter 2 cm or less. Patients were randomised to quadrantectomy with or without axillary dissection; all received radiotherapy to the residual breast but not the axilla, and all were prescribed tamoxifen for 5 years. Main outcome measures were overall survival and breast cancer mortality, with overt axillary disease assessed in those without dissection.
martelli-elderly-t1n0.results: After 15 years of follow-up, distant metastasis rate, overall survival and breast cancer mortality were indistinguishable between the axillary dissection and no axillary dissection arms. The 15-year cumulative incidence of overt axillary disease in the no axillary dissection arm was 6%.

masai.methods: Randomised, controlled, population-based, single-blinded, non-inferiority screening accuracy study at four Swedish sites. Women aged 40-80 years eligible for mammography screening were randomly allocated 1:1 to AI-supported screening or standard double reading without AI. The AI system scored malignancy risk on a 10-level scale, triaging examinations to single reading (score 1-9) or double reading (score 10). This prespecified clinical safety analysis assessed early screening performance and screen-reading workload in the modified intention-to-treat population.
masai.results: 80 033 women were randomised between April 2021 and July 2022, 40 003 to AI-supported screening and 40 030 to double reading, and 13 were excluded. AI-supported screening gave 244 screen-detected cancers, 861 recalls, and 46 345 screen readings. Standard screening gave 203 cancers, 817 recalls, and 83 231 readings. Cancer detection rates were 6.1 versus 5.1 per 1000 screened (ratio 1.2, 95% CI 1.0 to 1.5; p=0.052). Screen-reading workload fell by 44.3%.

mdacc-weekly-paclitaxel.methods: Patients with clinical stage I to IIIA breast cancer were randomly assigned to primary systemic chemotherapy with paclitaxel weekly for 12 doses or once every 3 weeks for four cycles, followed by four cycles of fluorouracil, doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide (FAC) every 3 weeks. Two paclitaxel doses were used according to nodal status defined by ultrasound and fine needle aspiration. Clinical response and residual disease in the breast and nodes were assessed after all chemotherapy.
mdacc-weekly-paclitaxel.results: 258 patients were randomly assigned, 127 to weekly and 131 to 3-weekly paclitaxel; 110 had histological nodal involvement and 148 clinical N0 disease. Clinical response was similar between groups (P = .25). Weekly paclitaxel gave a higher pathological complete response rate (28.2%) than 3-weekly paclitaxel (15.7%; P = .02), with improved breast conservation rates (P = .05).

mediola.methods: MEDIOLA is a multicentre, open-label, phase 1/2 basket trial of durvalumab and olaparib in solid tumours, with four initial cohorts, namely germline BRCA-mutated metastatic breast cancer, germline BRCA-mutated metastatic ovarian cancer, metastatic gastric cancer and relapsed small-cell lung cancer. This report covers the breast cancer cohort. Eligible patients were aged 18 years or older, 19 or older in South Korea, with germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations and histologically confirmed progressive HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer and no more than two previous lines of chemotherapy for metastatic disease, enrolled from 14 health centres in six countries. Patients received olaparib 300 mg orally twice daily for four weeks and thereafter olaparib 300 mg twice daily with durvalumab 1.5 g intravenously every four weeks until disease progression. The primary endpoints were safety and tolerability and the 12-week disease control rate; safety was analysed in patients who received at least one dose of study treatment and activity in the full-analysis set.
mediola.results: Between June 14, 2016 and May 2, 2017, 34 patients were enrolled, received both study drugs and were included in the safety analysis. 11 patients (32%) experienced grade 3 or worse adverse events, most commonly anaemia in four (12%), neutropenia in three (9%) and pancreatitis in two (6%). Three patients (9%) discontinued because of adverse events and four (12%) experienced a total of six serious adverse events, and there were no treatment-related deaths. 24 of 30 patients eligible for the activity analysis had disease control at 12 weeks, 80% (90% CI 64.3 to 90.9). The authors conclude that the combination showed promising antitumour activity with safety similar to that seen with either drug alone, and that randomised research is needed to determine whether adding durvalumab improves long-term outcomes over olaparib monotherapy.

menos1.methods: Randomised controlled trial in women from London breast clinics with problematic hot flushes and night sweats, at least ten a week, after breast cancer treatment. Participants were allocated 1:1 to usual care or usual care plus group CBT, one 90-minute session a week for 6 weeks of psycho-education, paced breathing and cognitive and behavioural strategies. The trial statistician and outcome assessors were masked. The primary outcome was the adjusted mean difference in problem rating (1-10) at 9 weeks, by modified intention to treat.
menos1.results: Between May 2009 and August 2010, 96 women were randomly allocated to group CBT (47) or usual care (49). Group CBT reduced the problem rating at 9 weeks compared with usual care (mean difference -1.67, 95% CI -2.43 to -0.91; p<0.0001), and the improvement was maintained at 26 weeks (-1.76, -2.54 to -0.99; p<0.0001). No CBT-related adverse events were recorded.

metronomic-mtx-ctx.methods: Phase 2 study of the efficacy and tolerability of metronomic chemotherapy, low-dose oral methotrexate and cyclophosphamide given continuously, as salvage therapy in metastatic breast cancer. Between January 2004 and December 2005, 42 patients received methotrexate 2.5 mg twice daily on days 1 and 2 each week and cyclophosphamide 50 mg daily continuously.
metronomic-mtx-ctx.results: Forty-two patients were evaluable. The overall clinical benefit (complete response, partial response and stable disease for 24 weeks or more) was 31% and the overall response rate 16.7%, with no complete responses. Toxicity was generally mild: transaminase elevation, reversible, in 40.4% and grade 1 or 2 neutropenia in 28.5%. Progression-free survival among patients with clinical benefit was 10 months (95% CI 6.65 to 13.44).

milan-primary-chemotherapy.methods: Two prospective non-randomised studies used different regimens of primary chemotherapy in operable breast cancer with tumours of 2.5 cm or more in largest diameter, followed by breast-sparing surgery in the presence of objective tumour remission, to decrease the size of the primary tumour and allow effective local and distant control while avoiding mastectomy. Additional postoperative chemotherapy was given to women at high risk of relapse. The median follow-up was 65 months.
milan-primary-chemotherapy.results: A total of 536 assessable patients were enrolled, with fairly comparable main characteristics in the two trials. After primary chemotherapy, 85% of patients could have breast-sparing surgery, and in 14 patients (3%) the surgical specimens showed no residual neoplastic cell. In the final multivariate analysis, the histologically assessed extent of axillary node involvement (P < .001) and the degree of response to primary chemotherapy (P = .034) were the significant variables influencing 8-year relapse-free survival. In women treated with a breast-conserving approach, the cumulative risk of local relapse as first event alone was 6.8% (95% CI 3.9% to 8.8%).

mindact.methods: Randomised phase 3 study. 6693 women with early-stage breast cancer had genomic risk determined with the 70-gene signature and clinical risk with a modified Adjuvant! Online. Women at low clinical and low genomic risk received no chemotherapy. Women at high clinical and high genomic risk received chemotherapy. Patients with discordant results were assigned by either the genomic or the clinical risk. The primary goal tested 5-year survival without distant metastasis against a 92% non-inferiority boundary.
mindact.results: 1550 patients (23.2%) were at high clinical risk and low genomic risk.
