Among those not given chemotherapy, the 5-year rate of survival without distant metastasis was 94.7% (95% CI 92.5 to 96.2). The absolute difference against patients who received chemotherapy was 1.5 percentage points, lower without chemotherapy. Similar rates were reported in the ER-positive, HER2-negative subgroup. The 2021 updated analysis reported 8-year distant metastasis-free survival of 92.0% with chemotherapy and 89.4% without (hazard ratio 0.66).

monaleesa1.methods: Presurgical window-of-opportunity study in postmenopausal women with resectable HR-positive, HER2-negative early breast cancer, randomised 1:1:1 to letrozole 2.5 mg daily alone or with ribociclib 400 mg or 600 mg daily. Circulating tumour DNA and tumour biopsies were taken at baseline and after 14 days of treatment, before or during surgery. The primary objective was antiproliferative response by Ki67 in the two ribociclib arms compared with letrozole alone; safety, pharmacokinetics and genetic profiling were also assessed.
monaleesa1.results: Fourteen women were randomised. Mean decreases in the Ki67-positive cell fraction from baseline were 69% with letrozole alone (range 38-100%, n = 2), 96% with ribociclib 400 mg plus letrozole (78-100%, n = 6) and 92% with ribociclib 600 mg plus letrozole (75-100%, n = 3). Phosphorylated Rb and CDK4, CDK6, CCND2, CCND3 and CCNE1 expression fell after ribociclib. Pharmacokinetics were consistent with single-agent data, suggesting no drug-drug interaction, and there were no grade 3 or 4 adverse events.

monaleesa2.methods: Randomised, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial in 668 postmenopausal women with HR-positive, HER2-negative recurrent or metastatic breast cancer and no previous systemic therapy for advanced disease. Patients received ribociclib 600 mg per day on a 3-weeks-on, 1-week-off schedule plus letrozole 2.5 mg per day, or placebo plus letrozole. The primary end point was investigator-assessed progression-free survival. Secondary end points included overall survival, overall response rate and safety. A preplanned interim analysis followed 243 progression events or deaths.
monaleesa2.results: Progression-free survival was longer with ribociclib (hazard ratio 0.56; 95% CI 0.43 to 0.72). Median follow-up was 15.3 months. At 18 months the progression-free survival rate was 63.0% with ribociclib and 42.2% with placebo. Among patients with measurable disease the overall response rate was 52.7% versus 37.1%. Grade 3 or 4 neutropenia occurred in 59.3% versus 0.9%. The 2022 final overall survival analysis reported median overall survival of 63.9 versus 51.4 months (hazard ratio 0.76).

monaleesa3.methods: Phase 3 trial in postmenopausal women with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer who were treatment naive or had received up to one line of prior endocrine therapy in the advanced setting. Patients were randomly assigned two to one to ribociclib plus fulvestrant (484 patients) or placebo plus fulvestrant (242 patients). The primary end point was locally assessed progression-free survival. Secondary end points included overall survival, overall response rate and safety.
monaleesa3.results: Median progression-free survival was 20.5 months with ribociclib plus fulvestrant and 12.8 months with placebo plus fulvestrant (hazard ratio 0.593; 95% CI 0.480 to 0.732). The effect held in treatment-naive patients (0.577) and after one prior line (0.565). Overall response rate with measurable disease was 40.9% versus 28.7%. Grade 3 neutropenia occurred in 46.6% versus 0%. The 2021 updated survival report gave median overall survival of 53.7 versus 41.5 months (hazard ratio 0.73).

monaleesa7.methods: Phase 3, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial at 188 centres in 30 countries. Eligible patients were premenopausal women aged 18 to 59 with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, ECOG performance status 0 or 1, and no prior CDK4/6 inhibitor. Up to one line of chemotherapy for advanced disease was allowed. Patients were assigned one to one to ribociclib 600 mg or placebo, each with tamoxifen or a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor plus goserelin. The primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival.
monaleesa7.results: 672 patients were randomly assigned, 335 to ribociclib and 337 to placebo. Median investigator-assessed progression-free survival was 23.8 months (95% CI 19.2 to not reached) with ribociclib and 13.0 months (95% CI 11.0 to 16.4) with placebo (hazard ratio 0.55; 95% CI 0.44 to 0.69). Grade 3 or 4 neutropenia occurred in 61% versus 4%. The 2022 updated survival analysis reported median overall survival of 58.7 versus 48.0 months (hazard ratio 0.76).

monarch2.methods: Global, double-blind phase 3 study of women with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer that had progressed on neoadjuvant or adjuvant endocrine therapy, within 12 months of the end of adjuvant endocrine therapy, or on first-line endocrine therapy for metastatic disease. Patients were assigned two to one to abemaciclib or placebo 150 mg twice daily on a continuous schedule, each with fulvestrant 500 mg. The primary end point was investigator-assessed progression-free survival.
monarch2.results: 669 patients were assigned, 446 to abemaciclib plus fulvestrant and 223 to placebo plus fulvestrant. Median progression-free survival was 16.4 versus 9.3 months (hazard ratio 0.553; 95% CI 0.449 to 0.681). Among patients with measurable disease the objective response rate was 48.1% versus 21.3%. Diarrhea occurred in 86.4% versus 24.7% and neutropenia in 46.0% versus 4.0%. The 2020 interim survival analysis reported median overall survival of 46.7 versus 37.3 months (hazard ratio 0.757).

monarch3.methods: Double-blind randomised phase 3 study of abemaciclib or placebo 150 mg twice daily on a continuous schedule plus a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor, anastrozole 1 mg or letrozole 2.5 mg daily, in 493 postmenopausal women with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer and no prior systemic therapy in the advanced setting. The primary objective was investigator-assessed progression-free survival. A planned interim analysis occurred after 189 events.
monarch3.results: Progression-free survival was prolonged with abemaciclib (hazard ratio 0.54; 95% CI 0.41 to 0.72). The median was not reached with abemaciclib and was 14.7 months with placebo. Among patients with measurable disease the objective response rate was 59% versus 44%. Diarrhea affected 81.3% of the abemaciclib arm. The 2019 final progression-free survival report and the 2024 final overall survival report gave medians of 28.18 versus 14.76 months (hazard ratio 0.540) and 66.8 versus 53.7 months (hazard ratio 0.804).

monarche.methods: Open-label phase 3 study in patients with HR-positive, HER2-negative, high-risk early breast cancer treated with surgery and, as indicated, radiotherapy and chemotherapy. Eligible patients had four or more positive nodes, or one to three nodes with tumour 5 cm or larger, grade 3 histology, or central Ki-67 of 20% or more. Assignment was 1:1 to standard adjuvant endocrine therapy with or without abemaciclib 150 mg twice daily for two years. The primary end point was invasive disease-free survival.
monarche.results: At a preplanned interim analysis of 5637 randomly assigned patients, 323 invasive disease-free survival events had occurred in the intention-to-treat population. Abemaciclib plus endocrine therapy was superior to endocrine therapy alone (hazard ratio 0.75; 95% CI 0.60 to 0.93), with 2-year invasive disease-free survival rates of 92.2% versus 88.7%. The 2025 overall survival report gave 7-year overall survival of 86.8% versus 85.0% (hazard ratio 0.842, P = 0.027).

monarcher.methods: Open-label three-group trial at 75 centres in 14 countries. Women aged 18 or older with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-positive unresectable, locally advanced, recurrent or metastatic disease, performance status 0 or 1, and at least two prior HER2-targeted therapies for advanced disease were randomised 1:1:1 to abemaciclib plus trastuzumab plus fulvestrant, abemaciclib plus trastuzumab, or physician's choice chemotherapy plus trastuzumab.
monarcher.results: Of 325 patients screened, 237 were randomised, 79 per group. Median follow-up was 19.0 months. Median progression-free survival was 8.3 months in group A versus 5.7 months in group C, hazard ratio 0.67, p=0.051. Group B was 5.7 months, hazard ratio 0.94, p=0.77. The commonest grade 3 or 4 event was neutropenia in 27%, 22%, and 26%. Two deaths were treatment related.

more-core.methods: The Continuing Outcomes Relevant to Evista trial examined the effect of 4 additional years of raloxifene on invasive breast cancer in women from the MORE trial who agreed to continue. Women assigned raloxifene 60 or 120 mg per day in MORE received raloxifene 60 mg per day in CORE (n = 3510), and women assigned placebo continued on placebo (n = 1703). Incidence was compared by log-rank test, with hazard ratios from a Cox model.
more-core.results: During CORE, the 4-year incidence of invasive breast cancer was reduced by 59% (HR 0.41, 95% CI 0.24 to 0.71) and of oestrogen receptor-positive invasive cancer by 66% (HR 0.34, 0.18 to 0.66) with raloxifene, with no difference in oestrogen receptor-negative cancer (P = .86). Over the 8 years of both trials, invasive breast cancer fell by 66% (HR 0.34, 0.22 to 0.50) and oestrogen receptor-positive invasive cancer by 76% (HR 0.24, 0.15 to 0.40). The relative risk of thromboembolism during CORE was 2.17 (0.83 to 5.70), an increase also seen in MORE.

morse-her2-dc-vaccine.methods: Patients with stage II (6 or more positive nodes), III or stage IV breast cancer with more than 50% HER2-overexpressing tumour cells who were disease-free after surgery and adjuvant therapy were eligible. Vaccines consisted of immature cultured dendritic cells (n = 3), mature cultured dendritic cells (n = 3) or mature Flt3-ligand mobilized peripheral blood dendritic cells (n = 1) loaded with the HER2 intracellular domain (ICD), or with tetanus toxoid, keyhole limpet hemocyanin or CMV peptide as controls, given intradermally or subcutaneously four times at 3-week intervals. ICD-specific T-cell and antibody responses were measured, cardiac function was determined by MUGA or echocardiography, and long-term disease status was obtained from patient contact.
morse-her2-dc-vaccine.results: All seven patients underwent dendritic cell generation and five received all four immunizations. There were no toxicities greater than grade 1 and no ejection fraction fell below normal. Delayed-type hypersensitivity reactions at the injection site occurred in 6 of 7 patients, and HER2 specificity was detected by cytokine flow cytometry or ELISPOT in 5. At more than 5 years of follow-up, 6 of 7 had detectable anti-ICD antibodies. One patient had a pulmonary recurrence 4 years after immunization, which was resected, and all patients were alive and disease-free at 4.6 to 6.7 years of follow-up.

muther.methods: Single-arm, multi-cohort phase 2 trial of neratinib in HER2-mutated, HER2 non-amplified metastatic breast cancer, on the premise that HER2 mutations induce endocrine resistance in oestrogen receptor-positive breast cancer. Patients with oestrogen receptor-positive, HER2-mutated disease received neratinib plus fulvestrant in one of two cohorts, a fulvestrant-treated cohort of 24 patients and a fulvestrant-naive cohort of 11. Patients with oestrogen receptor-negative, HER2-mutated disease received neratinib monotherapy in an exploratory cohort of 5. Clinical benefit rate was the efficacy measure reported for each cohort. Trastuzumab was added at progression in a small number of patients, and tumours were assessed for acquired HER2 mutations at progression.
muther.results: Clinical benefit rate was 38% (95% CI 18% to 62%) in the fulvestrant-treated cohort, 30% (7% to 65%) in the fulvestrant-naive cohort and 25% (1% to 81%) in the oestrogen receptor-negative cohort. Adding trastuzumab at progression in 5 patients produced three partial responses and one stable disease lasting 24 weeks or more. Clinical benefit appeared positively associated with lobular histology and negatively associated with HER2 L755 alterations. Acquired HER2 mutations were detected in 5 of 23 patients at progression. The authors concluded that neratinib and fulvestrant are active in oestrogen receptor-positive, HER2-mutated metastatic breast cancer and that the data support further evaluation of dual HER2 blockade.

n007.methods: Open-label, single-arm study of neoadjuvant letrozole with palbociclib in postmenopausal women with histologically proven ER-positive, HER2-negative invasive breast cancer of 2 cm or more. Twenty eligible patients received letrozole 2.5 mg per day with palbociclib 125 mg per day for 3 out of 4 weeks in repeated cycles for 16 weeks (four cycles) before surgery. The primary end points were clinical response rate and the preoperative endocrine prognostic index (PEPI); secondary end points were pathological response and EndoPredict gene expression testing of the tumour samples.
n007.results: Seventeen patients had a clinical response of 50% or more, 8 complete and 9 partial responses, with significant reductions in the area (P < 0.0001) and volume (P = 0.017) of the cancer. One patient had a pathological complete response, and all cancers were downgraded after treatment. Ki67 (P = 0.044) and EndoPredict scores (P < 0.0001) fell significantly, as did the expression of all proliferative genes, IL6ST and RBBP8. Six patients with intermediate and three with high PEPI risk scores had low EPclin scores.

n03c5.methods: Randomised trial in 118 patients with inadequate hot flash control on an antidepressant, assigned to an antidepressant plus gabapentin or to being weaned off the antidepressant onto gabapentin alone. Patients were observed for 5 weeks, including a baseline week on their current antidepressant without gabapentin, and completed validated daily hot flash diaries.
n03c5.results: Ninety-one patients provided complete data at 5 weeks. Whether or not the antidepressant was continued, hot flashes fell by about half: median frequency reduction 54% (95% CI 34% to 70%) with combined treatment vs 49% (26% to 58%) with gabapentin alone, and score reduction 56% (26% to 71%) vs 60% (33% to 73%). Continuing the antidepressant added no significant reduction.

na-pher2.methods: NA-PHER2 is a multicohort, open-label, exploratory phase 2 study done at seven sites in Italy. Patients were eligible for the first cohort if they had previously untreated, histologically confirmed, unilateral, invasive, HER2-positive, ER-positive breast cancer and were suitable for neoadjuvant therapy. They were treated every 3 weeks with intravenous trastuzumab and pertuzumab for six cycles plus oral palbociclib 125 mg once a day for 21 days in a 4-week cycle and intramuscular fulvestrant 500 mg every 4 weeks for five cycles. The coprimary endpoints were change from baseline in Ki67 expression at 2 weeks and at surgery 16 weeks after starting treatment, and change in apoptosis from baseline to surgery. Secondary endpoints were clinical objective response by modified RECIST and pathological complete response. Cohort B gave dual HER2 blockade and palbociclib without fulvestrant, and cohort C enrolled tumours with Ki67 above 20% and HER2 immunohistochemistry 1+ or 2+ without gene amplification and added fulvestrant.
na-pher2.results: 36 patients were enrolled in the first cohort, of whom one was ineligible and five were HER2-negative on retrospective analysis, leaving 35 in safety analyses and 30 assessed for the primary and secondary endpoints. Geometric mean Ki67 was 31.9 at baseline versus 4.3 at week 2 (n=25, p<0.0001) and 12.1 at surgery (n=22, p=0.013), and geometric mean apoptosis was 1.2 at baseline versus 0.4 at surgery (p=0.019). A clinical objective response immediately before surgery was achieved by 29 of 30 patients (97%, 95% CI 83 to 100), and 8 (27%, 95% CI 12 to 46) had a pathological complete response in breast and axillary nodes. The most frequent grade 3 adverse events were neutropenia in ten patients (29%) and diarrhoea in five (14%), with no grade 4 or serious adverse events and no deaths. In cohort B, without fulvestrant, the mean Ki67 change was -25.7 at week 2 and -9.5 at surgery, with objective response in 88.5% and pCR in 19.2%; in cohort C the mean Ki67 change was -29.5 at week 2 and -19.3 at surgery, with objective response in 78.3%. The biomarker analysis found that high immune infiltration and low ER signalling correlated with pCR while TP53 mutations were associated with high day 14 Ki67.

nala.methods: Randomised, active-controlled phase 3 trial in patients with centrally confirmed HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer who had received two or more previous HER2-directed regimens. Patients with stable asymptomatic CNS disease were eligible. Assignment was one to one to neratinib 240 mg daily plus capecitabine 750 mg/m2 twice daily on 14 of 21 days with loperamide prophylaxis, or to lapatinib 1250 mg daily plus capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 twice daily. Coprimary end points were centrally confirmed progression-free survival and overall survival.
nala.results: 621 patients from 28 countries were assigned, 307 to neratinib plus capecitabine and 314 to lapatinib plus capecitabine. Centrally reviewed progression-free survival favoured neratinib (hazard ratio 0.76; 95% CI 0.63 to 0.93). The overall survival hazard ratio was 0.88 (95% CI 0.72 to 1.07). Cumulative incidence of intervention for CNS disease was 22.8% versus 29.2%. Objective response rates were 32.8% versus 26.7%. Median duration of response was 8.5 versus 5.6 months. Diarrhea occurred in 83% versus 66%.

natalee.methods: Phase 3 trial in women and men with HR-positive, HER2-negative early breast cancer of anatomical stage IIA (N0 with risk factors, or N1), IIB or III. Patients were randomised 1:1 to ribociclib 400 mg per day, three weeks on and one week off for 36 months, plus a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor for 60 months (2549), or the aromatase inhibitor alone (2552). Premenopausal women and men also received goserelin. The primary endpoint was invasive disease-free survival.
natalee.results: At the 21 July 2023 cut-off, ribociclib had been stopped in 1996 patients (78.3%) and 1091 (42.8%) had completed three years. Median follow-up for invasive disease-free survival was 33.3 months. There were 226 events with ribociclib plus the aromatase inhibitor and 283 with the inhibitor alone (hazard ratio 0.749; 95% CI 0.628 to 0.892; P = 0.0012). Three-year invasive disease-free survival was 90.7% versus 87.6%. Overall survival data were immature.

nato.methods: Randomised trial of adjuvant tamoxifen against no treatment in early breast cancer, with tamoxifen 20 mg daily given for 2 years after local treatment. This report is the analysis at a maximum follow-up of 8 years, with a median of 5 years 6 months.
nato.results: A significant advantage persisted for patients receiving tamoxifen, independent of menopausal status, stage, grade and oestrogen receptor status. Log hazard rate analysis did not show a rebound effect on stopping the drug and suggested that more prolonged treatment might improve results further.

ncctg-89-30-52.methods: Randomised trial in postmenopausal women with resected early breast cancer known to be oestrogen receptor positive, testing whether fluoxymesterone added to tamoxifen improves on tamoxifen alone, as a previous randomised trial in metastatic disease had suggested. Patients received tamoxifen 20 mg daily for 5 years alone or combined with fluoxymesterone 10 mg twice daily for 1 year. The primary endpoint was relapse-free survival, counting local-regional or distant recurrence, ipsilateral ductal carcinoma in situ and death from any cause.
ncctg-89-30-52.results: There were 541 eligible patients entered between 1991 and 1995, with balanced arms. At a median follow-up of 11.4 years among patients still alive, neither relapse-free survival nor overall survival differed: the adjusted hazard ratio for relapse or death without relapse was 0.84 (95% CI 0.64 to 1.10) and for death 0.89 (0.67 to 1.18), tamoxifen plus fluoxymesterone against tamoxifen alone. Virilisation was more frequent with fluoxymesterone.

ncctg-n0574.methods: Patients with one to three brain metastases at 34 North American institutions were randomised between February 2002 and December 2013 to radiosurgery alone or radiosurgery plus whole brain radiotherapy. Whole brain radiotherapy was 30 Gy in 12 fractions. Radiosurgery was 18 to 22 Gy in the combined group and 20 to 24 Gy alone. The primary endpoint was cognitive deterioration at 3 months.
ncctg-n0574.results: Of 213 patients randomised, 111 received radiosurgery alone and 102 radiosurgery plus whole brain radiotherapy. Cognitive deterioration at 3 months was 63.5% versus 91.7%, difference -28.2%, p<0.001. Overall quality of life change was -0.1 versus -12.0 points, p=0.001. Time to intracranial failure was shorter with radiosurgery alone, hazard ratio 3.6. Functional independence did not differ, p=0.26.

ncctg-n107c-cec-3.methods: Randomised controlled phase 3 trial at 48 institutions in the USA and Canada. Adults with one resected brain metastasis and a resection cavity under 5.0 cm were assigned 1:1 to postoperative radiosurgery of 12 to 20 Gy in a single fraction by cavity volume, or whole brain radiotherapy of 30 Gy in ten fractions or 37.5 Gy in 15 fractions. Analyses were by intention to treat.
ncctg-n107c-cec-3.results: 194 patients were randomised, 98 to radiosurgery and 96 to whole brain radiotherapy, with median follow-up 11.1 months. Median cognitive-deterioration-free survival was 3.7 versus 3.0 months, hazard ratio 0.47, p<0.0001. Cognitive deterioration at 6 months was 52% versus 85%. Median overall survival was 12.2 versus 11.6 months, hazard ratio 1.07, p=0.70. Commonest grade 3 or 4 events were hearing impairment and cognitive disturbance.

ncic-ind163.methods: Multicentre, noncomparative, randomised phase 2 study of oral everolimus 10 mg daily versus 70 mg weekly in patients with metastatic breast cancer who had received no or one prior chemotherapy regimen for metastatic disease. The multinomial end points of response and progression were evaluated at 8 weeks, using a two-stage accrual design with 15 evaluable patients in each schedule in stage 1. pAKT, PTEN, carbonic anhydrase 9, oestrogen and progesterone receptors and HER2 were evaluated for correlation with response.
ncic-ind163.results: Only daily therapy met the criteria for continuing, and another 15 patients were added. The response rate was 12% (95% CI 3.4% to 28.2%) with daily therapy and 0% (0.0% to 20.6%) with weekly therapy. The most common drug-related toxicities were fatigue, rash, anorexia, diarrhoea, stomatitis, cough and pneumonitis; pneumonitis occurred at higher than expected rates and seemed schedule dependent. 27% of patients on daily therapy discontinued treatment against 13% on weekly therapy, 16% versus 6% with pneumonitis. No biologic correlates of response were identified, although there were trends favouring benefit in oestrogen receptor-positive and HER2-negative disease.

nelipepimut-trastuzumab.methods: Phase IIb, multicentre, randomised, single-blinded, controlled trial in disease-free patients after completion of standard therapy. Eligible patients were HLA-A2, A3, A24 or A26 positive and had HER2 IHC 1+ or 2+, FISH-non-amplified breast cancer that was node positive or hormone receptor negative. All received trastuzumab for 1 year and were randomised to nelipepimut-S with GM-CSF or to placebo, GM-CSF alone. The primary outcome was 24-month disease-free survival; secondary outcomes were 36-month disease-free survival, safety and immunological response.
nelipepimut-trastuzumab.results: Of 275 randomised patients, 136 received nelipepimut-S with GM-CSF and 139 placebo with GM-CSF, with no clinicopathological differences between groups. The combination added no overall or cardiac toxicity. At a median follow-up of 25.7 months, estimated disease-free survival did not differ significantly between nelipepimut-S and control (hazard ratio 0.62, 95% CI 0.31 to 1.25, P = 0.18). In a planned exploratory analysis of triple-negative disease, disease-free survival was better with nelipepimut-S (hazard ratio 0.26, 95% CI 0.08 to 0.81, P = 0.01).

neoaltto.methods: Parallel-group, randomised, open-label phase 3 study. Women from 23 countries with HER2-positive primary breast cancer and tumours larger than 2 cm were assigned to oral lapatinib 1500 mg, intravenous trastuzumab, or lapatinib 1000 mg plus trastuzumab. Anti-HER2 therapy alone ran for six weeks, then weekly paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 was added for 12 weeks before surgery. Adjuvant chemotherapy and the same targeted therapy followed to 52 weeks. The primary endpoint was pathological complete response.
neoaltto.results: 154 patients received lapatinib, 149 trastuzumab and 152 the combination. Pathological complete response was 51.3% (78 of 152) with lapatinib plus trastuzumab against 29.5% (44 of 149) with trastuzumab, a difference of 21.1 percentage points (9.1 to 34.2, p=0.0001). Lapatinib alone gave 24.7% (38 of 154). Grade 3 diarrhoea occurred in 23.4%, 21.1% and 2.0% of the lapatinib, combination and trastuzumab groups. The 2019 survival report gave 6-year event-free survival of 74% with the combination and 67% with trastuzumab.

neocarhp.methods: Multicentre, open-label, randomised phase 3 non-inferiority trial at 15 hospitals in China. Women aged 18 or older with previously untreated stage II to III HER2-positive invasive breast cancer were assigned 1:1, stratified by hormone receptor and nodal status. Both groups received six 3-weekly cycles of investigator-selected docetaxel, paclitaxel or nab-paclitaxel with trastuzumab and pertuzumab, one group also receiving carboplatin. The primary endpoint was pathological complete response (ypT0/is ypN0) in the modified intention-to-treat population, with a non-inferiority margin of -10%.
neocarhp.results: Between April 2021 and August 2024, 774 patients were randomly assigned and 766 were included in the modified intention-to-treat population, 382 given THP and 384 given TCbHP. Pathological complete response occurred in 245 (64.1%, 95% CI 59.1 to 69.0) with THP and 253 (65.9%, 60.9 to 70.6) with TCbHP. The absolute difference was -1.8% (95% CI -8.5 to 5.0), odds ratio 0.93 (0.69 to 1.25). Grade 3 and 4 adverse events occurred in 20.7% with THP versus 34.6% with TCbHP, and serious adverse events in 1.3% versus 4.7%. No treatment-associated deaths occurred.

neocent.methods: Randomised feasibility and translational study in postmenopausal women with oestrogen receptor-rich primary breast cancer requiring neoadjuvant therapy. Patients were randomised to chemotherapy, six 3-weekly cycles of FE100C, or to letrozole 2.5 mg daily for 18 to 23 weeks. The primary endpoints were recruitment feasibility and tissue collection; secondary endpoints included clinical, radiological and pathological response, quality of life and translational endpoints.
neocent.results: Of 80 patients approached, 63 were eligible and 44 (70%, 95% CI 57 to 81) were randomised. Radiological objective response was seen in 12 chemotherapy patients (54.5%, 32.2 to 75.6) and 13 letrozole patients (59.1%, 36.4 to 79.3). Mean Ki-67 fell in both groups by days 2 to 4 and at surgery. Plasma cell-free DNA rose to week 8 and stayed raised at surgery with chemotherapy only. Recruitment and tissue collection endpoints were met, but a larger trial was deemed unfeasible because of slow accrual.

neolbc.methods: Randomised phase II trial tailoring neoadjuvant therapy in postmenopausal patients with early, luminal, HER2-negative, stage II or III breast cancer according to the percentage of Ki67-positive cancer cells after two weeks of letrozole. Patients with a Ki67 of 1% or higher were randomised between ribociclib plus letrozole and standard chemotherapy. The primary endpoint was whether ribociclib plus letrozole doubles the rate of complete cell-cycle arrest, Ki67 below 1% by immunohistochemistry, in the surgical specimen compared with chemotherapy. Secondary endpoints included pathologic response and toxicity.
neolbc.results: Of 161 registered patients, 70 were randomised and 66 started the allocated treatment. Complete cell-cycle arrest in the surgical specimen was similar for both groups, 35.3% in the ribociclib plus letrozole group and 31.3% in the chemotherapy group (P = 0.73). Response according to Miller and Payne was not significantly different between the two groups, nor was the pathological complete response rate. Overall toxicity was observed more often in the chemotherapy group; eight patients discontinued for toxicity in the ribociclib plus letrozole group and 10 in the chemotherapy group. The authors conclude that although the primary endpoint was not met, ribociclib plus letrozole as an alternative to neoadjuvant chemotherapy merits further investigation.

neoletrib.methods: Trial report for NEOLETRIB, which evaluates the response of ER-positive, HER2-negative luminal A or B breast cancer to neoadjuvant letrozole plus ribociclib. Treatment runs for six months. Molecular work includes sequential single-cell RNA sequencing of tumour biopsies, with biobanking of blood samples, tumour biopsies and gut microbiome specimens.

neomonarch.methods: Phase 2 neoadjuvant study. Postmenopausal women with stage I to IIIB HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer were randomised to a two-week lead-in of abemaciclib, anastrozole, or abemaciclib plus anastrozole, followed by 14 weeks of the combination. The primary objective was change in Ki67 from baseline to two weeks of treatment. Additional objectives were clinical, radiologic and pathologic response, safety, and gene expression changes related to cell proliferation and immune response.
neomonarch.results: Abemaciclib, alone or with anastrozole, gave a significant decrease in Ki67 expression and potent cell-cycle arrest at two weeks compared with anastrozole alone. Complete cell-cycle arrest was reached in 58% and 68% of the abemaciclib-containing arms versus 14% with anastrozole (P < 0.001). At the end of treatment 46% of intent-to-treat patients achieved a radiologic response and 4% a pathological complete response. The most common all-grade adverse events were diarrhea (62%), constipation (44%) and nausea (42%).

neopact.methods: Open-label phase 2 trial with a single group of patients with stage I to III triple-negative breast cancer at 2 sites. Neoadjuvant carboplatin (AUC 6) and docetaxel 75 mg/m2 plus pembrolizumab 200 mg were given every 21 days for 6 cycles with myeloid growth factor support. Enrolment ran from 2018 to 2022. The primary end point was pathologic complete response. Secondary end points were residual cancer burden, event-free survival, toxicity and immune biomarkers.
neopact.results: Among 115 eligible female patients, median age 50 years, 39% had node-positive disease. The pathologic complete response rate was 58% (95% CI 48-67) and the rate of residual cancer burden 0 plus 1 was 69% (95% CI 60-78). Grade 3 or higher immune-mediated adverse events occurred in 3.5% of patients. Estimated 3-year event-free survival was 86% overall, 98% in the pathologic complete response group and 68% in the no-response group.

neopal.methods: NeoPAL was a randomised, parallel, non-comparative phase 2 study. Patients with ER-positive, HER2-negative, Prosigna-defined luminal B or luminal A node-positive stage II-III breast cancer who were not candidates for breast-conserving surgery were assigned to letrozole 2.5 mg daily plus palbociclib 125 mg daily 3 weeks in 4 for 19 weeks, or to three cycles of FEC100 followed by three cycles of docetaxel 100 mg/m2. The primary end point was residual cancer burden 0-I rate.
neopal.results: 106 patients were randomised, with a median Prosigna ROR score of 71 (22-93). Residual cancer burden 0-I was seen in 4 patients on letrozole-palbociclib (7.7%, 95% CI 0.4-14.9) and 8 on chemotherapy (15.7%, 95% CI 5.7-25.7). Pathological complete response rates were 3.8% and 5.9%. Clinical response was 75% and breast-conserving surgery 69% in both arms. Preoperative Endocrine Prognostic Index 0 scores occurred in 17.6% and 8.0%. Serious adverse events numbered 2 versus 17.

neopalana.methods: Single-arm phase II neoadjuvant trial assessing the antiproliferative activity of palbociclib in primary breast cancer as a prelude to adjuvant studies. Patients with clinical stage II or III oestrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative disease received anastrozole 1 mg daily for four weeks as cycle 0, with goserelin if premenopausal, after which palbociclib 125 mg daily on days 1 to 21 was added from cycle 1 day 1 for four 28-day cycles. Patients whose cycle 1 day 15 Ki67 exceeded 10% went off study for inadequate response. Anastrozole continued to surgery, which took place three to five weeks after palbociclib exposure; later patients received an extra 10 to 12 days of palbociclib as cycle 5 immediately before surgery. Serial biopsies at baseline, cycle 1 day 1, cycle 1 day 15 and surgery were analysed for Ki67, gene expression and mutation profiles, and the primary endpoint was complete cell cycle arrest, central Ki67 of 2.7% or less.
neopalana.results: Fifty patients enrolled. The complete cell cycle arrest rate was significantly higher after adding palbociclib to anastrozole, 87% at cycle 1 day 15 versus 26% at cycle 1 day 1 (P < 0.001). Palbociclib enhanced cell-cycle control over anastrozole monotherapy regardless of luminal subtype and across a broad range of clinicopathologic and mutation profiles. Ki67 recovery at surgery following palbociclib washout was suppressed by the cycle 5 palbociclib. Resistance was associated with nonluminal subtypes and persistent E2F-target gene expression, and the authors conclude that prolonged administration may be necessary to maintain the effect.

neophoebe.methods: Neoadjuvant, phase II, randomised, double-blind study in women with HER2-positive breast cancer, randomised within two independent cohorts by PIK3CA mutation status and stratified by oestrogen receptor status, to buparlisib or placebo with trastuzumab for the first 6 weeks, followed by buparlisib or placebo with trastuzumab and paclitaxel. The primary end-point was pathological complete response; the key secondary end-point was objective response at 6 weeks, with Ki67 and tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes at day 15 as exploratory end-points.
neophoebe.results: Recruitment was suspended, mainly because of liver toxicity, after 50 of the planned 256 patients. Each arm (buparlisib 25, placebo 25) held 21 PIK3CA wild-type and 4 mutant tumours. Pathological complete response was similar with buparlisib and placebo (32.0% versus 40%, one-sided P = 0.811). In the oestrogen receptor-positive subgroup there was a trend towards higher objective response (68.8% versus 33.3%, P = 0.053) and a significant decrease in Ki67 (75% versus 26.7%, P = 0.021) with buparlisib.

neorhea.methods: NeoRHEA was a single-arm phase 2 study that included patients with estrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative early breast cancer who received four cycles of neoadjuvant palbociclib and endocrine therapy. The primary outcome was baseline biomarkers of treatment resistance and the secondary outcome was post-treatment transcriptional and epigenetic changes of tumour, immune and stromal cells. Gene set enrichment analyses were run on genes residing in differentially accessible chromatin peaks, and marker findings were validated by multiplex immunohistochemistry. A linked report assessed circulating tumour DNA with the RaDaR assay on plasma drawn pre-treatment, after cycle 1, pre-surgery and 1 month post-surgery.
neorhea.results: E2F targets and G2M checkpoint proliferation-related gene sets were enriched in baseline samples from resistant patients. Downregulation of E2F targets and G2M checkpoint after treatment was observed in tumour, endothelial and T cells, and gene set enrichment on differentially accessible peaks revealed similar effects. Decreases in CD8+ CD103+ tissue-resident memory cell marker genes were observed post-treatment and validated by multiplex immunohistochemistry. The authors conclude that palbociclib with endocrine therapy diminishes adaptive anti-tumour immunity by decreasing T cell proliferation and the presence of tissue-resident memory T cells. In the linked ctDNA report, baseline ctDNA was detected in 55%, fell to 5% during treatment and was undetectable in all patients by 1 month post-surgery, with baseline detection higher in grade 3 tumours and in residual cancer burden 3, and baseline ctDNA predicted poor response to this regimen.

neosphere.methods: Multicentre, open-label, phase 2 study. Treatment-naive women with HER2-positive breast cancer were randomly assigned 1:1:1:1, stratified by operable, locally advanced and inflammatory disease and by hormone receptor expression, to four neoadjuvant cycles of trastuzumab plus docetaxel (group A), pertuzumab and trastuzumab plus docetaxel (group B), pertuzumab and trastuzumab (group C), or pertuzumab plus docetaxel (group D). The primary endpoint was pathological complete response in the breast in the intention-to-treat population. Neither patients nor investigators were masked.
neosphere.results: Of 417 eligible patients, 107 went to group A, 107 to group B, 107 to group C and 96 to group D. Pathological complete response was 45.8% (95% CI 36.1-55.7) in group B against 29.0% (20.6-38.5) in group A, p=0.0141. It was 24.0% in group D and 16.8% in group C. The most common grade 3 or higher event was neutropenia. The 5-year analysis reported progression-free survival of 81%, 86%, 73% and 73% in groups A to D.

neostar.methods: Investigator-initiated trial of neoadjuvant sacituzumab govitecan, an antibody-drug conjugate targeting TROP2, in localized triple-negative breast cancer. Participants with early-stage disease received four cycles of the conjugate before surgery. The primary objective was the pathological complete response rate in breast and lymph nodes, ypT0/isN0, to sacituzumab govitecan. Secondary objectives were overall response rate, safety, event-free survival and predictive biomarkers. A response-guided approach was used and subsequent systemic therapy decisions were at the discretion of the treating physician.
neostar.results: From July 2020 to August 2021, 50 participants were enrolled, median age 48.5 years, with 13 clinical stage I, 26 stage II and 11 stage III. Forty-nine (98%) completed four cycles. The pathological complete response rate with sacituzumab govitecan alone was 30% (n = 15, 95% CI 18% to 45%) and the overall response rate per RECIST V1.1 was 64%, 32 of 50. Higher Ki-67 and higher tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes were predictive of pathological complete response (P = 0.007 and P = 0.002), while baseline TROP2 expression was not (P = 0.440). Common adverse events were nausea (82%), fatigue (76%), alopecia (76%), rash (48%) and neutropenia (44%). With a median follow-up of 18.9 months the 2-year event-free survival was 95% for all participants and 100% among the 15 who had a pathological complete response.

neostop.methods: Multisite randomised phase 2 trial. Patients aged 18 or older with stage I to III triple-negative breast cancer were randomised 1:1 to weekly paclitaxel for 12 weeks plus carboplatin AUC6 every 21 days for four cycles followed by doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide every 14 days for four cycles, or to carboplatin AUC6 plus docetaxel every 21 days for six cycles. Stromal tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes were assessed.
neostop.results: 100 patients were randomised, 48 to arm A and 52 to arm B. Pathologic complete response was 54% in each arm and residual cancer burden 0 or I was 67% in each. Median stromal tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte density was 20% with pathologic complete response versus 5% with residual disease. Grade 3 or 4 neutropenia was 60% versus 8% and febrile neutropenia 19% versus 0%. Mean cost was lower in arm B.

neotala.methods: Phase II, single-arm, open-label study of neoadjuvant talazoparib in patients with germline BRCA1/2-mutated early-stage triple-negative breast cancer. Patients received talazoparib 1 mg once daily for 24 weeks, reduced to 0.75 mg for moderate renal impairment, followed by surgery. The primary endpoint was pathologic complete response by independent central review. Secondary endpoints included residual cancer burden by independent central review. Safety, tolerability and patient-reported outcomes were also assessed.
neotala.results: Of 61 patients, 48 received at least 80% of talazoparib doses and underwent surgery, or progressed before pCR assessment and were counted as non-responders. The pathologic complete response rate was 45.8%, 95% CI 32.0 to 60.6, in the evaluable population and 49.2%, 95% CI 36.7 to 61.6, in the intention-to-treat population. Residual cancer burden 0 or I was 45.8%, 95% CI 29.4 to 63.2, and 50.8%, 95% CI 35.5 to 66.0, in the evaluable and intention-to-treat populations respectively. Treatment-related adverse events were reported in 58 patients, 95.1%, the commonest grade 3 and 4 events being anaemia in 39.3% and neutropenia in 9.8%. There was no clinically meaningful detriment in quality of life, no deaths occurred during the reporting period, and two deaths from progressive disease occurred more than 400 days after the first dose. The authors conclude that talazoparib monotherapy was active despite pCR rates not meeting the prespecified threshold, and that the rates were comparable with those of anthracycline- and taxane-based regimens.

neotrip.methods: 280 patients with triple-negative breast cancer were enrolled in this multicentre randomised study. They received neoadjuvant carboplatin AUC 2 and nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 intravenously on days 1 and 8, without atezolizumab (n=142) or with atezolizumab 1200 mg intravenously on day 1 (n=138). Both regimens were given every 3 weeks for eight cycles before surgery, followed by four cycles of an adjuvant anthracycline regimen. The primary aim was event-free survival, with pathological complete response an important secondary aim.
neotrip.results: In the intention-to-treat analysis the pathological complete response rate was 48.6% with atezolizumab against 44.4% without, odds ratio 1.18, 95% CI 0.74-1.89, P=0.48. Treatment-related adverse events were similar between regimens except for significantly more serious adverse events and liver transaminase abnormalities with atezolizumab. In multivariate analysis PD-L1 expression was the most significant factor influencing the rate of pathological complete response, odds ratio 2.08.

neratinib-vs-lapatinib-capecitabine.methods: Randomised phase 2 trial comparing neratinib monotherapy with lapatinib plus capecitabine in patients with HER2-positive locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer and prior trastuzumab treatment. Patients received neratinib 240 mg/d continuously (n=117) or lapatinib 1250 mg/d continuously plus capecitabine 2000 mg/m2 per day on days 1-14 of each 21-day cycle (n=116). The primary aim was to show non-inferiority of neratinib for progression-free survival.
neratinib-vs-lapatinib-capecitabine.results: Non-inferiority of neratinib was not demonstrated (hazard ratio 1.19, 95% CI 0.89 to 1.60, against a non-inferiority margin of 1.15). Median progression-free survival was 4.5 months with neratinib versus 6.8 months with lapatinib plus capecitabine, and median overall survival 19.7 versus 23.6 months. Objective response (29% vs 41%, P=0.067) and clinical benefit (44% vs 64%, P=0.003) were lower with neratinib. Diarrhoea was the most frequent treatment-related adverse event of any grade (85% vs 68%, P=0.002) and of grade 3/4 (28% vs 10%, P<0.001), and neratinib had no significant skin toxicity.

nimbus.methods: Phase II single-arm trial in patients with HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer and high tumour mutational burden, defined as at least 9 mutations per megabase. Patients received nivolumab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks and low-dose ipilimumab 1 mg/kg every 6 weeks for 2 years or until progression. The primary endpoint was objective response rate per RECIST 1.1. Secondary endpoints were progression-free survival, overall survival, clinical benefit rate, and safety and tolerability including immune-related adverse events. A prespecified correlative outcome was the response rate in patients with a burden of at least 14 mutations per megabase. Exploratory genomic, circulating tumour DNA and stool microbiome analyses were also performed.
nimbus.results: Among 30 patients enrolled, the median tumour mutational burden was 10.9 mutations per megabase (range 9 to 110) and the confirmed objective response rate was 20%. The 6 patients with a burden of at least 14 mutations per megabase had a higher response rate, 60% versus 12% (p = 0.041), and showed a trend towards improved progression-free and overall survival compared with patients below that threshold. Exploratory genomic analyses suggested that ESR1 and PTEN mutations may be associated with poor response, while clinical benefit was associated with a decrease or no change in tumour fraction on serial circulating tumour DNA during treatment. Stool microbiome analysis showed that baseline blood tumour mutational burden, PD-L1 positivity and immune-related diarrhoea were associated with distinct taxonomic profiles. The authors conclude that some patients with hypermutated HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer experience extended clinical benefit with dual immunotherapy, and that a higher burden together with additional genomic and microbiome biomarkers may optimise selection.

noah.methods: Randomised superiority trial. Women with HER2-positive locally advanced or inflammatory breast cancer received neoadjuvant chemotherapy of doxorubicin, paclitaxel, cyclophosphamide, methotrexate and fluorouracil, with 1 year of trastuzumab given neoadjuvantly and adjuvantly (n=117) or without trastuzumab (n=118). Randomisation used a computer program with minimisation by geographical area, disease stage and hormone receptor status. A parallel cohort of 99 patients with HER2-negative disease received the same chemotherapy. The primary endpoint was event-free survival, analysed by intention to treat.
noah.results: Trastuzumab significantly improved event-free survival in HER2-positive patients. Three-year event-free survival was 71% (95% CI 61-78, 36 events) with trastuzumab and 56% (46-65, 51 events) without, hazard ratio 0.59 (95% CI 0.38-0.90), p=0.013. Two patients (2%) developed symptomatic cardiac failure despite concurrent doxorubicin, and both responded to cardiac drugs. The 2014 follow-up reported 5-year event-free survival of 58% with trastuzumab and 43% with chemotherapy alone, hazard ratio 0.64 (95% CI 0.44-0.93), p=0.016.

nrg-br002.methods: Randomised phase II/III trial across US and Canadian institutions. Participants had no more than four metastases and controlled primary disease, after up to 12 months of first-line systemic therapy without progression. All visible metastases had to be amenable to stereotactic body radiation therapy or surgical resection. Participants were randomly assigned 1:1 to systemic therapy alone or with metastasis-directed ablation. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival, defined as time to progression or death. Secondary endpoints included overall survival and toxicity. Circulating tumour cells were evaluated as exploratory biomarkers.
nrg-br002.results: From December 2014 to September 2019, 129 patients were enrolled and 125 were eligible for analysis. Median age was 54 years, 79% had hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative disease, 60% a solitary metastasis, 50% bone involvement and 37% bone-only disease. Ablation was delivered by stereotactic body radiation therapy in 93%. With 72 progression-free survival events at a median follow-up of 29.9 months, median progression-free survival was 23.0 months without ablation and 19.5 months with it, hazard ratio 0.92 (70% CI 0.71 to 1.17, 95% CI 0.57 to 1.47), one-sided P = .36, stratified P = .42. The trial therefore did not proceed to phase III. Overall survival did not differ significantly between arms. No grade 5 toxicities occurred. Exploratory analysis suggested improved progression-free survival with ablation in patients with low or absent pretreatment circulating tumour cells.

nrg-cc001.methods: Phase 3 trial enrolling adult patients with brain metastases, randomised to hippocampal-avoidance whole brain radiotherapy plus memantine or whole brain radiotherapy plus memantine. The primary endpoint was time to cognitive function failure, defined as decline by the reliable change index on at least one cognitive test. Secondary endpoints were overall survival, intracranial progression-free survival, toxicity, and patient-reported symptom burden.
nrg-cc001.results: 518 patients were randomised between July 2015 and March 2018, with median follow-up of 7.9 months for living patients. Cognitive failure risk was lower with hippocampal avoidance, adjusted hazard ratio 0.74, p=0.02, driven by less deterioration in executive function at 4 months, 23.3% versus 40.4%, and in learning and memory at 6 months. Overall survival, intracranial progression-free survival, and toxicity did not differ.

nrg-oncology-krog-rtog-1119.methods: Randomised phase 2 trial in patients with HER2-positive breast cancer and at least one measurable, unirradiated brain metastasis. Patients were randomised to whole brain radiotherapy of 37.5 Gy over 3 weeks or stereotactic radiosurgery at size-based dosing, with or without concurrent lapatinib 1000 mg daily for 6 weeks. Secondary endpoints were objective response rate, lesion-specific response, central nervous system progression-free survival, and overall survival.
nrg-oncology-krog-rtog-1119.results: 143 patients were randomised from July 2012 to September 2019, with 116 analysable for the primary endpoint. Intracranial complete response at 12 weeks was 0% with radiotherapy plus lapatinib versus 6% with radiotherapy alone, one-sided p=0.97, and 12-week objective response was not improved. At 4 weeks objective response was 55% versus 42%. Grade 3 and 4 adverse event rates were 8% and 0% for radiotherapy and 28% and 6% with lapatinib.

nsabp-b-05.methods: Between 1972 and 1974, patients with primary breast cancer and pathologically positive axillary nodes were entered into an NSABP trial of L-phenylalanine mustard (L-PAM) against placebo as an adjuvant to mastectomy. This report gives findings through 10 years of observation, by age, number of positive nodes and nuclear grade.
nsabp-b-05.results: Overall, disease-free survival differed by 8% (P = .06) and survival by 5% (P = .4) in favour of L-PAM. Women aged 49 or younger given L-PAM had significantly prolonged disease-free survival (P = .03) and a survival benefit (P = .05), with a 37% reduction in mortality, greatest with one to three positive nodes. No advantage was seen in women 50 or older overall. In tumours of poor nuclear grade, L-PAM improved disease-free survival, distant disease-free survival and survival through 10 years regardless of age and nodal status, while well-differentiated tumours showed no benefit.

nsabp-b-09.methods: Between January 1977 and May 1980, 1,891 women with primary operable breast cancer and positive axillary nodes were randomised to L-phenylalanine mustard and 5-fluorouracil with or without tamoxifen (PFT against PF). The report gives life-table disease-free survival and survival through 5 years of observation (mean time on study 72 months), overall and by age, nodal status and tumour oestrogen and progesterone receptor levels.
nsabp-b-09.results: Overall there was a significant prolongation of disease-free survival with PFT (P = .002) but not of survival. The benefit was almost entirely restricted to women 50 or older with four or more positive nodes, who had a 66% greater chance of remaining disease free (P < .001) and a significant survival benefit (P = .02). Disease-free survival improved with PFT in tumours with oestrogen or progesterone receptor of 10 fmol or more. Women 49 or younger had no significant benefit, and their survival was adversely affected by tamoxifen, particularly with progesterone receptor of 0 to 9 fmol (P = .007).

nsabp-b-14.methods: Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of postoperative tamoxifen 10 mg twice daily in 2,644 patients with breast cancer, histologically negative axillary nodes, and estrogen-receptor-positive tumours of at least 10 fmol. Disease-free survival and survival were compared over four years of follow-up, with multivariate analysis of subgroups. A later correlative study measured a 21-gene recurrence score by RT-PCR in tumour blocks from tamoxifen-treated patients.
nsabp-b-14.results: Disease-free survival was 83 percent with tamoxifen versus 77 percent with placebo (P<0.00001), and survival 93 versus 92 percent (P=0.3). Benefit held in women 49 or younger (P=0.0005) and 50 or older (P=0.0008). Tamoxifen reduced local and distant treatment failure, contralateral tumours, and recurrence after lumpectomy. In 668 assayed tumours, 10-year distant recurrence was 6.8, 14.3 and 30.5 percent across low, intermediate and high recurrence-score groups.

nsabp-b-18.methods: 1,523 women with primary operable breast cancer were randomly assigned to doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide given preoperatively or postoperatively. Clinical tumour response to preoperative therapy was graded complete, partial or absent, and clinical complete responses were classified as pathologic complete response or residual invasive cells. Disease-free survival, distant disease-free survival and survival were estimated through five years and updated through nine years.
nsabp-b-18.results: No significant difference in disease-free survival, distant disease-free survival or survival at five years (P=.99, .70 and .83). At nine years survival was 69 versus 70 percent and disease-free survival 55 versus 53 percent. Lumpectomy with radiotherapy was more frequent after preoperative therapy (67.8 versus 59.8 percent). Relapse-free survival was 85.7 percent after pathologic complete response versus 63.9 percent with no clinical response (P<.0001).

nsabp-b-20.methods: 2,306 patients with node-negative, estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer were randomly assigned after surgery to one of three groups. 771 assessable patients received tamoxifen alone, 767 received methotrexate, fluorouracil and tamoxifen, and 768 received cyclophosphamide, methotrexate, fluorouracil and tamoxifen. Disease-free survival, distant disease-free survival and survival were estimated by the Kaplan-Meier method with two-sided P values. A later analysis measured the 21-gene recurrence score in 651 tumours.
nsabp-b-20.results: Through five years, disease-free survival was 90 and 89 percent with the two chemotherapy plus tamoxifen regimens versus 85 percent with tamoxifen (P=.01 and .001), distant disease-free survival 92 and 91 versus 87 percent, and survival 97 and 96 versus 94 percent. Benefit was greatest in patients aged 49 or under. Chemotherapy benefit interacted with recurrence score (P=.038), being large at scores of 31 or more and minimal below 18.

nsabp-b-21.methods: After lumpectomy, 1,009 node-negative women with invasive breast cancers of 1 cm or less were randomly assigned to tamoxifen (336), breast radiotherapy and placebo (336), or radiotherapy and tamoxifen (337). Ipsilateral breast tumour recurrence, distant recurrence and contralateral breast cancer were among the end points, with cumulative incidence computed accounting for competing risks.
nsabp-b-21.results: Radiotherapy and placebo gave a 49% lower hazard of ipsilateral breast tumour recurrence than tamoxifen alone, and radiotherapy and tamoxifen a 63% lower hazard than radiotherapy and placebo; against tamoxifen alone the combination cut the hazard by 81%. Cumulative incidence through 8 years was 16.5% with tamoxifen, 9.3% with radiotherapy and placebo and 2.8% with both, and radiotherapy reduced recurrence below tamoxifen alone regardless of oestrogen receptor status. Distant failures were infrequent and did not differ (P = .28). Tamoxifen reduced contralateral breast cancer against radiotherapy and placebo (hazard ratio 0.45, 95% CI 0.21 to 0.95). Survival was 93%, 94% and 93% (P = .93).

nsabp-b-27.methods: 2,411 women with operable breast cancer were randomly assigned to preoperative doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide followed by surgery, to the same chemotherapy followed by docetaxel then surgery, or to the same chemotherapy followed by surgery then docetaxel. Tamoxifen was started concurrently with chemotherapy in all groups. Median time on study for the 2,404 patients with follow-up was 77.9 months.
nsabp-b-27.results: Adding docetaxel did not significantly change disease-free survival or overall survival, with trends toward better disease-free survival. Docetaxel reduced local recurrence as a first event (P=.0034). Preoperative but not postoperative docetaxel improved disease-free survival in patients with a clinical partial response after AC (hazard ratio 0.71, 95 percent CI 0.55 to 0.91, P=.007). Pathologic complete response, doubled by preoperative docetaxel, predicted overall survival (hazard ratio 0.33, P<.0001).

nsabp-b-28.methods: Between August 1995 and May 1998, 3,060 patients with resected operable breast cancer and positive axillary nodes were randomly assigned to four cycles of doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide (1,529) or the same followed by four cycles of paclitaxel (1,531). Patients aged 50 or older and younger patients with receptor-positive tumours also received five years of tamoxifen. Postlumpectomy radiotherapy was required. Median follow-up was 64.6 months.
nsabp-b-28.results: Paclitaxel reduced the hazard of a disease-free survival event by 17 percent (relative risk 0.83, 95 percent CI 0.72 to 0.95, P=.006). Five-year disease-free survival was 76 percent with paclitaxel versus 72 percent without. Five-year overall survival was 85 percent in both groups (relative risk 0.93, 95 percent CI 0.78 to 1.12, P=.46). No significant interaction with receptor status or tamoxifen use was seen. Toxicity was acceptable.

nsabp-b-33.methods: Randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial begun in May 2001. Postmenopausal patients with breast cancer who were disease free after 5 years of tamoxifen were randomly assigned to 5 years of exemestane 25 mg daily or 5 years of placebo, with disease-free survival as the primary aim. In October 2003 the MA.17 result with letrozole led to termination of accrual, unblinding, and an offer of exemestane to the placebo group.
nsabp-b-33.results: At unblinding 1,598 patients had been randomly assigned; 72% of the exemestane group continued exemestane and 44% of the placebo group elected to take it. At a median follow-up of 30 months, original assignment to exemestane gave a borderline improvement in 4-year disease-free survival (91% versus 89%, relative risk 0.68, P = .07) and a significant improvement in 4-year relapse-free survival (96% versus 94%, relative risk 0.44, P = .004). Toxicity up to unblinding was acceptable.

nsabp-b-40.methods: Randomised trial in women with operable HER2-negative breast cancer. 1206 patients were assigned to four cycles of neoadjuvant docetaxel (100 mg/m2), docetaxel (75 mg/m2) plus capecitabine (825 mg/m2 twice a day, days 1 to 14) or docetaxel (75 mg/m2) plus gemcitabine (1000 mg/m2, days 1 and 8), all followed by four cycles of doxorubicin-cyclophosphamide, and also to receive or not receive bevacizumab (15 mg/kg) for the first six cycles. The primary aims were whether capecitabine or gemcitabine, and whether bevacizumab, increased the rate of pathological complete response in the breast.
nsabp-b-40.results: Adding capecitabine or gemcitabine to docetaxel did not significantly increase pathological complete response (29.7% and 31.8%, against 32.7% with docetaxel alone, P = 0.69) and increased hand-foot syndrome, mucositis and neutropenia. Adding bevacizumab increased pathological complete response from 28.2% to 34.5% (P = 0.02), an effect that differed between the hormone receptor-positive and hormone receptor-negative subgroups. Bevacizumab increased hypertension, left ventricular systolic dysfunction, the hand-foot syndrome and mucositis.

nsabp-b-41.methods: Open-label randomised phase 3 trial in women aged 18 or older with operable HER2-positive breast cancer and ECOG performance status 0 or 1. All received four cycles of doxorubicin 60 mg/m2 and cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m2, then four cycles of weekly paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 with weekly trastuzumab, daily lapatinib 1250 mg, or weekly trastuzumab plus daily lapatinib 750 mg until surgery. Randomisation was 1:1:1. All received trastuzumab after surgery to complete 52 weeks.
nsabp-b-41.results: 529 women were enrolled and 519 had pathological response determined. Breast pathological complete response occurred in 93 of 177 patients on trastuzumab (52.5 percent), 91 of 171 on lapatinib (53.2 percent, p=0.9852) and 106 of 171 on the combination (62.0 percent, p=0.095). Grade 3 diarrhoea affected 2, 20 and 27 percent of the three groups (p<0.0001). Symptomatic congestive heart failure occurred in 4, 4 and under 1 percent.

nsabp-b06.methods: A randomised trial begun in 1976. A total of 1851 women with invasive breast cancer, for whom follow-up data were available and nodal status was known, underwent randomly assigned treatment consisting of total mastectomy, lumpectomy alone, or lumpectomy plus breast irradiation. Outcomes were estimated by Kaplan-Meier and cumulative-incidence methods. Follow-up extended to 20 years.
nsabp-b06.results: The cumulative incidence of recurrent tumour in the ipsilateral breast was 14.3% after lumpectomy plus irradiation against 39.2% after lumpectomy alone, P<0.001. Disease-free survival, distant-disease-free survival and overall survival did not differ significantly among the three groups. The hazard ratio for death was 1.05 (95% CI 0.90-1.23, P=0.51) for lumpectomy alone versus mastectomy and 0.97 (0.83-1.14, P=0.74) for lumpectomy plus irradiation versus mastectomy.

nsabp-b31-n9831.methods: Planned joint analysis of two adjuvant trials. In all, 4046 patients with HER2-positive operable breast cancer were enrolled to receive doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide followed by paclitaxel with or without trastuzumab. The required number of events for the definitive overall survival analysis, 710 events, was reached in September 2012. Updated analyses of overall disease-free survival and related subgroups were also performed.
nsabp-b31-n9831.results: Median time on study was 8.4 years. Adding trastuzumab gave a 37% relative improvement in overall survival, hazard ratio 0.63 (95% CI 0.54-0.73), P<0.001, and raised the 10-year overall survival rate from 75.2% to 84%. Disease-free survival improved by 40%, hazard ratio 0.60 (95% CI 0.53-0.68), P<0.001, with the 10-year disease-free survival rate rising from 62.2% to 73.7%. All patient subgroups benefited.

nsabp-b32.methods: Randomised controlled phase 3 trial at 80 centres in Canada and the USA between May 1999 and February 2004. Women with invasive breast cancer were randomly assigned 1:1 to sentinel lymph node resection plus axillary dissection (group 1) or to sentinel node resection alone with axillary dissection only if the sentinel nodes were positive (group 2). Sentinel node resection used blue dye and radioactive tracer. The primary endpoint was overall survival.
nsabp-b32.results: 5611 women were randomly assigned and 3989 had pathologically negative sentinel nodes. Among 3986 such patients with follow-up, 309 deaths occurred, 140 of 1975 in group 1 and 169 of 2011 in group 2, hazard ratio 1.20 (95% CI 0.96-1.50, p=0.12). Eight-year overall survival was 91.8% in group 1 and 90.3% in group 2. The disease-free survival hazard ratio was 1.05 (0.90-1.22, p=0.54), with 8-year estimates 82.4% and 81.5%.

nsabp-b39.methods: Randomised phase 3 equivalence trial at 154 clinical centres in the USA, Canada, Ireland and Israel. Adult women with stage 0, I or II breast cancer up to 3 cm and lumpectomy with negative margins were assigned 1:1 to whole-breast irradiation, 50 Gy in 25 fractions over 5 weeks, or to accelerated partial breast irradiation, 34 Gy brachytherapy or 38.5 Gy external beam in 10 fractions. The primary outcome was ipsilateral breast tumour recurrence as a first recurrence.
nsabp-b39.results: Between March 2005 and April 2013, 4216 women were enrolled, 2109 to whole-breast irradiation and 2107 to partial breast irradiation. At a median follow-up of 10.2 years, ipsilateral breast tumour recurrence occurred in 90 of 2089 partial irradiation patients (4%) and 71 of 2036 whole-breast patients (3%), hazard ratio 1.22 (90% CI 0.94-1.58). The 10-year cumulative incidence was 4.6% against 3.9%. Deaths from recurring breast cancer were 49 of 2093 and 44 of 2039.

nsabp-b42.methods: Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial at 158 centres in the USA, Canada and Ireland. Postmenopausal women with stage I-IIIA hormone receptor-positive breast cancer who were disease free after about 5 years of an aromatase inhibitor, or tamoxifen followed by an aromatase inhibitor, were assigned 1:1 to 5 years of letrozole 2.5 mg daily or placebo. Randomisation was stratified by nodal status, previous tamoxifen use and lowest bone mineral density T score. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival.
nsabp-b42.results: Between September 2006 and January 2010, 3966 patients were assigned to letrozole (n=1983) or placebo (n=1983), with follow-up data for 3903 and a median follow-up of 6.9 years. Letrozole did not significantly improve disease-free survival, with 292 events against 339 on placebo, hazard ratio 0.85 (95% CI 0.73-0.999), p=0.048. Seven-year disease-free survival was 84.7% with letrozole and 81.3% with placebo. The 10-year update reported a disease-free survival hazard ratio of 0.85 (0.74-0.96), P=.01.

nsabp-b51.methods: Randomised trial of regional nodal irradiation in patients with biopsy-proven node-positive breast cancer who reached ypN0 status after neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Patients with clinical stage T1 to T3, N1, M0 disease were assigned to regional nodal irradiation or no regional nodal irradiation. The primary end point was the invasive breast cancer recurrence-free interval, defined as freedom from invasive recurrence or death from breast cancer. Secondary end points were locoregional and distant recurrence-free interval, disease-free survival and overall survival.
nsabp-b51.results: A total of 1641 patients were enrolled and 1556 were included in the primary-event analysis, 772 in the irradiation group and 784 in the no-irradiation group. After a median follow-up of 59.5 months there were 109 primary end-point events, 50 with irradiation and 59 without. The hazard ratio for the invasive breast cancer recurrence-free interval was 0.88 (95% CI 0.60-1.28, P=0.51), with point estimates of 92.7% and 91.8%. Grade 4 adverse events occurred in 0.5% and 0.1%.

olaparib-hgsoc-tnbc.methods: Phase 2, multicentre, open-label, non-randomised study in women with advanced high-grade serous or undifferentiated ovarian carcinoma or triple-negative breast cancer, who received olaparib 400 mg twice daily and were stratified by whether they had a BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation. The primary endpoint was objective response rate by RECIST, analysed in patients with measurable lesions at baseline; all treated patients were included in the analysis of toxic effects.
olaparib-hgsoc-tnbc.results: 91 patients were enrolled (65 with ovarian and 26 with breast cancer) and 90 were treated between July 2008 and September 2009. In the ovarian cohorts, confirmed objective responses were seen in seven (41%, 95% CI 22 to 64) of 17 patients with BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations and 11 (24%, 14 to 38) of 46 without. No confirmed objective responses were reported in patients with breast cancer. The commonest adverse events in breast cancer patients were fatigue (50%), nausea (62%), vomiting (35%) and decreased appetite (27%).

olaparib-study42.methods: Multicentre phase 2 study of olaparib 400 mg twice daily in individuals with a germline BRCA1/2 mutation and recurrent cancer. Eligibility included ovarian cancer resistant to prior platinum, breast cancer with at least three chemotherapy regimens for metastatic disease, pancreatic cancer with prior gemcitabine, or prostate cancer with progression on hormonal and one systemic therapy. The primary efficacy end point was tumour response rate.
olaparib-study42.results: 298 patients received treatment and were evaluable. The tumour response rate was 26.2% (78 of 298; 95% CI 21.3 to 31.6) overall, and 31.1% (60 of 193), 12.9% (8 of 62; 5.7 to 23.9), 21.7% (5 of 23) and 50.0% (4 of 8) in ovarian, breast, pancreatic and prostate cancer. Stable disease for at least 8 weeks was seen in 42% overall and in 47% (34.0 to 59.9) of breast cancer patients. The commonest adverse events were fatigue, nausea and vomiting; grade 3 or higher events occurred in 54%, most often anaemia (17%).

olson-neoadjuvant-letrozole.methods: Multicentre phase II clinical trial conducted to investigate the value of neoadjuvant aromatase inhibitor therapy for US surgical practice. One hundred fifteen postmenopausal women with ER- or PgR-positive breast cancer larger than 2 cm were enrolled in a trial of 16 to 24 weeks of letrozole 2.5 mg daily before operation.
olson-neoadjuvant-letrozole.results: One hundred six patients were eligible for primary analysis; 96 underwent operations, 7 received chemotherapy after progressive disease and 3 did not undergo an operation. Baseline surgical status was marginal for breast-conserving surgery in 48 (45%), definitely ineligible in 47 (44%) and inoperable by standard mastectomy in 11 (10%). The overall RECIST clinical response rate in the breast was 62%, with 12% experiencing progressive disease. Fifty percent underwent breast-conserving surgery, including 30 of 46 (65%) patients initially marginal and 15 of 39 (38%) initially ineligible for it, and all 11 inoperable patients had operations, 3 (27%) with breast conservation.

olympia.methods: Phase 3, double-blind, randomised trial in patients with HER2-negative early breast cancer carrying germline pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants and high-risk clinicopathological factors, who had received local treatment and neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to 1 year of oral olaparib or placebo. The primary end point was invasive disease-free survival.
olympia.results: A total of 1836 patients underwent randomisation. At a prespecified interim analysis with median follow-up 2.5 years, 3-year invasive disease-free survival was 85.9% with olaparib and 77.1% with placebo, difference 8.8 percentage points (95% CI 4.5-13.0), hazard ratio 0.58 (99.5% CI 0.41-0.82), P<0.001. Three-year distant disease-free survival was 87.5% against 80.4%, hazard ratio 0.57. Deaths numbered 59 against 86. The 6.1-year update reported 6-year overall survival of 87.5% against 83.2%, hazard ratio 0.72 (95% CI 0.56-0.93).

olympiad.methods: Randomized, open-label, phase 3 trial comparing olaparib monotherapy with standard therapy. Patients had a germline BRCA mutation and HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer and had received no more than two previous chemotherapy regimens for metastatic disease. Randomisation was 2:1 to olaparib tablets 300 mg twice daily or to single-agent chemotherapy of the physician's choice, being capecitabine, eribulin, or vinorelbine in 21-day cycles. The primary end point was progression-free survival by blinded independent central review, analysed by intention to treat.
olympiad.results: Of 302 patients randomized, 205 received olaparib and 97 standard therapy. Median progression-free survival was 7.0 months with olaparib versus 4.2 months with standard therapy (hazard ratio 0.58, 95% CI 0.43 to 0.80, P<0.001). Response rate was 59.9% versus 28.8%. Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 36.6% versus 50.5%. Discontinuation for toxic effects occurred in 4.9% versus 7.7%. The 2019 final overall survival report gave median overall survival 19.3 versus 17.1 months (HR 0.90, P = 0.513).

ont-380.methods: Phase 1 study of ONT-380 (ARRY-380), an oral selective HER2 inhibitor, given twice daily in continuous 28-day cycles to patients with HER2-positive advanced solid tumours. A modified 3 + 3 dose escalation determined the maximum tolerated dose, after which an expansion cohort of patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer was enrolled. Pharmacokinetics of ONT-380 and a metabolite were determined and response was evaluated by RECIST.
ont-380.results: Fifty patients received ONT-380 (33 in escalation, 17 in expansion), 43 of them with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer, after a median of five prior anticancer regimens. Dose-limiting transaminase increases occurred at 800 mg twice daily, so 600 mg twice daily was the maximum tolerated dose. Adverse events were usually grade 1 or 2, including nausea (56%), diarrhoea (52%), fatigue (50%) and vomiting (40%); five patients (19%) at the maximum tolerated dose had grade 3 events. The half-life was 5.38 hours. In 22 evaluable patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer treated at or above the maximum tolerated dose, the response rate was 14% (all partial) and the clinical benefit rate 27%.

opera-01.methods: Ongoing global phase III, randomised, open-label, active-controlled study in men and women aged 18 years or older with ER-positive, HER2-negative inoperable locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer, regardless of ESR1 mutation status, whose disease progressed after endocrine therapy combined with a CDK4/6 inhibitor, with one additional line of endocrine therapy allowed. A dose-selection part first randomised patients 1:1:1 to palazestrant 90 mg or 120 mg once daily or to investigator's choice of standard endocrine therapy. The 90 mg dose was selected for the second part, which randomises patients 1:1 to palazestrant or to investigator's choice of fulvestrant or an aromatase inhibitor, stratified by ESR1 status in circulating tumour DNA, prior endocrine lines for advanced disease and visceral disease. The dual primary endpoint is progression-free survival by blinded independent review, assessed separately in tumours with an ESR1 mutation and in tumours without a detectable one. Overall survival in each population is the key secondary endpoint.

optimize-2.methods: Prospective randomised double-blind multicentre phase 3 trial at 102 centres in the United States. Women with bone metastases from breast cancer who had already received nine or more doses of zoledronic acid or pamidronate were randomised 1:1 to zoledronic acid every 4 weeks or every 12 weeks for one year, with placebo at the intervening infusions. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients with one or more skeletal-related event on study.
optimize-2.results: 416 women were randomised, 200 to the 4-weekly schedule, 203 to the 12-weekly schedule and 13 to placebo. After one year of follow-up, skeletal-related events occurred in 44 patients (22.0%) on the 4-weekly schedule and 47 (23.2%) on the 12-weekly schedule, proportional difference -1.2%, P = .02 for non-inferiority. Time to first skeletal-related event did not differ, hazard ratio 1.06 (95% CI 0.70 to 1.60, P = .79). Mean skeletal morbidity rate was 0.46 against 0.50 events per year. Safety profiles were comparable.

optitrop-breast01.methods: Randomised phase 3 trial of sacituzumab tirumotecan against chemotherapy in patients with locally recurrent or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer who had received two or more prior therapies, including at least one for metastatic disease. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival by blinded independent central review, which was met at the protocol-specified interim analysis. Overall survival was a key secondary endpoint.
optitrop-breast01.results: 263 patients were randomised, 130 to sacituzumab tirumotecan and 133 to chemotherapy. At the final progression-free survival analysis, median progression-free survival by blinded independent central review was 6.7 months (95% CI 5.5 to 8.0) versus 2.5 months (1.7 to 2.7), hazard ratio 0.32 (95% CI 0.24 to 0.44), P < 0.00001. At the protocol-specified interim overall survival analysis, median overall survival was not reached (95% CI 11.2 months to not estimable) versus 9.4 months (8.5 to 11.7), hazard ratio 0.53 (0.36 to 0.78), P = 0.0005. Objective response was 45.4% versus 12.0%, and median duration of response 7.1 versus 3.0 months. The most common treatment-related adverse event with sacituzumab tirumotecan was haematological toxicity. At the final overall survival analysis, at a median follow-up of 29.4 months, median overall survival was 14.7 months (12.1 to 20.1) versus 9.9 months (8.6 to 11.8), hazard ratio 0.60 (0.45 to 0.80), and 30-month overall survival 26.8% versus 13.2%. Subsequent antibody-drug conjugate therapy was received by 27.8% of the chemotherapy group. Adjusted for it by the rank-preserving structural failure time model, median overall survival was 14.7 months against an estimated 9.4 months, hazard ratio 0.55 (0.39 to 0.73), and a censoring analysis gave a hazard ratio of 0.59 (0.43 to 0.82). The most common grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events were decreased neutrophil count, decreased white blood cell count and anaemia.

p024.methods: Randomised, double-blind, multicentre study in 337 postmenopausal women with untreated primary breast cancer positive for estrogen or progesterone receptors. Patients received letrozole 2.5 mg or tamoxifen 20 mg once daily for four months before surgery. None were candidates for breast-conserving surgery at baseline and 14 percent were considered inoperable. The primary endpoint was overall objective response by clinical palpation, with response on ultrasound and mammography and breast-conserving surgery rate as secondary endpoints.
p024.results: Objective response by clinical palpation was 55 percent with letrozole versus 36 percent with tamoxifen (P<0.001). Ultrasound response was 35 versus 25 percent (P=0.042) and mammographic response 34 versus 16 percent (P<0.001). Breast-conserving surgery was performed in 45 percent of the letrozole group versus 35 percent of the tamoxifen group (P=0.022). Both treatments were well tolerated.

p1.methods: Women at increased risk for breast cancer were randomly assigned to placebo (n=6707) or tamoxifen 20 mg per day (n=6681) for 5 years, 13,388 in total. Eligible women were 60 years of age or older, were 35 to 59 years with a 5-year predicted breast cancer risk of at least 1.66% by the Gail algorithm, or had a history of lobular carcinoma in situ.
p1.results: Tamoxifen reduced invasive breast cancer risk by 49% (two-sided P<.00001), with cumulative incidence through 69 months of 43.4 versus 22.0 per 1000 women on placebo and tamoxifen. Noninvasive breast cancer fell by 50% (P<.002). Estrogen receptor-positive tumours fell by 69%, with no difference in receptor-negative tumours. Hip, radius and spine fractures were reduced. Endometrial cancer rose (risk ratio 2.53, 95% CI 1.35 to 4.97). Stroke, pulmonary embolism and deep-vein thrombosis rates were elevated.
