Patients were randomised to durvalumab 10 mg/kg every 2 weeks or to maintenance chemotherapy. Exploratory analyses examined PD-L1 status, CD274 gain or amplification, tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes and homologous recombination deficiency.
safir02-breast-immuno.results: 199 patients were randomised. In the overall population durvalumab did not improve progression-free survival (adjusted hazard ratio 1.40, 95% CI 1.00 to 1.96, P=0.047) or overall survival (adjusted hazard ratio 0.84, 0.54 to 1.29, P=0.423). In an exploratory subgroup of 82 patients with triple-negative disease, durvalumab improved overall survival (hazard ratio 0.54, 0.30 to 0.97, P=0.0377), with hazard ratios of 0.37 in PD-L1-positive and 0.49 in PD-L1-negative triple-negative disease. In triple-negative disease the hazard ratio for overall survival was 0.18 (0.05 to 0.71) with CD274 gain or amplification and 1.12 (0.42 to 2.99) with CD274 normal or loss. Maintenance chemotherapy was more effective than durvalumab in hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative disease.

scorad.methods: Multicentre non-inferiority randomised clinical trial at 42 UK and 5 Australian radiotherapy centres, recruiting between February 2008 and April 2016 with final follow-up in September 2017. Eligible patients had metastatic cancer with spinal cord or cauda equina compression, life expectancy over 8 weeks and no previous radiotherapy to the same area. They were randomised to single-fraction 8 Gy or to 20 Gy in five fractions. The primary endpoint was ambulatory status at week 8 on a 4-point scale, with a non-inferiority margin of -11%.
scorad.results: Of 686 randomised patients, 342 were analysed for the primary endpoint because 255 died before the week 8 assessment. Ambulatory grade 1 or 2 at week 8 was reached by 115 of 166 (69.3%) after a single fraction against 128 of 176 (72.7%) after five fractions, difference -3.5%, P for non-inferiority = .06. Non-inferiority was met at week 1 (-0.4%, P = .004), week 4 (-0.7%, P = .01) and week 12 (4.1%, P = .002). Overall survival at 12 weeks was 50% against 55%, hazard ratio 1.02 (95% CI 0.74 to 1.41).

senomac.methods: Noninferiority randomized trial. Patients with clinically node-negative primary T1 to T3 breast cancer and one or two sentinel-node macrometastases larger than 2 mm were assigned 1:1 to completion axillary-lymph-node dissection or to sentinel-node biopsy only. Adjuvant systemic treatment and radiation therapy followed national guidelines. The primary end point was overall survival. This report gives per-protocol and modified intention-to-treat analyses of recurrence-free survival, with a noninferiority margin of 1.44 for the hazard ratio.
senomac.results: 2766 patients were enrolled in five countries between January 2015 and December 2021. The per-protocol population was 2540 patients, 1335 assigned to sentinel-node biopsy only and 1205 to dissection. Nodal radiation therapy was given to 89.9% and 88.4% respectively. Median follow-up was 46.8 months and 191 patients had recurrence or died. Estimated 5-year recurrence-free survival was 89.7% with sentinel-node biopsy only and 88.7% with dissection, country-adjusted hazard ratio 0.89 (95% CI 0.66 to 1.19), P<0.001 for noninferiority.

sentina.methods: Four-arm prospective multicentre cohort study at 103 institutions in Germany and Austria. Women scheduled for neoadjuvant chemotherapy were enrolled. Clinically node-negative patients had sentinel-lymph-node biopsy before chemotherapy (arm A), and those with a positive node had a second biopsy afterwards (arm B). Clinically node-positive patients who converted to node-negative had biopsy plus axillary dissection (arm C). Those still node-positive had dissection alone (arm D). The primary endpoint was the false-negative rate in arm C.
sentina.results: 1737 patients received treatment. Among 1022 women biopsied before chemotherapy the detection rate was 99.1% (1013 of 1022). In arm C the detection rate was 80.1% (474 of 592) and the false-negative rate was 14.2% (32 of 226). The false-negative rate was 24.3% (17 of 70) with one node removed and 18.5% (10 of 54) with two. In arm B the detection rate was 60.8% (219 of 360) and the false-negative rate 51.6% (33 of 64).

serena2.methods: Open-label randomised phase 2 trial at 74 centres in Asia, Europe, the Middle East and North America. Post-menopausal women with oestrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, performance status 0 or 1, and progression on at least one prior endocrine therapy were randomised 1:1:1:1 to oral camizestrant 75 mg, 150 mg or 300 mg once daily, or intramuscular fulvestrant 500 mg. The primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival by intention to treat.
serena2.results: 240 patients were randomly assigned between May 2020 and August 2021: 74 to camizestrant 75 mg, 73 to 150 mg, 20 to 300 mg and 73 to fulvestrant. Median progression-free survival was 7.2 months with 75 mg, 7.7 months with 150 mg and 3.7 months with fulvestrant. Hazard ratios versus fulvestrant were 0.59 (90% CI 0.42-0.82, p=0.017) for 75 mg and 0.64 (0.46-0.89, p=0.0090) for 150 mg. Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 53%, 67% and 18%.

serena6.methods: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised phase 3 trial at 264 centres in 23 countries. Patients on first-line aromatase inhibitor plus CDK4/6 inhibitor for at least 6 months for oestrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer had ctDNA tested for ESR1 mutation every 2-3 months. Those with an ESR1 mutation and no radiological progression were randomised 1:1 to switch to camizestrant 75 mg daily with the same CDK4/6 inhibitor or to continue the aromatase inhibitor. The primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival.
serena6.results: 3325 patients were screened and 3256 had at least one ESR1 mutation test. 548 had a positive test and 315 were randomised, 157 to camizestrant plus CDK4/6 inhibitor and 158 to aromatase inhibitor plus CDK4/6 inhibitor. After median follow-up of 23.5 months, median progression-free survival was 16.8 versus 9.2 months (HR 0.45, 95% CI 0.34-0.59). Median second progression-free survival was 25.7 versus 19.1 months (HR 0.63, 0.46-0.86, p=0.0037). Grade 3-4 neutropenia occurred in 27% versus 17%.

sgntuc-019.methods: SGNTUC-019 is an open-label phase 2 basket study of tucatinib, a HER2-targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor, in combination with trastuzumab in patients with HER2-altered solid tumours. This record covers its breast cohort, 31 heavily pretreated female patients with HER2-mutated metastatic breast cancer who were also HER2-negative by local testing. Patients with hormone receptor-positive disease also received fulvestrant. The primary endpoint was overall response rate, with duration of response and progression-free survival as secondary endpoints. The regimen is chemotherapy-free.
sgntuc-019.results: The overall response rate, the primary endpoint, was 41.9% (90% CI 26.9 to 58.2). The secondary endpoints of duration of response and progression-free survival were 12.6 months (90% CI 4.7 to not estimable) and 9.5 months (90% CI 5.4 to 13.8) respectively. Responses were observed across various HER2 mutations, including mutations in the tyrosine kinase and extracellular domains. No new safety signals were detected. The authors concluded that the chemotherapy-free combination showed clinically meaningful antitumour activity with durable responses and favourable tolerability in heavily pretreated patients, and that the data support further investigation of HER2-targeted therapy in this population.

shorther.methods: Randomized phase III non-inferiority trial. HER2-positive breast cancer patients with node-positive disease, or node-negative disease with at least one risk factor (tumor over 2 cm, grade 3, lympho-vascular invasion, Ki-67 above 20%, age 35 years or younger, or hormone receptor negativity), were assigned to sequential anthracycline-taxane chemotherapy plus 1 year of trastuzumab (arm A) or plus 9 weeks of trastuzumab (arm B). The primary end point was disease-free survival, with a non-inferiority margin of 1.29.
shorther.results: 1254 patients were randomized, 627 to 1 year and 626 to 9 weeks. Five-year disease-free survival was 88% with 1 year and 85% with 9 weeks, hazard ratio 1.13 (90% CI 0.89 to 1.42), the upper limit crossing the non-inferiority margin. The Bayesian probability of non-inferiority was 80%. Five-year overall survival was 95.2% and 95.0% (hazard ratio 1.07, 90% CI 0.74 to 1.56). Cardiac events were fewer with 9 weeks, risk ratio 0.33.

sofea.methods: Composite multicentre phase 3 trial in the UK and South Korea. Postmenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer progressing on a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor were randomised 1:1:1 to fulvestrant 500 mg then 250 mg every 28 days plus anastrozole 1 mg, fulvestrant plus matched placebo, or exemestane 25 mg daily. Stratification was by centre and previous setting of aromatase inhibitor use. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival by intention to treat.
sofea.results: 723 patients were randomised between March 2004 and August 2010, 243 to fulvestrant plus anastrozole, 231 to fulvestrant plus placebo and 249 to exemestane. Median progression-free survival was 4.4, 4.8 and 3.4 months. Hazard ratios were 1.00 (95% CI 0.83-1.21, p = 0.98) for the two fulvestrant arms and 0.95 (0.79-1.14, p = 0.56) for fulvestrant plus placebo versus exemestane. 87 serious adverse events were reported and grade 3-4 events were rare.

soft.methods: Premenopausal women with breast cancer were randomly assigned to 5 years of tamoxifen, tamoxifen plus ovarian suppression, or exemestane plus ovarian suppression in SOFT. Randomization was stratified according to receipt of chemotherapy. This report gives updated results from SOFT and from the parallel TEXT trial, in which women received tamoxifen plus ovarian suppression or exemestane plus ovarian suppression.
soft.results: In SOFT, 8-year disease-free survival was 78.9% with tamoxifen alone, 83.2% with tamoxifen plus ovarian suppression, and 85.9% with exemestane plus ovarian suppression (P=0.009 for the first two). Eight-year overall survival was 91.5%, 93.3% and 92.1% (P=0.01 for the same comparison). Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 24.6%, 31.0% and 32.3%. The 12-year report gave disease-free survival of 71.9%, 76.1% and 79.0%, and overall survival of 86.8%, 89.0% and 89.4%.

soft-text.methods: Combined analysis of the SOFT and TEXT trials. Premenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive early breast cancer were enrolled, with 3047 in SOFT and 2660 in TEXT intention-to-treat populations. SOFT randomised women to 5 years of tamoxifen, tamoxifen plus OFS, or exemestane plus OFS. TEXT randomised women to 5 years of tamoxifen plus OFS or exemestane plus OFS. 4690 women were included in the combined intention-to-treat population for exemestane plus OFS versus tamoxifen plus OFS, of whom 86.0% had HER2-negative tumours. Median follow-up was 16 years for the combined analysis.
soft-text.results: In the combined analysis, 15-year disease-free survival was 74.9% with exemestane plus OFS and 71.3% with tamoxifen plus OFS (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.73 to 0.92, P<0.01). 15-year distant recurrence-free interval was 86.5% and 83.9% (HR 0.83, 0.71 to 0.97, P=0.02). 15-year overall survival was 87.8% and 87.0% (HR 0.94, 0.80 to 1.11, P=0.48). Among women with HER2-negative tumours (n=4035), exemestane plus OFS reduced distant recurrence (HR 0.75, 0.63 to 0.90), with a smaller reduction in deaths (HR 0.89, 0.74 to 1.06). The absolute 15-year overall survival improvement in HER2-negative cohorts was larger in those who received chemotherapy, at 3.9% in SOFT and 2.5% in TEXT.

solar1.methods: Randomized phase 3 trial comparing alpelisib 300 mg per day plus fulvestrant 500 mg with placebo plus fulvestrant in patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer who had received endocrine therapy previously. Patients were enrolled into two cohorts on the basis of tumour tissue PIK3CA mutation status. The primary end point was investigator-assessed progression-free survival in the mutated cohort. Secondary end points included overall response and safety.
solar1.results: 572 patients underwent randomization, including 341 with confirmed PIK3CA mutations. In the mutated cohort median progression-free survival at a median follow-up of 20 months was 11.0 months with alpelisib versus 5.7 months with placebo (HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.50 to 0.85). The hazard ratio in the non-mutated cohort was 0.85. Grade 3 or 4 hyperglycaemia occurred in 36.6% versus 0.7%. The final overall survival report gave 39.3 versus 31.4 months (HR 0.86).

sold.methods: Open-label trial that randomly assigned 2,176 women with HER2-positive early breast cancer 1:1 between 2008 and 2014 in seven countries. All received three cycles of three-weekly docetaxel, 80 or 100 mg/m2, plus trastuzumab for 9 weeks, then three cycles of fluorouracil, epirubicin and cyclophosphamide. The 9-week group received no further trastuzumab. Controls continued trastuzumab to 1 year. Disease-free survival was compared with a non-inferiority margin of 1.3.
sold.results: 2,174 women were analysed, median age 56 years, median follow-up 5.2 years. Non-inferiority of the 9-week treatment was not demonstrated for disease-free survival (hazard ratio 1.39, 2-sided 90% CI 1.12 to 1.72). Distant disease-free survival and overall survival did not differ substantially. Cardiac failure occurred in 36 patients (3%) in the 1-year group and 21 (2%) in the 9-week group. Patients given 80 mg/m2 docetaxel had inferior disease-free survival.

sole.methods: Multicentre open-label phase 3 trial at 240 centres in 22 countries. Postmenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive, node-positive operable breast cancer who had completed 4 to 6 years of adjuvant endocrine therapy were randomised 1:1 to continuous letrozole 2.5 mg daily for 5 years or intermittent letrozole for 9 months with a 3-month break in years 1 to 4 and continuous dosing in year 5. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival by intention to treat.
sole.results: 4884 women were enrolled and 4851 formed the intention-to-treat population, 2425 intermittent and 2426 continuous. At a median follow-up of 60 months, disease-free survival was 85.8% versus 87.5% (hazard ratio 1.08, 95% CI 0.93-1.26, p = 0.31). The final analysis at 84 months gave 7-year disease-free survival of 81.4% versus 81.5% (hazard ratio 1.03, 95% CI 0.91-1.17). Grade 3-5 hypertension occurred in 24% versus 21%.

sonia.methods: Phase 3 trial that randomized 1,050 patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer who had received no previous therapy for advanced disease to a CDK4/6 inhibitor in the first-line or the second-line setting. All patients received the same endocrine therapy, an aromatase inhibitor first line and fulvestrant second line. The primary end point was time from randomization to disease progression after second-line treatment, PFS2.
sonia.results: Median PFS2 was 31.0 months with first-line use and 26.8 months with second-line use (hazard ratio 0.87, 95% CI 0.74 to 1.03, P = 0.10). Health-related quality of life was similar. Median CDK4/6 inhibitor treatment duration was 24.6 versus 8.1 months, with 2,763 versus 1,591 grade 3 or higher adverse events. The later overall survival report gave median overall survival of 47.9 versus 48.1 months (HR 0.91).

sophia.methods: Final overall survival analysis of a randomized phase 3 trial in previously treated HER2-positive advanced breast cancer. 536 patients in the intention-to-treat population were assigned to margetuximab 15 mg/kg every 3 weeks plus chemotherapy (n = 266) or trastuzumab 6 mg/kg every 3 weeks after an 8 mg/kg loading dose plus chemotherapy (n = 270). Primary end points were progression-free survival, reported earlier, and overall survival. The analysis was triggered by 385 prespecified events.
sophia.results: Median overall survival was 21.6 months with margetuximab versus 21.9 months with trastuzumab (hazard ratio 0.95, 95% CI 0.77 to 1.17, P = .620). Preplanned exploratory CD16A genotyping suggested better overall survival with margetuximab in CD16A-158FF patients (23.6 versus 19.2 months, HR 0.72) and better overall survival with trastuzumab in CD16A-158VV patients (31.1 versus 22.0 months, HR 1.77, 95% CI 1.01 to 3.12). Safety was comparable.

sound.methods: Prospective phase 3 noninferiority randomised trial in Italy, Switzerland, Spain and Chile. 1463 women of any age with breast cancer up to 2 cm and a negative preoperative axillary ultrasonography result were enrolled between February 2012 and June 2017. Patients were randomised 1:1 to sentinel lymph node biopsy or no axillary surgery. The primary endpoint was 5-year distant disease-free survival analysed as intention to treat.
sound.results: 1405 women were analysed by intention to treat, 708 assigned to sentinel lymph node biopsy and 697 to no axillary surgery. 97 patients (13.7%) in the biopsy group had positive axillary nodes. Median follow-up was 5.7 years. Five-year distant disease-free survival was 97.7% with biopsy and 98.0% without axillary surgery (hazard ratio 0.84, noninferiority P = .02). There were 21 deaths in the biopsy group and 18 in the no axillary surgery group.

soy-beverage-hot-flashes.methods: Randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial in postmenopausal women with moderate hot flashes previously treated for early-stage breast cancer. Women were stratified for tamoxifen use and randomised to a soy beverage containing 90 mg of isoflavones (n = 59) or a placebo rice beverage (n = 64). Hot flash number and severity were recorded in a daily diary for 4 weeks at baseline and 12 weeks on 500 mL of soy or placebo beverage.
soy-beverage-hot-flashes.results: There were no significant differences between soy and placebo in the number of hot flashes or hot flash scores, although both groups had significant reductions. Mild gastrointestinal side effects occurred in both groups but were more frequent and severe with soy. Mean serum genistein at 6 weeks was higher with soy (0.61 vs 0.43 micromol/L, P = .02). Acceptability and compliance were high in both groups.

soy-tablets-hot-flashes.methods: Double-blind crossover trial in breast cancer survivors with substantial hot flashes. After randomisation and a 1-week baseline without therapy, patients took soy tablets or placebo for 4 weeks and then crossed over for the last 4 weeks. Patients completed a daily questionnaire on hot flash frequency, intensity and side effects.
soy-tablets-hot-flashes.results: Of 177 women randomised who started the study substance, 155 (88%) provided usable data over the first 5 weeks and 149 over the whole 9 weeks. There was no suggestion that soy was more effective than placebo. At study completion, patients preferred soy 33% of the time, placebo 37% and neither 31%. No toxicity was observed.

srs-plus-nivolumab.methods: Non-randomised open-label phase Ib study. Patients aged 18 or older with breast cancer brain metastases of any subtype, ECOG performance status 2 or better and 10 or fewer brain metastases received nivolumab 480 mg intravenously every 4 weeks, with stereotactic radiosurgery one week after the first dose. Blood was collected at baseline and every 4 weeks for flow cytometry and cell-free DNA assessment.
srs-plus-nivolumab.results: 12 patients received radiosurgery to 17 brain metastases, 50% triple negative, 33% HR+/HER2- and 17% HR-/HER2+. At a median follow-up of 56 months there was no radionecrosis. Two lesions failed locally, for 12-month local control of 94%. Median distant intracranial control was 7.4 months, systemic progression-free survival 7.7 months and overall survival 24.7 months. Intracranial control was associated with lower CD4 regulatory T cells and higher CD4 effector memory T cells.

stage.methods: Double-blind, randomised, parallel-group, multicentre phase 3 trial. Premenopausal women with ER positive, HER2 negative operable breast cancer were assigned 1:1 to goserelin 3.6 mg monthly plus either anastrozole 1 mg daily or tamoxifen 20 mg daily, with matching placebo, for 24 weeks before surgery. Randomisation was stratified by centre and all study personnel were masked. The primary endpoint was best overall tumour response in the intention-to-treat population, tested for non-inferiority and then superiority.
stage.results: 204 patients were enrolled and 197 randomised, 98 to anastrozole and 99 to tamoxifen. 185 completed 24 weeks of treatment and had surgery. Response occurred in 70.4 percent with anastrozole and 50.5 percent with tamoxifen, difference 19.9 percent, 95 percent CI 6.5 to 33.3, p=0.004. Treatment-related grade 3 events occurred in two anastrozole patients and one tamoxifen patient. One serious adverse event occurred in the anastrozole group.

star.methods: Update of the NSABP Study of Tamoxifen and Raloxifene with a median follow-up of 81 months, against 47 months in the initial report. Eligible women were postmenopausal with a 5-year breast cancer risk of at least 1.66% (actual mean risk 4.03%) and were randomly assigned to tamoxifen 20 mg per day or raloxifene 60 mg per day for 5 years. Of the 19,747 women originally randomised, 19,490 took part in this follow-up.
star.results: The risk ratio, raloxifene to tamoxifen, was 1.24 (95% CI 1.05 to 1.47) for invasive breast cancer and 1.22 (0.95 to 1.59) for noninvasive disease; compared with the initial results the ratio widened for invasive and narrowed for noninvasive cancer. Toxicity risk ratios were 0.55 (0.36 to 0.83, P = 0.003) for endometrial cancer, which was not significant in the initial results, 0.19 (0.12 to 0.29) for uterine hyperplasia and 0.75 (0.60 to 0.93) for thromboembolic events. Mortality did not differ significantly. Raloxifene retained 76% of the effectiveness of tamoxifen in preventing invasive disease.

start.methods: Prespecified 10-year analysis of two randomized trials. From 1999 to 2002, women with completely excised invasive breast cancer (pT1-3a, pN0-1, M0) were enrolled at 35 UK radiotherapy centres and randomly assigned after primary surgery. START-A compared 50 Gy in 25 fractions over 5 weeks with 41.6 Gy or 39 Gy in 13 fractions. START-B compared 50 Gy with 40 Gy in 15 fractions over 3 weeks. Primary endpoints were local-regional relapse and late normal tissue effects.
start.results: START-A enrolled 2,236 women, median follow-up 9.3 years, with 139 local-regional relapses. 10-year local-regional relapse rates were 6.3% with 41.6 Gy, 8.8% with 39 Gy and 7.4% with 50 Gy (HR 0.91 and 1.18 versus 50 Gy). START-B enrolled 2,215 women, median follow-up 9.9 years, with 95 relapses and 10-year rates of 4.3% with 40 Gy versus 5.5% with 50 Gy (HR 0.77). Normal tissue effects were less common with 39 Gy and 40 Gy.

study301.methods: Phase III open-label randomized study. Women with locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer who had received prior anthracycline- and taxane-based therapy were randomly assigned to eribulin or capecitabine as their first-, second- or third-line chemotherapy for advanced or metastatic disease. Stratification factors were HER2 status and geographic region. Coprimary end points were overall survival and progression-free survival.
study301.results: Median overall survival was 15.9 months with eribulin (n = 554) and 14.5 months with capecitabine (n = 548) (hazard ratio 0.88, 95% CI 0.77 to 1.00, P = .056). Median progression-free survival was 4.1 and 4.2 months (hazard ratio 1.08, 95% CI 0.93 to 1.25, P = .30). Objective response rates were 11.0% and 11.5%. Global health status and overall quality-of-life scores over time were similar.

success-a.methods: Randomised phase III trial of 3754 patients with high-risk early breast cancer, defined by at least one of nodal positivity, grade 3, age 35 or younger, tumour larger than 2 cm or negative hormone receptor status. Patients received three cycles of fluorouracil, epirubicin and cyclophosphamide followed by three cycles of docetaxel, or three cycles of FEC followed by three cycles of docetaxel with gemcitabine. The primary aim was disease-free survival, with overall survival and safety as the main secondary objectives.
success-a.results: Five-year disease-free and overall survival did not differ between the arms: the hazard ratio was 0.93 (95% CI 0.78 to 1.12, P = 0.47) for disease-free survival and 0.94 (0.74 to 1.19, P = 0.60) for overall survival. Five-year disease-free survival was 86.6% with FEC-docetaxel and 87.2% with FEC-docetaxel-gemcitabine, and five-year overall survival 92.8% and 92.5%.

summit.methods: Report of 71 patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-mutant metastatic breast cancer in the SUMMIT basket study, including 21 from a randomized substudy. Patients with activating HER2 mutations and prior CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy received neratinib 240 mg per day with loperamide prophylaxis plus fulvestrant and trastuzumab, or fulvestrant plus trastuzumab, or fulvestrant alone, with cross-over allowed on progression. Endpoints included objective response rate, clinical benefit rate, duration of response and progression-free survival.
summit.results: Objective response rate for the 57 patients given neratinib, fulvestrant and trastuzumab was 39% (95% CI 26% to 52%), and median progression-free survival was 8.3 months (95% CI 6.0 to 15.1). No responses occurred with fulvestrant alone or fulvestrant plus trastuzumab. Patients crossing over to the triplet responded. Responses occurred with ductal and lobular histology, one or more HER2 mutations and co-occurring HER3 mutations. Circulating tumour DNA showed acquired HER2 and PIK3CA alterations.

supremo.methods: International phase 3 randomised trial of omitting chest-wall irradiation in women with intermediate-risk breast cancer, defined as pT1N1, pT2N1 or pT3N0, or pT2N0 with histological grade 3, lymphovascular invasion or both, treated with mastectomy, an axillary procedure and systemic therapy. Patients were assigned to chest-wall irradiation of 40 to 50 Gy or to no chest-wall irradiation. The primary end point was overall survival with 10 years of follow-up; chest-wall and regional recurrence, disease-free survival, distant metastasis-free survival, causes of death and radiation-related adverse events were also assessed.
supremo.results: The intention-to-treat population was 808 patients in the irradiation group and 799 in the no-irradiation group, with a median follow-up of 9.6 years. Ten-year overall survival was 81.4% with chest-wall irradiation and 81.9% without (hazard ratio for death 1.04, 95% CI 0.82 to 1.30, P = 0.80). There were 29 chest-wall recurrences, 9 (1.1%) with irradiation and 20 (2.5%) without (hazard ratio 0.45, 95% CI 0.20 to 0.99). Disease-free survival was 76.2% versus 75.5% (hazard ratio 0.97, 0.79 to 1.18) and distant metastasis-free survival 78.2% versus 79.2% (hazard ratio 1.06, 0.86 to 1.31).

survive.methods: Partially double-blinded randomised phase III superiority trial in medium-to-high-risk early breast cancer. After completion of primary antineoplastic therapy, patients are randomised 1:1 to intensified liquid-biopsy-guided surveillance or to standard surveillance. Intensive surveillance tests blood every 3 months for circulating tumour DNA and the serum tumour markers CEA, CA 27.29 and CA125, and also tests circulating tumour cells. A positive biomarker or symptoms trigger staging examinations. The co-primary endpoints are overall survival and the overall lead time effect. In total 3500 patients are to be randomised.

swog-8814-int-0100.methods: Open-label phase 3 trial in postmenopausal women with hormone receptor positive, node positive breast cancer. Patients were randomised 2:3:3 to tamoxifen alone for five years, to six cycles of CAF every four weeks followed by tamoxifen, or to CAF with concurrent tamoxifen. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival, addressing chemotherapy benefit and then tamoxifen timing. Overall survival and toxicity were predefined secondary outcomes. Analysis was by intention to treat among eligible patients using stratified log-rank tests and adjusted Cox regression.
swog-8814-int-0100.results: Of 1558 randomised women, 1477 were eligible for analysis. Median follow-up was 8.94 years and 637 had a disease-free survival event. CAF plus tamoxifen beat tamoxifen alone for disease-free survival, hazard ratio 0.76, 95 percent CI 0.64 to 0.91, p=0.002, and marginally for overall survival, hazard ratio 0.83, p=0.057. Sequential versus concurrent tamoxifen gave hazard ratio 0.84, p=0.061. Neutropenia, stomatitis, thromboembolism, heart failure and leukaemia were more frequent with chemotherapy.

swog-s0226.methods: Phase 3 randomised trial. Postmenopausal women with previously untreated hormone receptor positive metastatic breast cancer were assigned 1:1 to anastrozole 1 mg daily, with crossover to fulvestrant at progression strongly encouraged, or to anastrozole plus fulvestrant. Fulvestrant was given intramuscularly at 500 mg on day 1 and 250 mg on days 14 and 28 and monthly thereafter. Randomisation was stratified by prior adjuvant tamoxifen. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival, with overall survival prespecified as secondary.
swog-s0226.results: Median progression-free survival was 15.0 months with the combination and 13.5 months with anastrozole alone, hazard ratio 0.80, 95 percent CI 0.68 to 0.94, p=0.007. Median overall survival was 47.7 versus 41.3 months, hazard ratio 0.81, p=0.05, despite 41 percent crossover. In the final analysis of 694 patients, median overall survival was 49.8 versus 42.0 months, hazard ratio 0.82. Grade 3 to 5 toxicity rates were similar.

swog-s0500.methods: Patients with metastatic breast cancer starting first-line chemotherapy were grouped by circulating tumour cell count, increased meaning five or more cells per 7.5 mL of whole blood. Those without increased counts at baseline stayed on initial therapy (arm A). Those whose counts fell by day 21 also stayed on it (arm B). Those with persistently increased counts were randomly assigned to continue initial therapy (arm C1) or change to alternative chemotherapy (arm C2). The primary outcome was overall survival.
swog-s0500.results: Of 595 eligible and evaluable patients, 276 (46%) had no increased counts (arm A). Of those with increased counts, 31 (10%) were not retested, 165 went to arm B and 123 were randomly assigned to arm C1 or C2. Median overall survival was 10.7 months in arm C1 versus 12.5 months in arm C2 (P = .98), and 35, 23 and 13 months in arms A, B and C (P < .001).

swog-s0800.methods: Randomised, open-label phase II trial comparing weekly nab-paclitaxel with bevacizumab followed by dose-dense doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide against nab-paclitaxel followed or preceded by AC as neoadjuvant treatment for HER2-negative locally advanced or inflammatory breast cancer. Allocation was 2:1:1 to the three arms. The primary endpoint was pathological complete response, stratified by disease type and hormone receptor status; overall survival, event-free survival and toxicity were secondary. Analyses were intention to treat, comparing bevacizumab with the combined control arms.
swog-s0800.results: 215 patients were accrued, 11% with inflammatory and 32% with triple-negative breast cancer. Bevacizumab significantly increased pathological complete response overall (36% versus 21%, P = 0.019) and in triple-negative disease (59% versus 29%, P = 0.014), but not in hormone receptor-positive disease (24% versus 18%, P = 0.41). The sequence of nab-paclitaxel and AC did not affect the rate. There were no significant differences in overall or event-free survival, with a trend favouring bevacizumab for event-free survival in triple-negative disease (P = 0.06). Grade 3 to 4 adverse events did not differ substantially by arm.

swog-s1416.methods: Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 trial at 154 community and academic sites in the USA. Eligible patients were 18 or older with metastatic or recurrent triple-negative breast cancer or germline BRCA1/2-associated metastatic or recurrent breast cancer, ECOG performance status 0-2, and up to one line of chemotherapy for metastatic disease. Patients were assigned 1:1 to cisplatin 75 mg/m2 on day 1 with veliparib or matching placebo 300 mg twice a day on days 1-14 of a 21-day cycle. Central testing after randomisation classified patients as germline BRCA1/2-mutated, BRCA-like or non-BRCA-like, and the primary endpoint of investigator-assessed progression-free survival was analysed separately in each group with a prespecified alpha.
swog-s1416.results: Between July 2016 and June 2019, 335 patients were randomly assigned and 320 were eligible for efficacy evaluation; 247 were classified as germline BRCA1/2-mutated (37), BRCA-like (101) or non-BRCA-like (109). Median follow-up was 11.1 months. Median progression-free survival with veliparib versus placebo was 6.2 versus 6.4 months in the germline-mutated group (hazard ratio 0.79, 95% CI 0.38 to 1.67, p=0.54), 5.9 versus 4.2 months in the BRCA-like group (0.57, 0.37 to 0.88, p=0.010) and 4.0 versus 3.0 months in the non-BRCA-like group (0.89, 0.60 to 1.33, p=0.57). The most common grade 3 or worse treatment-attributed adverse events were neutropenia (46% vs 20%), leukopenia (27% vs 7%), anaemia (23% vs 8%) and thrombocytopenia (19% vs 3%).

swog-s9313.methods: Phase III randomised study of two adjuvant schedules of doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide in high-risk node-negative or low-risk node-positive early breast cancer, asking whether sequential single agents give superior disease-free and overall survival to the same total dose in combination. Arm I gave doxorubicin 54 mg/m2 and cyclophosphamide 1.2 g/m2 concurrently every 3 weeks for six cycles; arm II gave doxorubicin 40.5 mg/m2 on days 1 and 2 every 3 weeks for four cycles followed by cyclophosphamide 2.4 g/m2 every 2 weeks for three cycles. Both arms had G-CSF support and prophylactic antibiotics, and all but premenopausal women with receptor-negative tumours received tamoxifen afterwards.
swog-s9313.results: Between 1994 and 1997, 3,176 patients were randomly assigned; 48% of eligible patients were node-negative and 48% oestrogen receptor-positive. No significant differences in overall or disease-free survival were observed; 5-year overall survival was 88% (95% CI 87% to 90%) with concurrent AC and 89% (87% to 91%) with sequential A then C. Grade 4 haematological toxicity was greater with the sequential schedule.

syd985-phase1.methods: First-in-human phase 1 dose-escalation and dose-expansion study of trastuzumab duocarmazine, a HER2-targeting antibody-drug conjugate of trastuzumab and a duocarmycin linker drug. Dose escalation enrolled adults with locally advanced or metastatic solid tumours of variable HER2 status refractory to standard treatment at three hospitals, giving 0.3 to 2.4 mg/kg intravenously on day 1 of each 3-week cycle (3 + 3 design), with safety and the recommended phase 2 dose as the primary endpoint. Dose expansion at 15 hospitals enrolled breast, gastric, urothelial or endometrial cancer with at least HER2 immunohistochemistry 1+ and measurable disease, with investigator-assessed objective response by RECIST 1.1 as the primary endpoint.
syd985-phase1.results: Between October 2014 and April 2018, 39 patients were treated in dose escalation and 146 in dose expansion. One dose-limiting toxic effect, death from pneumonitis, occurred at 2.4 mg/kg, and the recommended phase 2 dose was 1.2 mg/kg. In dose expansion, treatment-related serious adverse events occurred in 16 of 146 (11%); the commonest treatment-related adverse events were fatigue (33%), conjunctivitis (31%) and dry eye (31%), and 104 (71%) had at least one ocular adverse event. In the breast cohorts, 16 of 48 (33%) with HER2-positive disease, 9 of 32 (28%) with HER2-low hormone receptor-positive disease and 6 of 15 (40%) with HER2-low hormone receptor-negative disease had a partial response.

sysucc-002.methods: Open-label, noninferiority phase 3 randomised trial at nine hospitals in China. Patients were stratified by previous adjuvant endocrine therapy and by recurrent versus de novo metastatic disease, then assigned 1:1 to trastuzumab plus endocrine therapy, using investigator's choice of oestrogen receptor modulator or aromatase inhibitor with or without ovarian suppression, or to trastuzumab plus chemotherapy, using investigator's choice of taxane, capecitabine or vinorelbine. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival with a noninferiority margin of 1.35, analysed by intention to treat.
sysucc-002.results: 392 patients were randomised, 196 to each group. After a median follow-up of 30.2 months, interquartile range 15.0 to 44.7, median progression-free survival was 19.2 months, 95 percent CI 16.7 to 21.7, with endocrine therapy and 14.8 months, 95 percent CI 12.8 to 16.8, with chemotherapy. The hazard ratio was 0.88, 95 percent CI 0.71 to 1.09, noninferiority p less than 0.0001. Toxicity was significantly more prevalent in the chemotherapy group.

sysucc001.methods: Randomized trial at 13 academic centres and clinical sites in China from April 2010 to December 2016. 443 patients with early-stage triple-negative breast cancer who had completed standard adjuvant chemotherapy were randomized 1:1 to capecitabine 650 mg/m2 twice a day by mouth for 1 year without interruption (n = 222) or to observation (n = 221). The primary end point was disease-free survival. Secondary end points included distant disease-free survival, overall survival and locoregional recurrence-free survival.
sysucc001.results: 434 women formed the full analysis set, mean age 46 years, 61.8% node-negative, median follow-up 61 months. 94 events occurred, 38 in the capecitabine group and 56 in the observation group. Estimated 5-year disease-free survival was 82.8% versus 73.0% (hazard ratio 0.64, 95% CI 0.42 to 0.95, P = .03), distant disease-free survival 85.8% versus 75.8% (HR 0.60) and overall survival 85.5% versus 81.3% (HR 0.75). Hand-foot syndrome affected 45.2%.

tact.methods: Multicentre, open-label, phase III randomised trial in women with node-positive or high-risk node-negative operable early breast cancer. Patients were assigned to FEC (fluorouracil 600 mg/m2, epirubicin 60 mg/m2, cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m2, 3-weekly) for four cycles followed by docetaxel 100 mg/m2 3-weekly for four cycles, or to a control regimen chosen by centre: FEC for eight cycles, or epirubicin 100 mg/m2 for four cycles followed by four cycles of CMF. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival, analysed by intention to treat.
tact.results: 4162 women were randomised, 2073 to the docetaxel sequence and 2089 to control (1265 FEC, 824 E-CMF). With a median follow-up of 62 months, disease-free survival events occurred in 517 experimental and 539 control patients (hazard ratio 0.95, 95% CI 0.85 to 1.08, P = 0.44), and 75.6% versus 74.3% were alive and disease free at 5 years. Acute grade 3 or 4 adverse events were significantly more frequent with docetaxel (P < 0.0001), mainly neutropenia, leucopenia and lethargy.

tact2.methods: Multicentre, phase 3, open-label randomised trial with a 2 x 2 factorial design in patients 18 or older from 129 UK centres with node-positive or high-risk node-negative operable breast cancer, completely excised and due to receive adjuvant chemotherapy. Patients received four cycles of epirubicin 100 mg/m2 every 3 weeks or every 2 weeks with pegfilgrastim, followed by four 4-week cycles of CMF or four 3-week cycles of capecitabine 2500 mg/m2 a day on days 1 to 14. The primary endpoint was time to tumour recurrence, by intention to treat for epirubicin and per protocol for CMF against capecitabine.
tact2.results: From December 2005 to December 2008, 4391 patients were recruited. At a median follow-up of 85.6 months, time to recurrence did not differ between accelerated and standard epirubicin (hazard ratio 0.94, 95% CI 0.81 to 1.09, P = 0.42), with 87.1% and 85.9% free of recurrence at 5 years. In 4358 per-protocol patients, capecitabine was non-inferior to CMF (hazard ratio 0.98, 0.85 to 1.14, non-inferiority P = 0.00092). More patients taking CMF than capecitabine had clinically relevant worsening of quality of life at the end of treatment (58% versus 50%) and at 12 months (34% versus 22%).

tailorx.methods: Prospective trial involving 10,273 women with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative, axillary node-negative breast cancer. Of the 9,719 eligible patients with follow-up information, 6,711 (69%) had a midrange 21-gene recurrence score of 11 to 25 and were randomly assigned to chemoendocrine therapy or endocrine therapy alone. The trial was designed to show non-inferiority of endocrine therapy alone for invasive disease-free survival, defined as freedom from invasive recurrence, second primary cancer or death.
tailorx.results: Endocrine therapy was non-inferior to chemoendocrine therapy for invasive disease-free survival (hazard ratio 1.08, 95% CI 0.94 to 1.24, P = 0.26). At 9 years the groups had similar invasive disease-free survival (83.3% versus 84.3%), freedom from distant recurrence (94.5% and 95.0%), freedom from distant or local-regional recurrence (92.2% and 92.9%) and overall survival (93.9% and 93.8%). Chemotherapy benefit varied with recurrence score and age, with some benefit in women 50 or younger scoring 16 to 25.

talazoparib-beyond-brca.methods: Open-label phase II trial of talazoparib monotherapy, Talazoparib Beyond BRCA. Eligible patients had pretreated advanced HER2-negative breast cancer (n = 13) or other solid tumours (n = 7) with mutations in homologous recombination pathway genes other than BRCA1 and BRCA2, and were themselves wild-type for BRCA1 and BRCA2. Response was assessed by RECIST, with clinical benefit defined to include stable disease of at least 6 months. Tumour and plasma circulating tumour DNA homologous recombination deficiency scores were measured and correlated with treatment outcomes. A germline PALB2-associated mutational signature was also examined against tumour response.
talazoparib-beyond-brca.results: Among the patients with breast cancer, four had a RECIST partial response, an overall response rate of 31%, and three additional patients had stable disease of at least 6 months, a clinical benefit rate of 54%. All patients with germline PALB2 mutations had treatment-associated tumour regression. Tumour or plasma circulating tumour DNA homologous recombination deficiency scores correlated with treatment outcomes and were increased in all germline PALB2 tumours. A germline PALB2-associated mutational signature was associated with tumour response. The authors conclude that talazoparib has efficacy in advanced breast cancer with germline PALB2 mutations, showing activity in the context of homologous recombination pathway gene mutations beyond germline BRCA1 and BRCA2.

tam01.methods: 10-year follow-up of a phase III placebo-controlled trial. 500 women with breast intraepithelial neoplasia, comprising atypical ductal hyperplasia, lobular carcinoma in situ, or hormone-sensitive or unknown ductal carcinoma in situ, were randomly assigned after surgery with or without irradiation to low-dose tamoxifen 5 mg once daily for 3 years or placebo. The primary end point was the incidence of invasive breast cancer or ductal carcinoma in situ.
tam01.results: The population was 20% atypical ductal hyperplasia, 11% lobular carcinoma in situ and 69% ductal carcinoma in situ, mean age 54 years. After a median follow-up of 9.7 years, 66 breast cancers were diagnosed, 25 with tamoxifen and 41 with placebo (11.3 versus 19.5 per 1,000 person-years, hazard ratio 0.58, 95% CI 0.35 to 0.95). Contralateral cancers numbered six versus 16 (HR 0.36). In the DCIS cohort the HR was 0.50.

tamoxifen-fenretinide-2x2.methods: Two-by-two biomarker trial. 235 premenopausal women with pT1mic or pT1a breast cancer (n = 21), intraepithelial neoplasia (n = 160) or a 5-year Gail risk of 1.3% or more (n = 54) were randomly allocated to tamoxifen 5 mg per day, fenretinide 200 mg per day, their combination, or placebo. The report gives plasma insulin-like growth factor I, mammographic density, uterine effects and breast neoplastic events after 5.5 years.
tamoxifen-fenretinide-2x2.results: During the 2-year intervention tamoxifen lowered IGF-I and mammographic density by 12% and 20%, fenretinide by 4% and 10% (not significant), and the combination by 20% and 22%, with no synergistic interaction. Tamoxifen increased endometrial thickness, mainly in women becoming postmenopausal; fenretinide decreased it. The annual rate of breast neoplasms (48 events) was 3.5%, 2.1%, 4.7% and 5.2% in the tamoxifen, fenretinide, combination and placebo arms, with hazard ratios against placebo of 0.70 (95% CI 0.32 to 1.52), 0.38 (0.15 to 0.90) and 0.96 (0.46 to 1.99), and an adverse tamoxifen-by-fenretinide interaction (P = .03). Baseline IGF-I and density did not predict events.

tamrad.methods: Open-label phase 2 study that randomly assigned postmenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative, aromatase inhibitor-resistant metastatic breast cancer to tamoxifen 20 mg/d plus everolimus 10 mg/d (n = 54) or tamoxifen 20 mg/d alone (n = 57), stratified by primary and secondary hormone resistance. The primary end point was clinical benefit rate, the percentage of all patients with a complete or partial response or stable disease at 6 months. No formal statistical comparison between groups was planned.
tamrad.results: The 6-month clinical benefit rate was 61% (95% CI 47 to 74) with tamoxifen plus everolimus and 42% (29 to 56) with tamoxifen alone. Time to progression increased from 4.5 months with tamoxifen alone to 8.6 months with the combination, a 46% reduction in the risk of progression (hazard ratio 0.54, 95% CI 0.36 to 0.81). The risk of death was reduced by 55% (hazard ratio 0.45, 0.24 to 0.81). The main toxicities of the combination were fatigue (72% vs 53%), stomatitis (56% vs 7%), rash (44% vs 7%), anorexia (43% vs 18%) and diarrhoea (39% vs 11%).

tandem.methods: Randomised phase 3 trial. Postmenopausal women with HER2 positive and hormone receptor positive metastatic breast cancer were assigned to anastrozole 1 mg daily with or without trastuzumab, given as a 4 mg/kg intravenous loading dose on day 1 then 2 mg/kg every week, until progression. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival in the intention-to-treat population.
tandem.results: 103 patients received trastuzumab plus anastrozole and 104 received anastrozole alone. Median progression-free survival was 4.8 versus 2.4 months, hazard ratio 0.63, 95 percent CI 0.47 to 0.84, p=0.0016. Among 150 patients with centrally confirmed hormone receptor positivity it was 5.6 versus 3.8 months, p=0.006. Grade 3 and grade 4 events occurred in 23 and 5 percent with the combination versus 15 and 1 percent with anastrozole alone.

targit-a.methods: Prospective, open-label randomised trial at 32 centres in 10 countries. 2298 women aged 45 or older with invasive ductal carcinoma up to 3.5 cm, cN0-N1, eligible for breast conservation, were randomised before lumpectomy 1:1 to risk-adapted targeted intraoperative radiotherapy (TARGIT-IORT) or to a standard daily course of whole-breast external beam radiotherapy over three to six weeks. TARGIT-IORT was given immediately after lumpectomy under the same anaesthetic and was the only radiotherapy for around 80% of patients, supplemented by external beam radiotherapy when histopathology found unsuspected higher-risk factors. The outcomes were non-inferiority with a 2.5% margin for the absolute difference in 5-year local recurrence, and long-term survival.
targit-a.results: Between March 2000 and June 2012, 1140 patients were randomised to TARGIT-IORT and 1158 to external beam radiotherapy. TARGIT-IORT was non-inferior: 5-year local recurrence was 2.11% against 0.95% (difference 1.16%, 90% CI 0.32 to 1.99). With a median follow-up of 8.6 years there was no significant difference in local recurrence-free survival (hazard ratio 1.13, 95% CI 0.91 to 1.41), mastectomy-free survival (0.96, 0.78 to 1.19), distant disease-free survival (0.88, 0.69 to 1.12), overall survival (0.82, 0.63 to 1.05) or breast cancer mortality (1.12, 0.78 to 1.60), while mortality from other causes was significantly lower (0.59, 0.40 to 0.86, P = 0.005).

tbcrc-001.methods: Randomised phase II study in metastatic triple-negative breast cancer. Patients received the anti-EGFR antibody cetuximab, 400 mg/m2 loading then 250 mg/m2 per week intravenously, either alone with weekly carboplatin at an area under the curve of 2 added after progression, or with carboplatin as concomitant therapy from the beginning. Response rate was the primary endpoint; others were time to progression, overall survival and toxicity. Embedded correlative studies included molecular subtyping on archival tissue. Fresh tumour tissue taken before and after 7 to 14 days of therapy was used for microarray analyses exploring EGFR pathway activity and inhibition.
tbcrc-001.results: 102 patients with triple-negative breast cancer were treated. Response rates were 6%, two of 31, to cetuximab alone and 16%, four of 25, to cetuximab plus carboplatin after progression, while the response rate to cetuximab plus carboplatin from the beginning was 17%, 12 of 71, and 31% of patients responded or had prolonged disease stabilisation. The combination was well tolerated, but time to progression and overall survival were short at 2.1 months (95% CI 1.8 to 5.5 months) and 10.4 months (95% CI 7.7 to 13.1 months). Of 73 patients with archival tissue, 74% had basal-like molecular subtype. Among 16 patients biopsied before and one week after therapy, genomic patterns of the EGFR pathway showed activation in 13 and inhibition by therapy in five.

tbcrc-003.methods: Phase II study of lapatinib plus trastuzumab in HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer, testing the chemotherapy-free combination earlier than the heavily pretreated setting in which it had been shown to improve outcomes over lapatinib alone. Two cohorts were enrolled, the first with no prior trastuzumab for metastatic disease and at least a year from adjuvant trastuzumab if given, the second with one to two lines of chemotherapy including trastuzumab for metastatic disease and/or recurrence less than a year from adjuvant trastuzumab. The primary end point was objective response rate by RECIST v1.0. Secondary end points included clinical benefit rate, defined as complete plus partial response plus stable disease of at least 24 weeks, and progression-free survival. Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography scans were acquired at baseline, week 1 and week 8, and associations between metabolic response and clinical outcomes were explored.
tbcrc-003.results: Eighty-seven patients were registered and 85 were evaluable for efficacy. The confirmed objective response rate was 50.0% (95% CI, 33.8% to 66.2%) in cohort 1 and 22.2% (95% CI, 11.3% to 37.3%) in cohort 2. Clinical benefit rate was 57.5% (95% CI, 40.9% to 73.0%) in cohort 1 and 40.0% (95% CI, 25.7% to 55.7%) in cohort 2. Median progression-free survival was 7.4 months in cohort 1 and 5.3 months in cohort 2. Lack of a week-1 FDG-PET/CT response was associated with failure to achieve an objective response by RECIST, with a negative predictive value of 91% (95% CI, 74% to 100%) in cohort 1 and 91% (95% CI, 79% to 100%) in cohort 2.

tbcrc-008.methods: Multicentre randomised phase II neoadjuvant trial in women with stage II or III HER2-negative breast cancer, assigned to 12 weeks of carboplatin (AUC 2 weekly) and nab-paclitaxel (100 mg/m2 weekly) with vorinostat (400 mg orally on days 1 to 3 of every 7) or placebo. All patients had FDG PET and a research biopsy at baseline and on cycle 1 day 15. The primary endpoint was the pathological complete response rate; secondary objectives included correlation of the day-15 change in tumour SULmax and of Ki-67 with response.
tbcrc-008.results: In the intention-to-treat analysis of 62 patients, pathological complete response was 27.4% overall, 25.8% with vorinostat and 29.0% with placebo. In a pooled analysis of 59, the median reduction in SULmax at day 15 was 63.0% in patients with a complete response against 32.9% in those without (P = 0.003), and a reduction of 50% or more remained predictive after adjustment for oestrogen receptor status (odds ratio 5.1, 95% CI 1.3 to 22.7). Baseline and change in Ki-67 did not differ by response.

tbcrc-009.methods: Single-arm multicentre phase II trial of single-agent platinum in metastatic triple-negative breast cancer with biomarker correlates. Patients received first- or second-line cisplatin 75 mg/m2 or carboplatin at an area under the concentration-time curve of 6 once every three weeks, by physician choice. The coprimary endpoints were objective response rate and response prediction by p63/p73 gene expression. Secondary and exploratory endpoints included toxicity, response rate with cisplatin versus carboplatin, and response rate in molecularly defined subgroups including germline BRCA1/2 mutation carriers.
tbcrc-009.results: 86 patients were treated, 69 of them as first-line therapy, 43 with cisplatin and 43 with carboplatin. The response rate was 25.6% (95% CI 16.8% to 36%), numerically higher with cisplatin at 32.6% than with carboplatin at 18.7%, and 54.5% in the 11 germline BRCA1/2 carriers. Among the 66 patients without BRCA1/2 mutations, an exploratory BRCA-like genomic instability signature discriminated responding from non-responding tumours, with mean HRD-LOH/HRD-LST scores of 12.68 and 5.11, whereas the predefined analyses by p63/p73 expression, p53 and PIK3CA mutation status and PAM50 subtype did not. Five of the six long-term responders alive at a median of 4.5 years lacked germline BRCA1/2 mutations, and two of those had raised HRD scores. The authors conclude that platinum agents are active, especially in germline carriers, and that prospective controlled confirmatory trials are warranted.

tbcrc-011.methods: Multicentre phase II study of the androgen receptor antagonist bicalutamide. Tumours from patients with oestrogen and progesterone receptor-negative advanced breast cancer were tested centrally for androgen receptor by immunohistochemistry, with more than 10% nuclear staining counted as positive. Patients were eligible if either the primary tumour or a metastatic site was positive, and received bicalutamide 150 mg daily. The primary endpoint was clinical benefit rate, the total number of patients with a complete response, a partial response or stable disease beyond six months; secondary endpoints were progression-free survival and toxicity. Correlative studies measured circulating endocrine markers and immunohistochemical surrogates for basal-like breast cancer.
tbcrc-011.results: Of 424 patients with oestrogen and progesterone receptor-negative breast cancer screened, 12% tested androgen receptor-positive. The six-month clinical benefit rate with bicalutamide was 19% (95% CI 7% to 39%). Median progression-free survival was 12 weeks (95% CI 11 to 22 weeks). Bicalutamide was well tolerated, with no grade 4 or 5 treatment-related adverse events. The authors read the result as proof of principle for minimally toxic androgen blockade in a selected group of patients.

tbcrc-019.methods: Randomised 2:1 phase II trial of nab-paclitaxel with or without tigatuzumab, an agonistic anti-DR5 antibody that triggers apoptosis in DR5-positive tumour cells without crosslinking, in patients with metastatic triple-negative breast cancer stratified by prior chemotherapy. Patients received nab-paclitaxel weekly for three weeks, with or without tigatuzumab every other week, in 28-day cycles. The primary objective was the within-arm objective response rate. Secondary objectives were safety, progression-free survival, clinical benefit and tigatuzumab immunogenicity. Metastatic research biopsies were required.
tbcrc-019.results: Of 64 patients, 60 were treated, 39 with tigatuzumab plus nab-paclitaxel and 21 with nab-paclitaxel alone. The combination arm had three complete remissions, eight partial remissions, 11 stable diseases and 17 progressive diseases, an objective response rate of 28%; the nab-paclitaxel arm had no complete remissions, eight partial remissions, four stable diseases and nine progressive diseases, a response rate of 38%. Complete remissions were numerically more frequent with tigatuzumab and several patients in that arm had prolonged progression-free survival. Grade 3 toxicity occurred in 28% and 29% of the two arms with no grade 4 or 5 events. An exploratory analysis suggested an association between ROCK1 gene pathway activation and efficacy in the combination arm.

tbcrc-022.methods: Multicenter phase 2 study, cohort 4. Patients with measurable HER2 positive breast cancer brain metastases received neratinib 160 mg daily plus ado-trastuzumab emtansine 3.6 mg/kg intravenously every 21 days in three parallel enrolling cohorts: 4A with previously untreated brain metastases, 4B progressing after local central nervous system therapy without prior T-DM1, and 4C with prior T-DM1. Diarrhoea prophylaxis was required in cycle 1. The primary endpoint was central nervous system response by RANO-BM in each cohort.
tbcrc-022.results: Between 2018 and 2021, 6, 17 and 21 patients enrolled in cohorts 4A, 4B and 4C, and enrolment stopped early for slow accrual. Central nervous system objective response rates were 33.3, 35.3 and 28.6 percent. Between 38.1 and 50 percent had response or stable disease for at least six months. Grade 3 diarrhoea occurred in 22.7 percent. Median overall survival was 30.2, 23.3 and 20.9 months.

tbcrc-023.methods: TBCRC023 is a randomized phase II trial combining a Simon phase II design in the experimental arm with a pick-the-winner design, and it was not powered for direct comparison. Women with HER2-positive breast tumours measuring 2 cm or more were randomised in a 1 to 2 ratio to 12 versus 24 weeks of lapatinib and trastuzumab without chemotherapy. Letrozole, along with ovarian suppression if premenopausal, was administered to patients whose tumours were also oestrogen receptor-positive. All evaluable patients were assessed for in-breast pathological complete response. The trial followed earlier neoadjuvant studies in which 12 weeks of dual anti-HER2 therapy without chemotherapy produced a meaningful pCR rate.
tbcrc-023.results: Ninety-seven patients were enrolled, 33 in the 12-week arm and 64 in the 24-week arm, of whom 94 were evaluable. Median age was 51 years and 55% were postmenopausal; median tumour size was 5 cm and 65% were oestrogen receptor-positive. The rate of pCR in the 24-week arm was 28% and numerically superior to the 12-week arm at 12%. This was driven by increased pCR in the oestrogen receptor-positive subgroup, 33% versus 9%. Study treatment was well tolerated, with grade 1-2 diarrhoea and acneiform rash the most common toxicities.

tbcrc-026.methods: Multicentre phase II trial. Patients with stage II or III, oestrogen receptor-negative, HER2-positive breast cancer received four cycles of neoadjuvant pertuzumab and trastuzumab. FDG PET-CT was performed at baseline and 15 days after the start of treatment (C1D15). Eighty evaluable patients were required to test the null hypothesis that the area under the curve of percent change in SULmax by C1D15 predicting pathological complete response is 0.65 or less, with a one-sided type I error rate of 10%. A later analysis fitted logistic regressions combining the imaging biomarkers with tissue HER2 biomarkers, using the C statistic to assess prediction power and Youden's index to set the composite cut-off.
tbcrc-026.results: Eighty-eight women were enrolled and 83 were evaluable; 85%, 75 of 88, completed all four cycles. Pathological complete response after pertuzumab and trastuzumab alone was 22%. The area under the curve for percent change in SULmax by C1D15 was 0.72 (80% CI 0.64 to 0.80; one-sided P = .12), which did not reject the null hypothesis. Early metabolic change still separated the groups, with a median percent reduction in SULmax by C1D15 of 63.8% in patients obtaining pathological complete response against 41.8% in those who did not (P = .004), and a SULmax reduction of 40% or more more prevalent, 83% against 52% (P = .03), giving a positive predictive value of 31% and a negative predictive value of 91%. In the later composite analysis the strongest single predictors were C1D15 SULmax (OR 0.43, P = 0.007, c = 0.77), percent reduction in SULmax (OR 1.03, P = 0.006, c = 0.72) and tumour HER2 protein abundance (OR 1.75, P = 0.01, c = 0.76), and combining the two imaging measures with their interaction term raised the c statistic to 0.89, which adding tumour HER2 protein did not improve further.

tbcrc-030.methods: Prospective randomised phase 2 study. Patients with germline BRCA1/2 wild-type or unknown stage I to III triple-negative breast cancer entered a 12-week randomised comparison of preoperative cisplatin or paclitaxel. The homologous recombination deficiency assay (Myriad Genetics) was carried out on baseline tissue and a score of 33 or above was defined as positive. Crossover to an alternative provider-selected chemotherapy was offered when clinical response was inadequate. The primary objective was to detect an association of homologous recombination deficiency with pathological response, defined as residual cancer burden 0 or 1.
tbcrc-030.results: 139 patients were evaluable for response, 88 (63.3%) having surgery at 12 weeks and 51 (36.7%) crossing over to an alternative preoperative regimen for inadequate clinical response. Homologous recombination deficiency results were available for 104 tumours (74.8%), of which 74 (71.1%) were positive. Residual cancer burden 0 or 1 was 26.4% with cisplatin and 22.3% with paclitaxel. Odds ratios for residual cancer burden 0 or 1 if homologous recombination deficiency positive were 2.22 (95% CI 0.39 to 23.68) for cisplatin and 0.90 (95% CI 0.19 to 4.95) for paclitaxel, with no evidence of an interaction between homologous recombination deficiency and pathological response. The authors conclude that homologous recombination deficiency was not predictive and that tumours were similarly responsive to preoperative paclitaxel or cisplatin.

tbcrc-032.methods: Investigator-initiated multi-institutional phase Ib/II study of the androgen receptor antagonist enzalutamide alone or with the PI3K inhibitor taselisib, in metastatic breast cancer with androgen receptor expression of at least 10%. Phase Ib enrolled oestrogen receptor-positive or triple-negative patients, who received enzalutamide 160 mg in combination with taselisib to determine dose-limiting toxicities and the maximum tolerated dose. Phase II randomised triple-negative patients to enzalutamide alone or in combination with taselisib 4 mg until disease progression. The primary endpoint was clinical benefit rate at 16 weeks. Genomic analyses of tumour subtype, fusions and androgen receptor splice variants were correlative.
tbcrc-032.results: The combination was tolerated and the maximum tolerated dose was not reached, with hyperglycaemia and skin rash as the adverse events. The clinical benefit rate for evaluable patients receiving the combination was 35.7% and median progression-free survival was 3.4 months. Patients with luminal androgen receptor subtype tumours trended towards better response than non-luminal patients, 75.0% versus 12.5% at a p value of 0.06, and towards longer progression-free survival, 4.6 versus 2.0 months at a p value of 0.082. Genomic analyses revealed subtype-specific treatment response and novel fusions and androgen receptor splice variants. The authors conclude that androgen receptor protein expression alone is insufficient to identify patients with androgen receptor-dependent tumours, and that knowledge of the luminal androgen receptor subtype and of splice variants may identify who is more or less likely to benefit.

tbcrc-039.methods: Randomised phase 2 study with a nested window of opportunity in triple-negative inflammatory breast cancer. Treatment-naive patients received a 7-day run-in of ruxolitinib alone or ruxolitinib plus paclitaxel. Those who received ruxolitinib alone then proceeded to neoadjuvant therapy with either ruxolitinib plus paclitaxel or paclitaxel alone for 12 weeks, while those who had received ruxolitinib plus paclitaxel continued that treatment for 12 weeks. All patients subsequently received four cycles of doxorubicin plus cyclophosphamide before surgery. Research tumour biopsies at baseline and after the run-in were evaluated for phosphorylated STAT3 by immunostaining, with a subset analysed by RNA sequencing; the primary endpoint was the percent of phosphorylated STAT3-positive pre-run-in tumours that became negative, and pathological complete response was a secondary endpoint.
tbcrc-039.results: 23 patients were enrolled, of whom 21 completed preoperative therapy. Two patients achieved pathological complete response (8.7%). Phosphorylated STAT3 and IL-6/JAK/STAT3 signalling decreased in post-run-in biopsies of ruxolitinib-treated samples, while sustained ruxolitinib plus paclitaxel upregulated IL-6/JAK/STAT3 signalling compared with ruxolitinib alone. Both treatments decreased GZMB T cells, implying immune suppression, and ruxolitinib alone inhibited JAK/STAT3 signalling effectively while its combination with paclitaxel gave incomplete inhibition. The authors conclude that ruxolitinib was associated with a decrease in phosphorylated STAT3 despite a lack of clinical benefit, and that cancer cell-specific targeting of JAK2/STAT3 or combination with immunotherapy may be required.

tbcrc-041.methods: Randomised phase 2 trial conducted through the Translational Breast Cancer Research Consortium, enrolling participants from July 2017 to November 2019, asking whether adding fulvestrant to the selective Aurora A kinase inhibitor alisertib improves objective response rate in endocrine-resistant metastatic breast cancer. Postmenopausal women with endocrine-resistant, ERBB2-negative metastatic breast cancer previously treated with fulvestrant were eligible. Stratification factors were prior treatment with a CDK4/6 inhibitor, baseline metastatic tumour ERα level below 10% or 10% and above, and primary or secondary endocrine resistance. Arm 1 received alisertib 50 mg orally daily on days 1 to 3, 8 to 10 and 15 to 17 of a 28-day cycle, and arm 2 the same dose and schedule with standard-dose fulvestrant. The design sought an improvement in objective response rate in arm 2 of at least 20% over arm 1, where the expected arm 1 rate was 20%. Among 114 preregistered patients, 96 (84.2%) registered and 91 (79.8%) were evaluable for the primary endpoint.
tbcrc-041.results: All 91 evaluable patients, of mean age 58.5 years (SD 11.3), had received prior treatment with a CDK4/6 inhibitor, 46 (50.5%) in arm 1 and 45 (49.5%) in arm 2. Objective response rate was 19.6% (90% CI 10.6 to 31.7) for arm 1 and 20.0% (90% CI 10.9 to 32.3) for arm 2. In arm 1 the 24-week clinical benefit rate and median progression-free survival were 41.3% (90% CI 29.0 to 54.5) and 5.6 months (95% CI 3.9 to 10.0); in arm 2 they were 28.9% (90% CI 18.0 to 42.0) and 5.4 months (95% CI 3.9 to 7.8). The most common grade 3 or higher adverse events attributed to alisertib were neutropenia in 41.8% and anaemia in 13.2%. Treatment was discontinued for disease progression in 38 patients (82.6%) in arm 1 and 31 (68.9%) in arm 2, and for toxic effects or refusal in 5 (10.9%) and 12 (26.7%). The authors conclude that adding fulvestrant did not increase objective response rate or progression-free survival, while promising clinical activity was seen with alisertib monotherapy in endocrine-resistant and CDK4/6 inhibitor-resistant disease.

tbcrc-043.methods: Randomised phase 2 trial conducted at six centres from August 2017 to June 2021. Patients with metastatic triple-negative breast cancer were randomly assigned to carboplatin area under the curve 6 alone or to carboplatin with atezolizumab 1200 mg, each every three weeks until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity, with three years of follow-up. The primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival. Secondary endpoints were overall response rate, clinical benefit rate and overall survival. Other objectives correlated response with tumour PD-L1 level, tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes, DNA- and RNA-sequenced biomarkers, TNBC subtyping and multiplex analyses of immune markers.
tbcrc-043.results: All 106 enrolled patients were female, with a mean age of 55 years (range 27 to 79); 50 received carboplatin and 56 carboplatin with atezolizumab. The combination improved progression-free survival from a median of 2.2 to 4.1 months, hazard ratio 0.66 (95% CI 0.44 to 1.01; P = .05), raised the overall response rate from 8.0% to 30.4% and the clinical benefit rate at six months from 18.0% to 37.5%, and improved overall survival from a median of 8.6 to 12.6 months, hazard ratio 0.60 (95% CI 0.37 to 0.96; P = .03). Tumours that were PD-L1-positive did not benefit more from the addition of atezolizumab, hazard ratio 0.62 (95% CI 0.23 to 1.65; P = .35). Greater benefit on the combination was reported in patients with high tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes, in patients with high mutation burden and in patients with prior chemotherapy, the last with a hazard ratio of 0.59 (95% CI 0.36 to 0.95); better progression-free survival on the combination was also associated with obesity and with on-treatment blood glucose above 125 mg/dL. All TNBC subtypes except the luminal androgen receptor subtype benefited from the addition of atezolizumab.

tbcrc-049.methods: Phase 2, nonrandomised, single-arm, multicenter study. Women with magnetic resonance imaging confirmed newly diagnosed leptomeningeal metastasis and HER2 positive breast cancer received tucatinib, trastuzumab and capecitabine. The primary endpoint was overall survival, compared against a historical control of 4.4 months at a prespecified interim efficacy threshold. Secondary endpoints were central nervous system progression-free survival, leptomeningeal objective response, neurological symptom improvement, pharmacokinetics and safety.
tbcrc-049.results: 17 women enrolled, 15 were symptomatic and 8 had abnormal cerebrospinal fluid cytology. At a median follow-up of 18 months, 6 of 17 remained alive and median overall survival was 10 months, 95 percent CI 4.1 to not reached. Median time to central nervous system progression was 6.9 months, 95 percent CI 2.8 to 13.8. 5 of 13 evaluable patients had a composite leptomeningeal response and 7 of 12 had improved neurological deficits. Tucatinib reached therapeutic cerebrospinal fluid levels.

tbcrc006.methods: Multicentre phase II study. Women with stage II to III HER2-positive breast cancer received weekly trastuzumab (4 mg/kg loading, then 2 mg/kg) and lapatinib 1000 mg once daily for 12 weeks, without chemotherapy. Women with ER-positive tumours also received letrozole, plus a luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone agonist if premenopausal. Pathologic response was assessed by ER status. Biopsies were taken at baseline, at weeks 2 and 8, and at surgery.
tbcrc006.results: Sixty-six patients were enrolled. Sixty-four were eligible and evaluable for response. Median tumour size was 6 cm (range 1.5 to 30 cm). In-breast pathologic complete response (ypT0-is) was 27% overall, 21% in ER-positive and 36% in ER-negative disease. Low-volume residual disease (ypT1a-b) occurred in 22% overall, 33% ER-positive and 4% ER-negative. Adverse events were mainly grade 1 to 2. Grade 3 metabolic, gastrointestinal and liver toxicity affected 12 patients (18%).

tbcrc048.methods: Investigator-initiated phase II study of olaparib in metastatic breast cancer with measurable disease. Cohort 1 had germline mutations in homologous recombination related genes. Cohort 2 had somatic mutations in those genes. Prior PARP inhibitor use, platinum-refractory disease, or progression on more than two chemotherapy regimens for metastatic disease were not allowed. Patients received olaparib 300 mg orally twice a day until progression. A single-arm, two-stage design was used. The primary endpoint was objective response rate.
tbcrc048.results: Fifty-four patients enrolled. Seventy-six percent had oestrogen receptor-positive HER2-negative disease. Objective response rate was 33% (90% CI 19% to 51%) in cohort 1 and 31% (90% CI 15% to 49%) in cohort 2. Confirmed responses were seen in only two mutation groups, with response rates of 82% and 50%. Median progression-free survival was 13.3 months (90% CI 12 months to not available) and 6.3 months (90% CI 4.4 months to not available) in those two groups.

team.methods: Open-label phase 3 trial conducted in hospitals in nine countries. Postmenopausal women with hormone-receptor-positive breast cancer, median age 64 years (range 35 to 96), were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to oral exemestane 25 mg once a day alone or to the same exemestane following tamoxifen 20 mg once a day, for 5 years. Randomisation used a computer-generated random permuted block method. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival at 5 years, analysed by intention to treat.
team.results: 9779 patients were assigned to sequential treatment (n=4875) or exemestane alone (n=4904), with 4868 and 4898 analysed by intention to treat. At 5 years, 4154 (85%) of the sequential group and 4186 (86%) of the exemestane alone group were disease free (hazard ratio 0.97, 95% CI 0.88 to 1.08, p=0.60). Sequential treatment carried more gynaecological symptoms, venous thrombosis and endometrial abnormalities. Exemestane alone carried more musculoskeletal events, hypertension and hyperlipidaemia.

techno.methods: Evaluation of the efficacy and safety of epirubicin and cyclophosphamide followed by paclitaxel and trastuzumab as neoadjuvant treatment in centrally confirmed HER2-overexpressing breast cancer, 2 cm or larger or inflammatory. Patients received four 3-week cycles of epirubicin and cyclophosphamide (90/600 mg/m2) followed by four 3-week cycles of paclitaxel (175 mg/m2) and trastuzumab (6 mg/kg) before surgery, and trastuzumab was continued after surgery to complete 1 year. The primary end point was pathological complete response, no residual invasive tumour in breast and lymphatic tissue.
techno.results: Thirty-nine percent of 217 enrolled patients achieved a pathological complete response, and breast conservation was possible in 64%. Three-year disease-free survival was 88% with a complete response vs 73% without (P = .01), and 3-year overall survival 96% vs 86% (P = .025). Pathological complete response was the only significant prognostic factor for disease-free survival (HR 2.5, 95% CI 1.2 to 5.1, P = .013) and overall survival (HR 4.9, 1.4 to 17.4, P = .012) in multivariable analysis. Cardiac toxicity was reported in eight patients (3.7%), six with an asymptomatic fall in left ventricular ejection fraction and two with symptomatic chronic heart failure.

th3resa.methods: Randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial in medical centres in 22 countries. Eligible patients were aged 18 years or older with progressive HER2-positive advanced breast cancer after two or more HER2-directed regimens, including trastuzumab and lapatinib, plus previous taxane therapy. Randomisation was 2:1 to trastuzumab emtansine 3.6 mg/kg intravenously every 21 days or treatment of physician's choice, stratified by world region, number of previous regimens and visceral disease. Coprimary endpoints were investigator-assessed progression-free survival and overall survival.
th3resa.results: 602 patients were randomly assigned, 404 to trastuzumab emtansine and 198 to physician's choice. Median progression-free survival was 6.2 months versus 3.3 months (stratified hazard ratio 0.528, 95% CI 0.422 to 0.661, p<0.0001). The interim overall survival analysis favoured trastuzumab emtansine (stratified hazard ratio 0.552, 95% CI 0.369 to 0.826, p=0.0034) without crossing the stopping boundary. The 2017 final overall survival report gave median 22.7 months versus 15.8 months, hazard ratio 0.68 (95% CI 0.54 to 0.85).

time2.methods: Unblinded randomised controlled trial recruiting 106 patients with malignant pleural effusion and no previous pleurodesis from 143 treated at seven UK hospitals between April 2007 and February 2011, with 12 months of follow-up. Indwelling pleural catheters were inserted on an outpatient basis with initial large-volume drainage, education and home drainage. The talc arm was admitted for chest tube insertion and talc slurry pleurodesis. The primary endpoint was a daily 100 mm visual analogue scale for breathlessness over 42 days.
time2.results: Mean breathlessness score was 24.7 mm in the catheter arm and 24.4 mm in the talc arm over 42 days, difference 0.16 mm (95% CI -6.82 to 7.15, P = .96). At six months the difference was -14.0 mm in favour of the catheter (95% CI -25.2 to -2.8, P = .01). Median initial hospitalisation was 0 days against 4 days, difference -3.5 days (P < .001). Quality of life did not differ. Further pleural procedures were needed by 3 of 52 catheter patients against 12 of 54 talc patients. Adverse events occurred in 21 of 52 against 7 of 54.

tnt.methods: Phase 3 randomised trial in patients with unselected advanced triple-negative breast cancer. Carboplatin was compared with docetaxel. A prespecified protocol allowed biomarker by treatment interaction analyses in germline BRCA1/2 carriers and in BRCAness subgroups defined by BRCA1 methylation, low BRCA1 mRNA, a Myriad homologous recombination deficiency score, and basal-like phenotype. The primary endpoint was objective response rate.
tnt.results: Among 376 patients, 188 received carboplatin and 188 received docetaxel. Objective response rate was 31.4% versus 34.0%, P = 0.66. In germline BRCA1/2 carriers response was 68% with carboplatin versus 33% with docetaxel, interaction P = 0.01. No such benefit was seen with BRCA1 methylation, BRCA1 mRNA-low tumours or high Myriad homologous recombination deficiency score. The basal-like interaction was driven by high docetaxel response in nonbasal tumours.

tonic.methods: Adaptive, non-comparative phase 2 trial addressing the low efficacy of PD-1 blockade in metastatic triple-negative breast cancer and the preclinical suggestion that chemotherapy and irradiation have immunomodulatory properties. In the first stage, 67 patients with metastatic triple-negative breast cancer were randomised to nivolumab without induction or with two-week low-dose induction, or to irradiation (3 x 8 Gy), cyclophosphamide, cisplatin or doxorubicin, each followed by nivolumab. Response was assessed by iRECIST. Translational analyses compared gene expression after induction to test whether the priming strategies altered the tumour microenvironment.
tonic.results: In the overall cohort the objective response rate was 20%. The majority of responses were observed in the cisplatin cohort, objective response rate 23%, and the doxorubicin cohort, objective response rate 35%. After doxorubicin and cisplatin induction the investigators detected upregulation of immune-related genes involved in PD-1/PD-L1 and T cell cytotoxicity pathways. Among genes upregulated after doxorubicin there was enrichment for inflammation, JAK-STAT and TNF-alpha signalling.
