The authors conclude that short-term doxorubicin and cisplatin may induce a more favourable tumour microenvironment and that the findings warrant confirmation in TNBC and exploration in other cancer types.

top.methods: The neoadjuvant Trial of Principle (TOP), in which patients with oestrogen receptor-negative tumours were treated with epirubicin monotherapy, was designed to evaluate the predictive value of topoisomerase II-α (TOP2A) and to develop a gene expression signature identifying patients who do not benefit from anthracyclines. The trial included 149 patients, 139 of them evaluable for response prediction analyses, and the primary end point was pathological complete response. TOP2A and gene expression profiles were evaluated in pre-epirubicin biopsies, and gene expression data from ER-negative samples of the EORTC 10994/BIG 00-01 and MDACC 2003-0321 neoadjuvant trials were used for validation.
top.results: A pathological complete response was obtained in 14% of evaluable patients. TOP2A amplification, but not protein overexpression, was significantly associated with complete response (P ≤ .001 vs P ≤ .33). An anthracycline-based score (A-Score) combining a TOP2A gene signature with two published signatures of tumour invasion and immune response had a high negative predictive value, 0.98 (95% CI 0.90 to 1.00), overall and in the HER2-negative and HER2-positive subpopulations, confirmed in the anthracycline-based arms of the two validation trials (BIG 00-01 0.83, 0.64 to 0.94; MDACC 2003-0321 1.00, 0.80 to 1.00).

topacio.methods: Open-label, single-arm phase 2 study that enrolled 55 eligible patients with advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer at 34 US sites, irrespective of BRCA mutation status or PD-L1 expression. Data were collected from January 3, 2017 through October 29, 2018 and analysed through February 27, 2019. Patients received oral niraparib 200 mg once daily with intravenous pembrolizumab 200 mg on day 1 of each 21-day cycle. The primary endpoint was objective response rate by RECIST version 1.1. Secondary endpoints were safety, disease control rate, duration of response, progression-free survival and overall survival.
topacio.results: Among the 55 women enrolled, median age 54 years, 5 had a confirmed complete response, 5 a confirmed partial response, 13 stable disease and 24 progressive disease. In the efficacy-evaluable population of 47, the objective response rate was 21%, 10 patients (90% CI 12% to 33%), and the disease control rate 49%, 23 patients (90% CI 36% to 62%); median duration of response was not reached, with 7 patients still on treatment. In 15 evaluable patients with tumour BRCA mutations the objective response rate was 47% (90% CI 24% to 70%), disease control rate 80% (90% CI 56% to 94%) and median progression-free survival 8.3 months (95% CI 2.1 months to not estimable). In 27 evaluable patients with BRCA wild-type tumours the corresponding figures were 11% (90% CI 3% to 26%), 33% (90% CI 19% to 51%) and 2.1 months (95% CI 1.4 to 2.5). The most common grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events were anaemia in 10 patients (18%), thrombocytopenia in 8 (15%) and fatigue in 4 (7%); immune-related adverse events were reported in 8 patients (15%) and were grade 3 in 2 (4%).

torchlight.methods: Randomised double-blinded phase 3 trial of first-line toripalimab plus nab-paclitaxel in 353 women against placebo plus nab-paclitaxel in 178 women with metastatic or recurrent triple-negative breast cancer. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review in the PD-L1-positive and intention-to-treat populations. Secondary endpoints included overall survival and safety.
torchlight.results: PD-L1-positive disease was present in 200 patients in the toripalimab arm and 100 in the placebo arm. At the prespecified interim analysis median progression-free survival in the PD-L1-positive population was 8.4 versus 5.6 months, hazard ratio 0.65, P = 0.0102. Median overall survival was 32.8 versus 19.5 months, hazard ratio 0.62, P = 0.0148. Grade 3 or worse treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 56.4% versus 54.3%, and fatal events in 0.6% versus 3.4%.

touch.methods: TOUCH is an international, open-label, randomised phase II trial in postmenopausal patients with cT above 1 cm, cN0 or cN1, hormone receptor-positive, HER2-positive breast cancer. Patients were randomly assigned to 16 weeks of neoadjuvant weekly paclitaxel or to palbociclib and letrozole, both with trastuzumab plus pertuzumab. The primary objective investigated the interaction between a gene signature of E2F pathway activity, RBsig, and pathological complete response defined as ypT0N0 or ypTisN0. The hypothesis was a higher pCR for RBsig-high tumours in the paclitaxel group and for RBsig-low tumours in the palbociclib and letrozole group. RBsig was assessed by RNA sequencing of pre-treatment biopsies and intrinsic subtypes were estimated by absolute intrinsic molecular subtyping. The treatment-by-biomarker interaction was estimated using logistic regression in 115 assessable patients.
touch.results: 147 patients were randomly assigned, 74 to paclitaxel with trastuzumab and pertuzumab and 73 to palbociclib, letrozole, trastuzumab and pertuzumab, and 145 constituted the treated population, with a median age of 69 years. More patients completed palbociclib than paclitaxel, 94.4% versus 79.5%. The most frequent grade 3-4 adverse events were neutropenia, 6.9% with paclitaxel versus 43.1% with palbociclib, and diarrhoea, 11% versus 8.3%. The pCR rate was 32.9% (95% CI 22.3% to 44.9%) in the paclitaxel group and 33.3% (95% CI 22.7% to 45.4%) in the palbociclib and letrozole group, and no significant treatment-by-RBsig interaction was observed, P = 0.18. pCR was higher in non-luminal than luminal tumours, 45.5% versus 18.4%, with no interaction with treatment.

train-3.methods: Single-arm phase 2 study across 43 hospitals in the Netherlands. Patients received paclitaxel, trastuzumab, carboplatin and pertuzumab for up to nine cycles and were referred for surgery once MRI showed a complete radiological response. Patients with a pathological complete response completed one year of trastuzumab and pertuzumab. Patients with residual invasive disease completed nine cycles then received 14 cycles of trastuzumab emtansine. The primary endpoint was three-year event-free survival.
train-3.results: 235 patients with hormone receptor-negative and 232 with hormone receptor-positive tumours were enrolled. Median follow-up was 40.1 months. Three-year event-free survival was 92.2% and 92.0% respectively, with 40 events in 467 patients. By cycles given, event-free survival was 96.1% and 98.6% after one to three cycles, 89.2% and 94.2% after four to six, and 90.6% and 85.4% after seven to nine. Grade 3-4 neutropenia affected 40%.

train2.methods: Secondary analysis of an open-label, randomised phase 3 trial at 37 hospitals in the Netherlands. 438 patients with stage II and III ERBB2-positive breast cancer were randomised 1:1, stratified by age, tumour stage, nodal stage and oestrogen receptor status, to three cycles of fluorouracil, epirubicin and cyclophosphamide then six cycles of paclitaxel and carboplatin, or to nine cycles of paclitaxel and carboplatin. Both groups received trastuzumab and pertuzumab every three weeks. Outcomes were 3-year event-free survival and overall survival.
train2.results: Median follow-up was 48.8 months (interquartile range 44.1 to 55.2). There were 23 event-free survival events (10.5%) in the anthracycline group and 21 (9.6%) in the non-anthracycline group (hazard ratio 0.90, 95% CI 0.50 to 1.63). Three-year event-free survival was 92.7% with anthracyclines and 93.6% without. Three-year overall survival was 97.7% and 98.2%. A left ventricular ejection fraction decline of 10% or more to below 50% occurred in 7.7% versus 3.2% (P=.04).

trak-er.methods: Multicentre study in high-risk oestrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative early breast cancer. High risk included four or more involved lymph nodes, a tumour over 5 cm, or one to three involved nodes with additional high-risk features. Patients undergo circulating tumour DNA surveillance every 3 months for up to 3 years during adjuvant endocrine therapy, with a tumour-informed assay (Labcorp). On detection they have staging scans. Those without radiological recurrence are randomised to palbociclib plus fulvestrant or standard endocrine therapy. This report is a protocol-specified analysis of detection during surveillance and of contemporaneous radiological recurrence.
trak-er.results: By September 2025, 1133 patients had been registered. Panels were designed for 928, with design failing in 16.1% (178 of 1106). Surveillance began in 912 patients, who contributed 5810 tests, a median of 7 per patient. Detection was 5.0% (45 of 897) at the first test and 1.3% (66 of 4913) in subsequent tests (P<0.001). Patient-level detection was 12.0% (109 of 912). Clinical recurrence without prior detection occurred in 1.1% (10 of 912). Detection was associated with nodal burden (P<0.001) and grade (P=0.04). It was negatively associated with increasing time from surgery (P=0.01). Estimated cumulative detection at 5 years after surgery was 23.7% (95% CI 14.5 to 31.9%). Staging found radiological recurrence in 65.9% (29 of 44) of patients detected at the first test, against 26.6% (17 of 64) of those first detected on a later test (P<0.001).

trasturel.methods: Multicentre, randomised, two-arm, parallel-group comparative phase 3 study in patients with metastatic HER2-overexpressing breast cancer. Stage I measured single-dose pharmacokinetics in 42 participants after an 8 mg/kg loading dose. Stage II randomised 106 patients at 20 centres to biosimilar or reference trastuzumab with paclitaxel. The primary endpoint, objective response rate, was analysed after the last participant had completed the 25-week evaluation; secondary outcomes included time to tumour progression, progression-free and overall survival at week 48, and safety.
trasturel.results: Mean Cmax was 229.02 and 210.68 μg/mL and AUC0-336 24298.29 and 25809.33 μg×h/mL for reference and study trastuzumab. Objective response rates were comparable, 48.44% with study trastuzumab and 44.44% with reference trastuzumab, as were the proportions with complete and partial response. At least one adverse event occurred in 56 (68.29%) participants in the study arm and 13 (59.09%) in the reference arm, and no participant had a positive antibody titre.

trastuzumab-cisplatin-pegram.methods: Phase 2, open-label, multicentre trial of intravenous recombinant humanised anti-p185HER2 monoclonal antibody (rhuMAb HER2) with cisplatin in extensively pretreated patients with HER2/neu-overexpressing metastatic breast cancer and progression during standard chemotherapy. Patients received rhuMAb HER2 250 mg on day 0, then 100 mg weekly for 9 weeks, and cisplatin 75 mg/m2 on days 1, 29 and 57. Toxicity, pharmacokinetics, response rate and response duration were assessed.
trastuzumab-cisplatin-pegram.results: Of 37 patients assessable for response, nine (24.3%) had a partial response, nine (24.3%) a minor response or stable disease and 19 (51.3%) progression; median response duration was 5.3 months (range 1.6 to 18). Grade 3 or 4 toxicity occurred in 22 of 39 (56%), reflecting cisplatin, most often cytopenias, nausea and vomiting and asthenia. rhuMAb HER2 pharmacokinetics were unaltered by cisplatin.

trastuzumab-monotherapy-cobleigh.methods: Multinational study of recombinant humanised anti-HER2 monoclonal antibody (trastuzumab) as a single agent in 222 women with HER2-overexpressing metastatic breast cancer that had progressed after one or two chemotherapy regimens for metastatic disease. Patients received a 4 mg/kg intravenous loading dose followed by 2 mg/kg weekly.
trastuzumab-monotherapy-cobleigh.results: Patients had advanced metastatic disease and extensive prior therapy. A blinded, independent response evaluation committee identified 8 complete and 26 partial responses, an objective response rate of 15% in the intention-to-treat population (95% CI 11% to 21%). Median duration of response was 9.1 months and median survival 13 months. Infusion-associated fever or chills occurred in about 40%, usually only with the first infusion; cardiac dysfunction occurred in 4.7%, and 1% discontinued for treatment-related adverse events.

trastuzumab-weekly-baselga.methods: Phase 2 study of weekly intravenous recombinant humanised anti-p185HER2 monoclonal antibody (rhuMAb HER2) in 46 patients with HER2-overexpressing metastatic breast cancer. Patients received a 250 mg loading dose, then 10 weekly doses of 100 mg; those without progression at the end of this period were offered maintenance at 100 mg weekly.
trastuzumab-weekly-baselga.results: Patients had extensive metastatic disease and most had received extensive prior therapy. Adequate pharmacokinetic levels were obtained in 90%, toxicity was minimal and no antibodies against rhuMAb HER2 were detected. Objective responses occurred in 5 of 43 assessable patients, one complete and four partial (11.6%, 95% CI 4.36 to 25.9), in liver, mediastinum, lymph nodes and chest wall. Minor responses in two patients and stable disease in 14 lasted a median of 5.1 months.

tremelimumab-exemestane.methods: Phase 1 study in which 26 patients with advanced, hormone-responsive breast cancer received tremelimumab, a fully human CTLA-4 antibody, at 3 to 10 mg/kg every 28 days or every 90 days, plus exemestane 25 mg daily. The objectives were to determine safety and the maximum tolerated dose of tremelimumab with exemestane and, secondarily, tumour response, pharmacokinetics and immune pharmacodynamics.
tremelimumab-exemestane.results: Most treatment-related adverse events were mild to moderate, commonly diarrhoea (46%), pruritus (42%), constipation (23%) and fatigue (23%). Dose-limiting toxicities were transient serum transaminase elevation (one patient) and diarrhoea (four). The maximum tolerated dose was 6 mg/kg every 90 days, and none of the 13 patients treated at it had grade 3 or 4 treatment-related diarrhoea. No pharmacokinetic interaction was seen. Best overall response was stable disease for 12 weeks or more in 11 patients (42%). Treatment increased peripheral CD4 and CD8 T cells expressing ICOS and the ratio of ICOS-positive T cells to FoxP3-positive regulatory T cells.

trilaciclib-gemcitabine-carboplatin.methods: Randomised, open-label, multicentre phase 2 study in adults with evaluable, biopsy-confirmed, locally recurrent or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer and no more than two previous lines of chemotherapy, recruited in the USA, Serbia, North Macedonia, Croatia and Bulgaria. Patients were assigned 1:1:1, stratified by previous lines of systemic therapy and liver metastases, to gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 and carboplatin AUC 2 on days 1 and 8 (group 1), the same plus trilaciclib 240 mg/m2 on days 1 and 8 (group 2), or gemcitabine and carboplatin on days 2 and 9 plus trilaciclib on days 1, 2, 8 and 9 (group 3), in 21-day cycles. The primary endpoints were duration of severe neutropenia during cycle 1 and occurrence of severe neutropenia during treatment; overall survival was a key secondary endpoint.
trilaciclib-gemcitabine-carboplatin.results: Between February 2017 and May 2018, 102 patients were randomly assigned, 34 to group 1, 33 to group 2 and 35 to group 3; 38 (37%) had received one or two previous lines of chemotherapy for metastatic disease. Mean duration of severe neutropenia in cycle 1 was 0.8, 1.5 and 1.0 days (group 3 vs group 1 p=0.70), and severe neutropenia occurred in 26%, 36% and 23% of patients (p=0.70). Overall survival was 12.6 months in group 1, 20.1 months in group 2 and 17.8 months in group 3 (group 3 vs group 1 p=0.0023). Neutropenia and thrombocytopenia were among the most common treatment-emergent adverse events in every group, and there were no treatment-related deaths.

triniti-1.methods: Multicentre, open-label, single-arm, phase I/II study in patients with locally advanced or metastatic hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer. Treatment was ribociclib, everolimus and exemestane, all once daily on days 1 to 28 of a 28-day cycle. The recommended phase II doses were ribociclib 300 mg with everolimus 2.5 mg and exemestane 25 mg in group 1, and ribociclib 200 mg with everolimus 5 mg and exemestane 25 mg in group 2. The primary endpoint was clinical benefit rate at week 24 among patients with endocrine-therapy-refractory disease that had progressed on a CDK4/6 inhibitor. Other endpoints included safety and biomarker analysis.
triniti-1.results: Of 104 patients enrolled across phases I and II, 96 had received a prior CDK4/6 inhibitor. Clinical benefit rate at week 24 among the 95 efficacy-evaluable patients from phases I and II was 41.1% (95% CI 31.1 to 51.6), meeting the primary endpoint against a predetermined threshold of 10%. Common adverse events were neutropenia in 69.2% and stomatitis in 40.4%. No new safety signals were observed and no grade 3 or 4 QTc prolongation was reported. The authors describe the safety and efficacy results as preliminary and as supporting further investigation of combined CDK4/6 and PI3K/AKT/mTOR blockade in this setting.

trofuse-011.methods: Ongoing randomised phase III study in adults with previously untreated, centrally confirmed, locally recurrent unresectable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer with a PD-L1 combined positive score below 10, measurable disease by RECIST version 1.1, ECOG performance status 0 or 1, and a tumour tissue sample for central PD-L1 and TROP2 testing. Patients are randomised to sacituzumab tirumotecan (arm A), sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab (arm B), or treatment of physician's choice, which is paclitaxel, nab-paclitaxel, or gemcitabine plus carboplatin (arm C). The primary endpoints are progression-free survival for arm A against arm C and for arm B against arm C, and overall survival for arm A against arm C. Secondary endpoints include progression-free survival for arm B against arm A, overall survival for arm B against arm C and against arm A, objective response rate for each investigational arm against arm C, duration of response, patient-reported outcomes and safety.

trofuse-032.methods: Ongoing randomised, open-label, phase III study in adults with previously untreated high-risk, early-stage, non-metastatic triple-negative or HR-low-positive/HER2-negative breast cancer, centrally confirmed. Participants are randomised to sacituzumab tirumotecan with pembrolizumab followed by pembrolizumab with carboplatin and paclitaxel, or to pembrolizumab with carboplatin and paclitaxel followed by pembrolizumab with cyclophosphamide and doxorubicin or epirubicin. Both arms proceed to surgery and adjuvant pembrolizumab, with treatment of physician's choice allowed for residual disease. The primary endpoints are pathological complete response (ypT0/Tis ypN0) at definitive surgery and event-free survival. Overall survival is a secondary endpoint.

tropics02.methods: Randomised, open-label, multicentre phase 3 trial at 91 centres in North America and Europe. Patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative locally recurrent inoperable or metastatic breast cancer who had received at least one previous endocrine therapy, a taxane and a CDK4/6 inhibitor, plus two to four previous chemotherapy regimens for metastatic disease, were randomly assigned 1:1 to sacituzumab govitecan or chemotherapy (eribulin, vinorelbine, capecitabine or gemcitabine). This report is the final overall survival analysis.
tropics02.results: 543 patients were randomly assigned, 272 to sacituzumab govitecan and 271 to chemotherapy. With a median follow-up of 12.5 months, 390 deaths had occurred. Median overall survival was 14.4 months versus 11.2 months (hazard ratio 0.79, 95% CI 0.65 to 0.96, p=0.020), consistent across Trop-2 expression subgroups. Objective response rate was 21% versus 14% (odds ratio 1.63, p=0.035). The 2022 primary analysis reported median progression-free survival of 5.5 months versus 4.0 months, hazard ratio 0.66.

tropion-b01.methods: Global, open-label, randomised phase 3 trial. Adults with inoperable or metastatic hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer who had progressed on endocrine therapy or for whom it was unsuitable, and who had received one to two previous lines of chemotherapy in that setting, were randomly assigned 1:1 to datopotamab deruxtecan 6 mg/kg every 3 weeks or investigator's choice chemotherapy (eribulin, vinorelbine, capecitabine or gemcitabine). Dual primary endpoints were progression-free survival by blinded independent central review and overall survival.
tropion-b01.results: 365 patients were assigned to datopotamab deruxtecan and 367 to investigator's choice chemotherapy. Progression-free survival by blinded review favoured datopotamab deruxtecan (hazard ratio 0.63, 95% CI 0.52 to 0.76, p<0.0001), with consistent benefit across subgroups. Overall survival data were immature, with a hazard ratio of 0.84 (95% CI 0.62 to 1.14). Grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events occurred in 20.8% versus 44.7%. Commonest were nausea (51.1%) and stomatitis (50%) with datopotamab deruxtecan, neutropenia (42.5%) with chemotherapy.

tropion-b02.methods: Randomised, open-label, international phase III trial. Patients with previously untreated, locally recurrent inoperable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer for whom immunotherapy was not an option were randomly assigned 1:1 to datopotamab deruxtecan 6 mg/kg intravenously every 3 weeks or to investigator's choice of chemotherapy. Randomisation was stratified by geographic location, disease-free interval and programmed cell death ligand-1 status. Dual primary endpoints were progression-free survival by blinded independent central review and overall survival. Efficacy was analysed by intention to treat.
tropion-b02.results: Between 16 May 2022 and 11 June 2024, 644 patients were randomly assigned, 323 to datopotamab deruxtecan and 321 to chemotherapy. Median progression-free survival was 10.8 months versus 5.6 months (hazard ratio 0.57, 99% CI 0.44 to 0.73, P<0.0001). Median overall survival was 23.7 months versus 18.7 months (hazard ratio 0.79, 95.01% CI 0.64 to 0.98, P=0.029). Grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events affected 105 patients (33%) and 89 patients (29%). There were no treatment-related deaths.

tropion-b03.methods: Ongoing randomised phase III global trial in patients aged 18 years or older with stage I to III triple-negative breast cancer and residual invasive disease at surgical resection after neoadjuvant treatment. Patients are randomised 2:1:2 to datopotamab deruxtecan 6 mg/kg intravenously every 3 weeks for eight cycles plus durvalumab 1120 mg every 3 weeks for nine cycles, to datopotamab deruxtecan monotherapy, or to investigator's choice of capecitabine, pembrolizumab, or both. The primary endpoint is invasive disease-free survival.

tropion-b04.methods: Ongoing international, phase III, open-label, randomised controlled study in patients aged 18 years or older with previously untreated early-stage triple-negative or HR-low/HER2-negative breast cancer. Patients are randomised 1:1 to eight cycles of neoadjuvant datopotamab deruxtecan 6 mg/kg intravenously every 3 weeks plus durvalumab 1120 mg every 3 weeks, followed by nine cycles of adjuvant durvalumab with or without chemotherapy, or to eight cycles of pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks plus chemotherapy, followed by nine cycles of adjuvant pembrolizumab with or without chemotherapy. The dual primary endpoints are pathological complete response by blinded central review and event-free survival by investigator assessment. Overall survival is the key secondary endpoint, alongside distant disease-free survival, patient-reported outcomes and safety.

tropion-b05.methods: Ongoing randomised, open-label, multicentre phase III study in patients aged 18 years or older with PD-L1-high locally recurrent inoperable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer, defined as a combined positive score of 10 or more by the 22C3 assay. Patients are randomised 1:1 to datopotamab deruxtecan 6 mg/kg intravenously every 3 weeks plus durvalumab 1120 mg intravenously every 3 weeks, or to investigator's choice of chemotherapy (paclitaxel, nab-paclitaxel, or gemcitabine plus carboplatin) plus pembrolizumab 200 mg intravenously every 3 weeks. In selected countries patients are also randomised 1:1:1 to a third arm of datopotamab deruxtecan monotherapy. The primary endpoint is progression-free survival by blinded independent central review, datopotamab deruxtecan plus durvalumab against chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. Overall survival is the key secondary endpoint.

tryphaena.methods: Multicentre, open-label phase II cardiac safety study. Patients with operable, locally advanced or inflammatory HER2-positive breast cancer were randomised 1:1:1 to six neoadjuvant cycles every 3 weeks. Arm A gave fluorouracil, epirubicin and cyclophosphamide with trastuzumab and pertuzumab for three cycles, then docetaxel with both antibodies. Arm B gave the same chemotherapy alone for three cycles, then docetaxel with both antibodies. Arm C gave docetaxel, carboplatin, trastuzumab and pertuzumab. Adjuvant treatment completed one year of trastuzumab.
tryphaena.results: Two hundred twenty-five patients were randomised. During neoadjuvant treatment two patients (2.7%, arm B) had symptomatic left ventricular systolic dysfunction. Eleven patients had ejection fraction declines of 10 points or more from baseline to below 50% (four in arm A, four in arm B, three in arm C). Pathologic complete response (ypT0/is) was 61.6% in arm A, 57.3% in arm B, 66.2% in arm C. The 2017 long-term analysis gave 3-year disease-free survival of 87%, 88% and 90%.

tutor.methods: Prospective single-arm multicentre phase 1 trial at six United States centres. Eligible patients are aged 18 or older with ECOG 0 to 2 and up to ten newly diagnosed brain metastases. Any number of prior systemic therapies is allowed except tucatinib or capecitabine. Patients receive oral tucatinib alongside stereotactic radiosurgery and a two-week dose-limiting toxicity period, then capecitabine on days 1 to 14 and trastuzumab on day 1 of each 21-day cycle. A 3+3 de-escalation design starts at 300 mg.

tuxedo-1.methods: Prospective open-label single-arm phase 2 trial. Patients aged 18 years or older with HER2-positive breast cancer and newly diagnosed untreated brain metastases or brain metastases progressing after local therapy, with previous trastuzumab and pertuzumab and no indication for immediate local therapy, received trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg every three weeks. The primary endpoint was intracranial response rate. A Simon two-stage design tested a null response rate below 26% against 61%.
tuxedo-1.results: Fifteen patients were treated. Two patients (13.3%) had a complete intracranial response, nine (60%) a partial response and three (20%) stable disease, giving a best intracranial response rate of 73.3%, 95% CI 48.1 to 89.1. No new safety signals were seen and quality of life and cognitive function were maintained. At final analysis with 26.5 months median follow-up, median progression-free survival was 21 months and median overall survival was not reached.

u-bomb.methods: Non-randomised phase 2 trial at five hospitals in China. Adults with ERBB2-negative metastatic breast cancer and untreated or progressive brain metastases were enrolled between May 2022 and October 2023, with a data cutoff of May 2024. Patients received bevacizumab 15 mg/kg on day 1 and utidelone 30 mg/m2 on days 1 to 5 every 3 weeks. The primary endpoint was central nervous system objective response rate by RECIST version 1.1.
u-bomb.results: 47 female patients were recruited, median age 53 years. 35 had untreated brain metastases and 12 had brain metastases progressing after local radiotherapy. The central nervous system objective response rate was 42.6% (95% CI 28.3 to 57.8) by RECIST version 1.1 and 40.4% (95% CI 26.4 to 55.7) by RANO-BM criteria. Median follow-up was 11.0 months. Median progression-free survival was 7.7 months, median central nervous system progression-free survival 10.6 months and median overall survival 15.1 months. Grade 3 or higher events were uncommon and no fatal events occurred.

u31402-a-j101.methods: Multicentre phase 1/2 study (U31402-A-J101) of patritumab deruxtecan, a HER3-directed antibody-drug conjugate, in adults with HER3-expressing advanced breast cancer and disease progression on previous therapies. Patients in the dose-escalation, dose-finding and dose-expansion parts received 1.6 to 8.0 mg/kg intravenously every 3 weeks or one of two alternative dosing regimens. Dose escalation determined the maximum tolerated dose and recommended dose for expansion, and safety and efficacy at that dose were assessed in dose expansion.
u31402-a-j101.results: 182 enrolled patients received at least one dose, after a median of five previous therapies for advanced disease. Objective response and median progression-free survival were 30.1% and 7.4 months in hormone receptor-positive HER2-negative disease (n = 113), 22.6% and 5.5 months in triple-negative disease (n = 53) and 42.9% and 11.0 months in HER2-positive disease (n = 14). Responses occurred in cancers with high and low HER3 membrane expression. Dose-limiting toxicities were decreased platelet count and raised aminotransferases. In dose expansion grade 3 or higher treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 71.4% and 9.9% discontinued for them; there were three grade 3 and one grade 5 treatment-related interstitial lung disease events.

us-oncology-01062.methods: Randomised phase III study of whether adding capecitabine to doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide followed by docetaxel benefits patients with early breast cancer. Treatment was eight cycles of AC then docetaxel 100 mg/m2, or AC then docetaxel 75 mg/m2 with capecitabine 825 mg/m2 twice daily on days 1 to 14. The primary endpoint was 5-year disease-free survival.
us-oncology-01062.results: Of 2,611 women, 1,304 were assigned AC then docetaxel and 1,307 AC then docetaxel with capecitabine. After a median follow-up of 5 years the study failed to meet its primary endpoint (hazard ratio 0.84, 95% CI 0.67 to 1.05, P = 0.125). Overall survival, a secondary endpoint, improved with capecitabine (hazard ratio 0.68, 0.51 to 0.92, P = 0.011). In ER-positive, HER2-negative disease, 70% node-positive, 26% and 59% of tumours had a central Ki-67 below 10% or below 20%, with only 17 (2%) and 53 (6%) disease-free survival events in these groups at 7 years.

us-oncology-9735.methods: Patients with early breast cancer were randomly assigned to four cycles of doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide at 60 and 600 mg/m2 (n = 510) or four cycles of docetaxel and cyclophosphamide at 75 and 600 mg/m2 (n = 506), each given intravenously every three weeks. This report covers seven-year disease-free and overall survival and the effect of age, hormone receptor status and HER2 status on outcome and toxicity.
us-oncology-9735.results: Median age was 50 years in women younger than 65 and 69 years in those 65 or older, with more nodal involvement in older women. At seven years disease-free survival was 81% with docetaxel and cyclophosphamide versus 75%, hazard ratio 0.74, P = 0.033, and overall survival 87% versus 82%, hazard ratio 0.69, P = 0.032. The advantage held in older and younger patients. No interaction was seen with hormone receptor or HER2 status.

veritac2.methods: Phase 3, open-label, randomised trial enrolling patients with oestrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer who had received one previous line of CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy plus one line of endocrine therapy, and up to one additional line of endocrine therapy. Patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to vepdegestrant 200 mg orally once daily in 28-day cycles or fulvestrant 500 mg intramuscularly, stratified by mutation status and visceral disease. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival by blinded independent central review.
veritac2.results: 624 patients underwent randomisation, 313 to vepdegestrant and 311 to fulvestrant. Among the 270 patients with mutations, median progression-free survival was 5.0 months (95% CI 3.7 to 7.4) with vepdegestrant and 2.1 months (95% CI 1.9 to 3.5) with fulvestrant (hazard ratio 0.58, 95% CI 0.43 to 0.78, P<0.001). Among all patients it was 3.8 months versus 3.6 months (hazard ratio 0.83, 95% CI 0.69 to 1.01, P=0.07). Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 23.4% and 17.6%.

veronica.methods: Randomised phase II trial evaluating the BCL2 inhibitor venetoclax with fulvestrant in oestrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer after progression on a CDK4/6 inhibitor, reported as the prespecified primary results. Pre- and postmenopausal females aged 18 years or older were randomised 1:1 to venetoclax 800 mg orally daily plus fulvestrant 500 mg intramuscularly, given on days 1 and 15 of cycle 1 and on day 1 of subsequent 28-day cycles, or to fulvestrant alone. The primary endpoint was clinical benefit rate. Secondary endpoints were progression-free survival, overall survival and safety. Exploratory biomarker analyses covered tumour BCL2 and BCL extra-large expression and PIK3CA circulating tumour DNA mutational status.
veronica.results: At the primary analysis, with a cutoff of August 5, 2020 and 103 patients, venetoclax did not significantly improve clinical benefit rate, which was 11.8% (6 of 51; 95% CI 4.44 to 23.87) with venetoclax plus fulvestrant versus 13.7% (7 of 51; 95% CI 5.70 to 26.26) with fulvestrant, a risk difference of -1.96% (95% CI -16.86 to 12.94). Median progression-free survival was 2.69 months (95% CI 1.94 to 3.71) with venetoclax plus fulvestrant versus 1.94 months (95% CI 1.84 to 3.55) with fulvestrant, stratified HR 0.94 (95% CI 0.61 to 1.45; P = 0.7853). Overall survival data were not mature. A nonsignificant improvement in clinical benefit rate and progression-free survival was observed in patients whose tumours had strong BCL2 expression by immunohistochemistry at 3+, a BCL2 to BCLXL Histoscore ratio of 1 or more, or PIK3CA wild-type status. The authors conclude that the findings do not indicate clinical utility for venetoclax plus fulvestrant in endocrine-resistant, CDK4/6 inhibitor-refractory disease, but suggest possible increased dependence on BCLXL in this setting.

viktoria1.methods: Phase III randomised trial in patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative, PIK3CA wild-type advanced breast cancer whose disease progressed during or after CDK4/6 inhibitor and aromatase inhibitor treatment. Patients were randomly assigned 1:1:1 to gedatolisib with palbociclib and fulvestrant, to gedatolisib with fulvestrant, or to fulvestrant monotherapy. The primary objective was progression-free survival by blinded independent central review, comparing each gedatolisib group with fulvestrant.
viktoria1.results: 392 patients were randomly assigned. Median study follow-up was 10.1 months. Median progression-free survival was 9.3 months in the gedatolisib triplet group, 7.4 months in the gedatolisib doublet group and 2.0 months in the fulvestrant group. Hazard ratios for progression or death versus fulvestrant were 0.24 (95% CI 0.17 to 0.35) for the triplet and 0.33 (95% CI 0.24 to 0.48) for the doublet, both P<.001. Grade 3 or higher neutropenia was 62.3% and 0.8%.

viktoria1-s2.methods: Open-label randomised phase 3 study, Study 2 of VIKTORIA-1, in HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer with a PIK3CA mutation that progressed on or after a CDK4/6 inhibitor with a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor. Patients had at most two prior endocrine lines for advanced disease, no chemotherapy for advanced disease and no prior mTOR, PI3K or AKT inhibitor. They were randomised 3:3:1 to gedatolisib with palbociclib and fulvestrant, alpelisib with fulvestrant, or gedatolisib with fulvestrant. The primary endpoint is progression-free survival by blinded independent central review, gedatolisib with palbociclib and fulvestrant against alpelisib with fulvestrant.
viktoria1-s2.results: The ESMO 2026 slides show subgroup results, each gedatolisib regimen against alpelisib with fulvestrant. With liver metastases, median progression-free survival was 9.1 months with the triplet and 11.1 months with the doublet against 4.6 months (HR 0.47 and 0.38). With visceral metastases it was 9.8 and 11.3 against 5.6 months (HR 0.52 and 0.53). Without liver metastases it was 21.5 months with the triplet against 9.1 months (HR 0.46). Objective response was 43% to 59% with the gedatolisib regimens against 33%, and median duration of response 19.4 to 27.8 against 7.5 months. Discontinuation for adverse events was 5% with the triplet and 4% with the doublet against 19% with alpelisib.

vinorelbine-trastuzumab-q3w.methods: Single-centre phase 2 study of vinorelbine with trastuzumab every 3 weeks in HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer (IHC 3+ or FISH-positive), performance status 2 or less, normal left ventricular ejection fraction and no more than one chemotherapy line for metastatic disease. Vinorelbine 30 mg/m2 was given on days 1 and 8 every 21 days and trastuzumab 8 mg/kg on day 1, then 6 mg/kg, every 21 days. A single-stage design (p0 = 0.45, p1 = 0.65, type I and II error 0.10) required 22 objective responses in 39 patients.
vinorelbine-trastuzumab-q3w.results: From November 2002 to May 2005, 50 patients were enrolled, median age 54 years. Among 40 eligible for response assessment there were 7 complete and 13 partial responses (overall response 50%, 95% exact CI 33.8 to 66.2) and 11 with stable disease, over 6 months in 10. In the whole series median progression-free survival was 9.6 months (7.3 to 12.3) and median overall survival 22.7 months (19.5 to not reached). Fifteen patients (30%) developed brain metastases. There was one toxic death from renal failure; grade 3 or 4 neutropenia occurred in 23 (46%) and febrile neutropenia in 4 (8%).

vitamin-e-hot-flashes.methods: Placebo-controlled, randomised, crossover trial. After a 1-week baseline, patients received 4 weeks of vitamin E 800 IU daily and then 4 weeks of identical placebo, or the reverse. Diaries recorded toxicities and hot flashes during the baseline week and both treatment periods.
vitamin-e-hot-flashes.results: No toxicity was seen in the 120 patients evaluated. The 105 who finished the first period had similar reductions in hot flash frequency in the two arms (25% vs 22%, P = .90). A crossover analysis showed a minimal decrease with vitamin E, about one hot flash a day fewer than with placebo (P <= .05). At the end, patients did not prefer vitamin E over placebo (32% vs 29%).

vorinostat-tamoxifen.methods: Phase 2 combination trial with correlative end points in patients with oestrogen receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer progressing on endocrine therapy, treated with vorinostat 400 mg daily for 3 of 4 weeks and tamoxifen 20 mg daily continuously. Histone acetylation and HDAC2 expression in peripheral blood mononuclear cells were evaluated.
vorinostat-tamoxifen.results: 43 patients, median age 56 years, were treated; 25 (58%) had received adjuvant tamoxifen, 29 (67%) had failed one prior chemotherapy regimen, and 42 (98%) had progressed after one and 23 (54%) after two aromatase inhibitors. The objective response rate by RECIST was 19% and the clinical benefit rate (response or stable disease over 24 weeks) 40%, with a median response duration of 10.3 months (8.1 to 12.4). Histone hyperacetylation and higher baseline HDAC2 levels correlated with response.

vrp-her2.methods: Mouse-to-human translational study of VRP-HER2, an alphaviral vector vaccine encoding a portion of HER2. In preclinical studies mice were immunised before or after implantation of human HER2-positive tumour cells. In the phase 1 trial, subjects with advanced HER2-overexpressing malignancies received VRP-HER2 every 2 weeks for three doses, alone in cohort 1 or concurrently with a HER2-targeted therapy in cohort 2.
vrp-her2.results: In preclinical models VRP-HER2 induced HER2-specific T cells and antibodies and inhibited tumour growth. In patients it was well tolerated and induced HER2-specific T cells and antibodies. There was one partial response and two patients with continued stable disease. Median overall survival was 50.2 months in cohort 1 (n = 4) and 32.7 months in cohort 2 (n = 18). Perforin expression by memory CD8 T cells after vaccination correlated significantly with improved progression-free survival.

wbrt-with-or-without-temozolomide.methods: Multicentre prospective randomised phase 2 study in patients with newly diagnosed intraparenchymal brain metastases from breast cancer unsuitable for surgery or radiosurgery. All patients received conformal whole-brain radiation therapy of 3 Gy fractions to 10 to 30 Gy, with or without concomitant temozolomide 75 mg/m2 daily during irradiation. The primary endpoint was objective response rate at six weeks on brain MRI by modified WHO criteria. Secondary endpoints were progression-free survival, overall survival, neurologic symptoms and tolerability.
wbrt-with-or-without-temozolomide.results: 100 patients were enrolled between February 2008 and November 2010, 50 per arm. Median age was 55 years and median follow-up 9.4 months. Objective response rate at six weeks was 36% with whole-brain radiation alone and 30% with added temozolomide, not significant. Median progression-free survival was 7.4 months versus 6.9 months and median overall survival 11.1 months versus 9.4 months. The most common grade 2 or worse acute toxicity was reversible lymphopenia.

wisconsin-tamoxifen.methods: Two-year randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of tamoxifen in 140 postmenopausal women with axillary node-negative breast cancer. Bone mineral density of the lumbar spine and radius was measured by photon absorptiometry, with biochemical measures of bone metabolism in a randomly selected subgroup of each arm.
wisconsin-tamoxifen.results: Mean lumbar spine bone mineral density rose by 0.61% a year with tamoxifen and fell by 1.00% a year with placebo (P < 0.001). Radial bone density fell to the same extent in both groups. Serum osteocalcin and alkaline phosphatase fell significantly with tamoxifen (P < 0.001 for each), while parathyroid hormone and 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D did not change significantly in either group.

wsg-adapt-hr-her2.methods: Trial combining the 21-gene recurrence score with response to three weeks of preoperative endocrine therapy to guide systemic treatment. Baseline and post-endocrine Ki67 were assessed centrally. Patients with none to three involved nodes received endocrine therapy alone, in the control arm if recurrence score was 11 or lower and in the experimental arm if recurrence score was 12 to 25 with endocrine response, meaning Ki67 of 10% or less. All other patients received dose-dense chemotherapy then endocrine therapy.
wsg-adapt-hr-her2.results: The intention-to-treat population was 2,290 patients, 1,422 experimental and 868 control. Five-year invasive disease-free survival was 92.6% versus 93.9%, five-year distant disease-free survival 95.6% versus 96.3% and five-year overall survival 97.3% versus 98.0%. Results were similar across age and nodal subgroups. Endocrine response occurred in 78.1% on aromatase inhibitors versus 41.1% on tamoxifen, and in 78.8% of recurrence score 0 to 11, 62.2% of 12 to 25 and 32.7% above 25.

wsg-adapt-tn.methods: Randomised neoadjuvant multicentre phase 2 trial. Patients with triple-negative breast cancer, oestrogen and progesterone receptor under 1% and HER2-negative, cT1c to cT4c, cN0 or node-positive, were randomly assigned to 12 weeks of nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 with gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 or with carboplatin AUC 2, given on days 1 and 8 every 3 weeks. The trial was powered for a pathological complete response comparison by arm and for early response, defined as a Ki-67 decrease of more than 30% or fewer than 500 invasive tumour cells in the three-week serial biopsy. Omission of further neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy was allowed only in patients with pathological complete response. The final report added invasive and distant disease-free survival and overall survival, and quantified 119 genes including PAM50 subtype on the nCounter platform alongside stromal tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes.
wsg-adapt-tn.results: 336 patients were enrolled at 48 centres, 182 to nab-paclitaxel plus gemcitabine and 154 to nab-paclitaxel plus carboplatin; median age was 50 years, and 62.6% and 62.9% respectively had cT2 to cT4c tumours. Pathological complete response was 28.7% versus 45.9%, P = .002, and was lower in early non-responders than in early responders, 19.5% versus 44.4%, P < .001. Nab-paclitaxel with gemcitabine brought more dose reductions, 20.6% versus 11.9%, and more grade 3 to 4 ALAT elevations, 11.7% versus 3.3%. After 60 months of median follow-up the final analysis found 12-week pathological complete response favourably associated with outcome, hazard ratio 0.24, with 5-year invasive disease-free survival of 90.6% versus 62.8%. No survival advantage of carboplatin was seen despite the higher pathological complete response rate, hazard ratio 1.04 (95% CI 0.68 to 1.59), and additional anthracycline-containing chemotherapy was not associated with a significant invasive disease-free survival advantage in patients with pathological complete response, hazard ratio 1.29 (95% CI 0.41 to 4.02).

wsg-adapt-tp.methods: Phase 2 trial. 375 patients with centrally confirmed HR+/HER2+ early breast cancer, clinical stage I to III, were randomly assigned 1:1:1 to 12 weeks of neoadjuvant T-DM1, T-DM1 plus endocrine therapy, or trastuzumab plus endocrine therapy every 3 weeks. Adjuvant chemotherapy could be omitted after pathologic complete response. Patients receiving at least one dose were analysed. Survival used Kaplan-Meier, log-rank and Cox models stratified for nodal and menopausal status.
wsg-adapt-tp.results: Five-year invasive disease-free survival was 88.9%, 85.3% and 84.6% across the three arms, p=0.608. Five-year overall survival was 97.2%, 96.4% and 96.3%, p=0.534. Patients with pathologic complete response had 5-year invasive disease-free survival of 92.7% versus 82.7% without, hazard ratio 0.40. Of 117 patients with pathologic complete response, 41 omitted adjuvant chemotherapy, with rates of 92.1% versus 93.0%, p=0.848.

wsg-am-01.methods: Multicentre phase III trial in patients with at least nine positive axillary nodes, randomly assigned to two courses of accelerated conventionally dosed epirubicin and cyclophosphamide at 2-week intervals with filgrastim, followed by two courses of high-dose epirubicin, cyclophosphamide and thiotepa supported by peripheral-blood progenitors, or to four identical cycles of epirubicin and cyclophosphamide followed by three cycles of accelerated cyclophosphamide, methotrexate and fluorouracil. The primary endpoint was event-free survival, analysed by intention to treat and per protocol.
wsg-am-01.results: 403 patients were enrolled, 201 assigned high-dose and 202 conventional treatment, with a mean of 17.6 positive nodes and a median follow-up of 48.6 months. Four-year event-free survival by intention to treat was 60% (95% CI 53 to 67) with high-dose chemotherapy and 44% (37 to 52) with control (P = 0.00069), and overall survival 75% (69 to 82) against 70% (64 to 77, P = 0.02). There were no treatment-related deaths.

wsg-planb.methods: Phase 3 trial in HER2-negative early breast cancer, pT1 to pT4c, all node-positive and high-risk node-negative disease. After an amendment, hormone receptor-positive tumours had recurrence score testing and chemotherapy omission was recommended for recurrence score 11 or lower with pN0 to pN1 disease. Remaining patients were randomly assigned to four cycles of epirubicin and cyclophosphamide followed by four cycles of docetaxel, or six cycles of docetaxel and cyclophosphamide, every 3 weeks.
wsg-planb.results: Of 3198 registered patients, 348 with recurrence score 11 or lower omitted chemotherapy and 2449 formed the randomised intention-to-treat population. After 60 months median follow-up, 5-year disease-free survival was 89.6% versus 89.9% and overall survival was 94.5% versus 94.7%. Among endocrine-treated patients with recurrence score 11 or lower, 5-year disease-free survival was 94% and overall survival was 99%.

wsg-tpii.methods: The trial was a multicenter, randomized, open-label phase II trial. 207 patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-positive early breast cancer were randomly assigned 1:1 to 12 weeks of neoadjuvant trastuzumab and pertuzumab with endocrine therapy or with weekly paclitaxel. All patients received dual HER2 blockade in the adjuvant setting. Further standard chemotherapy was obligatory in patients without pathologic complete response and optional after pathologic complete response. This report is the final 5-year survival analysis.
wsg-tpii.results: The pathologic complete response rate was 56.4% with paclitaxel and 23.7% with endocrine therapy. At 5 years, overall survival was 100% with endocrine therapy and 97.9% (95.0 to 100.0) with paclitaxel. Event-free survival-ductal carcinoma in situ at 5 years was 92.1% (86.6 to 97.9) with endocrine therapy and 94.8% (90.5 to 99.3) with paclitaxel. Five-year invasive disease-free survival was 97.7% (94.5 to 100.0) and 79.8% (55.6 to 100.0).

young-pearl-kcsg-br15-10.methods: Multicentre open-label phase 2 trial at 14 institutions in South Korea. Premenopausal women aged 19 years or older with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer that relapsed or progressed on tamoxifen were randomly assigned 1:1 to palbociclib 125 mg plus exemestane 25 mg with leuprolide, or capecitabine 1250 mg/m2 twice daily. One previous line of chemotherapy for metastatic disease was allowed. Randomisation was stratified by previous chemotherapy and visceral metastasis. Analysis was modified intention to treat.
young-pearl-kcsg-br15-10.results: 184 patients were randomly assigned, 92 to each group, and 178 entered the modified intention-to-treat analysis. At 17 months median follow-up, median progression-free survival was 20.1 months versus 14.4 months, hazard ratio 0.659, one-sided p=0.0235. Grade 3 or worse neutropenia occurred in 75% versus 16%. Treatment-related serious adverse events occurred in 2% versus 17%. No treatment-related deaths occurred.

z0011.methods: Phase 3 randomised noninferiority trial enrolling patients from May 1999 to December 2004 at 115 sites. Eligible women had clinical T1 or T2 invasive breast cancer, no palpable axillary adenopathy, and 1 or 2 sentinel lymph nodes with metastases. All patients had planned lumpectomy, tangential whole-breast irradiation and adjuvant systemic therapy, with third-field radiation prohibited. Patients were randomised to sentinel lymph node dissection alone or axillary lymph node dissection. The primary outcome was overall survival, noninferiority margin 1.3.
z0011.results: 891 women were randomised, 446 to sentinel lymph node dissection alone and 445 to axillary dissection. At a median follow-up of 9.3 years, 10-year overall survival was 86.3% with sentinel dissection alone and 83.6% with axillary dissection (hazard ratio 0.85, noninferiority P = .02). 10-year disease-free survival was 80.2% and 78.2% (hazard ratio 0.85, P = .32). Between years 5 and 10, 1 regional recurrence occurred with sentinel dissection alone and none with axillary dissection.

z1031.methods: Z1031 was a randomized phase II neoadjuvant trial designed to select agents for phase III study. 377 postmenopausal women with clinical stage II to III estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer, Allred score 6 to 8, were randomly assigned to neoadjuvant exemestane, letrozole, or anastrozole. The primary end point was clinical response. Secondary end points were breast-conserving surgery, change in Ki67, the Preoperative Endocrine Prognostic Index, and PAM50-based intrinsic subtype.
z1031.results: Letrozole and anastrozole were selected for further investigation on the basis of clinical response rates. No other differences in surgical outcome, PEPI score, or Ki67 suppression were detected. The breast-conserving surgery rate among patients presenting as mastectomy-only candidates was 51%. PAM50 identified aromatase inhibitor-unresponsive nonluminal subtypes in 3.3%. Clinical response and surgical outcomes were similar in luminal A and luminal B tumors. A PEPI of 0 was more frequent in luminal A tumors (27.1% v 10.7%; P = .004).

z1071.methods: The trial enrolled 756 women at 136 institutions from July 2009 to June 2011 with clinical T0 to T4, N1 to N2, M0 breast cancer treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy. After chemotherapy each patient underwent both sentinel lymph node surgery and axillary lymph node dissection. Mapping with both blue dye and a radiolabeled colloid was encouraged. The primary end point was the false-negative rate of sentinel node surgery in women presenting with biopsy-proven cN1 disease.
z1071.results: Of 663 evaluable cN1 patients, 649 underwent both sentinel node surgery and axillary dissection. No sentinel node was found in 46 (7.1%) and only one in 78 (12.0%). Of the remaining 525 with two or more sentinel nodes, 215 had no nodal cancer, a 41.0% pathological complete nodal response (36.7% to 45.3%). In 39 patients the dissection found cancer that the sentinel nodes missed, a false-negative rate of 12.6% (90% credible interval, 9.85% to 16.05%).

zephir.methods: Patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer, IHC 3+ or FISH 2.2 or higher, scheduled for trastuzumab emtansine had a pretreatment HER2 PET/CT with 89Zr-trastuzumab, plus FDG-PET/CT at baseline and before cycle 2. HER2-PET/CT was graded into four patterns by the share of FDG-avid tumor load taking up 89Zr above blood pool. Predictive values were assessed against RECIST 1.1 response after three cycles and time to treatment failure.
zephir.results: Fifty-six patients were analyzed. HER2-PET/CT was negative in 29%. Intrapatient heterogeneity was present in 46%. Against RECIST 1.1, negative and positive predictive values were 88% and 72% for HER2-PET/CT and 83% and 96% for early FDG-PET/CT. Combining the two gave predictive values of 100% and separated a group with median time to treatment failure of 2.8 months (n = 12, 95% CI 1.4 to 7.6) from one with 15 months (n = 25, 95% CI 9.7 to not calculable).
